versions.title: Readable weapon selection
versions.notes: - Mark the equipped weapon with [selected] instead of a star that could display as a missing-glyph box. Update the weapon-count tooltip to match.

versions.title: Main menu and onboarding
versions.notes:
- Start on a main menu with New Game, Load Game, Story, How to Play, Settings, Version History, and Exit.
- Browse the complete version history from the main menu as well as Escape.
- Read the city backstory and a scrollable guide before starting.
- Adjust shared audio settings from the title screen or pause menu.
- Return to the main menu from Escape without losing the current session; Resume continues it. Starting over asks before discarding unsaved progress; canceling a title-screen load returns to the menu.
- World simulation stays paused while browsing the menu.

versions.title: First playable survival sandbox
versions.notes:
EXPLORATION & SURVIVAL
- Explore a bounded city with 48 enterable buildings, two-room interiors, themed furniture, and proximity roof cutaways.
- Search outdoor and indoor supply crates; harvest trees and salvage wrecked cars.
- Manage health, nutrition, rations, sprinting, and escalating nighttime danger.
- Fight zombies and faster ferals with mouse-aimed combat and visible hit/damage feedback.

WEAPONS & CRAFTING
- Hatchet, wood-only club, spear, renewable wood-only bow/arrows, scavenged pistols and rifles.
- Finite ammunition, crafting costs, carried weapon quantities, and equipped-weapon indicators.
- Ranged weapons fire over placed defenses; city walls remain cover. Spears reach through barricades.

BUILDING & BASE DEFENSE
- Build barricades, shelters, gates, farms, and ammunition-fed turrets.
- Placement previews and collision checks; Shift-click repeat placement; R rotates barricades/gates.
- Open/close gates with E, repair barricades with V, and demolish placed structures with Shift+X for condition-based material refunds.
- Shelter zones exclude enemy spawns but can be overrun; turrets need ammunition.
- Grow renewable food in farms and plant saplings for renewable wood.

SURVIVORS
- Recruit survivors, escort them to shelter, and take guards on expeditions.
- Spaced follower formations; point at a nearby ally and use T to follow/hold, G to equip, or U to reclaim a weapon.
- Health bars, numeric HP, targeted-ally status, J feeding, and gradual shelter recovery when threats are absent.
- Armed survivors defend the group and share your ammunition supply.

MAP, FEEDBACK & AUDIO
- District minimap and Q radar scans showing enemy/friendly last-known positions with range, fade, and cooldown.
- Recent interaction messages and a scrollable 500-event history saved with your game.
- Original positional sound effects, ambient drone, and persistent volume/mute controls.

SAVES & MENUS
- Separate Save Game and Load Game screens through Escape or F5/F9.
- Named snapshots without a fixed slot cap; explicit confirmations for overwriting and loading.
- Persistent world depletion, construction, allies, inventory, and interior loot; older-save migration.
- Pause, field guide, restart after death, and this in-game version log.

PROTOTYPE LIMITS
- Single-floor interiors and local AI steering; full pathfinding is not yet implemented.
- No multiplayer, controller support, world streaming, or indoor base construction.
- Code-drawn art and synthesized audio; balancing and listening-based mix review remain ongoing.

versions.title: Sound, growing crops, and clear roads
versions.notes:
- Add original synthesized wind, gunshots, dry clicks, hit confirmation, swings, gathering, crafting, building, and damage sounds. Nearby survivors and turrets have positional gunfire.
- Add a saved audio volume slider to the title and pause menus; zero mutes all sound. Wind pauses with gameplay.
- Farm plants grow continuously from green shoots to golden grain over their 60-second cycle. Aiming at the bed shows progress and harvest readiness; harvesting replants immediately.
- Face building entrances toward the main road and move rows clear of the crossroad, including roofs and awnings. Rotate indoor supplies with the buildings.
- Migrate occupants and placed structures near old building plots when loading older saves; retain resource IDs and crop growth.

**Limitations:** Audio is synthesized rather than recorded. Browser playback requires an initial user gesture. AI still uses direct steering rather than navigation meshes.

versions.title: An overgrown autumn county
versions.notes:
- Refresh the world with weathered surface shading, mixed evergreen/autumn trees, ground cover, layered rock mountains, roadside shoulders, and utility poles.
- Add pitched roofs, chimneys, framed windows, awnings, facade trim, interior shelving, floorboards, and warm ceiling lights.
- Give survivors and infected clothing details, backpacks, boots, and walking limb animation. Add a gloved first-person hand and a distinct hatchet edge.
- Rebalance sky/ambient light and material reflections; blend dusk and dawn with cooler night skies and warm indoor lighting.
- Batch repeated static scenery and grass to reduce draw calls. Preserve existing save IDs, world generation, collisions, and gameplay rules.

**Limitations:** Procedural low-poly art, not photorealism. Added trim, vegetation, poles, and pitched roofs are decorative; existing collision shapes remain. Browser performance still needs hardware-specific playtesting.

versions.title: Clearer gun feedback and menu shortcuts
versions.notes:
- Remove arrow glyphs from Begin Expedition and Resume so web fonts cannot display missing-character boxes.
- Press C again to close crafting and resume; typing C in save names does not close the save browser.
- Pistol shots show a muzzle flash, recoil, and nearby ammo count. Confirmed hits show a large hit marker and damage; lethal hits show KILL.
- Empty trigger pulls show a red EMPTY prompt without firing feedback. Misses show FIRED instead of a hit marker.

**Limitations:** Feedback is visual; sound effects are not included. Browser pointer-lock policies still apply when resuming from crafting.

versions.title: Mouse capture and compact saves
versions.notes:
- Use unscaled mouse movement for aiming, keep yaw bounded over repeated turns, and discard capture-transition and oversized motion events.
- Press P to pause/resume. Escape releases the cursor and leaves the game paused; Resume requests capture on the initial button press.
- Pause when focus or pointer lock is lost. Browser gameplay waits for pointer lock and returns to the pause screen if the browser refuses it.
- Place the save-name field beside Create Save, with compact save rows showing names and timestamps on the left and Overwrite/Load on the right.

**Limitations:** Browser policy still controls pointer lock; embedded hosts must allow it. Save compatibility and gameplay systems are unchanged.

versions.title: Named expeditions and survivor equipment
versions.notes:
- Create separate named saves, browse names and UTC timestamps, and confirm before overwriting or loading.
- Open Save Game with F5 and Load Game with F9, or use the menus. Existing single-slot saves appear as Legacy quicksave.
- Give your selected spear or pistol to a recruited survivor with G; reclaim their weapon with U. Swapping returns their previous weapon.
- Craft spare weapons and see carried quantities in the HUD. Equipped survivors visibly carry weapons, use spear reach or pistol gunfire, and share your ammunition.
- Preserve survivor equipment in every save. Older saves load with survivors unarmed.

**Limitations:** No save rename/delete controls or autosave. Your starting hatchet stays with you. Empty survivor pistols fall back to close-range melee. Existing bounded-map and steering-AI limitations remain.

versions.title: The Quiet After — initial prototype
versions.notes:
- Explore a first-person 3D forest and town with enterable supply buildings, roads, and wrecks.
- Harvest wood and metal, search supply crates, and manage health, nutrition, and stamina.
- Fight infected with a hatchet, crafted spear, or pistol. Sprint, jump, and use a flashlight after dark.
- Recruit survivors, command them to follow or hold, and help them recover near a shelter.
- Craft barricades, shelters, farms, and turrets with validated placement. Grow food and load turret ammunition.
- Survive day/night cycles with more dangerous infected at night. Scan nearby contacts with local radar.
- Save and restore expeditions, including depleted supplies, inventory, survivors, structures, and world time.
- Includes a title screen, pause menu, crafting menu, field guide, and scrollable version log.

**Limitations:** Prototype: bounded, fixed-seed map; direct-steering AI; finite wood and metal; one save slot. No audio, multiplayer, controller support, or full feature parity with 2D Deadblock.

versions.title: Free the block table
versions.notes:
- Dyed blocks are now ordinary planks, concrete, windows and banners with the color stored in the block itself. You craft, place, break and pick them as before (Red Planks, Green Glass, White Banner and so on), and they look the same.
- Hold a dye and right-click a placed plank, concrete, window or banner to recolor it, the way carpets already worked. Banners on the map and in the shelter card follow the new color.
- Dyed blocks can be dragged out with the build key, and blueprints copy their colors (builders want the dyed blocks in their crate).
- Worlds saved before this version load their dyed blocks, crates, packs, blueprints and banners into the new form. This frees 23 block ids for blocks to come.

versions.title: One Records tab
versions.notes: - One Records tab. The journal's Seed of the week (your code and the box for a friend's) moves off the Stats page and joins Past lives on a new Records tab; the Past lives tab goes, so the journal has one tab fewer. Stats and Achievements keep their own tabs. The library's "Read Past lives" opens Records.

versions.title: Expeditions can leave someone behind
versions.notes:
- Expeditions can leave someone behind (a new World option, on). When an expedition to a dangerous city (danger 3 or more) comes back hurt, the guard who came off worst can be left there, missing (the roster says "missing in <city>"), and a rescue job for them joins your quests the same dawn.
- Go to the city and they find you, the same follower with the same gear; bring them back to their shelter's beacon and they go back on guard. The expedition menu says someone might not come back without help while the option is on.

versions.title: Caravans can be lost
versions.notes:
- Caravans can be lost. At night, a caravan's road with a stretch that has no light, claimed ground or beacon within 32 blocks is risky, and so is the horde's line while a migration walks it. By day a dark road is safe (the Ashen are under cover).
- The first risky run in a world costs nothing: "Mara nearly lost the caravan on the dark stretch 60 m east of Northgate: light the road or claim it" (a toast, the chronicle, and a journal note, "Dark roads"). After that a risky run loses half of what it carries, and the chronicle names the stretch.

versions.title: Followed home
versions.notes:
- Followed home. A pack (three or more Ashen running together) that was chasing you at dusk and loses you for 30 seconds keeps your heading: about a game hour later it turns up 30 blocks back along your way, never on lit ground, and makes for your nearest boards or door to claw.
- A minute before they arrive you're told why ("Something is on your trail"), the dog barks, and the first time a journal note, "Followed home", explains it. Swim for a couple of seconds, sneak for 20, or cross lit or claimed ground and you lose them.

versions.title: A friend's own people
versions.notes:
- A friend's own people (co-op). A friend can now talk to an idle survivor in your game and take them in: the survivor is theirs ("Sam's" on the shelter overview), posts at the friend's nearest own shelter (else the nearest shelter, else where they stand), and takes the friend's orders without the friend co-owning a shelter. Talking to one of their own again opens the orders.
- Your friend's game holds a copy of their people's records (sent when they recruit and each dawn), so if the host leaves and they keep a copy of the world, their people come along. The host keeps everyone in their own world.

versions.title: Smoke
versions.notes:
- Smoke (a new World option, on). After dark a burning campfire, furnace or electric furnace sends up a plume of smoke, and from the second night the Ashen within about 32 blocks come to it, like loud machines. The first night with a fire burning brings the warning: a toast and a journal note, "Smoke".
- A chimney stops it: leave the air over the fire open straight up to the sky and wall that shaft with stone, brick or concrete on all four sides for at least 3 blocks. Look at a fire: it says Smoking or Smoking (chimney). A tip the first time you look at one with a chimney.

versions.title: The trader reads the gazette
versions.notes:
- The trader reads the gazette. Two of a visit's four trades now come from what the last week says you're short of: bolts after a raid, bandages after a death, food when a shelter has three days or less, seeds in spring, coal in the autumn before winter. One buys your biggest crop surplus (24 or more of a crop in the shelter's crates) for steel or a battery, and the rest are the usual mix.
- The visit's toast says what she brought and why ("after the raid: bolts"). New trades: bolts for cobble or scrap, coal for logs or planks, bandages for cloth, canned food for scrap, bread for planks.

versions.title: The board reads the world
versions.notes:
- The board reads the world. A shelter's quest board now opens with one offer from what's happening around it, when something is: the ash front creeping within 200 blocks (push it back: sweep or dig out 20 ash blocks in the marked zone), a nest within 96 (burn it by day), a pack that learned your defense (add another kind of defense before the blood moon), or a migration's line across your road (keep the carriers off it until the horde has passed). The usual offers fill the rest.
- These pay by the threat like the rest. Mix fails if the blood moon comes first; the horde's line fails if a carrier's run still crosses it when the horde has passed.

versions.title: Gone to ground at dawn
versions.notes:
- Gone to ground at dawn. An Ashen caught out by the sunrise within about 24 blocks of cover (a building, a cave, a roof) no longer just burns: it runs for the dark, with 20 seconds of grace from the sun, leaving prints on any ground on the way, and waits in there.
- At dusk it walks back out of that door. By day, come within a few blocks of the spot and it comes at you in the dark, so clear buildings with a light and a weapon. A heliostat beam on the doorway for two hours burns it out. Farther than 24 blocks from cover they burn as before.
- The first time it happens: a toast and a journal note, "They've gone to ground". A guard on watch names the building in the morning ("one went to ground in the building 40 m north").

versions.title: They come out of the dark, not thin air
versions.notes:
- They come out of the dark, not thin air. At night most Ashen near you now walk out of a source: an unlit doorway (a door, or a dark covered spot between two walls that opens to the sky), a cave mouth, a nest, or ash ground. The rest still rise from any dark ground, so an open field at night stays dangerous; blood moons and the deadlands ignore sources.
- The spawn marks (Shift+G) show the sources out past the usual marks as purple X's, and the spawn scan lists them ("Tonight they come out of 3 doorways, 1 cave mouth"). Board or light a doorway and that's one less way in.
- The first night's note says they come out of the buildings and the dark ground.

versions.title: A reclaimed city pays back
versions.notes:
- A reclaimed city pays back. Every seventh dawn, each city you've reclaimed sends a caravan to your nearest shelter on a road within 600 blocks: 6 scrap and 4 cloth into its crates, now and then 2 bandages, and one week in four a survivor who wants to stay.
- No caravan comes from a city the ash is pushing on (a surge), or across a road a migration crossed that week; the chronicle says why. A toast the first time one arrives.

versions.title: The goal line lives to day 30
versions.notes:
- The goal line lives to day 30. The "What next?" line under the compass no longer goes blank at Halcyon Labs: it carries on to the vault and the counter-agent, taking it to Ashford's mayor's hall, reclaiming Ashford, lighting a second shelter, sending an expedition, holding a shelter through a blood moon, and reclaiming a far city. It goes quiet once all of that is done.
- Settings still turns the line off.

versions.title: Guests do everything
versions.notes:
- Guests do everything. In co-op a friend can now aim a heliostat, light, feed and cook on a campfire, sit an evening at the fire with the host's followers (their lines come to the friend), put saddlebags on a horse, and give a follower a day off (co-owners only). The host's game does the work and answers; the friend pays from their own pack.
- Shelter upgrades, projects and blueprints stay with the host: they spend the shelter's crates and builders.

versions.title: Nights you can't sleep through
versions.notes:
- Light sleeper. Sleep no longer jumps to dawn: the night runs an hour every moment or so under the fade, and the world keeps going. Ashen close by, clawing at boards within 24 blocks, a siren, raiders at the shelter, or a surge or migration passing near the bed wakes you at that hour with the night still on. Lie down again once it's quiet.
- Watches. With a guard on a battle post within 32 blocks of the bed, the bed offers "Turn in" and only the wall giving (a clawed board or door broken through), a raider within 8 or a siren wakes you. At dawn the guard reports what the watch saw: a pack that passed, nests glowing nearby, or a quiet night. In co-op the line joins the morning report.
- In co-op the host's sleep carries everyone; if the host wakes, everyone does.
- Fix: a co-op village (a friend's shelter beside yours) holds a raid as one again; the enclosure bonus from v0.13.198 now counts once, for its best-closed shelter.

versions.title: Winter is the siege
versions.notes:
- Winter is the siege. With Seasons on, winter brings a blood moon every fifth night instead of every seventh, counted from winter's first night so two never come close together at the season's edges. The calendar marks them a week ahead.
- Ash storms come oftener in winter (more storm-dark days, when the Ashen walk by day) and less often in spring, the recovery.
- The toast the day before winter and the "Winter that bites" note say so.

versions.title: The cure spreads
versions.notes:
- The cure spreads. After you deliver the counter-agent, Ashford sends out doses of the cure every seventh dawn: two, plus one for every city you've reclaimed. The chronicle counts them, and the Ashford Gazette prints the running total.
- Each reclaimed city within 600 blocks of a player gets one cured survivor a week, waiting in its main square to be taken in. They remember waking there.
- Once ten doses are out, a cheaper cure dart shows at the workbench: 2 bolts and a bandage make 2.
- A reclaimed city whose square falls to a surge keeps its heart nest burned and its nests gone; relight the square to win it back.

versions.title: The counting voice
versions.notes:
- The counting voice. After the six Halcyon fragments, the voice counting down from ten turns out to be a person. Each repaired radio tower now takes a bearing on her: a dotted line on your map pointing at the signal. With two towers the lines cross at her camp, marked "The counting voice".
- Go there and you'll find Ines Varga, a radio operator, by her fire with two crates and a radio console. Take her in like any survivor. Posted near a repaired tower's console (or at your shelter once it has the radio station), she reads the week's gazette headline on the dusk broadcast, and your tower network reaches half as far again.
- A journal note explains the bearings the first time.

versions.title: Hunter job
versions.notes:
- Hunter job. A follower on the new Hunter job brings in a haul once a day at dawn: a wild deer or boar from within 48 blocks of their post, as raw meat and leather in their crate (two hauls with a crossbow), or raw fish when there's water and no game. They leave tame, led, tied and penned animals alone.
- Hunters also top up empty feed troughs within 48 blocks with wheat, berries or tubers from the crate. Hunter is on the survivor panel and the shelter's loadouts.

versions.title: Enclosure counts
versions.notes:
- Enclosure counts. When a raid comes to a shelter you're away from, its defense now counts its walls: if the ground round the beacon is closed in (walls, fences, boards, shut doors, and with Moats water two deep) so nothing can walk in, the shelter scores 6 more, less one for each cracked door or board on the way out.
- The ledger's Shelter page says "Walls: closed", "Walls: open to the east", or "closed, but the north boards are cracked", so you can fix the gap before a raid you won't be there for. A tip explains it the first time a shelter is closed.

versions.title: One guide
versions.notes:
- One guide. The first-time tips, the stuck tip, the night coach and the other first-time cards (the handcar, the broadcast, roadside finds) now share one queue: one card at a time, never over an open screen, and at least 20 seconds after the last one closed. The night coach still goes first.
- The starter steps' "Done" toast no longer adds a "Next:" line; the next step is on the goal line under the compass. The Tips switch turns every card off.
- L is free: the spawn marks live on Shift+G (Near, Scan, Off). Nothing is on L for now.

versions.title: Rewards follow the threat
versions.notes:
- Rewards follow the threat. Quest board and bounty rewards now grow with the ash threat: a quarter more XP for each tick past the first (double at 5/5), and the higher ticks add pay: torches at 2/5, steel and a battery at 3/5, then rounds and more steel up to a medkit at 5/5.
- The board and the bounty list say so ("threat 3/5 pay"). A quest you've already taken keeps what it was offered with.

versions.title: Days of food
versions.notes:
- Days of food. The base overview and the ledger's Shelter tab count each shelter's food in days: "Food: 6 days (18 for 3 mouths)", children and elders counting half.
- The ledger's Shelter tab shows "short in 2 days" when the crates are nearly empty and "out of food" when they won't feed everyone tomorrow, and the overview warns when it's out. A friend's welcome-back card lists each shelter's days of food.
- With Followers eat off, the line is a plain count of the food in the crates.

versions.title: Followers eat
versions.notes:
- Followers eat. Each dawn everyone at a post eats from the crate by their post or their shelter's crates: one food each, half for children and elders. Meals and preserves go first and feed someone for two days.
- When the crates run short a follower goes hungry; one hungry morning they put up with, two running and they're unhappy. The base overview counts the hungry, a toast and a journal note explain it the first time, and the chronicle records short mornings.
- A new World option, Followers eat (on). Worlds started before this version have it off, with a toast saying so: turn it on in World options.

versions.title: You, turned
versions.notes:
- You, turned. When you die (not on hardcore or creative), the ash keeps a copy of you: at the next dusk a brute with your name rises where you fell, marked on your map. The death screen says so, and a journal note explains it.
- It never rises within 30 blocks of your bed or on lit or claimed ground, keeps to its own ground and only comes for you if you get within about 12 blocks, so dying at home can't snowball. By day it goes back to the ground; it rises again each night until you deal with it.
- With the death penalty on, if your pack fell more than 24 blocks from your bed, your copy picks it up and drops it where it falls. Putting it down gives XP back (more the longer you'd lasted); a cure dart, once it's worn down, gives twice as much.

versions.title: Join as a survivor
versions.notes:
- Join as a survivor. A friend joining a co-op world can tick "Step into a follower" on the Join panel: they take over one of the host's followers (a grown one outside your squad, guards first) and play as them, with their name over their head, in the roster and in the chronicle, their gear in their pack, and a card with their work, mood and a few of their memories.
- While a friend plays them, the follower is off the roster. When the friend leaves, the follower is back, guarding where they stood. If there's no follower free, the friend joins as themselves.
- Fixed: the welcome-back card for a friend rejoining a world they'd played before (v0.13.180) now shows in their game.

versions.title: Followers leave
versions.notes:
- Followers leave. A follower unhappy at their post seven dawns running says so: a journal entry ("Mara is thinking of leaving") with what they're missing, a toast, and a line on their follower screen.
- Two days later, if they're still unhappy, they pack up and walk to another of your shelters, or out of the world if you have no other, taking their gear. A bonded friend goes with them. Cheer them up in time (food, a bed, a light near their post) and they stay.

versions.title: The Ashen learn your defenses
versions.notes:
- The Ashen learn your defenses. Each shelter remembers what put down most of the last blood moon pack there: shock fences, turrets, guards, or boards that held them clawing outside. While you were away, it's what the shelter leans on.
- The next pack there comes ready for it: fences bring brutes, turrets bring screamers and runners from every side, guards bring runners, and boards bring more of them to claw.
- The night before the first adapted pack, the journal says they're changing and what to expect, and the Gazette's Wanted names it. Mix your defenses.

versions.title: The raid finds the weak shelter
versions.notes:
- The raid finds the weak shelter. In co-op, a blood moon raid goes for the shelter with the least defense (light, turrets, fences, guards), whoever owns it, and the warning names it, and whose it is, on every friend's screen. Ash surges go for the weakest reclaimed square near any of you.
- Playing alone, or with one shelter, raids still come for your followers' shelter as before.

versions.title: Ash in a follower's blood
versions.notes:
- Ash in a follower's blood (with the Ash sickness World option on, which is off by default). A brute's hit on a follower can leave ash in their blood. A toast says so, and their follower screen and the base overview show it.
- A medic nearby, a herbal tea or a cure dart (right-click them with it) clears it. Left a full day, they turn at the next dusk, out about 30 blocks from the shelter, as an Ashen brute with their name.
- Wear a turned follower down and a cure dart brings them back to the roster as they were. Put down, they're gone for good.

versions.title: Seasonal nights
versions.notes:
- Seasonal nights. With Seasons on, winter nights run from 17:00 to 07:00 and summer nights from 19:00 to 05:00; spring and autumn stay 18:00 to 06:00. The sun's path across the sky follows the season's hours, and sleeping wakes you half an hour after the season's dawn.
- The calendar says when the nights change ("Winter begins: nights 17:00 to 07:00"), and so does the toast the day before winter. Help, the lamp and the bed texts read the season's hours.
- Solar panels still make exactly 300 a day in any season: they make a little more a second in winter's short days and a little less in summer's long ones.

versions.title: The sky clears where you've won
versions.notes:
- The sky clears where you've won. Each dawn (and as you travel) the game looks at the ground within about 300 blocks: how much of it is claimed, lit, by a shelter beacon or in a reclaimed city. The more you've won, the thinner the ash overhead: stars come out at night, the moon is smaller and sharper, noons turn bluer, you see a little farther and less ash falls around you.
- Over the deadlands the sky stays grey as ever, whatever you've built there. There's no bar: it's just the sky.
- Heliostats read the same sky: a mirror throws a third of its beam under grey ash and its full beam under a sky you've cleared.

versions.title: Migrations
versions.notes:
- Migrations (a new World option, on). About once a week the radio names a horde of 20 to 40 mixed Ashen that will walk a straight line across explored land the next night, away from the cities. Its line goes on your map and minimap, and the toast names any of your shelters on it.
- At night the horde walks the line from end to end. When it passes near you it's real, a few at a time, and tramples crops underfoot and claws at boards in its way. By dawn it's gone.
- A shelter on its line has to hold it, as against a raid (light, turrets, guards on posts): one that holds gets a chronicle line, and one that doesn't has its crops trampled and some boards clawed down. The horde's tracks stay on the map for three days and leave a mark in the History layer.

versions.title: One set of orders
versions.notes:
- One set of orders. U opens a ring of orders: for your squad, or for the follower you're looking at. Come, Hold here and Trail on the top; Aggressive, Defensive and Passive on the bottom. Click one or press 1-6; U or Esc closes it.
- The stance is now a squad setting: everyone in the squad takes it, and a follower who joins takes the squad's. A follower outside a squad keeps their own, set from the same ring when you look at them.
- The follower screen's stance row is gone; it says the follower's stance and that U gives orders. The status line shows the squad's order and stance.

versions.title: The gazette inside the chronicle
versions.notes:
- The Ashford Gazette moves into the Chronicle. Every seventh dawn the week's page prints as a divider block in the journal's Chronicle, above the last day of the week it covers, in the chapter dividers' style; the issues you already had print there too.
- The journal's Gazette tab and the beacon ledger's Gazette tab are gone. The Chronicle now keeps every issue rather than the last four.

versions.title: One survey key
versions.notes:
- One survey key. Shift+G now cycles the three ways of seeing where the Ashen will rise: Near (the spawn marks on the blocks around you), Scan (the spawn scan, with its marks on the maps and through the walls) and Off (clears them). If the scan is still recharging or you're too hungry, it stays on Near.
- L still toggles the spawn marks for this version; the first time you press it, a note says they've moved to Shift+G. Help, the Controls list and the hints say Shift+G.

versions.title: Two shelters, one village
versions.notes:
- Two shelters, one village. In co-op, a Shelter Beacon remembers who placed it. When friends' beacons stand within 64 blocks of each other (chained), they're one village: builders, the kitchen and loadouts draw on all of its crates, a follower counts the village's food for their mood, a raid or surge is held by all of its defenses together, and the journal's Shelters tab shows one card, 'Village: Northgate + Wren's Rest'.
- Lockers and build permissions stay personal: a friend's lockers are never pooled. Your own beacons near each other stay separate shelters, as before.

versions.title: While you were away
versions.notes:
- While you were away. A host's world now remembers when each friend was last on (by their player name, saved with the world). When a friend who has played there before joins again after a day or more, or after something went in the chronicle, they get the welcome-back card: the day they left, what was built since (blocks placed, new shelters), the chronicle since they left, and where the followers are.
- A quick reconnect a minute later gets no card, and a first-time friend gets the usual welcome.

versions.title: Lightning on the wires
versions.notes:
- Lightning on the wires. In a thunderstorm, a strike that comes down within 16 blocks of a power pole, solar panel or wind turbine standing above the ground there jumps to the tallest one and trips it: it's off, and cut out of its network, until you right-click it. The toast says where.
- A new block, the lightning rod (3 steel ingots and 1 wire at a workbench), takes any strike within 12 blocks harmlessly: no fire, nothing tripped. The first thunderstorm after this version brings a tip about them.

versions.title: Heliostats
versions.notes:
- Heliostats: a polished steel sun mirror (6 steel ingots, 4 windows, 2 wire at a workbench). Set it under open sky, right-click it, then right-click the doorway, window or wall you want it to shine on (within 20 blocks).
- From 09:00 to 15:00 in clear weather (no ash storm, thunderstorm, fog or sandstorm) it throws a one-block beam that stops at the first wall. The Ashen caught in it burn at half the open sun's rate and get out of the line; a nest it shines on for a whole day of beam (six hours) dries out and dies.
- It's a narrow tool, not a cure: under the ash it throws half the sun it would on ground you've claimed or lit around a shelter, it doesn't light the room or stop the Ashen rising, and it doesn't clear a building for you. Ashford's mirrors fogged in the first ash winter; a mirror only throws what sun the ash lets through.

versions.title: Past lives echo
versions.notes:
- Past lives echo. A world's past-lives record now keeps the names of its living followers. Start a new world on a device that has played others, and one survivor you find out there carries the name of a follower from a past world; when you take them in, they say you remind them of someone.
- The first crate you open in a city holds a note signed with that past world's name. Nothing changes if no past world kept followers (worlds from before this version didn't record them).

versions.title: Map memory
versions.notes:
- Map memory. The big map has a History layer: where things happened leaves a faint cross with the day and a few words (Day 12: Mara fell). Blood moon raids held or lost at a shelter, followers found and fallen, and cities reclaimed are marked; later rounds add more.
- Toggle it with the History checkbox beside the map's waypoint filters. It keeps the last 200 marks, and only the full map shows them (not the minimap).

versions.title: Friends and feuds
versions.notes:
- Friends and feuds. Two followers posted at the same shelter who work the same job or fight the same night (a blood moon, holding battle posts) grow closer, and after five such days they're friends: they take battle posts side by side, and if one falls the other grieves for three days, wherever they are.
- A grudge: when one follower is praised (you answered their request, or they held a post) the same day another at the shelter grumbled, the other holds it against them. The follower screen and the journal say so; settle it by handing either one a meal, or with the new Day off button (both rest until dawn). Grudges count as requests on the beacon's ledger.
- The follower screen and the journal's Followers tab show each pair: getting to know someone (days of five), friends, or a grudge.

versions.title: Evenings at the fire
versions.notes:
- Evenings at the fire. After dusk, sit by a lit campfire (right-click a chair or bench within 6 blocks of it, or crouch and right-click the fire to sit on the ground) with two or more followers within 8 blocks, and they talk: each says a line from what they remember or who they are.
- One evening in four, someone gives you a lead: a place they passed once, marked on your map. Everyone at the fire is in good spirits for the night and remembers it. One evening a night at each fire.

versions.title: Chapter cards
versions.notes:
- Chapter cards. A world now has acts: the first night survived, a first shelter, Halcyon found, the first reclaimed city and the cure carried home. The dawn after you cross one, a title card comes up (Part II: Through the night, Part III: Settling...) with the chronicle's last three lines and your next step, and the Chronicle gets a divider for it.
- Worlds from before this version get dividers for the acts they've already passed, without the cards.

versions.title: Torch upkeep
versions.notes:
- Torch upkeep, a new World option (off by default). With it on, a torch you place burns for five days, then sinks to embers: a dim orange glow that no longer keeps the Ashen from rising beside it. Right-click embers with coal or charcoal to relight the torch (a wall torch goes back on its wall).
- Lanterns, candles and electric lamps never burn down, and claimed ground stays safe as before. A new job, lamplighter, walks the torches within 32 blocks of its post with coal from the crate, relighting embers and topping up the ones about to go out.
- The base overview counts each shelter's torches running low, and a journal note explains it the first time torches burn down.

versions.title: Skills that choose
versions.notes:
- Skills that choose. Ranks 5 and 10 of each skill now offer a pick between two perks on the skills page (K), twenty in all: thick skin or field medic, second wind or mender (health); quartermaster or long wind, engineer or tireless (stamina); silent sprint or long dodge, fleet or sure foot (speed); spear through or heavy swing, finisher or marksman (damage); keen eye or long ping, scout or lingering marks (scouting).
- The co-op roles are now four of these perks (field medic, quartermaster, engineer and scout), so the role picker is gone from Settings, the Join panel and the beacon. Your roster tag shows the first old role you've picked. If you had a role before, its perk is marked (your old role) when the rank comes.
- Skill points you've already spent count: a world past rank 5 or 10 offers those picks the next time you open the skills page.

versions.title: The beacon as a ledger
versions.notes:
- The beacon as a ledger. A shelter beacon's menu now opens in tabs: Shelter (home, upgrades, projects, your role, co-owners), Travel, Boards (quests and the job board), Followers (expeditions and loadouts) and Gazette. It remembers the tab you last used.
- Tabs carry a badge when something there needs you: 2 requests, 1 job open, expedition back, kitchen idle, crate short (from a stoker), new issue.
- Each shelter's row in the base overview (journal, Shelters) has a Ledger button that opens its ledger from anywhere; travel works only at the beacon itself.

versions.title: Stokers
versions.notes:
- Stokers: a new job. A stoker keeps the generators and biomass burners within 24 blocks of their post fed from the crate there (four fuel items in each bin: coal, charcoal or wood for a generator, greenery for a burner), and tops up parked trains and hot air balloons with fuel cans.
- When the crate runs out of what a machine needs, the shelter beacon says so (Stoker: the crate is short of coal), and a toast says it once a day at dawn. Stokers have a loadout like any job.

versions.title: A stranger at the fire
versions.notes:
- A stranger at the fire. On the second or third night, if you have no followers yet, a lit campfire (or a camp of three or more torches you placed) within 200 blocks of Ashford draws a survivor: at dawn they walk up to it and ask to stay. Right-click them to take them in.
- It happens once a world, with a tip on what followers do. Not in creative worlds.

versions.title: Battle stations
versions.notes:
- Battle stations. A new block, the Battle Post (2 cloth, 2 sticks and a plank, by hand): set it on a rooftop or behind boards, and it goes to the nearest guard within 32 blocks, one guard a post.
- When the siren sounds at night, a blood moon raid comes or an ash surge marches, each posted guard runs to their post and holds it until dawn, then goes back to where they stood. Guards on a post skip their job for the night.
- A guard with a battle post counts for more when a raid is weighed, and the blood moon report and the chronicle say who held which post (Mara held the north rooftop post).
- The follower screen shows each guard's post, and Next post swaps it with the next one in reach.

versions.title: The ash front
versions.notes:
- The deadlands creep. Each dawn the ash takes a few blocks of open grass at its edge, turning it grey, but only on ground you've explored, and only near you. It never hurts on its own; dark open ground is simply where the Ashen rise.
- You can hold it and turn it back: light, a shelter beacon within 16 blocks, claimed ground and reclaimed cities stop it, and the grass comes back there a few blocks a dawn. Saplings and crops hold the ground around them, and a broom sweeps a greyed block clean at once. The map shows the grey as it spreads, the first time it comes within 200 blocks of a shelter a note says how to push it back, and the Stats page counts the ground you've taken back.
- A World option, Ash front (on), turns it off; what had crept in then fades over a few dawns.

**Limitations:** It only moves where the ground is loaded around you at dawn, so far-off edges stay where they were. Ground it took and gave back (or that you swept) stays yours: it won't grey again. Leaves don't grey (there's no dead-leaves block). The host's game moves it in co-op.

versions.title: Storm-dark days
versions.notes:
- A thick ash storm by day darkens the sky enough that the Ashen walk in it: they rise on open ground as they do at dusk (no more of them than a day brings; half on Calm), and none burn in the sun until the storm thins. When it passes, the sun takes them again.
- The storm warning now says so when the storm will come by day, the status line reads Storm · the Ashen are out while it lasts, and the first storm-day writes a journal note.

**Limitations:** A storm that starts at night is a night like any other. The Ash storms World option turns storms, and this, off.

versions.title: Voice chat
versions.notes:
- Push-to-talk in co-op: hold O (rebind it under Settings > Controls, or use the Talk touch button) and your friends hear you from your avatar, so a night run needs no other app. The first press asks the browser for the microphone; a toast says so. A small Talking line shows while you hold it.
- A friend who's talking gets (talking) on their name tag. The pause menu has a Mute button for each friend, for this session.
- Under the hood: 20 ms frames at 8 kHz, 16-bit mono, sent unreliably over the co-op connection (a dropped frame is a click, never a delay) and played through a small buffer.

**Limitations:** Not tested with a real microphone in Safari or Chrome yet (the headless co-op test sends a made-up frame). Phone-call quality: no echo cancelling or noise gate, so use headphones. The Talk touch button shows outside co-op too, where it does nothing.

versions.title: Seed of the week
versions.notes:
- A new title button, Seed of the Week: everyone who starts one in the same real week (Monday to Sunday) gets the same seed and the same start, rotating through Meadow, Stranded, Downtown and Deep Winter week by week, on Normal with default options. The world is named after the week (Week 43, 2026).
- The journal's Stats page shows how you're doing toward day ten (the day you reached, Ashen put down, cities reclaimed) and freezes it the morning day ten begins, with a short code (ASH-W43-K3D9) and a Copy button. Paste a friend's code into the box beside it to see their score next to yours. No server: the code carries the score itself, with a check that catches most typos.

**Limitations:** The code is easy to make up by hand; it's for comparing with friends, not a leaderboard. Weeks follow the computer's clock in UTC.

versions.title: Faster first load
versions.notes:
- The loading screen now says what it's waiting for: Engine 12 / 38 MB while the engine downloads (most of the wait: the engine is 38 MB, the game itself 2 MB), then Game data, then Starting... (a custom page for both the plain and the threaded build; invite, touch and receive links work as before).
- The title screen comes up sooner: the game's own scripts now load in the background after the title has drawn, instead of before it, and the Version Log lays out its text the first time you open it. Measured headless on the Mac: loading the title went from about 1,300 ms to 240 ms, its setup from 600 ms to 20 ms, and its first frame from 100 ms to 3 ms.

**Limitations:** The engine download itself is the same size, so a slow connection still waits for it; only what happens after it got faster. Starting a game right as the title appears can wait a moment for the game to finish loading.

versions.title: Built-in benchmark
versions.notes:
- Settings has a Run benchmark button: 15 seconds flying along the nearest city's main boulevard at noon, then 15 seconds circling your shelter at midnight, timing every frame. The Ashen stop spawning, you can't be hurt, and autosave waits while it runs.
- The report (average and 1% low fps for each part, plus your render distance, texture distance, block look and far terrain) shows under the button with a Copy button, so settings can be picked from numbers and builds compared the same way. If the slower part is under 45 fps, the pause menu offers the settings the first-launch suggestion would pick.
- Pausing stops it early; either way you, the clock and spawning are put back as they were, and the forced time doesn't count as days passing.

**Limitations:** Not in co-op. The report is kept on this device (one at a time). The first second of the street fly includes chunks still loading, which is part of what it measures.

versions.title: Show me
versions.notes:
- Help pages now answer where as well as how: each page that talks about something you can find starts with Show me the nearest links (coal ore, iron ore, water, a workbench, furnace, crate, bed, shelter beacon, solar panel, power pole, a spot that needs light, the visiting trader).
- Click one and Help closes, the nearest example in the ground loaded around you (48 blocks; 16 for a spot needing light) gets a mark on your map and minimap, and a route line leads there. Clearing the route drops the mark. If there's nothing nearby, a toast says so.

**Limitations:** It looks only at loaded ground, so something farther off won't be found. The mark isn't saved.

versions.title: Compass markers
versions.notes:
- A compass strip across the top of the screen shows places as marks at their bearing, with the distance under each (42 m, 1.5 km); something behind you sits as an arrow at the nearer end. Walk toward a mark without opening the map.
- The route's end and your quest places show on it (Settings: Route and quests on compass, on by default). Markers, shelters and cities show only once you tick Compass beside them in the map's list (M); that's separate from the minimap and map, off by default for every row, and kept for each world on this device.

**Limitations:** Your Compass ticks stay on your device and aren't shared with friends in co-op. The strip hides while there's nothing on it.

versions.title: Scout job
versions.notes:
- A new follower job, Scout. Park a bicycle (or tie a saddled horse) within 8 blocks of their post, and each morning they ride out to the nearest place you haven't found within 300 blocks: a city, an ash crater, a wreck, a ruin. By dusk they're home and it's on your map.
- Each trip writes a line in the journal's Scout reports note (Scout Mara: Ash crater, 220 m NE) and a toast; with nothing left in reach the report says so. The follower screen shows where they've gone, and two scouts never ride for the same place.

**Limitations:** The host's game sends scouts in co-op. A horse counts only while its ground is loaded at dawn; a bicycle counts wherever it is. Scouts never come to harm on the road.

versions.title: Festival day
versions.notes:
- Once a season, a shelter throws a feast. Put 20 meals by in crates within 16 blocks of its beacon (hearty stew, spiced broth, berry tart or preserves) and keep a record playing within 24, and at dusk the meals are eaten, string lights go up around the beacon until dawn, and everyone who lives there stays in good spirits for a week and remembers the night.
- The journal's Calendar shows "festival at <shelter>: ready for dusk" on the day one is ready; the first time a shelter has 20 meals put by, a dawn toast and a note explain it. The chronicle writes the feast, and the first one earns Festival Day.

**Limitations:** The host's game holds the feast in co-op; the Calendar line and the string lights show only on the host. The lights are decoration: they don't stop spawns.

versions.title: Preserves and a root cellar
versions.notes:
- Jars: two glass make four by hand. A jar and three of one produce (apples, pears, cherries, ashberries, potatoes or cooked fish) make preserves by hand: 6 food, and followers count a jar as a meal, so an autumn's picking keeps a shelter through winter.
- Root cellar (6 cobble, 3 planks at a workbench): a crate that, set with two solid blocks straight above it (dig it in or build over it), jars one batch from its own slots every game hour on its own, the fruit first. Without the cover it reads too warm and only stores. Its load comes back when it's broken, like any crate; hoppers and pipes reach it like one.

**Limitations:** Nothing spoils in Ashfall, so the cellar's job is jarring and storage, not freshness. It holds nine slots like other crates. The host's game runs the jarring in co-op.

versions.title: Orchards
versions.notes:
- Apple, pear and cherry saplings: old city parks have a few gone to seed (new chunks; old worlds hear about it), and a fruit tree's leaves drop its own sapling now and then, as oaks do. Plant one like any sapling. A season (14 days) after planting, the tree bears every autumn: look at the trunk to see the crop (Apple tree: 8 apples), right-click it to pick 6 to 10, once a year, for as long as the tree stands. Cut the trunk and the orchard forgets it.
- Fruit is food (2 each) and counts as shelter food like anything edible; a grinder presses any fruit into cider (4, and sprinting costs no stamina for 90 s); horses like apples as much as berries. Something to plant on day one that pays on day thirty.

**Limitations:** The orchard list lives with the host: in co-op only the host sees the crop on a trunk and picks it. There is no cider press; the grinder stands in, one fruit to one cider. Fruit never spoils (spoilage isn't in the game).

versions.title: Moats
versions.notes:
- The Ashen can't swim. Two blocks of water stops a walker cold (it paces the bank); a brute wades through one block deep and stops at two; a runner leaps a channel one block wide, so dig it two; sludge Ashen swim as before. One knocked into deep water flounders slowly for the nearest bank instead of swimming across. The pathfinder already never routed across water.
- World option Moats (on by default, Josh asked to playtest it) turns this off for a world without a restart. The first time one is stopped at your water within 24 blocks of a shelter beacon, a toast and a journal note: a dug ring with a plank bridge is a wall they can see through and can't cross, and a brute will still pound on the bridge.

**Limitations:** A runner's leap is a plain jump at run speed, so it can overshoot the far bank. Water placed by buckets counts the same as a lake.

versions.title: Wolves
versions.notes:
- Packs of three or four wolves hunt the pine hollows at night. A howl carries from one side about a minute before they come (a toast says which way, and the first howl writes a journal note); they rise 36 to 48 blocks out on dark ground, hunt deer and sheep within 24 blocks, stand over a kill for twenty seconds, and are gone at dawn, with five quiet minutes before the next howl. Lit ground turns them and fences hold them, so a lamp over the pen keeps the flock.
- They only come for you when you're alone and hurt: under 60% health with no follower or friend within a dozen blocks. Keep company or keep your health up and they leave you be. A wolf bites for 3 and falls to a few blows, leaving leather and raw meat. A codex page; co-op clients see the host's wolves like any animal.

**Limitations:** Creative worlds have none. A wolf turned by light backs away from you rather than from the lamp, and a deer that a wolf is after runs from you, not the wolf.

versions.title: Skybridges in Halcyon
versions.notes:
- Plank walkways run between neighbouring downtown towers in Halcyon, from one setback terrace to the next where the two stand at the same height and no more than 24 blocks apart: two planks wide with a fence rail down each side, a gap cut in each parapet to step through, and a crate on the terrace at both ends. One walking plank in eight is gone.
- The first time one is on screen within 40 blocks, a journal note: they're not well maintained, so watch your step for a missing plank or anything. Scouting from a height marks each as Skybridge. Old worlds get them in Halcyon chunks not yet generated and hear about it on load.

**Limitations:** Only terraces at the same height are bridged (a step of one story would need a stair); a tower whose landing has collapsed gets no bridge. Towers in ordinary cities have none.

versions.title: Shipwrecks
versions.notes:
- Broken hulls lie on the sea floor off the coasts: about one every 160 blocks of shore where the water is six or more deep, a rusted hull split in two with a stump of mast standing over it and what's left of a plank deck at the bow and stern. Three crates sit under the deck, in the dark, with sunken goods: steel, scrap, rope, batteries and wire, tins, bottles, a lantern, now and then a record or an air tank.
- Scouting from a height marks a wreck as a question mark on the surface above it (Wreck); the codex has a page. Old worlds get wrecks in the sea they haven't generated yet and hear about it when they load.

**Limitations:** Flooded basements and drowned metro tunnels were in the idea and are not here: the harbor's flooded ferry hold already covers diving under a roof, and each would be another worldgen change for old worlds. Wrecks don't appear near a harbor or inside a city's water.

versions.title: Diving gear
versions.notes:
- A snorkel (4 plant fiber, 2 sticks, by hand) in your pack keeps you breathing while your eyes are within a block of the surface, so shallow water and swimming across a river cost no air. An air tank (6 steel at a workbench) breathes for you under water for ten minutes a fill: the air bar above the hotbar reads the minutes left (Air 9:42), and the tank's hover text shows the same. Right-click a water pump holding the tank to fill it.
- Past four blocks down the water goes dark, the fog closing from 14 blocks to 5 by ten deep. The first dive with either piece of gear brings a tip: the gauge is on the HUD, it's dark down there, leave yourself the way back up.
- Gear works from anywhere in your pack or off-hand; with several tanks the fullest is used. A tank's air is saved with it, and in co-op it travels with your pack like any tool.

**Limitations:** There is nothing down there yet: shipwrecks come next. A pump fills a tank whether or not it has power.

versions.title: Rejoin in place
versions.notes:
- A friend who drops out of co-op (a closed tab, a lost connection) comes back where they stood: the host keeps their body for ten minutes, greyed and marked away, and the Ashen leave it be. Join the same room again under the same name and you're back on that spot with your pack, your health, hunger and air, and, if you were down, the downed timer carrying on from where it was.
- Clients report their pack and stats to the host every five seconds, so what comes back is at most that stale. After ten minutes the body is gone and a rejoin starts beside the host as before.

**Limitations:** The body is a marker, not a container: nobody can loot it, and a friend who rejoins under a different name starts fresh.

versions.title: Sound subtitles
versions.notes:
- Settings has Sound subtitles: nearby sounds show as short bracketed lines at the bottom left with where they came from: [Groans, east, close], [Screamer, north-west, far], [Footsteps, below], [A gunshot, south]. Up to four lines, each fading after a couple of seconds; a repeat keeps its line up rather than adding one. Weather gets a line when it changes (an ash storm, a blizzard, sandstorm or swamp fog, thunder).
- Your own placing, swinging and eating say nothing, nor do sounds past 48 blocks. Off by default; for playing quietly, or without hearing the game.

**Limitations:** Lines name the kind of sound, not who made it: a follower's footsteps and an Ashen's read the same.

versions.title: Draw on the map
versions.notes:
- The big map (M) has a Draw row: Pen draws a freehand line, Box drags out a rectangle, Label writes up to 16 characters at a spot, Erase takes away the mark you click, Undo takes back your last, and Color cycles six colors. With a tool on, dragging draws instead of panning (so a finger can draw on a phone); switch the tool off to pan again.
- Marks show faintly on the corner minimap too, so a planned wall or a route stays in view while you walk it. Up to 200 marks a world, the oldest dropped first; long strokes keep 64 points.
- In co-op everyone sees everyone's marks as they're drawn, Undo takes back only your own, and a guest can look but not draw. Saved with the world.

**Limitations:** Marks are block-accurate, not pixel-accurate: at the widest zoom a stroke is coarse.

versions.title: Trophy case and library
versions.notes:
- Trophy case (4 planks, 2 glass at a workbench): six exhibits behind glass, three on show. Right-click it holding a named Ashen's badge to display it (and take it back out from the case's menu); empty-handed, the menu adds copies of lab notes you've read and achievements you've earned, or removes them. Aim at the case to read the whole list. Breaking it hands the badges back. Friends in co-op see the same shelf.
- Bookshelf (6 planks, 3 cloth): right-click to read this world's chronicle, or the past lives of every world on this device, as a book. Followers with nothing to do who sit within 10 blocks of one are Reading, and remember it; a bookshelf stands in for a table in their comfort.

**Limitations:** Exhibits are tokens in the case's colors, not models of the thing. Notes and achievements shown are copies: nothing leaves your journal.

versions.title: Run the radio station
versions.notes:
- Once the radio station project is built, right-click its hut or mast: Broadcast tonight, or Stay quiet. A broadcast carries a day's walk: at each of the next three dawns one to three survivors who heard it arrive beside your nearest shelter beacon, remembering why they came, ready for a job or to be asked along.
- The Ashen hear it too: those three nights carry about a third more of them, and a pack waits up the nearest road the night you broadcast. The first broadcast's card spells both out, and the console says what's coming. A quiet night is always a choice.
- Saved with the world; the host runs it in co-op (friends can read the console's state).

**Limitations:** Arrivals need a shelter beacon to walk to; with none placed the dawn passes with a note instead.

versions.title: Scaffolding
versions.notes:
- Scaffolding: 4 sticks make 4 pieces of a stick frame you climb like a ladder. Right-click a piece and the next one goes on past the last piece along that side, up to 6 blocks from where you stand, so a column goes up before you climb it; build beside it, then sneak and hit any piece to take the whole frame (up to 64 pieces) down into your pack, or a bag at your feet.
- The Ashen treat scaffolding as a wall and claw through it as fast as dirt; the first-time tip and the Help page say so.

**Limitations:** A scaffold has no deck: you hang at the top piece (sneak holds you still) rather than stand on it. Taking a frame down isn't on the undo stack.

versions.title: Calendar page
versions.notes:
- The journal has a Calendar tab: the week ahead, a row a day from today, with the blood moon, full and new moons and ash moons, likely ash storms, the trader's next visits, the day new bounties go up on the board, and the day a season changes.
- It's worked out from what the world already knows (the night count, the seed, the trader's last visit), so nothing is saved and friends in co-op see the same page. The warnings that come one at a time as each day arrives still do.

**Limitations:** Storms read as "likely": the day's roll is fixed, its hour isn't shown. Festivals get their row when they arrive (a later chunk).

versions.title: Moon phases and the ash moon
versions.notes:
- The moon has phases now, an eight-night cycle drawn on a disc in the night sky. A full moon makes the night brighter and quieter (fewer Ashen, and they notice you a little later); a new moon is darker with a few more about. The first new moon gets a toast, and the status line names full and new moons.
- Every other new moon that isn't a blood moon is an ash moon: the sky goes the colour of a dead fire, thick ash fog closes to a quarter of the usual distance, the moon is a dull ember, and there are more Ashen out, though in that fog they notice you from much closer. The morning before warns you and a journal note explains it.
- Blood moons got the red fog Josh asked for: the haze itself is red now and closer.
- The journal's Stats page shows the phase and when the next ash moon falls.

**Limitations:** The moon disc sits at the camera's far distance, so very low render distances draw it small.

versions.title: Threat meter
versions.notes:
- The status line shows Ash threat 1/5 to 5/5, and the journal's Stats page spells out the sum: it rises a point for every night survived (up to 60) and falls 8 for every reclaimed city and 4 for every shelter beacon standing in light.
- Night spawns and brute / screamer odds follow it (from 0.7x to 1.4x of the usual cap), so the escalation that already happened is shown rather than hidden, and lighting shelters and reclaiming cities visibly pull it back.
- The first time it reaches 2/5 a toast explains what moves it.

**Limitations:** Not in creative worlds. A long-lived world loads to a harder night than before (at most 1.4x the cap); Calm still halves everything on top.

versions.title: Saddlebags
versions.notes:
- Saddlebags, from 6 leather at a workbench: right-click a saddled horse with them and it carries nine more slots on its flanks. Crouch and right-click the horse to open them.
- The horse's label says what the bags hold ("bags: 3 stacks (wheat, leather, rope)"), so a trip on horseback brings back more than your pack.
- They save with the horse. If the horse dies, the bags come back to your pack and whatever they held waits in a bag where it fell.

**Limitations:** In co-op the bags live in the host's game: friends can't open them.

versions.title: Bicycle
versions.notes:
- A bicycle, from 8 scrap and 2 rubber at a workbench: the first vehicle, long before the jeep. It fits in your pack; right-click open ground to set it down, right-click it to ride (W pedals, S brakes, A/D steer, Shift gets off), left-click to pack it up.
- Quick on roads (faster than sprinting on asphalt), slower than a sprint off them, silent (the Ashen aren't drawn by it), and it needs no fuel.
- It climbs one block at a time, as a slow 0.7 s climb, and won't take a second step until it's done: streets, slabs and stairs are fast, rough ground isn't. A drop on the bike hurts as it would on foot.

**Limitations:** No passengers, and like the jeep it isn't synced in co-op (friends don't see it move).

versions.title: Hand off a world to another device
versions.notes:
- Pause menu: Hand Off World opens a handoff room and shows its code (a link is copied too). On the other device, the title screen's Receive a World takes the code: the world arrives as a new save in its Load World list, with the same name.
- Your copy stays exactly as it is, and the room closes by itself once the world has arrived. Nothing is stored on the server: it only introduces the two devices, like a co-op room.
- A handoff room turns away players trying to join it, and Receive a World won't take a co-op room: each tells you which to use.

**Limitations:** Needs the web build on both devices, on the same version, both open at the same time (there's no stored code to come back to later). A world received twice becomes two saves of the same world.

versions.title: Trade window
versions.notes:
- In co-op, use (R or right-click) on a friend asks them to trade. They get a card; saying yes opens a two-sided window for you both.
- Each side puts up to 6 stacks on the table from their pack (click a stack to offer it, click an offered one to take it back) and presses Confirm. Changing an offer undoes both confirmations, so nobody swaps under a last-second change.
- Once both confirm, the host swaps the offers. Cancel, walking more than 6 blocks apart, or a lost connection puts each side's own offer back in their pack.
- Handing a single held stack over (F) still works as before.

**Limitations:** The host runs the swap, so it needs the host in the room. If a received offer doesn't fit, the rest lands in a bag at your feet (and Confirm refuses an offer that can't fit at all).

versions.title: Shared bounties
versions.notes:
- Hosting co-op with friends in the room, the bounty board offers each job a second way: Take as a group.
- A group bounty shows as (group) in the quest tracker, and every member's kills count toward it (hunts and clearing a city).
- When it's done, everyone in the group gets the full reward and XP, and the chronicle names them all.

**Limitations:** Only the host's board offers group bounties, and the host holds the quest: hand-ins happen in the host's game.

versions.title: Join by QR
versions.notes:
- Hosting co-op, the pause menu has a Show QR button: the invite link as a QR code. A phone or tablet joins by pointing its camera at the screen instead of typing the code.
- Opening the game from that code joins the room with touch controls on (unless that device's Touch controls setting is Off).

**Limitations:** Needs the web build (co-op runs through the browser). Very long invite links (over 134 characters) can't fit; copy those instead.

versions.title: Record player
versions.notes:
- Record player: 4 planks, 2 iron and 2 wire at a workbench. Right-click it holding a record and that tune plays for anyone within 24 blocks in place of the usual music (a fight still drowns it out); empty-handed takes the record off.
- Three records to find: Open Country, City Lights and Long Night. They turn up in city apartment crates and the fairground's candy stalls.
- Followers near a playing record hum along now and then.
- A follower who asked for news from a city will take a record instead.

**Limitations:** The three records are the game's own three themes.

versions.title: Crafting queue
versions.notes:
- Shift-click a recipe to queue a whole stack (20 planks, 64 wire...): it's made one batch a second from your pack and crates near you while you keep playing.
- A line under the quests shows the queue ("Crafting Planks 3/16"). Workbench recipes pause while you're more than 6 blocks from a workbench and pick up again when you're back.
- When the materials run out (or your pack is full) the queue stops and says how many it made. Shift-clicking another recipe replaces the queue.
- At a furnace, shift-clicking a stack in your pack still puts it straight in (ore and food in the top slot, fuel below).

**Limitations:** The queue isn't saved: quitting ends it (what's made is kept).

versions.title: Furniture, part 2
versions.notes:
- Curtain (3 cloth and a stick, by hand): hang it inside a window; right-click draws it open or shut.
- The Ashen now look before they come: with a wall or a shut curtain between you, an idle Ashen only notices you at half the distance (glass and open curtains don't hide you; it stacks with sneaking).
- Painting (a cloth and 4 sticks, by hand): hang it on a wall and it shows the last picture you snapped. In photo mode (F2), left-click snaps one. Before you've snapped anything it shows a plain landscape.
- Up to 32 paintings in a world; friends in co-op see them too.

versions.title: Furniture, part 1
versions.notes:
- New furniture at the workbench: table (6 planks, 4 sticks), chair (3 planks, 4 sticks), bench (4 planks, 2 sticks) and shelf (8 planks). Chairs, benches and shelves turn to face you when you place them.
- Shelf: 9 slots of storage against a wall; crafting counts what's on it like a crate.
- Carpet: 2 cloth make 2 by hand. Walk over it; right-click one holding a dye to color it.
- Followers with nothing to do sit on a free chair or bench near their post by day, and at the midday shelter visit they sit down at a table if there's a seat beside one.
- Comfort: a table and a chair or bench within 10 blocks of a follower's post counts toward their morale like food, a bed and light (any three of the four keep them well kept).

**Limitations:** Curtains and paintings come next.

versions.title: Hot air balloon
versions.notes:
- Hot air balloon: 12 cloth, 3 iron, 8 plant fiber and 2 rope at a workbench. Set it down on open ground, pour in fuel cans (90 seconds of burner each, 3 in the tank) and climb in.
- Hold Space to run the burner and rise (up to 190 high); let go and it sinks slowly and lands. There's no steering: off the ground it drifts with the wind.
- The world now has a wind that turns four times a day. The status line shows it ("Wind: NE, fresh") and the burner's fuel while you're in a balloon or holding one.
- Two followers fit in the basket. Land before you step out; break it on the ground to pack it up with its whole fuel cans.

**Limitations:** Balloons stay in your own game in co-op, like jeeps. The wind doesn't move clouds or anything else yet.

versions.title: Passengers
versions.notes:
- Followers ride along: when you board a jeep, boat, barge or train, or climb on a horse, followers on Come or Trail within 16 blocks climb in with you.
- Seats: the jeep's other seat, a boat's bow (two beside you on a barge), four in each passenger car, and one on each saddled horse you lead while you ride.
- Whoever rode with you last gets their seat back first (each vehicle remembers, and saves it), then your squad, then whoever's nearest. Everyone hops off when you do.

**Limitations:** Co-op friends can't ride along yet: vehicles stay in each player's own game.

versions.title: Railway, part 2
versions.notes:
- Cars: the garage builds a crate car (4 iron, 8 planks, a crate) and a passenger car (4 iron, 10 planks, 4 windows). Right-click a locomotive holding one to couple it on: up to three, each a little slower. Crouch and right-click the train to open the crate car.
- Ashen on the line: at speed the train shoves them aside (it hurts them and slows you); at a crawl they block it; a brute stops it dead, and you're told.
- Caravans by rail: when a line of rails runs from one shelter's beacon to the other's, the carrier's caravans run half again as often. The beacon menu says so.

**Limitations:** Followers don't sit in the passenger car yet; they keep up with you as before.

versions.title: Railway, part 1
versions.notes:
- Rails: 8 from a steel ingot and 2 planks at a workbench. Lay them on the ground and they join up like fences; a step up or down is fine.
- Locomotive: built at a garage (6 steel, 8 iron, 6 wire and a fuel can). Set it on a rail, pour in fuel cans (each runs it about 300 blocks; it holds 4), and ride it: W runs it up to 12 blocks a second, S brakes, and S when it's stopped turns it round.
- It follows your rails, takes a corner when there's only one way to go, and stops at the end of the line and beside a station block (3 concrete and a sign). A headlamp lights the line at night.

**Limitations:** Ashen don't react to trains yet, and there are no cars to pull: both come next. Trains stay in your own game in co-op.

versions.title: Fairgrounds
versions.notes:
- Fairgrounds stand at the edge of some cities (never Halcyon's): a Ferris wheel hung with lanterns, a shooting gallery, candy stalls and a haunted house. They glow at night, and the wheel shows on the far horizon.
- Climb the ladder behind the wheel to the top car: it's high enough to scout from, and the fairground joins your landmarks once seen.
- The shooting gallery's keeper pays a candy for every target you hit from behind the counter, six a day.
- The haunted house has an Ashen nest in its back room; the sign out front says so. Bring a torch.
- Candy: a small snack from the stalls' crates that keeps forever.

**Limitations:** Old worlds get fairgrounds only where the ground hadn't been generated yet.

versions.title: Harbor
versions.notes:
- Every world has a harbor on the shore by the nearest city that has one (Ashford first): a concrete yard of shipping containers, a crane, a plank dock, and a ferry run aground offshore.
- Each container is padlocked with a crate inside (shipping goods: steel, rubber, wire, cans and more). Bolt cutters (2 iron, a steel ingot and rubber at a workbench) cut the padlock; they don't wear out.
- Climb the crane's ladder to its deck, high enough to scout from; the harbor joins your landmarks once seen.
- The ferry's hold is flooded to the waterline with a crate at the bottom. The first time you're in it, a note says how long your air lasts.
- Barge: a boat, 12 planks, a crate and 2 iron at a workbench (there's one on the dock). Slower than a boat, but it carries a 9-slot crate: crouch and right-click it to load it.
- Fixed: since 0.13.124 every new chunk re-searched for the airport's site (about 25 ms each), so the world loaded slower. It's found once now.

**Limitations:** Old worlds get the harbor only where the ground hadn't been generated yet. Barges stay in your own game in co-op, like boats.

versions.title: Regional airport
versions.notes:
- Every world has a regional airport on level ground just outside the nearest city that isn't Ashford: a 120-block runway (the longest flat road there is, so the jeep's at its fastest), two rusted hangars, a fuel shed, and a control tower.
- Strip the wrecked plane in the first hangar for scrap, wire and rubber. Past the runway's end an airliner lies broken in two in a scorched field, with luggage crates thrown round it (clothes, and now and then a backpack).
- Climb the tower's ladder to the glass cab: it's high enough to scout from, and the airport joins your landmarks once you've seen it.
- Fuel cans: three in the fuel shed's crate, or 2 scrap and 3 coal at a workbench. Engines to come will burn them.

**Limitations:** Old worlds get the airport only where the ground hadn't been generated yet; you're told on loading.

versions.title: Stadium nights
versions.notes:
- Every overgrown stadium has a pit boss at its south gate now, a fence round the pitch (open at both ends) and three staked training dummies for trying weapons by day.
- After dark, talk to him for a fight: three waves of Ashen in the bowl, the last with a brute. Each wave cleared pays steel; the second adds a battery and the last a cure dart and counter agent. His menu says all of this before you agree.
- Leave by a gate or over the stands any time: the fight stops and you keep what you've won. One fight a night per stadium.
- Followers within 32 blocks watch, and cheer a win (a few days of better morale).

**Limitations:** Fights are run in the host's game; friends can join in but can't start one. Old worlds' stadiums get their pit the first time you come near.

versions.title: The Ashen find the door
versions.notes:
- An Ashen that gets stuck against your wall now looks for the way in: round to the gap, the open door or window, from up to 32 blocks away, instead of pressing on the nearest face.
- Wooden doors and boards still slow them, and they'd rather claw at a dark doorway than walk far; a lit doorway puts them off more. Fences and stone they walk round. Brutes still just break through.
- A journal note at nightfall: they've learned the streets.

**Limitations:** Paths are searched in the host's game, one a frame; a big pack may take a moment to spread out.

versions.title: Ash sickness
versions.notes:
- A new World option, off by default: Ash sickness. With it on, a brute's or screamer's hit can leave ash in your blood: you lose a little health every 40 seconds and don't heal until it's cleared. Never on Calm.
- Three cures: a medic follower close by, a herbal tea (2 berries, honey and a mushroom), or a cure dart used on yourself. The first time, a toast and a journal note explain them.
- Mushrooms: found breaking dead logs and in swamp mud. Eat one as a snack, or brew it into tea.

versions.title: Bedroll and stuck tips
versions.notes:
- Bedroll: 4 cloth and 6 plant fiber, by hand. Right-click with it after dark to sleep wherever you are; you keep it. It doesn't set your spawn point, and you never wake well rested on it.
- If you die twice before day 3, or a whole day goes by without you placing a block, one card offers the tip that fits: somewhere to sleep, lighting your doorway, or the mayor's hall note. Once per world.
- Settings has a Reset tips button, so the first-time tips can show again in this world.

versions.title: Campfire
versions.notes:
- Campfire: 3 sticks and 2 cobblestone, by hand. Light it with a torch for a small light the Ashen won't rise in.
- It cooks raw meat, fish or a tuber one at a time, and keeps the blizzard's cold off you when you stand near it.
- It burns out at dawn unless you feed it logs: each one keeps it going another day, up to two.

**Limitations:** In co-op only the host can light and tend campfires for now (a friend still gets warm by one).

versions.title: Creative mode
versions.notes:
- New World has a Creative mode for building: the crafting window opens on a Palette of every block and item (click for a full stack), and placing never uses up a stack.
- In a creative world you start flying (F4 toggles it), nothing hurts you, hunger stands still, and no Ashen rise anywhere: no nests, Named, raids or surges.
- Achievements are off, and creative worlds leave no past life or heirloom. The Load list marks them Creative. Like Hardcore, the mode is set when the world is made and never changes.

**Limitations:** Opening Halcyon's vault in a creative world still wakes what's inside it.

versions.title: Pin a recipe
versions.notes:
- Every recipe has a Pin button: the pinned recipe stays on screen under your quests with each ingredient as have/need ("4/8 planks"), the missing ones dimmed, and "Ready" once you have it all.
- The counts include crates near you, the same as crafting does, and update as you gather.
- Crouch-click an auto-crafter with nothing craftable in hand to pin what it makes.
- One pin at a time; it's saved with the world. Pin it again to clear it.

versions.title: Sewers, part 2: sludge Ashen
versions.notes:
- Sludge Ashen live in the sewers: slow, tough (twice a common Ashen's health), and they drip as they move, so you hear them before you see them. The first one brings a journal warning.
- Where a sludge Ashen has been it leaves a dark puddle for a while that slows anyone wading through it.
- A wrench strips the sewers' old pipes for scrap and their cables for wire and rubber.
