- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **222/222 checks passed** (all 176 v0.1.4 checks — one adapted to dict research costs — plus 46 new: recipe/tech-cost data and gates incl. the dual prerequisite, belt-speed stacking x1.0/1.25/1.5, green science hand-craft and assembler production from building items, assembler rejection of non-input items and its piercing gate, lab dual-pack completion of Steel Processing with both counters resetting, the furnace plate gate and the 5-plates + 1-coal -> steel smelt, Piercing Ammo completing on both pack types, piercing hand-craft and assembler production after research, turret piercing-first loading with the regular magazine untouched, piercing player damage (60) and loaded-type memory, Reinforced Turrets upgrading an existing turret to 375/full with range 8.5 and new turrets placed at 375, and save/load preserving the player/turret magazine types and tier-2 research). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.5/README.md`.

versions.title: Splitters + underground belts patch
versions.notes:
"Splitters + underground belts" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Splitter (new building):** hand recipe in the Buildings crafting tab — 4 iron plates + 2 iron gears, no tech gate, 1.5 s craft time. It reuses the belt's one-item buffer mechanics (`belt_item` in `scripts/building.gd`), so belts, inserters, and miner eject all feed it with no special cases, and inserters can take its buffered item back out (belts, splitters, and underground ends are one "belt-like" family for inserter source/target rules in `scripts/main.gd`). Its tick advances the item at belt speed, then delivers **round-robin — front, then left, then right relative to facing**: each delivery tries outputs starting at the round-robin pointer, the first building that can accept takes the item, and the pointer advances past it; if all three outputs are blocked the item is held. Passive — **0 power draw**, like belts. Visual: a belt-style flat base in a distinct green with raised side blocks and the travelling plate/item meshes; no working lamp (documented as not required for a passive building). The building panel shows the buffered item and the last output used.
- **Underground belt (new building, one item type for both ends):** hand recipe in Buildings — 5 iron plates + 2 iron gears, no tech gate, 2.0 s. **Pairing model (the documented simplification):** each end has a role, entrance or exit. Placing an end that lies in the front line (straight row/column, same facing) of an unpaired entrance within **4 tiles** makes it that entrance's **exit** and links the pair both ways; otherwise the new end is an **entrance**, and if an unpaired exit already sits in its own front line within 4 tiles they pair up (orphaned exits can be re-paired). An already-paired entrance is never stolen. **Flow:** the entrance accepts items like a belt; on its tick, with a linked exit and nothing in transit, the item goes underground and surfaces on the exit after **distance ÷ (1.4 × belt-speed multiplier)** seconds; the exit then outputs forwards exactly like a belt (it is part of the belt tick). If the exit is occupied when a transit completes, the item waits inside — **queue of 1 in transit per entrance** (the entrance may buffer one further item meanwhile). Deconstructing either end unlinks the pair (the survivor keeps its role, unpaired) and refunds 1 item per end as normal, plus any in-transit item. The role is shown by a marker post on the building (orange = entrance, cyan = exit) and in the building panel (role, linked cell or "unpaired", item in transit). While the underground ghost is up, a pairable hover cell shows **"Will link to underground entrance/exit (N tiles)"** in the hover readout and the ghost's secondary marker highlights the partner cell. Single placement only — drag-place stays belts/walls only (these types are excluded from the drag list, so dragging with one selected is a no-op, not a crash).
- **Both buildings:** normal `can_place` validation, rotation with R (both are directional), minimap/big-map colours (splitter green, underground belt purple), inventory-menu placement (they are not added to the number-key hotbar), building-panel support, hover readout ("Splitter - Working", "Underground Belt - Unpaired entrance (no exit)", and so on via the shared status derivation), deconstruct refunds of the building plus its buffered item, and no power draw. Biters walk past them like belts (they do not block).
- **Save format:** building records gain optional splitter fields (round-robin pointer, last output) and underground fields (role, partner cell, in-transit item and remaining time). Links are rebuilt on load and validated for mutuality, so a one-way link cannot survive a load. v0.1.0–v0.1.3 saves still load (new fields default cleanly).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **176/176 checks passed** (all 138 v0.1.3 checks unmodified, plus 38 new checks: both recipes exist in Buildings with no tech gate; splitter round-robin distribution over front/left/right acceptors including the wrap-around 4th item, hold-when-blocked, and inserter extraction; underground pairing in line within 4 tiles, no pairing at 5 tiles, transit delivery through the exit onto a belt into a chest, deconstruct-the-exit unpairs the entrance with refund, re-pairing with a fresh exit; hand-craft enqueue of both buildings; and a save/load round-trip preserving the splitter buffer and the pair's roles and links). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.4/README.md`.

versions.title: Audio + build QoL patch
versions.notes:
"Audio + build QoL" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Procedural event SFX (new `scripts/sfx_player.gd`, no new autoload):** main creates an `SfxPlayer` node in code — a pool of 8 AudioStreamPlayers playing AudioStreamWAV streams synthesized in code (16-bit PCM sine/square/noise bursts with envelopes, different pitch and shape per event). Events wired at their real call sites: place building, deconstruct complete (hold channel and X demolish), craft queue item finished (main now consumes the completed-output list returned by `GameState.tick_crafting`), player and turret shooting, biter hit, biter killed, research complete, wave incoming warning, victory sting, UI click (every HUD button, via the shared button factory), and error buzz (no inventory to place, miner off-patch / occupied placement, unaffordable craft queue, failed building feed, out of ammo). HARD RULE kept: event sounds only — there is no ambient or background loop of any kind (a constant ambient drone was a P0 player complaint in a sibling game).
- **Audio settings in the pause menu:** a Master volume slider (0-100, driving the SFX pool's volume and the Master bus) and a Mute checkbox. Both persist in `user://settings.cfg` (ConfigFile, section "audio"), loaded at startup and saved on change — they are NOT stored in game saves.
- **Drag-place belts and walls:** with a belt or wall ghost selected, holding left-click and moving across cells places a continuous line — each newly entered cell (plus any cells skipped between frames, interpolated along the dominant axis) that passes `can_place` and where the player still has the item is placed, consuming 1 item each. Belt facing follows the drag direction (dominant axis of the movement into the cell; last movement direction wins). The place sound is throttled to at most one per 0.06 s. A simple click still places exactly one; drag-place inherits placement's existing precedence over the deconstruct/hand-mine/shoot channels and stops cleanly when inventory runs out or the button is released.
- **Hover readout:** a dedicated HUD label above the hotbar (separate from the hint line, so transient hints are never overwritten) updated from `_update_hover`. A resource patch cell reads "<Resource> patch" (for example "Iron Ore patch"), a building cell reads "<Building Name> - <status>" reusing `building_status` (the same derivation as the building panel), and empty cells are blank — the chosen option, so the line stays out of the way on bare ground.
- **Save compatibility:** no save-format changes; v0.1.0-v0.1.2 saves still load. Audio settings live outside saves.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **138/138 checks passed** (all 114 v0.1.2 checks unmodified, plus 24 new checks: sfx player exists, all 11 named events resolve to generated AudioStreamWAV streams with length > 0, muted playback is a no-error no-op, settings round-trip at volume 0.4 + muted true, hover text for patch/furnace/empty cells, and drag-place over a 4-cell run with facing, inventory, out-of-items, and occupied-cell cases). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.3/README.md`.

versions.title: Second playtest batch
versions.notes:
Second playtest batch (twelve items from Josh's playtest of the v0.1.1 web build):

- **Hold-to-deconstruct:** with nothing selected, holding left-click on a building channels a 0.8 s deconstruction — an overhead progress bar (dark backing, orange fill, facing the camera) shows the hold; releasing, moving to another cell, selecting a ghost, or opening a panel cancels with no effect. Completion refunds the building item, any belt item, and all buffer contents (the existing `remove_building` refund). X demolish mode remains as the instant alternative. Left-click precedence is now: place > repair > deconstruct > hand-mine > shoot — clicks on buildings/patches no longer fire shots.
- **Hand mining:** holding left-click on a bare resource patch channels 0.7 s per item of that patch's resource. Patches are infinite, as they already were for miners.
- **Crafting queue (replaces instant crafting):** hand recipes have craft times; clicking a recipe consumes the cost up front and queues it (FIFO — only the front item progresses, leftover tick time carries over). The crafting panel lists the queue with a live percentage on the front row; clicking any queued row cancels it and refunds the full cost, including the in-progress item. A compact queue strip above the hotbar shows the front item and how many are queued. The queue is written into saves.
- **Inventory menu (E):** lists everything carried; building stacks are buttons that select that building for placement (click again to deselect), materials are shown with counts, research-locked buildings say what they need, and the Repair Pack row toggles repair mode.
- **Building interaction panel (E or right-click on a building):** name and cell, HP bar, a live status line derived from the building's real state (Working / Idle / No power / No fuel / Output blocked / No recipe / missing inputs), all buffer contents, machine progress for furnaces and assemblers, the current research for labs, loaded shots for turrets, and — for assemblers — the recipe picker, which now lives in this panel. Non-pausing; refreshes live.
- **Manual fueling / quick-insert:** the building panel carries Feed Coal +1/+5 for boilers and furnaces (the boiler case was the request — it is how you bootstrap power before any inserter exists), Load Ammo +1/+5 for turrets, and Insert Red Science +1/+5 for labs, all respecting the buildings' normal buffer caps.
- **Working indicator:** machines get a status lamp — green while working (state tracked from the actual simulation ticks), red when blocked (unpowered powered-machine, or a boiler without coal), grey when idle. Animated cues: the miner drill rotates while mining, and the furnace flame's emission flickers while smelting.
- **Health bars for everything:** one shared overhead bar component (visible only while damaged, fill colour runs green to red) attached to every building, every biter, every nest (which keeps its text label too), and the engineer (the HUD HP readout also remains).
- **Repair packs:** new hand-crafted item (2 iron plates + 2 copper cable, Intermediates). Selecting it in the inventory enters repair mode; holding left-click on a damaged building repairs at 40 HP/s, one pack restoring up to 100 HP with fractional credit kept across buildings. Clamps at max HP (Reinforced Walls respected for walls); a healthy building reports "already at full health" and consumes nothing.
- **Starting kit:** 10 power poles at game start (was 8).
- **Scrollable menus:** crafting and research lists, help, version log, the save-slot list, the recipe list, and the new inventory and building panels all scroll inside their fixed-size panels.
- **No more tofu-box symbols:** every pictograph/emoji was removed from the game's UI strings (the web export's font cannot draw them, so they showed as boxes with numbers). The HUD now uses plain words — "Power:", "Research:", "Nests:", "Time:", "HP:", "[locked]", "> " selection markers, "->" arrows.
- **Save compatibility:** v0.1.1 and v0.1.0 saves still load (craft queue defaults empty; building HP was already serialized in v0.1.0 and still is).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **114/114 checks passed** (all 60 v0.1.1 checks, with the instant-crafting ones rewritten against the queue, plus 54 new checks for this batch). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.2/README.md`.

versions.title: Playtest-fix patch
versions.notes:
Playtest-fix patch (from Josh's first playtest of the web build):

- **Ammo economy fixed (headline):** ammo magazines are no longer gated behind Military research — the hand-craft recipe (C → Military) and the assembler recipe both cost **2 iron plates** (down from 4) with **no tech requirement**. Military research now unlocks the Gun Turret only (tech text updated; the assembler recipe picker no longer locks ammo). The engineer's gun now fires **rounds**: 1 magazine = 10 rounds, and a magazine is only consumed when the gun runs dry — the same per-magazine yield turrets already had (was: a whole magazine per player shot, so the starting 6 magazines were 6 shots; now 60). Loaded rounds are shown in the HUD inventory panel and persist in saves.
- **Wave pacing:** first wave now arrives at **5 minutes** (was 90 s), later waves every **2 minutes** (was 90 s). Wave sizes are gradual — 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4… capped at 10 (was 3, 4, 5…) — and biter toughness scales more gently (+5% per wave, was +15%). Nest ambient spawns slowed: first spawn at 60 s, then every **40 s** (was 18 s), and only while fewer than 8 biters are alive in total (the old cap counted all biters against a 24 limit).
- **Belt items clearly visible:** the item cube on a belt is now 0.52×0.30×0.52 (was 0.34×0.22×0.34), sits on a thin dark base plate that travels with it, and its material uses **emission** in the item's colour so items pop at normal camera distances.
- **Placement preview with direction/flow:** the placement ghost is now a small rig — footprint box (green/red validity as before) plus a bright yellow-white **direction arrow** for directional buildings (belt, inserter, miner, assembler, furnace, turret), a translucent cyan **destination marker** on the front/output cell, and — for inserters — a fainter marker on the back/pickup cell. Arrow and markers track the hover cell and rotate when you press R. The pole coverage ring is unchanged.
- **Save compatibility:** v0.1.0 saves still load — `player_rounds` defaults to 0 and `wave_timer` defaults to the wave interval when the fields are absent; both are written by v0.1.1 saves.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **60/60 checks passed** (all 41 v0.1.0 checks plus 19 new ones for the four fixes). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.1/README.md`.

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build — 3D grid factory automation on one flat building layer:

- 56×56 tile world; resource patches (iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone) from a fixed seed (12345) so saves regenerate them identically.
- Controllable engineer: WASD movement with a following angled camera and wheel zoom; mouse ground raycast build cursor; shooting with ammo magazines.
- Buildings (all 1×1): Miner, Conveyor Belt, Inserter, Furnace, Assembler, Chest, Lab, Boiler, Steam Engine, Power Pole, Stone Wall, Gun Turret — placement ghost with rotation (R), demolish mode (X) with refunds, hotbar (1–9/0) with research locks.
- Item flow: miners auto-eject, belts visibly carry items tile to tile, inserters move items between belts and building buffers; furnaces smelt ore→plate and stone→brick at 1 coal per smelt (burner, no power draw).
- Steam power: boilers burn coal (assumed piped — no fluid system in v0.1.0), adjacent steam engines generate, power poles project a 4.5-tile coverage radius; global satisfaction scales machine speed; HUD power readout.
- Hand crafting (C) in a clean tabbed panel — Buildings, Intermediates, Science, Military — instant crafting, locked recipes greyed with the required tech named.
- Research (T): labs consume red science packs. Techs: Automation, Military, Logistics, Power Efficiency, Reinforced Walls, with prerequisites and immediate unlocks.
- Biters and 5 destroyable nests at the map edge: nest spawns plus escalating timed waves; turrets consume ammo magazines; the player can walk out and shoot nests dead (each drops 2 red science); destroying all nests shows a victory banner and sandbox play continues. Player knockout = respawn at spawn, factory untouched.
- Minimap (live) + big map on M with drag-pan and wheel-zoom.
- Pause menu on Tab or Esc with real SceneTree pause (Tab is primary because Esc exits pointer lock in web builds), containing Help, the in-game Version Log, named save/load, and a safe Restart.
- Named save/load slots as JSON in `user://saves/` — buildings (with buffers, recipes, HP), inventory, research, player, elapsed time, and nests — plus F5 quicksave / F9 quickload.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, and a feature harness run as a scene — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.0/README.md` for the harness result and the single-threaded Web export record.

versions.title: Requested by Josh on 2026-10-08
versions.notes:
Requested by Josh on 2026-10-08:

- **Named saves + load, quicksave/quickload:** pause menu → Save Game (type a name, or click an existing save to overwrite) and Load Game (each save listed with its Day/time; load or delete). F5 quicksaves into the `quicksave` slot, F9 quickloads it (pause-menu buttons too — F5 reloads the page in a browser). Saves live in `user://saves/<name>.json` and capture day/time, player vitals/inventory/weapons/ammo, survivors (recruited, order, guard post, HP), zombies, tree and loot-container state, farm plots, and barricades. The city is now generated from a fixed seed (424242) so saved entity positions line up with the same layout after a restart.
- **Title menu:** the game launches paused on a title screen — New Game, Load Game, Help — with the version shown. Death-screen Restart skips the title and starts a fresh run directly.
- **Melee swing arc:** every melee swing flashes a pale arc in the aim direction sized to the weapon's exact range (Fists 50, Bat 62, Spear 84), fading over ~0.2s, so hit range is always readable.
- **Message feed:** the single latest-message line is now a feed list (max 8 entries) at the lower-left — pickups, finds, crafting, and healing all stack up and each entry fades out after ~5s.

Validation: Godot 4.7.2 headless — import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, 35/35 feature-harness checks passed (title flow, swing arc, feed, save/load + quicksave/quickload round-trip, delete, plus all v0.1.0 systems). Single-threaded Web export generated and verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`). Export record: `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival2D/v0.1.1/README.md`.

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build — the full requested feature set in 2D top-down form:

- **Explore a city:** 3600×3600 procedural city (road grid, ~50 buildings, abandoned cars, park with garden), Camera2D follow.
- **Zombies + day/night:** wander/chase/attack AI, barricade chewing, 240s day cycle with night darkening, night spawns faster, zombies faster/tougher at night and scaling by day; kill counter; 35% ground-loot drops.
- **Scavenge:** loot containers with a random loot table and 45s respawn.
- **Crafting (C):** Wooden Bat, Spear, Pistol, Rifle, Bandage, Barricade Kit, Farm Plot Kit.
- **Weapons:** Fists / Bat / Spear melee (hold click; also chops trees) and Pistol / Rifle ranged with magazines, reserve ammo, and R reload.
- **Trees:** click/E chops for +1 wood per hit, +5 on felling, 60s regrow.
- **Barricades (B build mode):** ghost preview, Barricade / Reinforced / Farm Plot variants, HP, zombie damage, E repair for 1 wood.
- **Farming:** plant 1 seed → 30s growth → harvest 2–3 food + 1–2 seeds (renewable).
- **Survivors:** 6 recruitable (first free, then 1 food); orders Follow / Guard Here / Stay / Work Farm via mouse-aim + 1–4, plus G (all Follow) and J (all Guard); survivors auto-fight zombies; name/order/HP labels.
- **Healing:** Q heals self, F heals nearest recruited survivor (bandage +30, medkit +70); X eats food (+35 hunger, +5 HP); hunger drains and starving hurts.
- **Menus:** Tab/Esc pause menu with Help and an in-game Version Log; any open menu pauses the game; death screen with Restart.

Validation: Godot 4.7.2 headless — import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, 28/28 feature-harness checks passed, single-threaded Web export generated and verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`). Export record: `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival2D/v0.1.0/README.md`.

versions.title: An old pit becomes a pond
versions.notes:
- When a drill's ore patch runs low, the Old pits card comes. From the next day, every ore tile mined out leaves a pit: bare ground you can't build on, counted against its region as land that isn't green.
- Rain fills a pit over about a season (faster where lakes have a level), and a ditch or water beside it fills it at once. A full pit becomes a pond: real water, for fish and pumps.
- Or fill it back in: Landfill (5 stone, or 10 scrap from rubble, crafted by hand). Hold it and click a pit. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Only tiles mined out from the day after the card leave pits; ore you mined out earlier left nothing. Pits look like dark hollows, and muddy water once half full.

versions.title: Buyers with shopping lists
versions.notes:
- Every 7 days each town buyer writes a shopping list: 3 or 4 named things it wants that week, from what you can make, spread across the buyers. The dock's board shows each list, how many they still want today, and what each pays.
- Each listed item has its own appetite and its own price per buyer (up to 30% more on top of their hunger). A listed item goes to the buyer paying most; once they've had enough, it sells like any other of its kind.
- Anything on nobody's list sells for 80%, from the day after the first lists (the Shopping lists card comes first). Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Worlds from before this version switch at their next list day (every 7th day). Orders, contracts and cravings still come from the buyers as before.

versions.title: Storms ground the drones
versions.notes:
- A new world option, Storms ground the drones (on for new Normal and Hard worlds): on a storm day construction, logistic and cargo drones stay home. Any already flying finish their trip. Carts, wagons and barges run as usual.
- The evening before a storm the forecast says no drones will fly tomorrow. The first time, while you own a drone, the Storms ground the drones card comes, and storms ground them only after that day.
- The option can be switched in the farmhouse. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Off for Relaxed worlds and worlds started before this version (switch it on in the farmhouse).

versions.title: Fire follows the wind
versions.notes:
- A new world option, Fire follows the wind (on for new Normal and Hard worlds): a grass fire runs twice as fast downwind and half as fast across or into the wind. On a calm day it spreads alike every way.
- The drought forecast the evening before says which way the wind will blow and which side of your fields to cut the fire break on, and a burning tile's hover says which way the fire is heading.
- The Fire country card explains it. The option can be switched in the farmhouse. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Off for Relaxed worlds and worlds started before this version (switch it on in the farmhouse). Fires still only start in the dry hills.

versions.title: Smoke the company out
versions.notes:
- The mill company's mill runs only while its region is under 60% green. Green it past that and the workers give a week's notice in the news; if the region is still green when the week is up, they quit.
- The mill then stands cold, a plain wreck again: a town crew or the Clearing Kit can clear it. The journal records it.
- The mill's hover shows how green its region is and, once notice is given, how many days are left. If the region falls back under 60%, the notice is off.

**Limitations:** Only the new mill from the company's second letter; company land you sold stays company land.

versions.title: Families come from the valley
versions.notes:
- Every family comes from somewhere: their letter names the region of the valley they left when it dried, and so does their cottage.
- A family living in their home region or a region next to it, or whose home region you've restored, is happier every morning.
- Their favourite dish pays two and a half times its price (not double) when it was made from crops grown in their home region. Crops a Farm Tower or a farmhand picks remember where they grew, through belts, carts and kitchens.

**Limitations:** Crops you pick by hand, a tractor's, and bought ones don't remember where they grew, so they never count as home-grown. A dish whose crops came from several regions counts by their average place.

versions.title: Roads and rails are neighbours too
versions.notes:
- Cottages notice the traffic next door. A cart rail with carts running on the line, or the road out of the valley, within 3 tiles is a bad neighbour; a stone path or a grown hedge is a good one. As with other neighbours, the bad ones only count from the day after the Neighbours card.
- Traffic brings trade too: a Farm Stand, Diner or Lodge right beside a busy rail or the road out gets passers-by (more shoppers, customers or guests).

**Limitations:** A rail counts as busy while any Cart Station has a cart, not by how many carts pass that tile.

versions.title: A Diner's customers come from somewhere
versions.notes:
- A Diner's customers are the people near it now: regulars from the families within 12 tiles, hikers from Lodges within 12, and passers-by from busy Cart Stations or the road out of the valley within 6.
- The more people about, the sooner the next customer comes: every 8 seconds with nobody nearby, down to every 2 seconds with a crowd. A corner still serves 25% faster on top.
- A Diner's hover and the Site card count who's nearby and how often a customer comes. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Diners standing in a save from before this version keep at least their old rate (a customer every 4 seconds).

versions.title: Demand grows with the valley, not the calendar
versions.notes:
- The town's buyers no longer want more just because the days go by. Their appetite grows by steps instead: one for each restored region, each reputation tier (10, 30 and 60) and each town trade that reopens. Each step adds half of what they wanted at the start.
- Orders grow the same way: about $15 at first plus $40 a step, instead of $12 more every day.
- A news line says why demand grew each time it does, and the dock's Buyers section counts the steps. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Saves from before this version keep the demand their days had built up as a floor, so an older farm's buyers and orders don't shrink.

versions.title: Wildlife moves between linked valleys
versions.notes:
- Neighbour valleys now share their wildlife. A valley's summary lists the keystone species living there and the ones that left, and the farmhouse's link lines say what lives in each linked valley.
- A species that leaves your valley stays away for a week before its need can bring it back. If you have a linked valley, it goes down the river there, and while a linked valley has it, it comes back up the river as soon as its need holds, a week sooner.
- The geese say which linked valley they're flying from or to.

**Limitations:** This needs the game server's new version (VibeServer) to carry the species lists. Until then linked valleys share water, smog and shipments as before, and a species that leaves waits its week.

versions.title: Farmhands feed the village
versions.notes:
- A Farmhand's Post's hand now looks after the cottages in its square: it carries food from the post's chest to any cottage there that wants it, their basket first and then a family's favourite.
- It also harvests ripe beds in its square into the chest, leaving beds that a belt, an inserter or a Farm Tower already works.
- Two checkboxes in the post's window switch each job on or off. New posts start with both on.

**Limitations:** Posts from older saves start with both off, so layouts already built keep working as they were. Tick the boxes to turn them on.

versions.title: Hire the town to move a line
versions.notes:
- The farmhouse's Hire the town section has a new job: Move a line. Box what you want moved with your first two map pins and put a third where its top-left corner should go. $30 a building, $5 a belt, pole or pipe; no roboport needed.
- The crew walks in, takes everything in the box down at once (with its contents, recipe, settings, modules and quality) and puts it back up at the new spot, 8 buildings a day (belts, poles and pipes count a quarter). Links and schedules hold, since each building keeps its id.
- A building that can't go back (the spot is taken, water, unexplored land) comes to your backpack with its things, and a news line says where. Cancel and whatever isn't back up comes to your backpack, with half the money for it.

**Limitations:** No turning or mirroring. The farmhouse, cottages, trees and saplings stay where they are. A hitching post's pairing may need setting again.

versions.title: Ash
versions.notes:
- What a grass fire burns turns to ash, and ash is good for the soil. For a season (10 days without seasons) beds on a burnt tile grow 25% faster, and the grass there comes back twice as fast.
- The bed that stood in the fire, or the first one you put up on the ash, gets +20 worms, once. The Alt view marks ash tiles, a tile's hover says how long the ash lasts, and the Fire country card mentions it.

**Limitations:** A tile that burns again starts a fresh season of ash, worms and all.

versions.title: Exposed turbines
versions.notes:
- Where a turbine stands now matters in a storm. One in the dry hills catches more wind (125%) but a storm knocks it out 45% of the time. One with a grown tree or hedge within 3 tiles upwind is sheltered: 85% of the wind, and a storm breaks it only 15% of the time. Anywhere else: 100% and 30%, as before.
- The Site card, the map's Site key and a turbine's hover say which it is, and the storm forecast counts your exposed turbines. Like the weather's other power rates, this starts the day after the Power and the weather card. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Shelter reads the day's wind, so a turbine sheltered on a west wind may be open on an east one.

versions.title: The days draw in
versions.notes:
- With seasons, the days change length: the sun is up for 60% of a summer day, half a spring or autumn day and 40% of a winter day. Solar panels make more in summer and much less in winter, lamps burn longer and the blight has longer nights to raid in.
- A card, The days draw in, comes the first autumn morning; winter's short days start after it (summer's long days need no warning). The forecast says when the days draw in and when the long summer days begin, and the morning report counts the day's daylight. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Without seasons every day is half daylight, as before. Sleeping still ends at the same hour.

versions.title: Turbines you can read
versions.notes:
- Once your power follows the weather, the farm shows it: turbine blades barely turn on a calm day and race in a storm, a broken one stands still, and water wheels turn faster when the river runs high.
- Solar panels go dull grey on rain and snow days, so the day's power reads off the farm before you open the power window.

**Limitations:** Solar Frames over beds don't dull yet.

versions.title: Power and the weather
versions.notes:
- With weather on, your power follows the forecast. Wind turbines turn with the day's wind: calm 25%, a breeze 100%, a strong wind 130%, a storm 160%. Solar panels make 40% on rain and snow days and 110% in a dry spell. Water wheels run at 150% on rain days (the spring flood too) and 70% in a dry spell.
- A card, Power and the weather, comes the first morning you own a turbine, panel, solar frame or wheel, with the week's wind in it; the new rates start the next day. The forecast gets a power line for each day ("power: turbines 130%, panels 40%"), and hovers say today's wind, sky and the river's level.
- The windmill and the hill weather station read the same wind once the card has shown. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** Worlds without weather keep the old gusting wind and a steady sun and river.

versions.title: Chapter goals that teach the arrangement
versions.notes:
- Chapters 2 to 5 each ask for one thing about where buildings stand: harvest a bed kept warm by a burner or oven beside it (Power), give a cottage two good neighbours (The village), grow a plant guild (The first region), and move a building to a spot the map's Site key scores higher (The river).
- Each of those goals has a button in the Collection's Chapters tab: Read the card, Look it up, or Take the lesson.

**Limitations:** A move counts when the same kind of building goes up within 3 days of one coming down, somewhere the survey scores higher; it works for the kinds the Site key scores. A chapter you're in the middle of gains its new goal.

versions.title: Survey the valley
versions.notes:
- Hold a Garden Bed, Cottage, Diner, Greenhouse, Wind Turbine, Solar Panel, Sapling or Dock and open the map (M): the new Site key colours the explored land by how good a spot it is for that building, green good and red poor, from the same rules the Site card reads (growth, green nearby, water, neighbours, corners, wind, sun, the road out).
- Colours run from the worst spot found (red) to the best (green). Numbered pins mark the three best, spread apart (ties go to the nearest), and the map's key says their scores and what wins there ("wins water, green nearby"). The map surveys a little each frame, so a big valley fills in over a second or two.

**Limitations:** Scored at one spot per 3×3 tiles; a bed is scored for the seed you hold most of. Untick Site on the map to hide it.

versions.title: The blight forgets
versions.notes:
- The blight forgets: every zero-smog day (the valley soaked up more than you made) takes 2% off its strength, so a valley that cleaned up stops fighting the brutes it earned early on.
- Hover a Blight Nest: its strength and which way it is going ("Blight strength 34%, falling: 3 clean days in a row"), and how much smog it soaks a second. A tame nest reads as what it is: an air cleaner you feed, turning that smog into Blight Jelly.

**Limitations:** Strength only falls on zero-smog days; there is no other way to lower it.

versions.title: Batteries before burners
versions.notes:
- A power network now uses sun, wind and water first, then its batteries, and only then steam engines and burners. Fuel burns only while the batteries are under 30% charged (or there are none), or for what the batteries can't deliver fast enough, so a backup burner is a backup and doesn't smoke all night beside a charged battery.
- A power pole's window says "Burn fuel when batteries are under 30%" and whether the network is under it now. Still being playtested.

**Limitations:** The 30% line is fixed for now; there's no per-network setting.

versions.title: Fresh from next door
versions.notes:
- A new world option for valleys where food spoils: Fresh from next door (on with food spoiling for new worlds; switch it in the farmhouse). Still being playtested.
- Crops a Farm Tower picks remember where and when. The stamp rides with them on belts, splitters, inserters, carts, barges and drones, and a crate knows its crops' average place and time.
- A dish (or flour, dough, sauce) whose ingredients were all picked within 10 tiles and a minute comes out a tier better. One with an ingredient from more than 40 tiles or 5 minutes away comes out a tier worse, from the day after the card. Made ingredients pass on their crops' place and oldest time, so bread is as fresh as its wheat.
- Iceboxes, Ice Houses and a cart station touching either stop the clock. Hover a machine: "Ingredients from 6 tiles, 40 s".
- Fix: a quality star left behind by a path that forgets it can no longer pass to the next item in the stack.

**Limitations:** Crops picked by hand or by the tractor, bought, or from logistics drones carry no stamp and count neither way. No freezer or cold wagon yet.

versions.title: Quality on the lot: belts, carts, drones and stars
versions.notes:
- Splitters, carts and their wagons, barges, cargo drones and logistics drones now carry each item's quality, so a Fine loaf that goes by cart arrives Fine. A load is handed off best first.
- The critic tastes the best plate of each dish on your Diners' shelves, the fair judges the stack you enter (best first), the museum shows an Excellent dish from your backpack, the vault's provisions want the dish you hand in to be Fine (or Excellent), and a sister valley's dish kit counts the best ten of the stack. Aging racks put their grade on the stack.
- Stars on icons are per stack now: a crate, machine or backpack slot shows a silver star when it holds Fine and a gold one when it holds Excellent. Hover a slot to see how many of each.

**Limitations:** Recipe and shop icons no longer show stars. Crops still take their quality from today's score (strain, season, freshness), not from where they were picked.

versions.title: Quality on the lot: stores, machines, backpack, selling
versions.notes:
- Quality now lives on the stack. A crate, a machine, the Diner and your backpack count how many of each stack are Fine and how many Excellent; the rest are plain. Nothing is averaged, so one Excellent batch is never lost in a big plain stack, and it no longer lifts every loaf on the farm.
- A machine's batch is as good as what it actually took: Excellent flour makes Excellent dough and bread, plain flour plain bread. It takes the best first.
- Inserters and belts carry each item's quality with it, and so does taking from a crate or putting in by hand.
- Docks, the town downriver and the Diner pay each item by its own quality (Fine +15%, Excellent +30%). Prices shown are for plain.
- Older saves: every stack of a dish takes the quality its old farm-wide level gave, once, so nothing gets worse. Hover a backpack stack to see how many are Fine and Excellent.

**Limitations:** Splitters, carts, wagons, barges and drones don't carry quality yet (what goes through them arrives plain), and the fair, museum, vault and critic still read the farm-wide level; the next release does those and puts stars on icons.

versions.title: Quality on the lot: investigation
versions.notes:
- No change to play. A bench (tests/bench_quality.gd) measured what it costs for each stack to carry its own quality instead of one level per dish for the whole farm.
- Verdict: go, in the next two releases. A star tag on belt items costs under 2% of belt time and under 1% of save size. Stacks keep their plain names and count how many are Fine and Excellent beside them, so a rare Excellent batch is never averaged away. The numbers and the design are in PLAN.md.

**Limitations:** Quality is still one level per dish for the whole farm in this version.

versions.title: Lakes have a level
versions.notes:
- A new world option, Lakes have a level (on for new Normal and Hard valleys, off in older saves; switch it in the farmhouse). Still being playtested.
- Offshore Pumps draw their lake down: one pump at full speed takes about 8 tiles' worth of water a day. A little seeps back every day, rain refills a lake faster, and green land within 4 tiles of it faster still, so lakes in restored land hold up and bare ones sink.
- The shore draws back as a lake sinks (mud round its edge; the water tiles stay water, so nothing built moves). Hover a lake or a pump for its level and how fast it fills and drains.
- A card comes the first time a pump takes a lake under 80%. From the next day a pump on a lake under half full pumps at half speed. It never stops, and a lake never runs dry.

**Limitations:** Rivers and ditches don't have a level. The mud ring is flat; the water surface itself doesn't drop.

versions.title: Trees are a promise
versions.notes:
- With Green needs roots on, a meadow sapling takes about 2 days to grow up instead of a minute and a half. It soaks smog and greens the land in step as it grows, so tomorrow's clean air is planted today.
- New: the Tree Nursery (6 planks, 4 wood, Farming), 2×2 frames for young trees. Saplings and pines within 3 tiles of it grow 3 times faster.
- Holding a smog maker, the preview says trees planted now take 2 days to soak it; a sapling's site card says how long it will take there.
- A card explains it the first time you hold or plant a sapling.

**Limitations:** Grown trees can't be lifted and moved with their growth: a nursery speeds trees where they stand. Worlds without Green needs roots keep the 90-second sapling.

versions.title: Paving costs green
versions.notes:
- With Green needs roots on, a solid building on green land holds that green while it stands: the tiles stay green but don't count toward restoring a region or the greenery bonus.
- Take the building down, or give it a green roof, and the tiles count again.
- Light buildings sit on the land without covering it: belts, poles, pipes, roads, lamps, fences, hedges, beds, trees, benches and signs, and (Josh's call) wind turbines and solar panels.
- Holding a building, the site card says how many green tiles it would cover.
- A card comes the day a building first stands on green land; tiles are held from the next day.

**Limitations:** The count of held tiles is worked out with the green each half second, so a huge factory on green land costs a little more time per tick with the option on.

versions.title: Green needs roots
versions.notes:
- A new world option, Green needs roots (on for new Normal and Hard valleys, off in older saves; switch it in the farmhouse).
- Green land with nothing living near it (a planted bed, a grown tree or hedge, reeds, a sod roof, wildflowers or a wild plant) settles over about 3 days from lush down to a resting meadow. It stays green, so regions stay restored; land beside living things stays lush.
- A card comes the first time a patch is found with nothing living near it, and nothing fades until the next day.
- The map's Change layer shows where land is fading (red: withered since dawn).

**Limitations:** The hover doesn't say yet that a tile is settling. Settled land greens up again only when something living is planted in reach.

versions.title: Winter-bare trees
versions.notes:
- With seasons and Strict smog planning, leafy trees (meadow trees, fruit trees and hedgerows in a guild) drop their leaves in winter and soak only 15% of their smog while bare.
- Pines, Reed Beds, green roofs, grass and Air Scrubbers keep working through the winter.
- New: the Pine Sapling (3 wood, Farming). An evergreen: it grows in two days instead of 90 s and soaks 70% of a meadow tree, but all year.
- A card comes the first autumn morning you own a smog maker while most of your trees are leafy; trees only stand bare on winter days after it. Plant a pine belt or a scrubber before the frost.
- The forecast counts down: leaves falling in 3, 2, 1 days, then the leaves fall.

**Limitations:** A Pine Sapling is drawn full-size from the day it's planted (it doesn't grow on screen yet), and Foresters only plant meadow trees. Wild woods from succession count as evergreen.

versions.title: Spread the big passes
versions.notes:
- The sim's three heaviest steps (plants greening the land round them, green spreading to its neighbours, and the smog step) each run on a tick of their own now, instead of sometimes landing on the same tick together with the once-a-second work.
- On the big benchmark factory the slowest tick of each second drops from about 12 ms to 10-12 ms, with the same green and smog as before.
- In co-op every farm runs those steps on the same ticks, so a friend who joins mid-game stays level.

**Limitations:** The greening of one big cluster still runs in one go (no worker thread: round 11 measured that no-go). The average tick is unchanged; only the spikes are smaller.

versions.title: Choose where to settle
versions.notes:
- A new valley's arrival fly-over now passes three places you could settle before it comes down at the farmhouse: the river bend, the hills and the marsh edge, each picked from that world's own land.
- The river bend sits by the old riverbed, on the most sandy soil (potatoes, berries, olives, grapes). The hills are open loam with rock and few trees. The marsh edge is heavy clay near the pond (rice, cabbage, mint, mushrooms).
- A card asks where the farm should go. Pick one and the farmhouse, the farmer and (in a fixer-upper valley) the old broken farm move there; or stay in the open meadow.
- You can only move on the first day, once, and before you build or take anything down. In co-op the host picks and everyone moves with the farm.
- Older valleys stay where they are.

**Limitations:** The sites stay inside the home region, within 28 tiles of the old start, so the river, pond, nests and the road out are where they always were. Hills and marsh here are a soil choice, not a new biome. The card only comes once; Later skips it for good.

versions.title: Dock on the road out
versions.notes:
- One old road, the merchant's, now leaves the valley: a straight run of paving from near the farmhouse out to the edge of the land, in a direction the seed picks.
- A Shipping Dock pays full price when it touches that road, or any road joined to it, or the river where it flows again. Anywhere else, haulage takes a fifth: it pays 80%.
- Holding a dock, the site card says which before you place it, and the dock's hover says when it's paying less.
- Docks already standing in older valleys keep full price, and the old road is laid there on free ground.

**Limitations:** Goods don't yet visibly leave on a cart or barge. The town dock downriver always pays its own prices.

versions.title: The company writes back
versions.notes:
- Once 3 regions are restored and 40% of the valley is green, letters arrive from the old mill company, the villain of the journal. Answer them in the farmhouse window: Accept or Refuse.
- First it offers $1500 for a region you haven't built in. Accept and it's company land: nothing can be built there (the hover and ghost say so).
- A week after you answer, it offers $3000 to build a new mill at the farthest wreck. Accept and the wreck becomes its mill: it can't be cleared and makes 6 smog a second from then on, a smog source you'd have to contain.
- Refusing costs only the money. Each choice is written in the Journal tab of the collection book.

**Limitations:** The company writes these two letters once per valley. Its mill looks like the wreck it was built on.

versions.title: Restoration changes the map
versions.notes:
- When a region is restored, the land itself answers once: a spring pond fills (3 by 3), wild apple trees come up where an old orchard was, a wildflower meadow blooms, or a grove of trees grows back. Which one is picked by the valley's seed.
- It only uses free, dry, explored ground in that region: nothing you built is moved. The morning news and the restored card name it and say where.
- The cash reward for restoring a region stays the same.

**Limitations:** Regions restored before this version keep their land as it was. If a region has no free room for any of the four, nothing changes there.

versions.title: Seeds ride the wind
versions.notes:
- In valleys with weather, wildflowers spread on their own: on a windy morning each patch in full bloom has a one-in-four chance to seed a new one 3 to 6 tiles downwind (a tile either side), on free land that's already a little green.
- Up to 8 new patches a morning, and the wind stops seeding once the valley has 300 patches.
- The morning news says which way the seeds went; the forecast says on which days wildflower seeds drift, and which way.
- Alt view shows "seeds east 3-6" (or north, south, west) over bloomed patches on a windy day.

**Limitations:** Seeds only land on bare-but-greening ground (green at least 15%), never on fully bare land, water, rock or anything built. Calm days and valleys without weather carry no seeds.

versions.title: Tall chimneys
versions.notes:
- New module: the Tall Chimney (4 bricks, 2 iron plates), part of Machine Modules research. It fits Biomass Burners, Stone and Electric Furnaces, Burner and Electric Ovens and Kilns, in the usual module slots.
- With one, the building makes the same smog, but it lands a third as thick on each of three smog cells downwind (4 to 12 tiles off), so less harm right next door and more drift to deal with out there. On a calm day it spreads thin round the stack instead.
- A plain stack keeps its smog close, where one Air Scrubber catches most of it: the choice is containing it here or spreading it thin.
- Holding one of these buildings, the smog preview shows both shapes: the red square for a plain stack and an orange one for a Tall Chimney, with the beds inside each.

**Limitations:** Speed Gears, Smog Filters and Thrift Plates still fit only powered machines, so a burner or stone furnace takes only the chimney. Two chimneys on one building do no more than one.

versions.title: Hives need a winter store
versions.notes:
- In valleys with seasons, a hive's honey is its colony's winter store. Each hive keeps 5 honey back; its window shows the line with - and + buttons (0 to 20), and inserters and taking by hand stop at it.
- A Hives need a winter store card shows the first autumn (or winter) day you own a hive.
- From then on, a colony whose hive has no honey left on the first morning of spring has died over the winter. The hive isn't destroyed: it stands empty, making no honey and pollinating nothing, until a spring swarm from another hive moves in. The window says so.
- Without seasons there's no winter, so hives work as before.

**Limitations:** The store only counts honey, not beeswax. A hive that has never made honey isn't a colony yet, so it can't die.

versions.title: Families with tastes
versions.notes:
- Every family has a favourite dish and one they don't care for, picked by the valley's seed so the twelve families together want a spread. Their letter says which, and so do the cottage's window and hover.
- Bring a family their favourite, even on top of the basket, and they pay double its price on the spot (once a day) and are a little happier next morning.
- A dish they don't care for counts half toward their basket: they want twice as many of it. The basket in the cottage window shows it.
- A Families with tastes card shows the first morning a family lives here; dislikes count from the next day, so older valleys get a day's notice too.

**Limitations:** Tastes are picked from the dishes in cottage baskets, so a Settlers family may love a dish you can't make yet. Village depots hand out favourites too, but only once the basket is full.

versions.title: The worst two count
versions.notes:
- New world option, on for new valleys: only a bed's two worst slowdowns count. A bed held back by smog, shade, the season and a poor soil all at once now feels just the two worst; boosts all still count, and a bed that's stopped (a night crop by day, wilting in a heatwave) is still stopped.
- The bed's hover and window say "(two worst count)" when more than two things slow it, so fixing the worst one shows the next.
- Switch it in the farmhouse, or on the new-world screen. Older valleys keep every slowdown until you switch it on.
- Needs playtesting (Josh, 11-06): say if beds feel too forgiving.

**Limitations:** Beds only: machines still multiply every factor. A hardy strain's smog boost counts only when smog is one of the two worst.

versions.title: Compressed saves
versions.notes:
- Saves are packed: everything after a save's first line is gzipped, so a save takes a small fraction of the space it did (a few percent of the old size), and the browser's storage lasts much longer.
- Older saves load as before, and are packed the next time they're saved. Load, the save list, rename, export, import and the atlas all read both kinds.
- The Load screen says "packed" beside a packed save's size.
- Exported saves stay plain text, so an older version of the game can still import them.

**Limitations:** Old saves stay unpacked until they're saved again (autosaves turn over on their own). Sending a save to another device was already packed, so it's the same size as before.

versions.title: Neighbour valleys
versions.notes:
- New: neighbour valleys, co-op without playing at the same time. The farmhouse shows your valley's code; type a friend's code to link their valley upstream or downstream of yours. The game checks the server about once a minute while you play.
- A green valley upstream (half green or more) sends more water: your river flows one region further.
- Smog from the valley upstream rides the river down: river pumps can draw dirty water. The Dirty water card comes first and names the valley upstream, and the dirt only counts from the next day. Sand Filters clean it as usual.
- A Barge Dock can be set to Neighbour: once a week it ships up to 50 goods to the valley downstream, and barges from the valley upstream tie up at yours.

**Limitations:** The server keeps valley summaries in memory for two weeks and forgets them if it restarts; it reaches the live site only with the next VibeServer publish. One valley each way. Water the river already brought stays if a link goes away. In co-op only the host talks to the server.

versions.title: A short valley
versions.notes:
- New challenge: A Short Valley. Three in-game weeks (21 days) to do what you can: beds grow and the land greens 20% faster, and everything sells for 20% more. The morning report counts the days down.
- The morning after the last day, a score card: regions restored (100 each), wildlife back (40 each), your best-selling dish (60 plus its price, up to 60 more) and a point off for every 100 smog you made.
- Keep playing ends the challenge (prices and growth go back to normal) and keeps the score in the Journal tab of the Collection book; Back to title leaves. Your best score shows on the new-world screen, and the atlas page lists each valley's score.

**Limitations:** Trees, hedges and machines run at their usual speed; only beds and greening are faster. The score is worked out once, on day 22's morning: a valley loaded after that keeps the score it got. The seed of the week never picks this challenge.

versions.title: Regions that follow the land: investigation
versions.notes:
- No change to play. A bench (tests/bench_regions.gd) tried region borders that follow biome edges and the river instead of the 64-tile grid.
- Verdict: not this round. Working out the borders roughly tripled the time to make each new piece of land as you walk, re-measuring a region every second got seven times slower, and about a fifth of every tile would change region, so old valleys could never switch. The numbers and what a later attempt would need are in PLAN.md.

**Limitations:** Regions stay a 64-tile grid. The planned build step (chunk 307) was skipped.

versions.title: A blight without guns
versions.notes:
- New: a third way to have the blight. On the new-world screen, tick "Creep instead of bugs (no guns)" under Blight nests attack: nests never attack, and there are no guns, turrets or walls.
- Instead the blight creeps out from each wild nest, about two tiles a day and faster where smog reaches the nest. Inside the creep, grass withers and beds lose soil life.
- Push it back with the game's own tools: green land at the creep's edge, hedges near the nest, a stocked Blight Trough (a tamed nest's creep draws back), and birds, deer or the white stag in its region.
- The map draws each nest's creep and, dashed, where it will reach tomorrow; a nest's hover gives both. A Blight creep card comes the first time a nest is on your map, and the creep only starts spreading the day after.

**Limitations:** Creep is a circle around each nest; it doesn't follow rivers or roads, and overlapping nests wither the land twice as fast. It isn't drawn on the land itself (the withering shows), only on the map. Bug worlds and peaceful worlds are unchanged.

versions.title: Pick your valley's threads
versions.notes:
- New: pick your valley's threads. The new-world screen has a Threads row (bees, dairy, fish, cloth, preserving, village extras), all on by default; the farmhouse can switch each one later. The blight is still the combat option.
- A thread that's off stays out of the build menu and hotbar, crafting, the research tree, the seed shop, the almanac's ideas and the village's secret recipes, along with everything that needs it (no dairy: no cheese, cake or lasagne; no bees: no honey, candles or cherry trees).
- Buildings you already placed keep working, and their hazard cards still show while one stands. Research that waited on a left-out building (the Seed Vault on the hive and the barn) no longer does, and a field study's sample from a left-out thread counts as done.
- Preserving can't be left out in a world where food spoils. Old saves have every thread on.

**Limitations:** Turning a thread off doesn't take away what you hold or have built. Contracts and the town's buyers aren't checked against threads yet. The blight can't be switched after the valley is made.

versions.title: A vault of everything
versions.notes:
- The Great Seed Vault now wants breadth, not volume. Foundations: 100 each of bricks, glass and planks, from the kiln, the furnace and the sawmill (instead of 2,600 bricks, plates and gears).
- The seed bank: 20 seeds of every crop in your Collection book, and a grown tree in each restored region (the vault's window names the regions still without one).
- Provisions: twenty different dishes at Fine quality or better, five of each (instead of 950 of five dishes). The window lists what's in and which dishes in your backpack it would take.
- Worlds with a vault already started keep their stage, and what's gone in still counts toward the new needs.

**Limitations:** Bred strains count as their crop's seed. Orchard fruit (apples, peaches, cherries) needs no seeds. The seed bank's tree check runs every few seconds, so it can finish a moment after the last tree grows.

versions.title: Region health card
versions.notes:
- New: click any explored region on the map (on open ground) for its health card: one row each for green, smog, water, soil life, wildlife and plant guilds, and the weakest one called out in words, like "Dusty Bend is held back by smog, mostly from two biomass burners to the north".
- A Show me button opens the map on the weakest spot (the worst smog, or the region's middle).
- Restored regions keep their perk choice and Rewild button on the same card.

**Limitations:** Smog makers are the six working ones nearest the worst smog, within 48 tiles; it doesn't trace the wind. Guilds are sampled every 8 tiles. Clicking a building on the map still opens that building.

versions.title: One microclimate per tile
versions.notes:
- New: every tile has one microclimate reading: warm, scorching, shaded, sheltered, damp or frosty, from the warmth, shade, hedge shelter, watering and frost rules that were already there. Hover a tile or bed to see it as one line ("Microclimate: warm, sheltered, damp"), and the soil view (G) tags each bed with it.
- New worlds get one Microclimate card in place of the separate Warmth, Shade, Root rot and Frozen ponds cards; each of those then shows up as a short note the first time it's near you. Worlds started before this version keep their cards as they were.
- Nothing grows any differently: it's a new way to read the rules, not a new rule.

**Limitations:** The reading is words, not numbers (the bed's factor list from v0.1.285 has the numbers). Frosty is the whole valley on a frozen-pond day. The soil view tags beds only, not open ground.

versions.title: Hire the town
versions.notes:
- New: hire the town. The farmhouse window has a Hire the town section: pay the town crew to pave a road or dig a ditch between your first two map pins ($6 or $4 a tile), or to clear the wreck nearest the first pin ($250 and up).
- The crew walks in from the farmhouse and works over a few in-game days (16 tiles a day); you can watch the two of them at it. Up to three jobs at once, each with a Cancel button that gives back half of what's left of it.
- They bring their own shovels and paving, so it needs no Shovel or road items, only money: a way to spend a late-game purse on the valley itself.

**Limitations:** Jobs use the first two pins on the map (in the order they were placed). Roads and ditches go along x then along y between the pins, skipping tiles they can't use. A cleared wreck's scrap goes with the crew.

versions.title: The town recovers
versions.notes:
- New: the town recovers. As regions are restored the town's own trades open again: the bakery at 2 regions, the dairy at 4, the brewery at 6. Each is in the news a week ahead (with a card the first time).
- Once open, a trade buys its inputs at the dock for 50% more (bakery: flour, eggs, honey; dairy: milk, salt; brewery: apples, grapes, sugar) and pays only half for what it now makes itself (bread, sourdough and cornbread; cheese and yogurt; cider). Moving up the chain pays.
- Contracts keep the price they were agreed at. The dock's window lists the open trades and the next one to come.

**Limitations:** Only the dock's prices change: diners, stalls and the town downriver price as before. Worlds that already have regions restored get their notices on the next morning.

versions.title: The market is people
versions.notes:
- New: the market is people. The dock sells to the town's buyers: Hale's grocery, the Crust bakery, the Wheatsheaf inn and the school kitchen, then a tailor, a river hotel, a chandler and a tea room as your reputation grows and regions are restored. Each wants so many crops, pantry goods, dishes or goods a day, more as the days go by.
- A kind pays up to 25% more while the buyers are hungry for it and slides to 40% once they've had their fill, until they come back hungry the next morning. Today's market (wanted and glut items, prices that dip as you sell) still applies on top. A farm that sells a spread earns more than before; one that floods a single kind earns less.
- The dock's window has a Buyers section: who wants what and how much is left, what each kind pays now, and when a kind is glutted. Orders and contracts now come from the buyer who wants that kind most, and what you deliver fills its appetite.
- Fair warning: the buyers arrive on a morning with a card, and prices follow their hunger only from the next day. Diners, stalls, the town downriver and family cravings sell to their own customers, as before.

**Limitations:** Cravings and the harvest festival keep their own faces (the families and the village), not a buyer's. The buyers are a section in the dock's window rather than a tab of their own. Appetites are per kind, so many crops of one sort still fill the same grocer.

versions.title: Wildlife hunts the blight
versions.notes:
- New: wildlife hunts the blight. A pack leaving a nest in a region where the birds live (their need holds there, see the Wildlife page) is a quarter smaller; where birds and deer both live, two fifths smaller. A nest in the white stag's region (a rewilded region and the land beside it) sends no packs at all.
- A nest's hover says when its packs are thinned, or that it sends none.

**Limitations:** Only the packs a nest sends at your buildings are thinned; bugs that go for a farmer who shoots at their nest are not. Nests still soak up smog and spread as before.

versions.title: Keystone species
versions.notes:
- New: keystone species. Every animal that comes back has a need, listed on the Wildlife page of the Collection book with a tick: birds an old-growth tree in a region, deer a green corridor between two restored regions (one restored region will do until two side by side are), wild bees three wildflower patches in bloom by their tree, fish a lake clean of smog, the white stag a rewilded region.
- While a species stays, beds in the regions where its need holds grow 5% faster for each species living there (a bed's hover lists it as "wildlife").
- Never a surprise: a species gets two weeks to settle in, and if it then loses its need you get a week's forecast in the news, the morning report and the page (and the Wildlife can leave card the first time). It leaves only if the need still fails when the week is up, and it comes back once the need holds again. While the fish are gone, Fish Traps catch at half speed.

**Limitations:** Wildflowers bloom all year in Bloomworks, so the wild bees' "flowers in every season" is wildflowers near their tree. Wild bees that leave come back with the next swarm that settles in a tree. The page's notes keep the last 20 events.

versions.title: Overfishing
versions.notes:
- New: lakes have fish stocks. Each lake breeds its fish back slowly; two Fish Traps on one lake hold it steady, and more fish it down. A trap on a fished-out lake catches only as fast as the fish come back (never quite nothing).
- Fair warning first: the Overfishing card shows when you put a third trap on one lake, and only from the next day do catches start to draw the stock down. It points at the Fish Pond as the way to raise more fish.
- Reed beds on a lake's shore and clean water help it breed back. A trap's hover and window show its lake's stock and how many traps fish it.

**Limitations:** The stock isn't drawn on the map or in Alt view yet, only in a trap's hover and window. A lake bigger than 4,000 tiles is counted as its first 4,000.

versions.title: Names that heal, market news you can act on
versions.notes:
- New: names that heal. When a region is restored it drops its dead name: "Dry Creek" becomes "Clear Creek", "Ashen Flats" becomes "Green Flats", on the map, its labels and the atlas. The news of its restoring keeps the old name and says the new one.
- Market news you can act on: the day's "everyone wants" and "glut" items now come from what your farm can make, or is one unlock away from, instead of anything at all. And tomorrow's pair is told with today's, so a line can be switched in time.

**Limitations:** Journal entries written before this version keep whatever name they used. The market pool counts crops whose seeds you hold or can buy, and recipes unlocked or one unlock away, whether or not you've built the machine.

versions.title: Research that reads the valley
versions.notes:
- New: a few unlocks ask the valley for something as well as money. Eco-tourism wants a restored region (hikers need green land to walk), the Seed Lab wants beds growing on two different soils, and Lightning Rods want a storm you've lived through.
- Their research cards say what they're waiting for. Unlocks you already own stay owned, and a world without weather doesn't wait for a storm.

**Limitations:** The Heritage wing's clean-air week from the idea isn't asked for yet: the wing is a Seed Vault stage, not research. The Seed Lab counts beds growing now, so pulling them up before you buy it closes it again.

versions.title: Spring planting rush
versions.notes:
- New: the spring planting rush. For the first three days of spring every planted bed grows 15% faster and greens a tile farther, so the year has a beat to plan for: lay the fields out in winter, plant in the rush.
- The morning report counts down to it over winter's last three days and names it on spring's first morning. A bed's speed list shows "spring rush" while it lasts.

**Limitations:** Only in worlds with seasons. The first spring of a world started in spring gets the rush too.

versions.title: Winter is moving season
versions.notes:
- New: winter is moving season. All winter construction drones fly half again as fast and five more can be out at once, so it's the time to take the farm apart and put it back better.
- The first winter morning's report names the three worst-placed lines (a Farm Tower's beds or a machine, with where they are, how fast they run and what slows them most), and the last days of autumn count down to it.

**Limitations:** The worst-placed lines are named by map position in the report text, not as buttons that jump the map there. Hand removal already gives everything back, so winter changes drones only.

versions.title: The first move on day one
versions.notes:
- New: the first-day checklist (and the fixer-upper farm's list) ends with a move: take a bed or your Farm Tower down and set it up again where the Site card under it scores higher.
- Taking it down gives everything back, so the move is free; the step's tooltip says so. It counts in the first three days.

**Limitations:** The step ticks for any bed or tower taken down and put up again in the first days; it doesn't check that the new spot actually scores higher.

versions.title: Site survey with numbers
versions.notes:
- New: the Site card under a building in hand now shows for every building (not only beds, cottages and machines) and gives each thing the spot offers with its number.
- Green nearby: "+14% speed (56% of the land within 12 tiles is green)" for beds, machines, towers, drills, inserters and foresters.
- Beds: soil, water, sun and heat, the crops beside it (and the row bonus a different crop would get), pollinators, and "Would grow at 78% here (tomato 78%, lettuce 70%)" for the seeds you hold, worked out by the same rules the bed would grow by.
- Greenhouses say how much sun they'd get, wind turbines how much wind (other turbines close by take some).

**Limitations:** Water for pumps and fish traps and a solar panel's sun aren't scored yet; the best-crop line only counts seeds you hold (every crop if you hold none). The card doesn't wrap, so a long line can run wide.

versions.title: What's holding this bed back
versions.notes:
- New: a bed's hover now says what's holding it back, with numbers, worst first: "41% of full speed · smog ×0.62, shade ×0.90 · green nearby ×1.14". Its window lists every factor.
- Machines do the same: power, fuel, green nearby, wind, modules, mastery, an engineer, a greenhouse's shade, hot spring and fish pond.
- Alt view: a bed's ripe timer names its worst slowdown when it costs a third or more ("1:20 · smog"), tinted redder the worse it is.
- Nothing grows faster or slower than before: the numbers are the same ones the game already used, now shown.

**Limitations:** The list shows a bed's own factors; things that change a bed's harvest rather than its speed (pollinators, bees, bounty strains) and a thirsty crop's whole-day wait aren't in it yet. Machine fuel shows as half speed whether or not the burner is mid-batch.

versions.title: A second town downriver
versions.notes:
- New: once the river flows again, a town opens a dock on the bank at its far end, downstream of everything. Barges reach it like any Receive dock (and it can be a stop in a schedule); carts reach it through a Receive Cart Station within 10 tiles of it, which sells what they bring.
- It keeps its own prices: fish × 1.5, drinks and preserves × 1.4, raw crops only × 0.7. Selling there lowers its prices, not the big market's, and they recover three times slower. So a glut at home has somewhere else to go.
- The dock's window lists the town's prices under Downriver; the town dock's own window has the full list.

**Limitations:** The town is only its dock (no streets or townsfolk yet). It may open far out, beyond what you've explored: its site is marked as explored.

versions.title: Tractor
versions.notes:
- New: the Tractor (research $600, after the Farm Tower; 20 iron plates, 10 gears, 10 planks). It comes with a 2×2 shed: fill the shed with fuel, seeds and Garden Beds by hand or inserter.
- Stand by the tractor and press Y to drive it with the walk keys, 3 tiles a second. Over bare ground it lays beds (Plough, on by default), it plants empty beds, and it harvests ripe ones into its 40-stack hold, keeping the seed, then replants.
- Or give it a field in its window (6×6, 10×10 or 16×16 in front of the shed): it works the rows back and forth on its own until the hold is full or the seeds run out.
- It burns fuel while it moves: wood or coal make smog like a Burner Drill, biogas makes none.

**Limitations:** The shed's stores are the tractor's wherever it is (no driving home to unload). A field tile it can't reach is skipped.

versions.title: Draft horse and wagon
versions.notes:
- New: Hitching Posts (6 planks, 2 iron plates; research Draft horse and wagon, after the Dairy Barn). Put one beside a chest at each end of a road: a new post pairs with the nearest free one, or pair it in its window.
- A horse from a Dairy Barn with feed within 20 tiles pulls a wagon between them along stone road, stone path and bridges (up to 120 tiles): 20 items a trip at 2 tiles a second, both ways. Each loaded trip it eats 1 wheat or straw from the chest it loads at (5 are always left for it); with none it waits, hungry. An empty trip back is free.

**Limitations:** The horse doesn't need its barn's feed to come along; it just needs a fed barn nearby. A broken road parks the wagon where the route was.

versions.title: Maple sap
versions.notes:
- New: the Sap Tap (2 iron plates, 1 plank). Hold one and click an old-growth tree to tap it: from the last third of winter to the second day of spring it gives 1 maple sap an hour, up to 6, taken with Ctrl-click or an inserter. When the sap stops the tap drops off for you to take back.
- Boil 4 sap into Maple Syrup in an oven, for Pancakes (flour, egg, milk, syrup) or jam with syrup instead of sugar (2 jars a batch).

**Limitations:** The tap isn't drawn on the tree yet: hover the tree to see it. Without seasons the sap runs all year.

versions.title: A local green bonus
versions.notes:
- Machines, drills, inserters, Farm Towers and beds now take half their greenery speed bonus from the green land within 12 tiles of them (up to +50% when it's all green) and half from the whole valley's, so greening round the factory pays more than a tree farm far away.
- The HUD's Greenery line shows the bonus where you stand; a bed's hover shows its green nearby.

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before this version keep the bonus they had as a floor, so nothing there gets slower. The green nearby is measured every 5 seconds.

versions.title: The land rests
versions.notes:
- Take down a building that stood for a season or more and the land under it rests for a season: it greens twice as fast, and a garden bed placed there starts with lively soil (60 worms).
- Hover the ground to see it; the soil view (G) tags resting land.

**Limitations:** Only buildings put up from this version count (older ones don't know when they went up). Belts, poles, hedges and trees don't rest the land.

versions.title: Pollinator crops
versions.notes:
- New crop: Beans, a summer crop from the seed shop, and Bean Stew in the oven (3 beans, a tomato, a potato).
- New world option, on for Normal and Hard: Pollinator crops. Strawberries, pumpkins, beans and orchard trees give a full crop only with wildflowers, a Beehive, a wild colony or a Bloom Nest within 4 tiles; without one they give half. A card explains it the day you first hold such a seed, and halving starts the next day.
- Older worlds start with it off; the farmhouse window can switch it. Bed hovers and seed tooltips say whether something visits.

**Limitations:** Nothing shows the 4-tile pollinator reach while you place a bed yet; hover the bed to check.

versions.title: Good neighbours in the row
versions.notes:
- A planted bed grows 10% faster for each different crop on its four sides, up to +20%: mixed rows beat one crop wall to wall. Hover a bed to see its neighbours; Alt draws a green line to each.
- A Farm Tower set to any seed plants the kind least present beside each bed, so a tower holding two or three seeds plants mixed rows on its own.

**Limitations:** Only planted beds count, and only on the four sides (not corners). The bonus is worked out every 5 seconds.

versions.title: Crash-safe autosave
versions.notes:
- New in Settings, beside Autosave: Copy to server. Each autosave also goes up to the game's server (at most one every 2 minutes), so a browser crash or cleared storage doesn't lose the farm.
- Load Game shows when each world's server copy last went up, with Restore from server (it adds the copy as a new save; nothing is overwritten).

**Limitations:** The server keeps copies in memory for a week: it forgets them when it restarts or sleeps. The live server gets this with its next update; until then backups quietly don't go up. Restore needs this browser's settings (your player key).

versions.title: Installable
versions.notes:
- Bloomworks can be installed like an app (Install or Add to Home Screen in the browser) and has its own icon: a flower in a gear.
- Installed from bloomworks.onrender.com it opens without a connection after the first visit (co-op still needs one).

**Limitations:** On the Vibes site it installs but still needs a connection: the engine files live in a shared folder outside the game's own.

versions.title: Keep a copy when the host leaves
versions.notes:
- When the host leaves a co-op game, you keep the farm you were playing: it's saved as "<world> (copy)" and you choose Carry on alone (offline, as yourself, with your own backpack and wallet; everyone else's are kept) or Back to title.
- Leave a co-op game and come back later: you start where you left off, with your own backpack.

**Limitations:** The copy is the farm as your game had it, a few ticks behind the host. Visitors don't keep a copy.

versions.title: Valley atlas
versions.notes:
- New on the title screen: the Valley Atlas, a page of every valley you've played on this computer, last played first.
