- Each one shows its last time-lapse picture (or its save's thumbnail), its seed and day, its valley number and challenge, the regions you restored, its best dish and the day its Seed Vault opened. Open loads its last save; Forget takes it off the page and leaves its saves alone.
- The Journal tab in the Collection book has a link to it. Worlds from before this version fill in from their saves the first time you open it.

**Limitations:** The atlas lives in this browser's settings, like your hats and records, so it doesn't move with an exported save.

versions.title: Sandbox copy
versions.notes:
- Every save in the Load list has a new Try it button: it opens a scratch copy of that farm with the clock stopped, so you can try a new layout and throw it away.
- Nothing in a sandbox is kept: no autosave, quicksave, save or exit save, and no records, weekly bests, vault bests or hats. A strip at the top says so, with a Free build switch and a Discard button; the Esc menu's last button becomes Discard and Quit.
- A sandbox can't be hosted for co-op.

**Limitations:** To keep something you tried, build it again in the real save (a blueprint copied in the sandbox stays in your library).

versions.title: Belt route planner
versions.notes:
- With a belt in hand, Shift-drag from one tile to another: the game plans the cheapest belt route between them and shows it as a ghost, with its length and what it takes.
- It goes round things where that's short, tunnels under walls of rocks, buildings or water with an underground pair, and bridges water when there's no other way.
- Let go and pick Build what I have (the rest go down as ghosts for drones), Ghosts only, or Cancel. Esc or right-click cancels while dragging.

**Limitations:** Routes stay within about 140 tiles each way. Water tiles can't be ghosts, so a bridged stretch only goes down with Build what I have and bridges in your backpack.

versions.title: The old railway
versions.notes:
- A derelict railway from before the smog now runs across the far valley, more than three regions from home. You get a note and a map pin the first time you come near it.
- Its rotten ties can't be cleared, only mended: hold right-click on one with 2 planks in your backpack and it becomes a Cart Rail, free. A farmhand whose post holds planks mends the ties in its square.
- At the far end is a ruined town (its heaps give bricks) and the old station house: 10 planks and 4 iron plate open it as a Cart Station set to Receive.
- Older saves get the line too, in the land already explored, skipping anything built or under water; fill those gaps with your own rails.

**Limitations:** Ties under a building or in water in an older save are left out. Taking a mended rail down gives the rail back, not the tie.

versions.title: Cart wagons
versions.notes:
- New item: the Wagon (6 planks, 2 gears, 4 iron plate), unlocked with the Cart Station. Hitch up to three at a station (its window, or an inserter puts them in).
- Every cart that leaves the station pulls them all: a cart and three wagons carry four times as much, a Send station waits for a load that big, and timed stops on a schedule last that much longer.
- On a signalled line, a stopped train holds every block its wagons stand in, so the block behind it stays red until its last wagon is through. The wagons trail behind the cart along the rails.

**Limitations:** Wagons hitch to a station, not to one cart: every cart from it pulls the same number.

versions.title: Apprentices
versions.notes:
- The Test Kitchen has a new Apprentices list: teach a family at tier 2 (Villagers) or above one dish you can make, of two or three ingredients.
- Each morning, after the Village Depot's round, they take up to five batches' ingredients from the depot that serves them, cook at home and put 80% of it back in the depot (the rest is their dinner), so the next round hands it out.
- A family that drops back below tier 2 stops until they're back. Teach them something else, or nothing, any time.

**Limitations:** One dish per family, and only from a Village Depot in reach of their cottage.

versions.title: Market day
versions.notes:
- Once a week, on a day picked by the valley, a village of two or more families holds a market by your farmhouse, from mid-morning to late afternoon.
- The stalls sell what the village makes (eggs from the start, milk once a family is Villagers, cloth once one is Townsfolk), a seed or two for crops you've never grown, and whatever the last caravan didn't sell.
- Happier families sell cheaper: from half again the usual price down to the usual price. Buy from the farmhouse window, below the merchant.

**Limitations:** Each stall sells its whole lot at once. The takings go to the villagers, not to a village purse.

versions.title: Terroir
versions.notes:
- A crop picked in season from its favourite soil now carries the name of the region it grew in, for ten days: "Dry Creek tomatoes".
- A dish made with such crops carries their regions too (see its tooltip). The Diner charges 5% more for each region a dish names, up to four.
- At the fair, each region counts like half a quality point with the judges, and a dish from three regions or more earns a star more from the critic.
- A bed's hover says when its crop will be named for its region.

**Limitations:** It's a ledger per crop, not a tag on each tomato: any tomato counts as from Dry Creek while Dry Creek has picked good ones in the last ten days.

versions.title: Hydroponics
versions.notes:
- New research after the Greenhouse: the Hydroponic Rack, a small powered indoor farm for greens and herbs (lettuce, cabbage, thyme, mint, chamomile).
- It grows in any season, on any soil, in any smog, and 40% slower than a Greenhouse, at 30 kW instead of 100.
- It needs a water pipe from a pump touching it, and compost tea: one Fertilizer makes four harvests' worth.

**Limitations:** Only greens and herbs: bigger crops still want a Greenhouse.

versions.title: Night crops
versions.notes:
- New night crops: Moonflowers and Glow Mushrooms grow only after dark, on land at least half green. By day they wait; they never die for it.
- Their first plants sprout wild at night on very green land: forage them, then make seeds by hand. No Seed Lab needed.
- They glow softly at night. Oven recipe: Moonlight Soup (a moonflower, a glow mushroom, milk), a dear starter for the Diner.

**Limitations:** A Greenhouse can't grow them, since they want the dark.

versions.title: Diner menus
versions.notes:
- A Diner's window now has a set menu: pick a starter, a main and a drink. While it has all three, a customer buys the set: 30% more than the dishes apart, and 40% when the crops going straight into them are in season.
- The food critic reviews the set when there is one, and what's on the shelves when there isn't.
- A Diner with no set, or short of one of its dishes, serves one dish at a time as before.

**Limitations:** Menus copy with blueprints. Drinks are cider, juice, tea and coffee.

versions.title: Shared walls
versions.notes:
- Three or more food machines touching each other now form a kitchen, with a shared roof. Point at one to see it.
- One pole reaching any part of a kitchen powers all of it. A Burner Oven out of fuel takes it from a kitchen mate, so one feed does.
- An inserter on any part of a kitchen can take what the other machines made, so one line out can do. A machine with its own inserter keeps its own output, so blocks you've already built work as before.

**Limitations:** Mills, ovens, prep tables, juicers, roasters, presses, smokehouses and canning lines count. A bulk inserter takes its extra items only from the machine it faces.

versions.title: Hot springs
versions.notes:
- Every valley now has one hot spring, at least two regions from home: a steaming pool you can't build on, marked on your map when you first come near.
- A Steam Engine touching it runs on free steam, with no boiler or water. Run a long line home.
- The land within 3 tiles stays warm all winter, Greenhouses within 4 tiles run 15% faster, and a lodge within 12 tiles gets half as many hikers again.

**Limitations:** Worlds you've already explored get theirs in land you haven't reached yet, or the first free spot of the seeded list that has already been generated.

versions.title: Logistics overview
versions.notes:
- New Logistics tab in the Production window (P), also opened with a button on any Roboport: every logistic network with its Supplier and Requester Chests, what each holds and wants, what's on its way, and the drones in the air.
- Click any row to see it on the map.
- Chests outside any roboport's cover are listed on their own, so a forgotten one is easy to spot.

**Limitations:** It's a view only: requests are still set in each chest's window.

versions.title: Power network names
versions.notes:
- Each power network now has a name and a colour. A pole's window has a box for the name and eight colours to pick from; new networks start as Grid A, Grid B and so on.
- The full power view shows every network side by side in its colour, with what it makes, what it wants and how much of that it gets. Click one to chart it.
- The low power alert says which network is short: "Low power on North Grid".
- The map's power view draws each network's wires in its colour.

**Limitations:** When two networks join, the lower-numbered pole's name wins; if they split again, both halves keep a name.

versions.title: Hotbar pages
versions.notes:
- The hotbar now shows up to three rows at once, like Factorio's quickbars. Settings has "Hotbar rows" (1, 2 or 3).
- Each row shows one of the ten hotbar pages. The small number at a row's left picks its page; the mouse wheel over a row turns it. If another row shows that page, the two rows trade.
- The number keys use the top row, and Shift + a number still sets the top row's page.
- Click an empty slot with a building or item in hand to put it on the bar. Dragging between rows works too.

**Limitations:** Rows are saved per player, not per world. Touch screens start with one row.

versions.title: Delta autosaves: measured
versions.notes:
- No change to play: this release adds a benchmark for testing (tests/bench_delta.gd) and the numbers behind it.
- Result: saving only what changed since the last full save isn't worth it. In a big factory almost every building changes within a minute (belts move, beds grow), so the changes are still 44 to 46% of a whole save. Packing saves small, as the save handoff already does, would shrink them far more.

**Limitations:** Autosaves are unchanged.

versions.title: Seed of the week
versions.notes:
- New World has a Seed of the week button: the same seed and twist for everyone this real week, from a table in the game (no server).
- Reach Valley in Bloom on it and your best day is kept. Copy my code gives a code to send friends; paste theirs to see everyone's days side by side.
- The New World screen scrolls now, so every option fits on a smaller screen.

**Limitations:** Week codes compare days you tell each other; nothing checks them. The table repeats its twists each year with new seeds.

versions.title: Fixer-upper start
versions.notes:
- A new-world option, Fixer-upper start: the valley begins beside a half-broken farm a previous owner left, with a note on the door.
- Five things to put right: a belt laid backwards, a furnace with ore and no fuel, an electric oven with no power, a ditch that stops short of the water, and a crate of odds and ends.
- The first-day checklist becomes a fix-it list and ticks off each repair. You start with fewer belts, beds and crates, since the old farm has some.

**Limitations:** The old farm is always laid just east of the start, whatever the map has there.

versions.title: Remove in a box
versions.notes:
- The removal planner (K) has a strip of filters while it's in hand: Everything, Belts, Ghosts, or One kind (the kind of building you start the drag on).
- Marks your drones can't reach no longer wait forever: walk past one and your farmer takes it down. The planner says how many are out of reach.
- Farmhands take marked buildings in their square back to their post, with whatever they held.

**Limitations:** Walking past takes buildings, not marked rocks or rubble (salvage those as before).

versions.title: Family recipes and the schoolhouse
versions.notes:
- A family that stays perfectly happy for three mornings shares a family recipe, like Grandma Baker's Apple Pie with honey. That dish sells for 30% more at the Diner and scores 30% higher at the fair. Each family shares one.
- Once five families live in the village, they send a schoolhouse to the farmhouse mailbox.
- With the schoolhouse up, new families write sooner, two a morning can build their own cottage in a village zone, and on the first morning of each season the children plant up to 6 saplings along the paths and roads near it.

**Limitations:** There are six family recipes, so the seventh happy family has none left to share. Planting day needs free ground beside a road or stone path within 12 tiles of the schoolhouse.

versions.title: Sim on a worker thread: investigation
versions.notes:
- No change to play: this release adds a benchmark for testing (tests/bench_thread.gd) and the findings of the worker-thread investigation.
- Result: ticking the farm on a second thread isn't worth it. A big factory's tick is about 7 ms, and handing its state back to the screen every frame would cost more than half of that; the web build would also need special page headers that the game's hosts can't send.

**Limitations:** Nothing changes in game; the threaded build won't be made (chunk 260 is skipped).

versions.title: Fly-over
versions.notes:
- Press F7 (or Esc menu, Fly-over) for a slow camera tour: from the farmhouse along the river you've explored, over every region you've restored, and home again, with the HUD hidden.
- Shift+F7 does the same and saves it as a GIF clip when it finishes, for showing a friend.
- Any key stops it.

**Limitations:** The clip is 60 frames at 480 pixels wide. Unexplored river is skipped, so a brand-new valley's fly-over is short.

versions.title: Visitors
versions.notes:
- Show your valley to a friend without handing them the keys: on the title screen, type the room code and press Visit to join as a hiker.
- Hikers walk the paths, follow a farmer, take photos (F2), chat, wave and point; anything else they try is politely refused, and the host refuses it too.
- The farmhouse window has a guestbook: anyone can sign it, hikers included. It keeps the last 30 notes with the day and the name.

**Limitations:** A hiker has no build tools at all (the hotbar hides), so they can't pick up anything either. The guestbook keeps 30 notes.

versions.title: Save handoff between devices
versions.notes:
- Load Game has a Send button on each save: it goes to the game's server and you get a 6-character code (copied for you).
- On the other device, open Load Game and type the code under From another device: the save joins your list, ready to load.
- Saves are packed small first, so even a big factory sends quickly. Codes last a day.

**Limitations:** The server keeps codes in its memory, so if it restarts (the free server sleeps when nobody's playing) they're gone; export the save too if it matters. The live server needs an update before Send works there.

versions.title: Join by QR code
versions.notes:
- The co-op box has a Show QR code button: the invite link as a QR code, so a phone or tablet joins by pointing its camera at the screen instead of typing the room code.
- On the title screen, the QR button next to Join Co-op shows this page as a QR code (with the room, if you typed a code), to open the game on another device.
- The QR codes are made in the game itself; nothing is sent anywhere to draw them.

**Limitations:** Links longer than 106 characters can't fit the small codes the game makes; the copy button still works for those.

versions.title: Map bookmarks and target lines
versions.notes:
- Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 saves the spot you're looking at as a bookmark for this world. Alt+1 to Alt+9 opens the map there, and the map shows your bookmarks as pins.
- The Production window has a Target column: set a goal in items a minute, and the item's chart draws it as a dashed line.
- Each morning a quiet line names the items that fell short of their target yesterday. Targets are shared in co-op and saved with the world.

**Limitations:** Bookmarks are kept on this device, per world, and open the map rather than moving your farmer. They're numbered, not named.

versions.title: Village requests
versions.notes:
- With two or more cottages, every few days a family asks for something built near their home: a bench by the water, a lamp by the road, a bridge over the water, a flower border by the door, or a path to the door.
- Build it and the next morning they thank you: happier, and $40 to $80.
- Requests last 10 days and lapse with no penalty. At most two at a time, and only things that make sense where they live.
- Requests show on the cottage's hover and window and on the farmhouse's orders board.

versions.title: The village grows where you say
versions.notes:
- A Signpost can mark a village zone: tick "Village zone" in its window (up to 6 zones, up to 15 tiles each way). The map outlines your zones.
- When a family's cottage is waiting in the mailbox, they build it themselves the next morning, on green land in a zone, beside a road or stone path, and a tile clear of other cottages.
- No zone, or no good spot yet: the cottage waits in the mailbox as before, and you can still place it yourself. Families never build outside a zone.

**Limitations:** A zone signpost doesn't claim a co-op plot.

versions.title: Weather Station and weather vanes
versions.notes:
- New Weather Station (research after Lightning Rods, $300): with one built, the forecast reaches two weeks. Days 8 to 14 flag hail, frost, heatwaves, storms and spring floods, and otherwise give the chance of rain in words.
- Each morning the station names any event that has just come into sight: "Plan around: hail on day 23".
- Built in the dry hills, it also tells you how hard tomorrow's wind will turn the turbines.
- A weather vane on the farmhouse roof turns to face the day's wind, and grass and crops lean downwind. Chimney smoke already drifted with it.

**Limitations:** One station is enough; more add nothing.

versions.title: Succession
versions.notes:
- Green land you leave alone grows wild: each 4x4 patch that stays mostly green with nothing built on it climbs a stage every season, from wildflowers to shrubs, pioneer trees and old growth. You'll see it in the world.
- Wildflowers count for biodiversity, shrubs bring the birds as a new biodiversity kind, pioneer trees soak smog like a grown tree, and old growth soaks half again as much. A lodge near old growth earns the wild-land price from hikers.
- Building or removing anything on a patch starts it over, and so does letting it lose its green. Nothing stops you building. Hover a tile to see its stage.
- Worlds without seasons climb a stage a week.

**Limitations:** Trees you planted yourself keep a patch from counting (they're buildings).

versions.title: Domesticate wild plants
versions.notes:
- Wild garlic, wild bilberries and wild rice now sprout on very green land (wild rice only beside water or marsh), up to 12 at a time. Forage them by hand like wild herbs.
- Set a Seed Lab to Domesticate one of them: 8 foraged plants become 6 seeds over 3 powered days. From then on it grows in beds, and you can make its seeds by hand.
- New dishes: Garlic Bread (bread and garlic at the Prep Table), Bilberry Tart (dough and bilberries, oven) and Wild Rice Pilaf (wild rice and garlic, oven).

**Limitations:** You can't buy their seeds. They come only from the Seed Lab and then from your own harvests.

versions.title: Shredder
versions.notes:
- New Shredder (research after the Assembler, $250): a powered 2x2 machine that turns what a line got wrong back into something useful, 2 seconds an item.
- Food and dishes become Fertilizer (4 for 1, like the Composter), parts, tools and drones become Scrap, and cloth, yarn, paper, straw and feathers become Fibre.
- 2 Fibre make a sheet of Paper by hand or at the Assembler.
- Raw materials, fuel, soil, spoiled food and buildings are refused. Feed it by hand or inserter; inserters take what it made.

**Limitations:** There's no compost item, so food shreds into Fertilizer.

versions.title: Clocks and counters
versions.notes:
- Inserters, belts and sluice gates can follow the day instead of a chest: a Clock (run between two hours, even past midnight), a Season, a Pulse (on for some seconds of every period) and, on inserters, a Counter that lets a set number of items through and then stops until you press Reset.
- Pick one from the building's window under "Or follow the day"; the window says in words when it runs and shows whether it's running now.
- Copy-paste and blueprints carry these conditions (a pasted counter starts from zero).

**Limitations:** Display Signs still only count a chest, machine or belt. Counters are for inserters only.

versions.title: Brownouts you control
versions.notes:
- Fair warning first: the Brownouts card shows the first time a power network wants 85% or more of what it can make (or is already short), before anything has slowed. That day, a short network still slows everything the same.
- From the next day you choose who slows first: a power pole's window lists five groups (ovens and furnaces; machines and drills; inserters and drones; Farm Towers, greenhouses and scrubbers; lamps and iceboxes) with Up and Down buttons, and each group's share while the network is short. The top group gives up its power first; by default ovens slow first and lamps last.

**Limitations:** Groups, not single buildings. Burner machines run on their own fuel and aren't in any group. Worlds with free power never brown out.

versions.title: Machine modules
versions.notes:
- New research, Machine Modules ($450, after the Assembler): two module slots on every powered machine. A Speed Gear (2 gears + a copper plate) makes it 25% faster for 50% more power; a Smog Filter (2 glass + a copper plate) cuts its smog by 40%; a Thrift Plate (2 copper plates, glass and a gear) gives each craft a 12% chance to keep its ingredients.
- Open a powered machine and click a slot to fit the next module you carry, or to take it out. Two of a kind stack. The hover lists a machine's modules, and taking the machine down (or upgrading it in place) keeps them.
- The same lines keep paying off without a rebuild: fit gears where a line is short, filters where the smog piles up.

**Limitations:** Blueprints and copy-paste don't copy modules (they're items you carry). Burner machines, and machines without power like the Mill, take none.

versions.title: Loading progress
versions.notes:
- Loading a save shows a card with a progress bar and what it's doing (reading the save, building the world, drawing the view) instead of a frozen screen.
- Joining a friend's game shows the same card while the world arrives, part by part.

**Limitations:** The bar moves in three steps, between the stages: each stage still runs in one go (the web build has one thread).

versions.title: Vault clock
versions.notes:
- A run timer from day one to the Seed Vault opening: the vault's window and the Scrapbook tab show "Vault clock: day N, H:MM since you arrived" until it opens, then the day and play time it opened.
- Your fastest Seed Vault is kept for each challenge (and for no twist) as a record to beat on the next valley: the challenge note on the new-world screen shows it, and a new record gets a toast.
- The year's scrapbook page says when the vault opened.

**Limitations:** The clock counts in-game days and play time (paused time and sleeping don't add play time). Old saves whose vault is already open have no time recorded.

versions.title: Meteor showers and constellations
versions.notes:
- Once a year, on an autumn night, a meteor shower crosses clean skies: it's in the forecast as "Meteor shower (night)", and streaks cross the screen that night while the sky over you is clear.
- Each season has two constellations (the Plough and the Heron in spring, the Scythe and the Swan in summer, the Harvest Cart and the Fox in autumn, the Lantern and the Stag in winter), drawn a little brighter with faint lines between their stars.
- A new Collection page, The night sky: after a clean day (your valley soaked up more smog than it made) with no rain or snow that night, the morning report says what you saw, and the season's constellations, the Milky Way (after a zero-smog day) and the meteor shower go in the book.

**Limitations:** Sightings come from the day's smog numbers and the weather, the same for every co-op player, not from where your camera was. Worlds without seasons have a 28-day year and a new pair of constellations each week.

versions.title: The night sky
versions.notes:
- The sky clears: at night faint stars show over the valley, thinner and dimmer the more smog hangs over the land in view; the night after a zero-smog day, the Milky Way crosses the screen. Stars twinkle in the lakes and ponds you can see.
- By day, smog over the land in view tints the screen edges brown, and the haze fades as the valley clears.
- Settings: a Night sky checkbox beside Graphics (on by default; photo mode keeps it).

**Limitations:** The sky is drawn over the top-down view, not a 3D sky: it shows above the land, buildings and water. It doesn't follow the camera's turn.

versions.title: Lane control on inserters
versions.notes:
- An inserter's window has a "Drops onto" row: Far lane (the usual), Near lane, or Emptier lane (whichever lane has room and fewer items). A mixed belt no longer needs a side-loading trick: two inserters on the same side can fill both lanes.
- The lane choice shows in the inserter's hover and is carried by blueprints, copy-paste of settings and upgrades.

**Limitations:** Inserters that drop along a belt's length (from behind it) use the right lane for Far and the left for Near.

versions.title: Upgrade in place
versions.notes:
- Inserters upgrade in place like furnaces and assemblers: click a Burner Inserter with an Inserter in hand, an Inserter with a Fast Inserter, or a Fast Inserter with a Bulk Inserter, and it swaps on the spot. The upgrade planner (U) marks inserters too.
- An upgrade now keeps every setting, not just the recipe and contents: filters, conditions, chest limits, requests and splitter settings come across, and nearby ghosts and marks are left alone.
- Upgrade a whole area: hold Shift and drag from an old building with its upgrade in hand. Everything in the box that it upgrades is swapped right away, as many as you hold.

**Limitations:** The box only swaps buildings of the same size (the Long Inserter isn't an upgrade of anything, since its reach differs).

versions.title: Catering orders and the food critic
versions.notes:
- Catering: every 14 days a big one-off order lands on the farmhouse board for an occasion (a wedding, the harvest dance...): two dishes you can make, 40 of one and 60 of the other, due in 3 days at double the going rate. It sits on top of the usual three orders, and missing it costs no reputation.
- The food critic: once you own a Diner a visit is set a couple of weeks out and announced 7 days ahead (news, and the Diner's hover). On the day they score what your Diners have on the menu: variety (4 dishes for full marks), quality and freshness, 0 to 3 stars. Diner customers pay 15% more a star for a week, and the review is pinned on the Journal tab of the collection book. They come back about three weeks later.

**Limitations:** The critic scores every Diner together, not one at a time. Catering wants dishes only (no crops), and only ones you can already make.

versions.title: Wetlands
versions.notes:
- Wetlands: a bare clay tile beside a full ditch that wakes wet three mornings running turns to marsh. Marsh is always green, grows reeds you cut by hand (hold right-click: 2 reeds, back the next day; 4 reeds make a Reed Bed), and its frogs keep moles off beds within 6 tiles, like an Owl Box. Reed Beds stand on marsh as on a shore. Nothing else goes on it but ditches; with the Shovel, hold right-click on a cut marsh tile to drain it back to clay.
- Fair warning: the Wetlands card shows the morning a tile by your ditch is on its second wet morning, and no tile turns before the next day. Marsh shows dark and wet on the ground and the map (teal in the soil view), and the hover says how many wet mornings a clay tile has had.

**Limitations:** Reeds have no model yet: the hover says when they're ready. A ditch beside a drained tile wets it again from the next morning.

versions.title: Heatwaves and the water tower
versions.notes:
- Heatwaves (worlds with weather events): some summer days come in a three-day heatwave, shown in the week's forecast and announced the evening before. In a heatwave a bed that is neither watered (sprinkler, full ditch, mulch or your can) nor shaded (a solar frame, or the row north of a grown tree, hedge or big building) stops growing until the heat breaks; nothing dies. The Heatwaves card shows the first summer morning you own beds, and only a later heatwave bites. Wilting beds say so in their hover.
- Water Tower (research, $250, after the Sprinkler; 10 iron plates, 12 planks, 4 pipes): a 2×2 tower beside a pipe fills from the line (500 water) and feeds every Sprinkler within 12 tiles that no pipe reaches, so a far garden needs no pipework. Its hover shows the water and how many sprinklers it serves.

**Limitations:** A sprinkler on a pipe never draws from a tower. Several towers in reach are drawn from lowest id first. Greenhouses don't mind the heat.

versions.title: Pasta
versions.notes:
- Pasta Press (research, $220, after the Chicken Coop; 8 iron plates, 4 gears, 6 planks): a 2×2 machine on 30 kW that rolls 2 flour and an egg into 2 pasta ($8), so the Mill and the coop feed one line.
- Lasagne ($55): 2 pasta, tomato sauce and cheese in the Oven. Noodle Soup ($18, two a batch): 2 pasta, mushrooms and an egg at the Prep Table; it counts as a soup for packed lunches (faster crafting). Both are dishes for the Diner, the Kitchen and the fair.

**Limitations:** Pasta is a dish for freshness (it goes stale in 40 minutes), not a keeping good like flour.

versions.title: Ice house and aging racks
versions.notes:
- Ice House (research, $250, after the Icebox; 24 stone, 12 planks, 8 straw): a 2×2 store of 20 stacks that needs no power. While it holds a block of ice nothing in it spoils; it melts one block every 10 minutes (twice as fast beside a working furnace, oven or kiln). Cut ice from frozen ponds in winter and the summer's food keeps.
- Aging Rack (research, $200, after the Root Cellar; 8 planks, 4 stone): shelves that take cheese and cider in lots of up to 20 (4 lots a rack). After 3 days a lot can be taken down as Aged Cheese ($30) or Vintage Cider ($55), Fine; left 7 days it comes down by itself as Excellent. Its window shows each lot's day and a button to take it down; a click switches the rack to take lots down at 3 days instead. Aged goods keep like smoked food and sell for half again as much in winter.

**Limitations:** Aged goods share one quality level per item (like dishes): a lot taken down pulls it three quarters of the way to its grade, so one early Fine lot after Excellent ones dents the level. A rack holds 2 stacks of aged goods; when they're full, lots wait on the shelves until something takes them.

versions.title: Farmhouse board and mail
versions.notes:
- A shared to-do board in the farmhouse: anyone adds a job ("build the bread line", "200 wood"), friends claim it, tick it done or take it down; up to 20 jobs, saved with the world.
- Gifts and mail: from the farmhouse mailbox, send a friend an item or dish from your backpack with a short note. It waits in the world's mail for their player and is theirs from the next morning, whenever they next open the farmhouse, in any session of this world.

**Limitations:** Buildings can't be mailed. A player's mailbox holds 20 parcels; the sender gets nothing back if it's full (the Send is refused).

versions.title: Specialties
versions.notes:
- Specialties: in the farmhouse each player picks grower, cook or engineer, and can change once a season. Grower: beds you place grow 5% faster. Cook: you cook 10% faster by hand. Engineer: machines you place run 5% faster.
- A weekly goal per specialty, counted from your own actions: 60 skill XP in that line of work (hand farming, hand cooking, building and crafting parts) by the end of the week pays $150 into the shared purse. The farmhouse shows everyone's pick and progress.

**Limitations:** The bonuses apply to things placed after v0.1.218 (beds and machines remember who placed them from then). The goal resets every 7 days whether or not it was met.

versions.title: Names on the map
versions.notes:
- Alt-drag a box on the valley map to name an area and pick a colour (gold, sky, rose, leaf, plum, slate): the map paints the box faintly in that colour with its name, and a faint sign floats over its middle in the world. Alt-right-click a named area to remove it. Up to 40 areas, shared in co-op and saved.
- Cart Stations, Barge Docks and Drone Pads take a name and colour of their own in their window: the map marks them with a coloured dot and the name, and schedules and hovers say the name instead of "Station at 12, 40".

**Limitations:** Names are 24 letters at most. Area labels don't move with a blueprint.

versions.title: Find on map and map blueprint capture
versions.notes:
- Find on map: a search box on the valley map (Ctrl+F with the map open). Type a building or item name and every building with that name, or holding that item (a chest, machine, coop or cottage pantry), lights up yellow; the box says how many.
- Map blueprint capture: Shift-drag a box on the map and the buildings inside become a blueprint in hand, as if you'd pressed C there, without walking over. Explored land only, up to 64 tiles a side.

**Limitations:** The search matches names, not recipes (type the dish's name to find the ovens holding it). A box with unexplored tiles in it captures nothing.

versions.title: Pastures
versions.notes:
- Fence (2 planks make 2): drag to build a line, like walls. Bugs don't care about it.
- Pastures: fence in green land touching a Chicken Coop, Dairy Barn or Fish Pond (hedges, walls, water and other buildings close the pen too; 12 or more green tiles inside, 200 tiles at most) and the animals graze. A barn or pond needs half the feed a batch (a pond beside a Greenhouse already has that; it doesn't stack), a coop lays two eggs a batch, and the building's hover says how big and how green the pen is.
- Hens and cows wander their pasture by day and night, ambling from tile to tile.

**Limitations:** The pen must be closed: one gap and the animals stay in. A pen bigger than 200 tiles isn't a pasture. Fish stay in their pond.

versions.title: Villagers with trades and picnics
versions.notes:
- Tradespeople: a village of 3 or more cottages that stays 70% happy for 3 mornings running draws a baker, then a smith, then a carpenter. Each makes their kind of hand crafting (food; anything with metal plates or gears in it; anything made of wood or planks) 50% faster, for good. The cottage window says who has come.
- Picnics: on a dry weekend morning (days 5 and 6 of each week, no rain or snow) the villagers picnic at the prettiest decorated block within 24 tiles of the village. Every cottage is 5% happier that morning, the morning report names the spot, and a blanket with three villagers sits there by day.

**Limitations:** Trades don't leave when the village sours. A picnic needs a block with some decoration (a bench, flowers, a path); flowers and fruit trees alone don't draw one.

versions.title: Paper and packaging
versions.notes:
- The Mill leaves a straw behind for every flour it grinds, piled at its side like sawdust from planks (an inserter filtered to straw, or you, takes it). 4 straw make 2 paper by hand or in an Assembler.
- Packing Table (research, $150): a small table that holds only paper. Touching a Contract Crate, it boxes what the town collects from that crate, and the town pays 1.35× the goods' value instead of 1.15×. Within 6 tiles of the farmhouse, it boxes what you sell the travelling merchant, who pays 1.25×.
- One paper boxes 10 items; without enough paper the goods go out loose as before. The crate's hover says when its goods are boxed and what the town pays.

**Limitations:** Cornmeal and olive oil leave no straw. Boxing counts whole paper per collection (3 items still cost one paper).

versions.title: Charcoal kiln and salt pans
versions.notes:
- Charcoal Kiln (research, after the Shovel): an unpowered 2×2 mound that smoulders 4 wood into 2 charcoal with little smog. Charcoal burns long and far cleaner than coal in furnaces, ovens and the Smokehouse: a greener step before going electric.
- Salt pans (research, after the Fish Trap): a Salt Pan on a lake or river shore dries salt in the sun, by day when it isn't raining, with no power or fuel.
- Salted Fish (fish and salt at the Prep Table) and Pickles (cabbage and salt in the Fermenting Crock) keep like smoked food and sell for more in winter: a slower, smokeless way to preserve.

**Limitations:** No ham: there are no pigs in the valley. A Salt Pan makes one salt every 40 seconds of sun.

versions.title: Farmer skills and dish mastery
versions.notes:
- Farmer skills: four tracks per player, Green thumb (planting, watering and harvesting by hand), Cook (cooking by hand), Builder (placing buildings and crafting parts by hand) and Steward (planting trees, hedges, reeds and flowers, throwing seed bombs). Five levels each, shown on a Skills tab in the collection book (J), with small bonuses on what's yours: beds you place grow faster, your hand crafts go quicker, your trees and hedges green farther (2% a level).
- Dish mastery: a dish made 500 times, by machines or by hand, is Mastered: its machines run 10% faster, it sells 5% higher, and its recipe wears a gold badge in the crafting list. The Skills tab lists them.

**Limitations:** Dishes made before this version count only from where their made-count already stood (machine-made dishes were always counted; hand-made ones start now). Skills are per player key; a friend joining with a new key starts fresh.

versions.title: Hand tools
versions.notes:
- Hand tools: a Watering Can, a Hoe and a Scythe, each in wood, copper and iron (crafted from the inventory; each tier is made from the last). Wood works one tile, copper a row of three, iron a 3×3 patch.
- Hold a tool and click the ground: the can waters the beds there by hand for the day (thirsty crops grow at full speed, dry spells don't slow them), ten clicks a fill, refilled by clicking water, a ditch or a Rain Barrel. The hoe lays Garden Beds from your backpack over the patch in one click. The scythe reaps every ripe bed in the patch.
- The first hour of hand farming gets faster before towers and inserters take over.

**Limitations:** Tools work within 6 tiles of your farmer. A hand-watered bed counts as watered until the day ends, whatever the weather. The copper tools' row is always east-west.

versions.title: Emotes
versions.notes:
- Emotes: hold I for a wheel of four words (Hi!, Look!, Nice!, Come here!) and let go over one. It floats above your farmer for two seconds on every screen, so co-op friends can talk without typing. A quick tap on I still opens the inventory.

**Limitations:** Four fixed words; no custom ones. Emotes aren't shown on the map.

versions.title: Watched items and the almanac
versions.notes:
- Watched items: Alt-click an item in your inventory, or press Watch in its lookup window (middle-click any item), to pin it to the HUD. A Watching box shows how many you have across your backpack, chests and machines, and whether that's rising, falling or steady over the last minute. Up to 6; right-click one there to stop.
- The farmer's almanac: the morning report now opens with a tip about what's coming in the next three days: a storm, hail, a drought or a flood and what to do about it; a harvest festival or the fair; a season about to turn and what it means for the beds. On a quiet week it suggests the next thing you haven't tried.

**Limitations:** Watched counts don't include items on belts or in drones' hands. The watch list is yours (saved with your settings), not the world's.

versions.title: Farmhouse gramophone
versions.notes:
- Records: seven of them, one for each tune the valley plays (the day, the night and the three seasons) plus two new ones, Harvest Reel and Farmhouse Lullaby. Four turn up now and then when you clear a ruin or a wreck; the other three come with your first fair ribbon for a dish, a crop and a signature dish.
- Carry a record to the farmhouse and put it on the shelf (the farmhouse window has a Gramophone section once you own one), then put one on: it plays within 24 tiles of the house, fading with distance, over the season's music. Co-op friends near the house hear it too.

**Limitations:** Records found before the shelf exists stay in your backpack until you open the farmhouse. The gramophone has no sound of its own (no crackle); the record simply takes over the music near the house.

versions.title: Alert filters
versions.notes:
- Right-click an alert at the side of the screen to hide that kind, or to keep it to the region you're standing in (an Output full alert from the home farm only, say). A limited alert says its region on the icon.
- Settings has an Alert kinds screen: every kind with a Show box, and where one is limited to, with an Everywhere button to lift it. Under attack and Fire can't be hidden.
- Filters are yours (saved with your settings, not the world), so co-op friends each see their own.

**Limitations:** A region limit is by region (64×64), not by distance from you.

versions.title: Soil stays put
versions.notes:
- Soil stays put: a new-world option (on in Normal and Hard, off in Relaxed) where soil types stay where the map put them. The Shovel still bags a tile's soil for bricks, glass, filters and green roofs, but the tile keeps its kind, and bags can't be laid on the ground or under beds.
- So the farm fits the land: put each crop where its soil is (the soil view, G, shows every patch), and let fertilized harvests turn a bed's soil into its crop's favourite over three harvests, as before.
- Why: Josh's lever for a valley you work with rather than against, the land side of optimizing versus growing organically. An optimizer still wins by reading the soil view and laying fields out by patch; nothing is slower, only the land has a say.
- The farmhouse's World options section switches it in a running world; the Shovel's card in the shop says which kind of world this is. Older saves have it off until you switch it on.

**Limitations:** A valley code from before this version starts its world with soil staying put off. Digging a tile over and over bags the same soil every time (it did before too, as clay).

versions.title: Field studies
versions.notes:
- Field studies: in a new world (Normal and Hard), research past the first tier that costs $200 or more also needs a study before money or field notes can pay for it: 5 each of a crop, a made food and a part, picked for that research from chains its own prerequisites already let you make. The card in the shop says which three and how far along the study is.
- Click a Research Desk to put it on a study: samples that match count toward it as the desk studies them, and still earn field notes. The desk window shows each item's count and lets you put samples in from your backpack; a belt and inserter feed it like before.
- Why: a farm that grows one crop down one belt can't research its way forward any more; progress asks for a spread of crops, dishes and parts, the way Factorio's science packs do. An optimizer still wins: a sample line fed by belt gets through a study in minutes, and the money cost hasn't changed.
- New-world option Field studies (on in Normal and Hard, off in Relaxed), and a World options section in the farmhouse window where it, and Trees need room (smog planning), can be switched in a running world. Older saves have field studies off until you switch them on.

**Limitations:** A valley code from before this version starts its world with field studies off. Studies are picked for each research once, the same in every world; they don't change with the season or what you already grow.

versions.title: Soak view
versions.notes:
- A smog maker's hover now says what happens to its smog: how much is made around it each second, how much is soaked there (and by how many trees, scrubbers and reed beds, plus green land), and how much gets away.
- New map view, Soak: orange where the air is saturated (thick smog, and the plants there soak less than half of what's made round it), green where there's soak to spare. It shows where the next scrubber, reed bed or guild would do the most good.
- The zero-smog ledger now counts crowded trees and plant guilds the way the air does.

**Limitations:** The Soak view is worked out from the last smog step when the map is painted; it doesn't follow wind drift from far away.

versions.title: Plant guilds
versions.notes:
- Plant guilds: plants that grow together clean more air than any one kind alone. Where a grown tree, a grown hedge, flowers (wildflowers or a flower border) and something wet (a Reed Bed, a ditch or water) all grow within a few tiles of each other, they make a guild.
- Inside a guild, trees and Reed Beds soak half as much smog again, and grown hedges soak smog too (they don't anywhere else).
- Alt view tags each guild, and blocks that are one plant short say which one they need; the ground's hover says so too.

**Limitations:** Guilds are counted in 4×4 blocks (with the blocks round them), like biodiversity, so the edge of one is a little blocky.

versions.title: Canopy spacing
versions.notes:
- Trees need room: a grown tree soaks its full share of smog only with open ground round it. Each grown tree among the 8 tiles round it takes an eighth off, down to half when 4 or more crowd it.
- So a solid wall of trees soaks about half of what the same trees spaced out would. Cleaning the air now takes planning: space the trees, and mix in Air Scrubbers and Reed Beds.
- With a sapling in hand, its Site card says whether the spot is open (full soak), crowded or packed.
- Foresters have a new setting, Space the trees: they plant and cut every other tile, in a checkerboard. New Foresters start with it on.
- New-world option Trees need room (smog planning): on in Normal and Hard, off in Relaxed. Older worlds have it on.
- Fair warning first: a Trees need room card shows the first time two grown trees stand side by side, and crowding costs nothing until the next day.

**Limitations:** Hedges, beds and buildings don't crowd a tree, and crowding doesn't change how fast trees green the land. The option can't be changed in an existing world yet.

versions.title: Redesign with bots
versions.notes:
- No layout is final: a new lesson, Moving the farm (Tutorials, Automation), walks you through copying a cramped first line with C, marking the old one with K, and pasting it by the water with V while construction drones take it down and rebuild it.
- Chapter 5 (The river) has two new goals: mark 4 buildings for drones to take down, and paste a blueprint of 4 or more buildings. Saves already past chapter 5 aren't affected.
- Hazard cards you can build your way out of (wind and smog, dirty water, moles, shade, warmth, neighbours, root rot, wrecks) now end with a note on how to move things with drones, once you have them.
- Fixed: taking down a working inserter (or anything else that works without a recipe) by drone or by hand could stop with an error.

**Limitations:** The lesson's wreck doesn't leak smog in the practice world. Cards you've already seen don't show again with the new note.

versions.title: Neighbour lines and site survey
versions.notes:
- Neighbour lines: the Alt view draws a short green line for every bonus a spot gets from its neighbours and a red one for every cost: warm beds and scorched ones, shaded beds, a Fish Pond feeding a Greenhouse, a Village Depot's cottages, and each cottage's good and bad neighbours.
- Site card: with a bed, cottage, Diner, machine or heat maker in hand, a small card under the ghost says what that spot gives: soil, water, sun or shade, warmth or scorching, a cottage's neighbours, whether a Diner is on a corner.
- The Site card also says when a machine's output face touches a belt, machine or chest, so it hands what it makes straight over (that already worked; now you can see it before you place).

**Limitations:** The ghost shows the Site card as text, not lines (the lines are in the Alt view, for what's built). Hedge shelter, owl boxes and hives aren't drawn as lines (their hovers say what they cover). Hidden while Alt is held.

versions.title: Neighbours for the village
versions.notes:
- Neighbours: villagers care what's next door. Each cottage looks 3 tiles around it, and its hover lists what it sees.
- Flowers (borders or wildflower patches), a fountain, a bench or fruit trees cheer a cottage up; a dairy barn, chicken coop, smelter, furnace, biogas digester or a busy belt gets it down. Each kind is worth 5% happiness a morning, up to 15% either way.
- A Diner on a corner, with road touching it on two sides, serves 25% faster. Its hover says so.
- Fair warning first: a Neighbours card shows the first morning a cottage has a bad neighbour, and the bad ones only count from the morning after.

**Limitations:** Neighbours don't show as lines in the world yet (a later version adds them to the Alt view).

versions.title: Sun side
versions.notes:
- Sun side: the sun is in the south, so a grown tree, hedge or fruit tree, and any building 2 tiles or bigger, shades the row of tiles right north of it.
- A bed in shade grows 10% slower, but stays sheltered on dry days like a bed beside a hedge. A Greenhouse with any tile in shade runs 10% slower.
- Put the tall things on the north side of your fields: where things stand now matters to the beds beside them.
- Fair warning first: a Shade card shows the first time a bed or greenhouse stands in shade, and shade slows nothing until the next day. A bed's hover and the soil view (G) say which beds are shaded.

**Limitations:** Shade is one row deep and doesn't show as a shadow in the world (the soil view tags shaded beds). Solar panels aren't affected.

versions.title: Warmth
versions.notes:
- Warmth: a working burner, furnace, smelter, oven, kiln, smokehouse, boiler or roaster warms the tiles within 2 of it. Where you put the bakery now matters to the garden next door.
- A warm bed keeps growing in winter: 80% speed instead of 35%, so a winter garden beside the ovens pays its way.
- Too close is too hot: a bed right beside a Kiln, Stone Furnace or Smelter is scorched and grows at half speed (it never dies). Keep one tile between them.
- An unpowered Icebox in the warm melts its ice twice as fast, and spoils faster once its ice is gone.
- Fair warning first: a Warmth card shows the first time a bed stands in the warm or beside a kiln, furnace or smelter, and no bed is scorched before the next day. The ghost warns before you place a bed beside a scorcher (or a scorcher beside beds), and a bed's hover says whether it's warm or scorched.

**Limitations:** Heat doesn't show in the world or on the map yet (the Alt view's neighbour lines come in a later version). Greenhouses aren't warmed.

versions.title: Sister valleys
versions.notes:
- Sister valleys: once the Great Seed Vault opens, three neighbouring dry valleys write to you, and the farmhouse window gets a Sister valleys section.
- Send each valley one kit a day from your backpack: a seed kit (10 each of 3 different seeds), 10 saplings, or 10 of one dish (Fine or better counts more). Each kit greens that valley.
- A valley that's at least 30% green sends a parcel to your farmhouse mailbox each season (seeds from far biomes, and saplings once it's well along), with a letter.
- A valley in full bloom sends $1,000; all three in bloom earn a new hat, the Neighbour's hat.

**Limitations:** The sister valleys are a farmhouse-window section, not places you can visit. One kit a day per valley.

versions.title: Storm surges and lightning rods
versions.notes:
- Storm surges (worlds with weather events): on a storm day, lightning can trip power poles. Each pole with no Lightning Rod within 8 tiles may trip (about 1 in 7), at most a tenth of your poles a storm.
- A tripped pole drops out of its grid until you open it and press Reset. A "Poles tripped" alert shows where, and the storm's morning news says how many.
- Lightning Rod ($300 in the shop after iron poles; 4 copper and 2 iron plates): a copper spike that guards every pole within 8 tiles. A pole's window says whether it's guarded.
- Fair warning first: a Lightning card shows the first evening a storm is forecast while you own power poles, and no pole trips before that storm. The storm forecast mentions poles too.

**Limitations:** Power Switches and the poles' wires aren't hit. The map's power overlay doesn't mark tripped poles (the alert does).

versions.title: Root rot
versions.notes:
- Root rot (weather worlds): clay holds water. On the third rainy day in a row, beds on clay soil get waterlogged and grow at 60% until the first day without rain.
- Crops that love clay (rice, cranberries, cabbage, mint, tea, mushrooms) don't mind, a drainage ditch within 2 tiles keeps a bed dry, and a bed on clay can be raised (4 planks, a button in its window) so it always drains.
- Fair warning first: a Root rot card shows the first time you have a clay bed at risk with two rainy days running (or two ahead in the forecast), and no bed rots before the next day.
- The forecast flags root-rot days, the morning news says how many beds are waterlogged, and a bed's hover says whether it's at risk, rotting or raised.

**Limitations:** A raised bed looks the same as before (its hover and window say it's raised). Blueprints don't carry raised beds.

versions.title: Grain silo and root cellar
versions.notes:
- Grain Silo ($200; 20 stone, 10 planks, 4 iron plates): a 2×2 store for wheat, corn, rice, flour, cornmeal, sugar and every kind of seed, 40 stacks, filled and emptied like a crate (slot limits too).
- Root Cellar ($250 after the Composter; 24 stone, 6 planks, no power): a 2×2 grassy mound for potatoes, beets, cabbage, fruit, cheese and eggs, 20 stacks. In worlds where food spoils, food in it spoils at a quarter of the usual rate, so a big autumn harvest can feed the winter.
- Each only takes what belongs in it, so a belt into one is a tidy filter.

**Limitations:** Grain never spoiled, so the silo is room, not preserving. The cellar has a cap (20 stacks), and the market still pays less for a crop you've flooded it with.

versions.title: Fluid tanks and barrels
versions.notes:
- Tanks and barrels ($250 in the shop after the Offshore Pump): a Storage Tank (2×2, 8 iron plates, 4 pipes) beside a pipe line holds 2000 more of its water or crude oil, a buffer for boilers, refineries and sprinklers.
- Barrel Filler (2×2, 30 kW): beside a pipe line it fills empty Barrels (2 iron plates each) with 50 water or crude oil, or in Empty mode pours full barrels back into its line. Pick the mode and fluid in its window.
- Barrels are items, so inserters, belts, carts, barges and drones carry them: a far line with no pump or pumpjack of its own can run on barrels.
- Milk, juice and oil were already items on belts and stay that way.

**Limitations:** Blueprints don't carry a filler's mode. A line fed water and crude oil at once carries nothing, as before.

versions.title: Rewild a region
versions.notes:
- Rewild a region: click a restored region on the map (an empty spot) and choose Rewild it, once nothing but trees, hedges, reed beds and signposts stands there.
- A wild region can't be built on, but its wildlife comes back faster (twice the rabbits, deer and butterflies there), lodges in or beside it charge their hikers 50% more, and birds come twice as often and carry its seed to the land around it.
- After a season (10 days without seasons) you can open it to farming again from the same card.
- The map label says Wild, the region hover says wild, and the restore card mentions it the first time.

**Limitations:** Home Meadow can be rewilded too, but only once the farmhouse and everything else is gone from it, so in practice it's for outlying regions.

versions.title: Moles and owl boxes
versions.notes:
- Moles: lively soil (soil life 60 and up) draws them. A mole tunnels under a lively bed and slows it and the beds around it by 30% for 3 days; you'll see a molehill on the bed.
- Fair warning first: a Moles card shows the first time any bed's soil life reaches 50, and no mole can come until the next day.
- Owl Box (Farming, 6 planks): a nesting box on a pole that keeps moles off every bed within 6 tiles and sends any already there packing.
- A bed's hover says when moles are under it, or when its soil is lively enough to draw them and no owl box covers it; the owl box's hover counts the beds it guards. Help has a Moles entry.
- At most one mole per 9×9 patch and 12 in the valley.

**Limitations:** Moles only come to beds (not fruit trees or towers). The owl isn't drawn.

versions.title: Signature dish
versions.notes:
- Signature dishes: in the Test Kitchen's recipe book, give a dish you discovered there your own name (up to 24 letters, once per dish).
- Its name shows in the recipe book, the Diner and the fair, like "Hearth Pie (Apple Pie)", and the Diner's customers pay 10% more for it.
- The county fair gets a third category, Signature dish, for a dish you've named, judged against the rival farms with its own ribbon and prize.
- In co-op the news says whose signature dish it is, and the first name given sticks.

**Limitations:** Only dishes found in the Test Kitchen can be named, and a name can't be changed. The market and the Shipping Dock pay the usual price.

versions.title: Farm stand
versions.notes:
- Farm Stand (Home, 8 planks and 2 iron plates, no research): a 2×2 roadside stall for food and crops (6 stacks) where you set your own price for each item in its window (- and +, Shift for $5, or back to Market).
- Shoppers come by all day, one every 20 s: a family from each cottage, last night's hikers from your lodges and a couple of passers-by, half as many again when the stall is by a road or near the village or a lodge.
- Each shopper looks at up to three different things, best value first, and buys each with a chance that falls as your price rises: half the market price nearly always sells, the market price half the time, one and a half times the market never.
- So a varied stall sells more than a one-crop one, and it sells at most 40 things a day. The big market's prices aren't touched.
- Fix: the Village Depot now hands out after the day's craving is picked, so it can fill the craving too.

**Limitations:** Shoppers aren't drawn walking to the stall. Sales go to the stall's builder in own-backpack co-op.

versions.title: Mushroom cellar, finished
versions.notes:
- The Mushroom Cellar has a second recipe, Mushrooms (wood and sawdust): pick it and inserters can feed the cellar wood and the Sawmill's sawdust straight in, no Mushroom Logs to craft by hand. Same 6 mushrooms every 90 s, any season, any soil, no power.
- Mushroom Pie: 2 mushrooms, dough and an egg in the oven, worth $32. It comes with the Pine cooking recipes, the Diner serves it and the Test Kitchen can find it.
- So sawdust and fallen trees now have a food use beside mulch.

**Limitations:** The Mushroom Cellar itself isn't new (v0.1.113); this adds direct feeding and the pie.

versions.title: Per-cluster smog and greening
versions.notes:
- Huge worlds run smoother: the smog and greening updates now only look at the land around your buildings, plants and smog, not every tile in one big box around all of it.
- Far outposts strung across an endless world no longer make the game sweep the empty land between them: in the outposts benchmark, greening went from about 8.5 to 4.7 ms a pass and smog from about 10.5 to 8.3 ms.
- Nothing in the game changes: the land greens and the smog drifts exactly as before, tile for tile.

**Limitations:** A compact farm runs at the same speed as before; the gain is for outposts far apart.

versions.title: Seasons you can see
versions.notes:
- Seasons now show on the farm itself, not only in the HUD.
- Spring: apple, peach and cherry trees blossom (white, pale pink and pink), and other trees put out fresh light-green leaves.
- Autumn: leaves turn gold, orange and red (apples gold, peaches orange, cherries red), hedges go russet.
- Winter: trees stand bare and frosted, hedges and pines carry snow, and roofs, beds and rocks get a snow cap on top, alongside the snowy ground.
- Summer looks as it always did, and worlds without seasons don't change.

**Limitations:** The farm changes look when the season turns, not gradually. Ore patches and belts don't get snow.

versions.title: Village depot
versions.notes:
- Village Depot (Home, $250 in the shop; 10 planks and 4 iron plates): a 2×2 chest for the village's food, filled by belt, inserter or hand.
- Each morning, once the families have eaten, it hands every cottage within 10 tiles what its basket wants, plus today's craving and any home comfort the family hasn't had yet.
- When it runs short it shares: one item to each cottage in turn. A cottage two depots reach is served by the older one first.
- Its window and hover say how many cottages it serves and what it's short for tomorrow, and from evening a "Depot short" alert shows when it can't cover the next morning's baskets.
- Build it in the middle of the village: feeding the families becomes one line you build once.

**Limitations:** It only serves cottages within 10 tiles of it, so a spread-out village needs more than one. It doesn't take raw crops.

versions.title: Aquaponics
versions.notes:
- Aquaponics: put a Fish Pond right beside a working Greenhouse (their sides touching) and they help each other.
- The fish waste waters and feeds the beds, so the Greenhouse runs 25% faster while the pond beside it has fish or feed.
- The beds clean the pond's water, so the pond needs half the feed a batch (1 grain instead of 2).
- Hover either one to see whether it's paired; the Greenhouse and Fish Pond descriptions, tips and the Help page say how.

**Limitations:** Only one pond counts per greenhouse (more ponds don't stack), and a corner touch or a tile's gap doesn't pair them.

versions.title: Blueprint swaps
versions.notes:
- Blueprint swaps: with a blueprint in hand, press Tab to swap what's in it, like a parametrised blueprint.
- Each recipe can become another the same machines make (bread to cake), each tower crop any other crop (wheat to rice), and each item in filters, requests, splitters, tower rules and signs another item of the same kind (iron ore to copper ore).
- Pick the swaps, press Swap, and paste the changed copy as usual: one smelting column blueprint now serves every ore.
- The blueprint tooltip mentions Tab.

**Limitations:** The swap changes the blueprint in your hand, not the one saved for V. Items only swap within their own kind (ores for ores, food for food).

versions.title: Region perks you pick
versions.notes:
- Each restored region now offers a choice of two perks, for that region only and for good: Orchard country (fruit trees bear half as much again), Calm land (tame nests bloom twice as fast), Rich waters (Fish Traps catch half as many again), Bee country (hives make honey half as fast again), Deep soil (beds grow 15% faster) or Herb meadows (wild herbs twice as often).
- Pick one on the region's restore card, or later by clicking the region on the map. In co-op the first pick counts.
- The region's hover and its map label show the perk, or the two still on offer.
- Regions you restored before this version get their offer too.

**Limitations:** Rich waters only shows up for regions with water, and Calm land only in combat worlds. Perks can't be changed once picked.

versions.title: The Blight moves on
versions.notes:
- Blight nests don't like green land. When 6 in 10 land tiles around a wild nest (a 25-tile square) are green, it gets restless: it stops attacking, and 3 days later it leaves.
- It heads for the nearest smog wreck at least 40 tiles from your buildings and settles beside it, or leaves the valley if there's no such wreck.
- A nest's hover shows how green its land is and when it leaves; the forecast shows the day it goes, and the map draws a dashed path to where it's heading.
- A card explains it once any nest's land is 4 in 10 green, before anything moves, and warns that a far wreck near a future outpost could end up with a nest beside it.

**Limitations:** Combat worlds only. Tame and Bloom Nests stay put (taming a restless nest calls off its move). The land is checked once a minute.

versions.title: Packed lunch
versions.notes:
- Packed lunch: put a dish on the hotbar and right-click it to eat one for a boost. Shift-right-click now empties a dish's slot.
- Oven-baked dishes (bread, cake, pizza...) make you salvage 1.5× faster; fruit dishes (apple pie, tarts, jam, juice...) walk 1.25× faster; soups and stews craft 1.5× faster; anything else, walk a little faster.
- A boost lasts 2 minutes, 3 for Fine dishes and 4 for Excellent ones. One at a time: a new lunch replaces the last.
- A badge under the clock shows the boost and the time left, and the hotbar tooltip says what each dish would give.

**Limitations:** Ingredients (flour, dough, sauce, sugar...) can't be eaten. Time asleep counts, so a lunch is gone by morning. Walking and salvaging boosts are your own; in co-op with a shared backpack the craft queue takes the best craft boost anyone has.

versions.title: Bee swarms
versions.notes:
- Once each spring, on a day of their own, a busy hive (6 or more flowers around it and 10 honey in it) swarms. It's a friendly event: the hive it leaves keeps going.
- If an empty hive (one that hasn't made any honey yet) stands within 12 tiles, the swarm moves in and you get a full colony with 10 honey for free.
- Otherwise it settles in the nearest grown tree within 20 tiles as a wild colony: a golden comb in the branches that pollinates beds within 3 tiles, as long as the tree stands (up to 10 wild colonies).
- Wild bees join the Wildlife page. A card explains swarms the first spring you own a hive, and hive and tree hovers say what's going on.

**Limitations:** A hive swarms at most once a year. Without seasons a swarm day comes every 16 days. Wild colonies don't make honey you can collect.

versions.title: Solar over beds
versions.notes:
- New: the Solar Frame (1 Solar Panel and 4 planks, comes with Solar research). Put it up over a Garden Bed from the bed's window, or hold one and click the bed.
- A frame makes 80% of a Solar Panel's power when a power pole reaches the bed, and the bed keeps growing underneath.
- Its shade helps on dry days: a thirsty bed under a frame grows at 3/4 speed instead of half, like a bed sheltered by a hedge (the two don't add up).
- Taking the bed up gives the frame back. The bed's hover and the power network's window count frames.

**Limitations:** Hail doesn't crack frames. Blueprints copy the bed but not its frame. A watered bed gets the power but doesn't need the shade.

versions.title: Dirty water
versions.notes:
- Smog over a lake now dirties the water drawn from it. When the smog over a pump's water (or a ditch's lake) passes 10, the beds that water reaches grow slower, up to 30% slower in thick smog. Clean water from anywhere else (another sprinkler, a rain barrel) wins.
- A card explains it as soon as the smog over water you use reaches 5, before anything slows.
- New: the Sand Filter (2 glass, 4 sandy soil, 2 pipes). Build it into a pipe line like a pipe and it cleans the water for everything on that line. Reed Beds on the shore still clean the lake itself.
- A pump's hover shows how clean its water is, beds watered with dirty water say how much slower they are, and an alert marks pumps drawing dirty water.

**Limitations:** Ditches can't be filtered; clean their lake instead. Only pumps and ditches are affected: rain barrels and rain are always clean.

versions.title: Fertigation
versions.notes:
- New: the Mixing Tank (research, $300, after Sprinklers). Put it on a water line, touching the pipes, and fill it with Fertilizer or Manure (20 at most, by hand or inserter).
- Every Sprinkler on that line then fertilizes the beds it waters as well: they grow at full speed whatever the soil, without using up the beds' own fertilizer.
- The tank uses one feed for every 200 water its sprinklers spray. Its window and hover say how many sprinklers it's feeding; sprinkler and bed hovers say when they're fertigated.

**Limitations:** Ditches don't carry it, only pipes. One fed tank is enough for a whole line; with more than one, the first with feed supplies it and the others wait their turn.

versions.title: Green roofs
versions.notes:
- Green roofs: open any machine 2×2 or bigger and add a green roof for a sapling and a bag of soil. A sod roof grows on top over 2 days.
- A grown roof soaks smog (more on bigger buildings) and greens the land under the building, which counts toward the greening bonus, regions and the valley's climate.
- Hovering a roofed building shows how its roof is coming along.

**Limitations:** Not on the farmhouse, cottages, the Seed Vault, greenhouses, solar panels, the museum or the lodge. The roof is lost if the building is taken down, and blueprints don't copy it.

versions.title: Wind carries smog, smog preview
versions.notes:
- In worlds with weather, each day the wind blows one way (about one day in five is calm). Smog drifts faster downwind and slower upwind, so it piles up on the downwind side of a burner or furnace. No smog is added or lost, it only moves.
- The forecast and the top-left status say the wind in words, for example "a breeze from the west". Chimney smoke leans with it.
- A card explains wind the first time you hold or own a building that makes smog, before any of your smog has drifted.
- Smog preview: hold a smog maker and a red square shows where its smog will mostly settle today, leaning downwind, with red marks on the beds, trees and green land inside. The tooltip counts them.

**Limitations:** The preview square is a guide (8 tiles round the building, shifted up to 5 tiles downwind), not an exact smog map; the Smog map layer shows the real thing. Worlds without weather have no wind.

versions.title: Ripe timers and belt lanes in the hover
versions.notes:
- Alt view shows "1:20" over growing beds (time until ripe at today's speed), "ripe" over ripe ones, and "fruit in 6 h" over grown fruit trees.
- Hovering a bed says when it'll be ripe; a fruit tree says when it bears next; a Farm Tower says when its next harvest is due.
- Hovering a belt shows each lane: how full it is, what's on it, and whether it's moving or backed up (and for how long).
- Alt view marks belts in red ("stuck") when a lane hasn't moved for 30 seconds, so the jam in a long line is easy to find.

**Limitations:** Ripe times assume today's weather, soil and smog stay the same. Belt rates per minute still need a wired condition (as before).

versions.title: Camp tent
versions.notes:
- New: the Camp Tent (8 planks, no research), a 2×2 tent you can put up anywhere. Sleep in it with Z or its Sleep here button, so long trips no longer end with a walk home at dusk.
- It has a 4-stack chest for your things (inserters can use it too).
- One tent each: put up another and the old one comes down, with its things moved into the new one and the tent back in your backpack. In co-op you can only sleep in your own.

**Limitations:** Bugs can bite a tent like any building. If the blight knocks you out you still wake at the farmhouse.

versions.title: Plan before you can afford it
versions.notes:
- Hold Shift while placing (click or drag) to lay down a ghost of the building in your hand, even if you don't have one yet. Anything you've unlocked can be planned; drag a line of belts or a row of beds the same way.
- A "Still to build" list (top right, under pinned recipes) adds up the planned buildings you're short of and what's missing to craft them. Its Craft button crafts what you're short of, parts first, the same as clicking the recipe.
- Click a ghost with an empty hand to build it once you have the building, as before. Settings can hide the list.

**Limitations:** Ghosts laid by a Shift-drag don't turn the corners of a belt line; turn them with R after building. The list counts the recipe's direct ingredients, not what those are made from.

versions.title: Recent and starred recipes, ratio helper
versions.notes:
- The crafting menu has a Recent & starred row at the top: the last six things you crafted, with any you star first (up to 12). It follows the search box.
- Alt-click a recipe in the crafting menu to star it (a yellow corner), Alt-click again to unstar.
- Ratio helper: machine recipe tooltips and the item lookup say how many machines keep each other busy, for example "1 Prep Table keeps 2 Electric Ovens busy" or "2 Mills keep 1 Prep Table busy".

**Limitations:** Ratios use base recipe times and machine speeds: modules, quality, power shortfalls and burner fuel aren't counted. Recent and starred recipes are kept per browser, not per world.

versions.title: Arrival scene and follow a friend
versions.notes:
- A new world now opens with a 15-second fly-over: the camera drifts from a smog wreck, over the dry riverbed, and settles on your farmhouse with "Bring the valley back". Any key or click skips it, and Settings can switch it off. Tutorials don't have it.
- Co-op: click a friend's farmer with an empty hand, or press Follow by their name in the co-op box, to ride their camera and see what they're building. Any key or click brings you back.

**Limitations:** Following is view only: your farmer stays where you left them, and your own camera comes back when you press a key.

versions.title: Soil life
versions.notes:
- Soil life: every Garden Bed keeps an earthworm count from 0 to 100. Beds left planted gain worms, and mulch and compost add more; empty beds and heavy smog lose them.
- Lively soil grows crops up to 15% faster and greens its tile sooner, so beds you look after get better over time.
- The soil view (G) shows "worms 42" over every bed, and hovering a bed shows its soil life.
- Co-op: a farm copied from the host's snapshot now has exactly the host's greenness, so crops on both sides grow in step (it was rounded before, which could make a rejoined friend's farm drift).

**Limitations:** Soil life is per bed, not per tile: open ground doesn't keep worms.

versions.title: Outpost sleep: investigation
versions.notes:
- No change to play: this release adds an outpost benchmark for testing (tests/bench_outposts.gd) and the findings of the outpost sleep investigation.
- Result: far outposts cost no more per tick than the same outposts packed together, so putting them to sleep isn't worth it. What grows with distance is the smog and greening updates, which sweep the empty land between outposts; a cheaper fix for that is now an idea for a later round.

**Limitations:** Nothing changes in game; outpost sleep itself won't be built (chunk 190 is skipped).

versions.title: While you were away
versions.notes:
- While you were away: joining a friend's world again shows a card of what changed since your last visit: what each friend built (by name), regions restored, money in and out, and anything that needs a look.
- Loading your own save a day or more (real time) after you saved it shows a short Welcome back card: the day, your money, regions restored, the next chapter goal and open alerts.

**Limitations:** Buildings from before this version don't remember who built them, so they never show on the card. Money goes back a week at most.

versions.title: Ride the cart
versions.notes:
- Ride the cart: stand beside a Farm Cart or a barge and press Y to climb aboard; you ride along its route and press Y again to hop off anywhere, landing beside the rails or the bank.
- At a Cart Station or a sending Barge Dock with one parked, Y waits aboard: you leave with the next cart or barge that sets off.
- A cart that parks (or a barge that sinks in a flood) sets its riders down safely beside it. Before a flood no barge leaves, and the message says so. In co-op, friends see you ride along.

**Limitations:** You can't sleep while riding. In combat worlds, bugs can still reach you on the way.

versions.title: Remote view from the map
versions.notes:
- Click a building on the map (M) to open its window from afar, if a Roboport covers it: change the recipe, filters, schedules and conditions, or read why it's idle.
- A remote window says so in its title and has a "Take a look" button that shows the spot live on the map. Putting items in or taking them out still needs you (or a drone) there.
- Pointing at a building on the map says whether it can be opened remotely.

**Limitations:** Without a Roboport network over it, you have to walk there, so the early game still walks.

versions.title: Valley chapters
versions.notes:
- Valley chapters: the game is split into six chapters (First harvest, Power, The village, The first region, The river, The Vault), each with three or four goals and a money reward.
- After the first-day checklist, the panel at the side of the screen shows just the current chapter's next goal; click it to open the new Chapters tab in the Collection book (J), with every goal ticked as you go.
- Finishing the last chapter earns the Keeper's hat.

**Limitations:** In co-op, chapters are shared by the whole world and the reward goes into everyone's purse. Worlds from before this version start at the first chapter they haven't finished, without paying for the ones already done.

versions.title: Balance report
versions.notes:
- No change to play: this release adds a balance report for testing (tests/balance.gd) that lists money per minute for every machine recipe and flags the ones that lose money or break even.
- Its first findings (Cherry Jam and the two berry juices sell for less than their fruit; Sugar and Honey Tart break even) are written up for a later price pass.

**Limitations:** Prices aren't changed yet; the report uses base prices, not today's demand.

versions.title: Change layer
versions.notes:
- A new map layer, "Change since dawn": tiles that turned greener today show green, tiles that withered show red, and the rest of the map dims, so you can see at a glance where you're winning against smog.
- The legend counts how many tiles greened and withered, and pointing at a tile says how much it changed since dawn.

**Limitations:** It compares with this morning, not a full day back; the minimap doesn't show it.

versions.title: Why can't I place this?
versions.notes:
- A red placement ghost now says why under the cursor: someone's standing there, you don't have one, rubble or a rock in the way, water (build a bridge), a ditch, the old riverbed, unexplored land, a nest, needs the shore or a river bank, a pump needs water behind it, and so on.
