- Clicking or dragging onto a spot that won't take the building shows the reason once as a message, instead of nothing happening.
- The Forester's line says when there's no room to plant in its square.

**Limitations:** Claimed plots never block building by hand, so they don't show a reason.

versions.title: Share a strain or a valley
versions.notes:
- Strain codes: in a Seed Lab, copy a bred crop's strain as a short code (BWS1:...) and send it to a friend; they paste it in their Seed Lab and Import it. Each trait keeps the better of the two levels.
- Valley codes: the farmhouse window copies this world's code (BWV1:...), its seed and world settings, challenge included. Paste one on the new-world screen to start the same valley.

**Limitations:** Codes only carry the start of a valley, not anyone's farm.

versions.title: Year in review
versions.notes:
- Year in review: on the first morning of each new year (four seasons, or 28 days without seasons) a scrapbook page goes into the Collection book's new Scrapbook tab, with a picture of the valley as it was.
- Each page has the year's top dish, what you earned, the regions you restored, new wildlife, your best fair ribbon and your zero-smog days. A card explains it the first time.

**Limitations:** Pictures are saved on this computer (like the time-lapse), so a friend in co-op sees the pages but their own pictures.

versions.title: Valley challenges
versions.notes:
- Valley challenges on the new-world screen, each with one twist: Drought Valley (no lakes but the little starting pond), Long Winter (you arrive in winter, and every winter lasts twice as long), Islands (three times the lakes, half the rubble) and No Burners (nothing that burns fuel; you start with solar panels and an electric furnace).
- The goal is Valley in Bloom, and the screen keeps your best day for each challenge.

**Limitations:** No Burners still lists burner research in the shop; buying it does nothing there.

versions.title: Comfort settings
versions.notes:
- A Comfort section in Settings. Reduced motion turns off greening sparkles, region bursts, harvest pops, rainbows and swaying grass, and the camera snaps instead of gliding.
- Pause when the tab or window is hidden (single player) opens the pause menu as soon as you switch away.
- Status colours: Normal, Blue / orange (colour-blind friendly) or High contrast, for the Idle map layer, building ghosts (can / can't build) and cart signal lights.
- Bolder text, and Click once to take apart: one right-click starts taking things apart (as if holding the button), another stops.
- Fixed: the v0.1.160 entry in this list was missing a field, which made the version list error.

**Limitations:** The palettes don't reach the soil view, power overlay or alert buttons yet.

versions.title: Pause and game speed
versions.notes:
- Single player: Backspace stops the clock but not you. While paused you can still walk, build, plan and open windows, and everything you do happens at once. A Paused banner shows at the top.
- = cycles the game speed between 1×, 2× and 3× (a badge shows it). Sleeping uses its own fast-forward and puts the speed back to normal, as do loading and starting a world.
- Both keys can be rebound. In co-op they do nothing, since everyone's clock has to stay in step.

versions.title: Rotate the camera
versions.notes:
- Turn the camera a quarter at a time with comma and period (rebindable in Settings, Keys). It eases round, and walking (keys, gamepad and touch stick) follows it, so up is always up the screen.
- A small compass shows which way north is while the camera is turned. The game remembers your turn, and photo mode puts it back when you leave.

**Limitations:** The map and minimap stay north-up.

versions.title: Harvest pop, dawn chorus and rainbows
versions.notes:
- Harvest pop: picked crops and fruit hop out of the bed in a little arc to the farmer, and a run of harvests shares one toast that counts up ("+36 Wheat") instead of stacking.
- Dawn chorus: birds sing at sunrise, from one to four of them, more over green, clean land with many kinds of plants. Not in winter or in the rain.
- Rainbows: on a clear morning after a rainy day, a rainbow hangs in the sky over green land.

**Limitations:** Only harvesting by hand pops; taking dishes out of machines doesn't yet.

versions.title: Display signs
versions.notes:
- Display Signs: wire one to a chest, machine or belt the same way as an inserter condition, pick the item, and it shows the count ("128 Wheat", or items a minute on a belt) in big letters over the sign.
- Zoom the map in and the signs' numbers show there too. Blueprints and copy-paste carry what a sign counts.

**Limitations:** The text updates once a second.

versions.title: Cart signals
versions.notes:
- Cart Signals (with Farm Carts research): put one beside a Cart Rail and that rail becomes a gate splitting the line into blocks. A cart waits at the gate while the block past it has another cart stopped in it (loading at a station, or queuing), so several carts can share one line and take turns at the platform.
- Carts passing through a block never hold anyone up, two carts each waiting for the other's block both go, and after 30 seconds a cart goes anyway, so a line can't lock up. The signal's light shows red while it's holding carts back.

**Limitations:** Blocks aren't tinted in Alt view; hover a signal to see whether it's red or green.

versions.title: Frozen ponds
versions.notes:
- Frozen ponds: on snowy winter days and on the coldest days of each winter (the forecast says Freezing) small ponds ice over. An Offshore Pump on a frozen pond runs at a quarter speed, unless a working Boiler stands within 2 tiles to keep the water open. Big lakes and rivers never freeze.
- A Frozen ponds card as soon as you own a pump on a small pond, before the first freeze.
- Cut ice: hold right-click on a frozen pond for a block of ice. An Icebox without power melts one block every 5 minutes to stay cold.

**Limitations:** Frozen ponds don't show on the map; the pale ice is only in the world.

versions.title: Hail
versions.notes:
- Hail: now and then summer rain turns to hail (in the forecast a week ahead, and announced the evening before). It can crack the glass of Greenhouses and Solar Panels: a cracked greenhouse stops growing, a cracked panel makes no power, until you repair it with 1 glass pane.
- A Hail and glass card the moment you own a greenhouse or solar panel, before hail can ever reach them.
- Hail Shutters research ($400, after Solar Panels): shutters close over every greenhouse and panel on hail days, so nothing cracks.

**Limitations:** Cracked glass doesn't look different yet: the hover, window and a Repairs needed alert say so.

versions.title: Zero-smog days
versions.notes:
- A Smog ledger tab in the Production window: all the smog your buildings have made against what your valley's beds and trees could soak up, today so far, and a badge for each of the last two weeks.
- A day your plants could soak up more than you made is a zero-smog day (and a new Clean air achievement at 7). Seven in a row and an eagle comes back to circle over the valley.

**Limitations:** A day with no smog made at all doesn't count as clean: it's a goal for replacing burners, not for an empty farm.

versions.title: Eco-tourists
versions.notes:
- Eco-tourism (research, $800, after the museum): a 2×2 log Lodge. Once regions are restored, hikers come to walk your green land and pay $25 a night each: 2 for every restored region (up to 6), more the greener the lodge's region is and the more kinds of crop and fruit tree grow there.
- Smog at the lodge, or a smog wreck within 20 tiles, sends them all home. The lodge's window explains tonight's count. By day the guests stroll round it.

versions.title: Beavers
versions.notes:
- Beavers come back once the river flows again, and now and then they dam it: a new pond beside the river in a restored region (more fish, more water for pumps).
- Fair warning first: 3 days ahead a card explains it and the tiles that will flood show in blue in the world, on the map and in the hover tip. Anything built there goes back in your backpack. Hold right-click on the dam site with the Shovel to break it up, and they move on for a while.

versions.title: Valley museum
versions.notes:
- The Valley Museum (research, $600; 20 bricks, 20 planks, 4 glass panes): a 3×3 hall that shows off your Collection trophies, county fair ribbons and journal pages by itself, and one Excellent dish of each kind you give it from its window.
- Visitors pay $2 for every exhibit each morning, so the fee grows as it fills. One museum is enough: a second doesn't double it.

versions.title: Decorations and beauty
versions.notes:
- Decorations: benches, flower borders and stone paths (drag to lay a line), a 2×2 fountain and a statue. Each 8×8 block of land gets a beauty score from its decor (plus a little for flower patches and fruit trees), shown in Alt view.
- Families in cottages in a beautiful block get happier each morning (up to +15%). Decor shows in a warm colour on the map and in the time-lapse.

versions.title: Beeswax and candles
versions.notes:
- Beehives give a lump of beeswax with every 3 honey. A Chandler (6 planks, 2 iron plates, no power) dips 4 candles from 2 beeswax and a flax or cotton yarn wick.
- Lamps take up to 10 candles and burn one on a night they have no power, so they work off the grid. Candles are a cottage comfort too.

versions.title: Farmhands
versions.notes:
- Farmhands: a well-fed village lends you helpers, one for each cottage at tier 2 or more (up to 3). Each works from a Farmhand's Post (6 planks): in the 9×9 square round it, it carries items on the ground and wild plants it forages back to the post's chest, and takes fuel from the chest to burner buildings running low.
- Slower than drones, but there from the early game. Hands walk about in blue smocks; the post's window says whether it has one.

**Limitations:** Hands don't check claimed plots.

versions.title: Supply contracts
versions.notes:
- Supply contracts: each season a neighbouring town offers a deal on the farmhouse's orders board, say 12 bread a day for the season at a fixed price the market glut can't touch. Accept it and fill a Contract Crate (a crate and 2 planks): they collect each morning.
- The board and the crate count the days met and missed. A short morning costs a point of reputation, and 3 of them end the deal. A card explains this the moment you take a contract, and from the evening before each collection the crate, the board and an alert say if you're short.

**Limitations:** One contract at a time.

versions.title: Daily cravings and harvest festivals
versions.notes:
- Daily cravings: each morning one cottage craves one dish you can make (on the morning report and its hover). It takes up to 5 of it on top of its basket today, paying 3× the price for each, on the spot.
- Harvest festivals (worlds with seasons): one day near the end of each season, shown in the forecast a week ahead. That day one in-season dish sells for 3× at the dock; sell 30 and every family is happier, and you earn the Festival hat.

versions.title: Hedgerows
versions.notes:
- Hedgerows: a sapling and 2 wood make two hedges, dragged out in a line like belts. They grow in two days, then green their line (it counts toward regions and green corridors), feed bees like flowers, and shelter beds within 2 tiles in a dry spell (3/4 speed instead of half).
- Deer, once they're back, like to graze beside them. A living alternative to stone walls.

**Limitations:** Storms don't hurt beds, so the shelter is from dry spells.

versions.title: Rain barrels
versions.notes:
- Rain Barrels (4 planks, 1 iron plate, no research): a barrel fills on rainy and snowy days, then keeps the beds within 2 tiles watered for the next 3 dry days. Early watering far from lakes and ditches, and a reason to read the forecast.
- Its hover says how many dry days of water it has left. In worlds without weather it fills every 4 days.

versions.title: Footsteps by ground
versions.notes:
- Footsteps: a dry crunch on barren dirt, soft steps on green grass, a splash in water and ditches, a clack on roads and bridges, so walking from ruined land into restored land sounds different.
- They're quiet, and have their own Footsteps slider in Settings (it follows the Sounds slider too). Only your own farmer makes them, and riding a belt doesn't.

versions.title: A 5×5 farmhouse that grows
versions.notes:
- The farmhouse is 5×5 now: a small house at the back of a fenced yard, with room to grow. It gains a porch once you fill a villager order, a kitchen garden once a family moves into a cottage, a little windmill once a region is restored, and a wall of ribbons at 3 county fair ribbons. Its hover says what it has and what's still to come.
- Old worlds: your farmhouse grows round where it stood, picking the spot that's on land and in the way of the least. Anything it still covers goes back in your backpack with what it held, and a note says how many.

versions.title: First-time building cards
versions.notes:
- The first time you place each kind of building, a small card shows what goes in and what comes out (an icon row: in > building > out), what it needs (power or fuel), and its most common mistake.
- Cards are remembered per player, not per world, so a new world doesn't repeat them. Settings can switch them off or show them all again.

**Limitations:** Belts, pipes, poles, roads, walls, rails, ditches, bridges and saplings have no card.

versions.title: The wood wide web
versions.notes:
- The wood wide web: an old-growth tree's roots reach 4 tiles under the soil. Garden Beds in reach grow 20% faster and saplings 50% faster, so keeping an old grove next to a farm pays off.
- Alt view draws the fungal threads faintly from each old tree to the beds and saplings it feeds; their hover says when they're under the web.

versions.title: Co-op county fair
versions.notes:
- Co-op county fair (own backpacks): each player enters their own dish and crop, and each is judged against the rival farms, prizes to whoever entered.
- With two or more dishes in, the village votes for its favourite: the winner gets a Village Choice ribbon, tallied per player in the farmhouse window, and wears it on their name tag until the next fair.

versions.title: Claimed plots
versions.notes:
- Claimed plots (co-op with own backpacks): a Signpost (2 planks) claims the square around it for whoever put it up. Other players' construction drones, take-apart and upgrade plans, and pasted blueprints skip it, so friends can build side by side.
- Building by hand still works anywhere. Open the signpost to make the plot bigger or smaller (4 to 16 tiles each way) or share it; holding or hovering a signpost shows its square. A card explains plots the first time one goes up.

versions.title: Bottleneck finder and idle map layer
versions.notes:
- Bottleneck finder: a new Bottlenecks tab in the Production window (P). Pick a dish and it looks at every machine and Farm Tower in its chain, naming the one that's idle most (with why) and the one whose output backs up most, each with a Show on the map button.
- Idle map layer: tick Idle on the map (M) to mark every machine and tower that's been idle for a minute, coloured by why: red no power, yellow no input, blue output full, grey anything else.

versions.title: Morning report and next ideas
versions.notes:
- Morning report: a small card each morning with yesterday's money in and out, your three best sellers, how happy the village was, the region closest to restored, and today's weather and events. Turn it off in Settings.
- Next ideas: the Journal tab (J) suggests one or two things you haven't tried yet, based on what you do (crafting by hand: try an Assembler; animals: try the Biogas Digester; and so on), with a Help button and the lesson that teaches it.

versions.title: Smart Farm Towers
versions.notes:
- Smart Farm Towers: in a tower's window, wire it to a chest and give it a rule: grow one crop while the chest has under some amount of an item, another once it's stocked (say tomatoes while the tomato chest is under 200, else wheat).
- The tower keeps seeds of both crops and switches by itself. Copy/paste and blueprints carry the rule.

versions.title: Conditions read machines and belts
versions.notes:
- Conditions read more than chests: wire an inserter, belt or sluice gate to a machine (its output or its input), a Farm Tower (its products), or a belt tile (items passing a minute).
- Stop feeding an oven when its output backs up, or run a line only while another belt is busy. Pick what it reads in the condition's Reads: list.

versions.title: Bulk Inserter
versions.notes:
- Bulk Inserter (research it after the Fast Inserter): moves up to 5 of the same item each swing. Into a crate or machine it drops them all at once; onto a belt one by one as there's room. Made from a Fast Inserter, 5 gears and 5 iron plates.
- Inserter tooltips show how many items the arm is holding.

versions.title: Green corridors
versions.notes:
- Green corridors: two side-by-side restored regions are linked when a strip of green land at least 3 tiles wide crosses the border between them. The map draws a green line between linked regions, and the first link earns the Green corridor achievement.
- Linked regions share their wildlife: deer show up more often there and wander across toward the next region. Every other seed the birds drop lands along a corridor as a wildflower patch.

**Limitations:** Only regions that touch can link; a corridor through an unrestored region doesn't count.

versions.title: Migrating geese
versions.notes:
- Migrating geese: one morning each autumn (every 12 days without seasons) a flock flies over the valley and lands only on lakes with clean air over every tile.
- Each lake they rest on gets 4 feathers on its shore. Feathers and cloth make Pillows, another home comfort for a cottage.
- The first landing adds Migrating geese to the Wildlife page of the collection book (a page you'd already finished keeps its trophy and isn't paid twice).

versions.title: Old-growth trees
versions.notes:
- Old-growth trees: a planted tree left standing 12 days becomes old-growth: it grows bigger, soaks up twice the smog, and greens the land 7 tiles out instead of 5. The tooltip counts down the days.
- In the cold pines, an old-growth tree grows a truffle at its roots every 3 days: click the tree to dig it up. Truffles make Truffle Pasta at the Prep Table.
- Foresters leave old-growth trees standing unless you tick "Cut old-growth trees too" in their window.

versions.title: Herb garden and drying rack
versions.notes:
- Herb garden: thyme, mint and chamomile sprout wild on green land in restored regions. Pick them by hand; their seeds grow in beds.
- The Drying Rack (planks and flax yarn) dries herbs in the sun: no power or fuel, but only by day when it isn't raining.
- Dried herbs make Herb Tea (Roaster) and Seasoning (Prep Table). Give Seasoning to an Oven, Assembler or Prep Table: each batch uses one and comes out a quality point better.
- A flower pot and a sprig of mint make a Potted Herb, another home comfort for a cottage.

versions.title: Sourdough starter
versions.notes:
- Sourdough starter: a Fermenting Crock can make a starter from 2 flour. It lives in the crock, which then makes Sourdough Dough from flour; ovens bake it into Sourdough, worth three times bread. The gentry now want a loaf a day.
- A starter is alive and has to eat: every morning it takes 1 flour from its crock. A morning with no flour and it's hungry (news, and the crock says so all day); a second morning in a row and it goes flat.
- A warning card explains this the moment your first starter comes alive.

versions.title: Sugar beets and the Sugar Refinery
versions.notes:
- Sugar beets: a new crop (seed packs in the shop) that grows best in summer and autumn, on loam.
- The Sugar Refinery (research "Sugar" after the Canning Line): a 3×3 machine that boils 4 beets into 2 Sugar and 1 Molasses.
- Sugar makes Candy (Prep Table, with milk), Frosted Cake (Oven, from a cake) and Jam with sugar (Canning Line, from fewer strawberries). The old cake and jam recipes are unchanged.
- Molasses feeds a Biogas Digester, or a Dairy Barn, which then gives an extra milk per batch.

versions.title: Sand and glass
versions.notes:
- Sand and glass: put sandy soil (dig it with the Shovel) in a furnace and it melts into glass, 2 for 1.
- Glass makes Glass Panes and Bottles by hand. Panes are a second, cheaper way to build Greenhouses (8 panes, 4 iron plates, 6 planks) and Solar Panels (3 panes, 3 copper plates, a gear); both show up in the crafting menu.
- Bottles on the Juicer and Cider Press make Bottled Juice and Bottled Cider, which sell for half as much again.

versions.title: Clay and the kiln
versions.notes:
- Clay and the Kiln (research it after the Shovel): a 2×2 burner kiln fires the clay the Shovel leaves behind into bricks (2 clay for 1), jars (1 clay for 2) and flower pots.
- Jars on the Canning Line: strawberries and a jar make 2 jam instead of 1.
- A flower pot on a cottage's doorstep is a home comfort, like curtains and quilts: the family is a little happier and thanks you a little more.

versions.title: Letters from old valleys
versions.notes:
- Letters from old valleys: after you move to a new valley, the farm you left keeps going. Each season (every 4 days without seasons) a crate from it waits in your farmhouse mailbox.
- A crate holds 10 each of the old valley's three best sellers, some of its best dish and 10 seeds of its biggest crop, with a letter. The postcard is the old valley's last time-lapse picture, if it's on this computer.
- The last three valleys you left all keep writing.

**Limitations:** What a crate holds is fixed when you leave (from what that valley sold most), not worked out from its machines.

versions.title: Heritage wing
versions.notes:
- The Heritage wing: after the Great Seed Vault opens, it has three optional stages more, in its window. Each gives the whole valley a perk.
- The tasting hall (Excellent bread, pizza, cheese and cake only): bees range 6 tiles from their hives instead of 4.
- The far gardens (every far-biome crop): fruit trees bear twice in autumn.
- The river room (fish and preserves): the merchant visits every 3 days.

versions.title: Valley climate
versions.notes:
- Valley climate (worlds with weather): each morning, the share of the explored valley that's green sets the climate, from Harsh to Gentle, a step per quarter.
- Each step brings a little more gentle rain, fewer dry spells, and fewer storms and floods. From the Mild step, winter thaws a day early (two days when Gentle): those days feel like spring for weather and crops.
- The forecast shows the climate meter: the current step, how green the valley is, and what the next step brings.

**Limitations:** A new climate step can change the forecast for the days after it.

versions.title: Bring back the river
versions.notes:
- Bring back the river: a dry riverbed now winds from far up the valley down to near your farm. Nothing can be built on it, and a card explains it the first time you stand by it.
- Its headwaters are a chain of regions (the map marks each "River headwater 1 of N"). Restore them from the far end in, and the river flows again region by region; once every one is restored it reaches the Home Meadow.
- Flowing riverbed is real river: barges, water wheels, fish traps and ditches all work on it. Anything an older save had built in the bed goes back to your backpack when the water comes.

**Limitations:** The headwaters are far out (up to 300 tiles), so most of the chain is in land you haven't explored yet.

versions.title: Field guide and cloth goods
versions.notes:
- Field guide: wildflower patches now come in five kinds (pink campion, buttercup, violet, oxeye daisy, poppy), each its own colour. Walk by one in full bloom to add it to the new Meadow page of the collection book (J).
- The Meadow page also asks for a spot where crops, trees, fruit trees, wildflowers and wild plants all grow together. Finish it for $400 and the Botanist's hat.
- Cloth goods: the Loom makes Curtains (3 linen) and Quilts (3 cloth, 2 flax yarn). Give a cottage one of each: the family is a little happier every morning and thanks you a little more.

versions.title: Ditch gates
versions.notes:
- Sluice Gates (3 planks and a gear): set one on an irrigation ditch. Open, water flows through; closed, the ditch past it runs dry, and so does the land beside it. Send water down one ditch or another.
- Click a gate to open or close it, or wire it to a chest (like inserters and belts) so it opens only while the chest has less, or more, than some amount.

versions.title: Barge schedules
versions.notes:
- Barge schedules: a Send dock can have a list of stops (other docks on the same river). Each barge goes to the next stop in turn instead of the nearest Receive dock.
- Leave rule per dock: a full load or 20 seconds (as before), only a full load, or every 20 seconds with whatever is there.
- Before a forecast flood, from the evening no barge leaves, and barges out on the river turn for home with their loads (the barge card says so).
- Benchmark fix: the big test factory builds its farm towers again, so the benchmark measures farming and greening.

versions.title: Region quests
versions.notes:
- Region quests: every named region except Home Meadow has one wish, shown on a card the first time you walk in: plant 20 trees there, green its lake shore, bring its old mill back (build a Mill there), or clear its ruins and wrecks.
- A done quest pays $400 (plus $100 for each quest done before) and 6 seed bombs, on top of the reward for greening the region.
- Quest progress shows in the hover tip and under the region's name on the map (M).

versions.title: No more beeping, metal inserters, soil favourites
versions.notes:
- The beeping near miners is gone. It was the greening sparkle: smog from miners wilted the grass around them, the grass grew back, and every time it turned fully green again it sparkled and chimed. Grass regrowing under smog is quiet now; land turning green in clean air still sparkles.
- The factory sound near working machines no longer ticks (it had a fast high click); it's a soft hum and clank now, with its own Factory hum slider in Settings (0 turns it off).
- Inserters are made from 2 gears and 1 iron plate instead of a plank (Burner Inserters still use planks).
- Soil: every crop grows 25% faster on its favourite soil and at normal speed on the others, so loam is no longer best for everything. Wheat, tomatoes, lettuce, corn and flax like loam; potatoes and berries like sandy soil; rice, cranberries, mushrooms and cabbage like clay. Fertilized harvests turn a bed's soil into its crop's favourite.

versions.title: Rename a save, Fast Inserter
versions.notes:
- Rename a save: every save in the Save and Load lists has a Rename button. Type the new name and press Enter (Esc cancels); its picture moves with it, and if it's the farm you're playing, it keeps saving under the new name.
- Fast Inserter (research it in the shop after the Long Inserter): swings more than twice as fast as an Inserter, for busy ovens, smelters and docks. Made from an Inserter, 2 gears and 2 copper plates.

versions.title: Sawdust and mulch
versions.notes:
- Crafting planks now also leaves sawdust (a weak fuel). Assemblers making planks pile it on the side, so it never ends up on the plank belt: take it by hand or with an inserter filtered to Sawdust.
- Mulch (4 sawdust make 2): put it on a garden bed and the bed stays watered for 3 harvests, through dry spells too.
- Mushroom Logs (wood and sawdust) sprout 6 mushrooms each in a dark Mushroom Cellar, which needs no power.

versions.title: F3 overlay and save sizes
versions.notes:
- F3 shows a performance overlay: how long a sim tick and a frame take, buildings, belts and belt items, machines, drones, carts, barges, bugs, the world's size, and chunks generated, so slowdowns in big factories are easy to report and find.
- The load menu shows each save's size and, at the top, how full storage is.
- When storage is nearly full (80%: the browser's own estimate on the web, otherwise 50 MB of saves), a card warns you after a save, and the load menu offers to clear old autosaves (all but the newest of each world); Export saves anything you want to keep.

versions.title: Night ambience and graphics presets
versions.notes:
- Night on green land: fireflies blink over green meadows, glowing mushrooms light up the green pines, and crickets sing, louder the more green, clean land is around you. Barren and smoggy land stays dark and silent, so you can hear the difference between restored and ruined land.
- Graphics presets in Settings: Low (no shadows, wildlife, water ripples, or swaying grass, and a lower render scale), Medium, and High.
- On first launch the game watches the frame rate for a few seconds of play and picks a preset for you (it says so if it picks Low or Medium).

versions.title: Recipe pins and drag-to-set crops
versions.notes:
- Pin a recipe to the screen: Ctrl-click it in the crafting grid (or press Pin in the item lookup). Its ingredients show at the top right with how many you have, turning green as you gather them, and the recipe says when it's ready to craft. Up to three pins; Unpin removes one.
- Drag to set crops: hold a seed and drag across Garden Beds and Farm Towers. Empty beds are planted with it and every tower you pass is set to grow that crop.

versions.title: First-day checklist, idle reasons, item lookup
versions.notes:
- First-day checklist: on a new world (not a tutorial), a small list on the left walks you through the real game in place (salvage scrap, craft and place a bed, plant wheat, sell a crop, build a burner, lay a belt), ticking off each step. Hide it for the world with its Hide button, or turn it off for new worlds in Settings.
- Why is this idle? Every working building's window starts with one plain sentence: working, no power, low power, out of fuel, no recipe, missing flour, output full, no seeds, needs feed, out of season, or too much smog. Its Show button looks up the missing item, or opens the map at the building with the power overlay on.
- Item lookup: middle-click (or Ctrl-click) an item in the inventory or the crafting grid to see every recipe that makes it and every recipe that uses it, with the machine. Click any item there to look that one up (Back returns).

versions.title: Valley journal and field notes
versions.notes:
- Valley journal: ten pages of an old diary and letters turn up, in order, while you salvage ruins and wrecks, telling why the valley dried up and what the old farm grew. Read them on the new Journal tab of the collection book (J).
- Some pages teach a lost recipe (cornbread, the tart, cheese), and one marks an overgrown greenhouse on your map.
- Field notes: a Research Desk studies samples (crops, dishes, and parts like gears and plates), one a second, by hand or inserter, earning field notes worth about a quarter of each sample's price. Shift-click a research card in the shop to pay for it in field notes instead of money (one note pays for $5), so an automated sample line feeds the tech tree without flooding the market.

versions.title: Named regions and greening ripple
versions.notes:
- The valley is split into named regions (64×64 tiles: Home Meadow where you start, then names like Dry Creek, Ashen Flats, or Old Mill Hollow), each with a restoration %: how much of its land is green. The map (M) shows their borders, names, and %, and the hover tooltip says which region you're in.
- Restoring a region (60% green) pays a reward that grows with each one, with a little scene: a ring of sparkles, a chime, and a card.
- Returning wildlife now follows the regions: birds come back when a region is a quarter green, deer when one is restored, and the white stag after three.
- Greening ripple: a soft flash and sparkle (and a faint twinkle) where a tile turns fully green near you.

versions.title: Irrigation ditches and river barges
versions.notes:
- Irrigation Ditches: with the Shovel, dig channels (lined with ditch boards, 1 plank makes 4) and drag to dig a line. A ditch joined to a lake or river, directly or through other ditches, fills with water, and the land beside it counts as watered: thirsty crops grow at full speed and dry spells don't slow them. Belts, pipes, and poles can cross ditches; hold right-click to fill one in.
- River barges (research after Cart Stations): a Barge Dock on a river bank is a crate set to Send or Receive. Put Barges in a Send dock and they float loads along the river to the nearest Receive dock on the same water. Rivers flow away from where you started: fast downstream, slow coming back.
- Hazard, with a warning card the first time you have a dock or barge: on a spring flood day barges stay moored, and a barge already out on the river when the flood comes sinks with its load. Floods are forecast the evening before.

versions.title: Reed beds and returning wildlife
versions.notes:
- Reed Beds (shop, after the Fish Trap): place one on a lake or river shore and its reeds slowly clean the smog out of the water and air around it, with no power or filters, so fish come back to polluted lakes. They green the shore too.
- Wildlife comes back as the valley greens: birds (at 1,500 green tiles), then deer (5,000), then a rare white stag (12,000). Each arrival is news and an entry on a new Wildlife page of the collection book.
- Birds fly over green land and now and then drop wild seeds where the green thins out, and wildflowers grow there: slow, free greening. Deer graze on green land, and once it's back you may spot the white stag.

**Limitations:** Wildlife milestones count green tiles across the whole valley for now.

versions.title: Seed bombs and biodiversity
versions.notes:
- Seed Bombs (2 wheat seeds and a stone make 2): hold one and click bare ground within 8 tiles to throw it. Wildflowers grow there over a couple of minutes and slowly green the land around them: weaker than a tree, but a fun way to green places you won't build on, and bees visit them.
- Seed Spreader (shop, after the Composter): fill it with seed bombs and it throws one every 20 s onto bare ground up to 6 tiles away.
- Biodiversity bonus: land greens a little more strongly where several kinds of plant grow close together (crops, trees, orchard trees, wildflowers, wild plants): +8% for each kind past the first, up to +32%. The hover tooltip names the kinds near a tile, and Alt view shows the bonus over the land.

versions.title: Fermenting Crock
versions.notes:
- New Fermenting Crock (no research, stone and planks): it needs no power or fuel but takes about half a day a batch. Cabbage becomes Sauerkraut, milk Yogurt, and grapes Vinegar.
- Ferments never spoil and sell for half again as much in winter, a cheap early alternative to the Canning Line.
- New crop: Cabbage (seeds in the shop; grows best in spring and autumn, on clay). The Diner serves sauerkraut and yogurt.

versions.title: Fibre and cloth
versions.notes:
- Two fibre crops, Flax and Cotton (seeds in the shop), that never spoil.
- New research, Fibre and cloth: the Spinning Wheel spins them into yarn and the Loom weaves Linen and Cloth.
- Cloth bags 50 wheat into a Grain Sack (hand or assembler) that ships for more than the loose wheat and doesn't push the wheat price down.
- An Apron (3 cloth) makes hand crafting 15% faster while it's in your backpack; crafting a Sun Hat (linen and cloth) lets you wear one.
- A fifth village tier, Gentry, wants linen with apple pie and cider.

versions.title: Biogas Digester
versions.notes:
- Chicken Coops and Dairy Barns now leave manure on a pile of its own (up to 20). It never mixes with the eggs or milk: take it by hand from the window, or with an inserter filtered to Manure.
- New Biogas Digester (shop, after the Chicken Coop): it rots manure, spoiled food, and spare crops into Biogas canisters. Manure gives the most gas.
- Biogas is a fuel that burns with no smog at all, so a Biomass Burner on biogas is a clean generator (it works in furnaces and other burners too).
- Hazard, with a warning card the first time you have a digester: if its canister shelf fills, the tank fills and pressure builds (a gauge in its window and tooltip), and after a minute and a half at full pressure it vents a burst of smog.

versions.title: Splitter and chest filters
versions.notes:
- Splitters have an item filter: pick an item and which side it goes, and that item only leaves on that side while everything else leaves on the other, for sorting a mixed harvest belt.
- Crates, supplier and requester chests and iceboxes have slot filters: lock a slot to one item (click a slot under the chest's stacks) and it only ever holds that item, so mixed crates stay tidy for inserters. Right-click opens a slot again.
- Both are copied by blueprints and Shift-click copy and paste.

versions.title: Belt and pipe drag helpers
versions.notes:
- Dragging a belt or pipe line through something in the way (a building, a rock, a river) tunnels under it: once the drag comes out the other side, the last piece before the obstacle becomes an underground entrance and the exit goes down past it, if you have a pair of undergrounds and it's within their reach.
- Pipes now follow the drag one tile at a time like belts, so fast drags leave no gaps.
- Ctrl+Z undoes a tunnel like any other part of the drag.

versions.title: Round belt corners
versions.notes: - Belt corners carry you round the curve, keeping your distance from the corner, instead of pushing you straight ahead: sit on a 2×2 loop of belts and you go round and round.

versions.title: Seeing the ground
versions.notes:
- Soil view: press G (or the Soil button) to see every tile's soil in strong colours, even under grass: brown loam, red clay, yellow sandy.
- Hovering a building that isn't square (like a 3×2 Boiler) now highlights only the ground under it.
- Zooming the map's live view in far from your farmer now shows the rubble, trees, plants, ore and ruins there too.
- Choking vines and overgrown greenhouses have models now (they were invisible), and show on the map in purple and cyan.
- The map's Show row has an All off / All on button, and an inserter's filters can be switched off (it moves anything) without clearing them.

versions.title: Right Alt, FPS counter, smoother inventory, time-lapse rate
versions.notes:
- Only the right Alt key toggles Alt view now (the button says so); the left Alt is free for pings.
- Settings has a Show FPS option: frames per second and the slowest recent frame, under the minimap.
- The open inventory rebuilds about five times faster and at most four times a second, and no longer rebuilds whenever money comes in, so walking with it open doesn't stutter.
- The time-lapse window lets you choose how often a snapshot is taken: 4 or 2 a day, every morning, every 2 or 3 days, or once a week.

versions.title: Belt cost, steady farmhouse window, boilers
versions.notes:
- Conveyor belts now cost an iron plate and a gear (2 belts per craft) instead of a plank and a gear.
- The farmhouse window (and other long windows) no longer flickers: it waits for its text to settle before resizing, and its scroll bar no longer comes and goes.
- Boilers: a pipe on a boiler's steam outlet used to join the water pipes, so it showed (and carried) water. Steam pipes now stay steam, and only the two end ports take water.

versions.title: A new valley
versions.notes:
- Once the Great Seed Vault opens, its window offers a new valley: a fresh world a step harder (more smog, less soaked up, ore thinner and farther apart).
- Take two perks along: a seed bank (30 of every seed you've grown), your bred strains, your recipe book, or a nest egg.
- The old world stays saved; the HUD shows which valley you're in.

**Limitations:** Solo only: in co-op, start the new valley from a solo game.

versions.title: Co-op trading and weekly goals
versions.notes:
- Co-op trading (own backpacks): stand near a friend, open your inventory, and hand them the item you're holding (one or all) or money.
- Co-op goals: once a friend has joined, each week brings a shared goal to make a dish together; when it's met everyone gets the reward. It shows under your orders.

**Limitations:** Goals count dishes made by machines.

versions.title: Tutorials for the wider world
versions.notes:
- Five new tutorials under The wider world: Biomes and far crops, The village, Breeding seeds, Keeping food fresh, and The Great Seed Vault.
- The Tutorials screen now shows its lessons in two columns.

versions.title: Money charts and the factory planner
versions.notes:
- Production window, Money tab: your balance, what you earned and spent each in-game hour, and reputation, over the last day or week. Point at it for the numbers.
- Production window, Planner tab: pick a dish and how many a minute; it lists the machines, garden beds, Farm Towers, and seeds needed, back to the crops, and what to bring in.
- Settings: the factory planner can be switched off.

**Limitations:** The planner assumes full speed (powered machines, loam, no strains). Money history starts from this version.

versions.title: Conditions, cart schedules, cargo drones, personal logistics
versions.notes:
- Conditions: wire an inserter (or a belt: Ctrl-click it) to a chest and it only runs while the chest has less or more than an amount.
- Cart schedules: give a Cart Station a list of stops; its carts go round them in order, loading or unloading and waiting until full, empty, or 30 s at each.
- Cargo drones (research): Drone Pads that send goods by air to the nearest Receive pad anywhere, no rails needed.
- Personal logistics (research): logistic drones keep chosen items stocked in your backpack and take away what you mark as trash, while you're in a roboport network.

**Limitations:** A schedule holds up to 8 stops. Conditions read one chest.

versions.title: The merchant, overgrown greenhouses, rivers
versions.notes:
- A travelling merchant visits your farmhouse every few days (announced the evening before): rare seeds, goods, a tool at 30% off, ready-made blueprints, and good prices for odd surplus, for one day only.
- Overgrown greenhouses far out in the valley: clear the choking vines, then open them for heirloom seeds (pumpkin, saffron, vanilla) found nowhere else, and new dishes from them.
- Rivers wind across the land beyond the home valley, with fords to cross. Bridges (craftable from the start) carry you, belts, pipes, rails, and poles over water; Water Wheels on a river bank make steady power.
- Orders now only ask for things you can make (no smoked fish before you have a Smokehouse).

**Limitations:** Rivers and greenhouses only appear in land explored from now on.

versions.title: Dish quality and drinks
versions.notes:
- Dish quality: dishes made from bred, in-season, or fresh ingredients come out Fine (silver star) or Excellent (gold star), selling for up to 30% more and counting for more at the fair.
- Drinks (research): tea grows wild in the cold pines and coffee in the dry hills. A Roaster makes tea and coffee; a Juicer makes juice from apples, grapes, strawberries, or blueberries.
- Villagers want a drink: juice at tier 2, tea at tier 3, coffee at tier 4. The Diner serves drinks, cider, and apple pie.

**Limitations:** Quality is one level per dish (like freshness), not per item.

versions.title: Soil types and orchards
versions.notes:
- Soil types: loam, clay, and sandy patches across the valley (more clay in the wetlands, more sand in the dry hills). Each crop grows 20% faster on its favourite soil, and fertilized harvests slowly turn poor soil into loam. Hover the ground to see it.
- The Shovel (shop): dig up soil and lay it somewhere else, under garden beds or bare ground.
- Orchards (research): Apple, Peach, and Cherry Trees take two days to grow, then fruit every season for good. A Cider Press, apple pie, and peach and cherry jam.

**Limitations:** Soil in land you'd already explored is worked out from the seed (nothing there changes otherwise).

versions.title: Fair warning, difficulty presets, creative mode
versions.notes:
- Fair warning: the first time you come near a hazard (the dry hills, lakes that flood, smog wrecks, blight nests, heavy smog, spoiling food), a card explains it so you can plan before it costs you anything.
- Grass fires now only start and spread in the dry hills, and the evening before a storm, drought, or flood you're told what's coming.
- Difficulty presets on the new-world screen: Relaxed, Normal, and Hard set the sliders and options for you.
- Creative mode (a new-world option): build for free with everything unlocked, an endless backpack, instant free crafting, and a million dollars. No achievements; saves are marked creative.
- The new-world screen fits again: the extra options moved to the right-hand column.

**Limitations:** Each hazard card shows once per world.

versions.title: Collection book, message log, save pictures
versions.notes:
- The collection book (J, or the pause menu): every crop, dish, wild find, and biome you've come across, with hints for the ones you haven't. Finishing a page wins a trophy for the farmhouse and money; the Dishes page also earns a Chef's hat and the Biomes page an Explorer's hat.
- The message log (O): scroll back through the news, events, and chat, by day and time.
- Each save in the load menu shows a picture of the farm when it was saved.

**Limitations:** Saves made before this version have no picture until you save them again. The book fills in what an older save had already sold or made.

versions.title: Village mailbox, cottage tiers, fairer freshness
versions.notes:
- The village: families' letters and cottages now arrive in your farmhouse mailbox. Take the cottage and place it wherever you like; pick it up to move it and the family moves with it.
- Cottage tiers: every cottage of a tier wants the same basket. Fed two mornings running, a cottage moves up a tier (settlers, villagers, townsfolk, merchants), wanting more and thanking you more.
- Serve-only economy (experimental new-world option): the dock doesn't buy food; families pay for what you bring them, and food given at the dock becomes reputation through the food bank.
- Freshness is fairer: each food has one freshness level for all of it, raised by new food in proportion and lowered by time. Stacks only start spoiling below 30%, a little at a time, and moving food can't refresh it. Alt view shows a freshness bar.
- Weather events (storms, droughts, floods) are now a new-world option.
- Photo mode: H hides your farmer (and friends') for the picture.

**Limitations:** Worlds made before this keep the village's old cottages; new families arrive by mail. Weather events are off in older worlds.

versions.title: Seed breeding and weather events
versions.notes:
- Seed breeding (research): a Seed Lab breeds better strains of a crop, Bountiful, Quick, or Hardy, up to level 3. Beds take on the best strain when they're planted, and bred seeds show a gold star.
- Storms (in weather worlds) can knock out wind turbines until you repair them (2 gears).
- Droughts can start grass fires that spread over green land and burn crops and saplings. Bare ground, water, roads, and sprinklers stop them; rain puts them out.
- Spring floods wash out unripe crops near the lakes.
- The forecast and the top-left weather show storms, droughts, and floods coming, and there are Fire and Turbines down alerts.

**Limitations:** You can't put a fire out yourself; plan fire breaks and sprinklers. Greenhouse crops don't use strains.

versions.title: Music, photo mode, and your farmer
versions.notes:
- New music: tracks for spring, autumn, winter (with bells), and the night, alongside the original. The music follows the season and the time of day, crossfading as they change.
- The factory sounds busier as it grows: a soft hum and clatter that rises with the machines working around you.
- Photo mode (F2, or the pause menu): the HUD hides, the camera flies free (WASD, Q/E to turn, R/F to tilt, wheel to zoom), and Space saves a picture.
- Your Farmer (pause menu): pick a hat (straw hat, cap, beanie, flower crown, or none), a shirt colour, a name tag colour, and a name. Co-op friends see them, and chat uses your name.

**Limitations:** The new music is built in the background after the game starts, so the first minute plays the original loop.

versions.title: Co-op chat, own backpacks, touch and gamepad
versions.notes:
- Co-op chat: press Enter to type a message everyone sees.
- Own backpacks and wallets (a new-world option for co-op): buildings are shared, but each player has their own backpack, money, and crafting queue, and comes back to it when they rejoin. A dock or diner pays whoever built it; village thanks are split.
- Gamepad support: the left stick walks, the right stick moves a cursor that works like the mouse, and the buttons click, rotate, open the inventory and map, switch hotbar slots, zoom, and shoot.
- Touch screens: a joystick to walk and buttons to take apart, rotate, put away, and zoom (or pinch to zoom). They appear when you touch the screen.

**Limitations:** With own backpacks, guns, armor, and research are still shared. Gamepad buttons can't be remapped yet.

versions.title: Undo, search, and accessibility
versions.notes:
- Undo (Ctrl+Z, or Cmd+Z on a Mac): takes back your last build, take-down (putting the building back with its settings), dragged line of belts or walls, or blueprint paste.
- Search (Ctrl+F): a search box in the inventory (filters the backpack and crafting), the shop (highlights matching research), and help (finds text across every tab).
- Settings: interface size (75% to 150%), smog colour on the map (red, purple for red-green colour blindness, or dark grey), and a Controls screen to change any key.
- Windows now open over the minimap and alerts.

**Limitations:** Undo covers your own last 100 actions in this session; it isn't saved. Shift, Ctrl, and Alt can't be remapped.

versions.title: The village
versions.notes:
- A village grows around your farmhouse: as your reputation rises, families move in and build cottages (up to 12).
- Each family needs a basket of food every day, delivered to its cottage by hand, belt, or inserter. The basket grows richer as the village grows, from bread and salad to cake and fish pie.
- Well-fed families thank you each morning. A well-fed village shares a family recipe at each new level, opens a market (cheaper seeds), and lends helpers in the kitchen (faster hand crafting).
- A Village hungry alert in the evening if families haven't had half their basket.

**Limitations:** Cottages go up on free land near the farmhouse; keep some space clear around it.

versions.title: Freshness, the Test Kitchen, and the county fair
versions.notes:
- Freshness (a new-world setting, off by default): fresh crops, eggs, milk, fish, and dishes slowly spoil into Spoiled Food (compost it). Keep food in a powered Icebox, smoke fish and cheese in a Smokehouse, or can tomatoes and make jam in a Canning Line. Preserved food never spoils and sells for half again as much in winter.
- The Test Kitchen (research): try two or three ingredients together. If they make a dish you haven't unlocked, you learn it for free (it goes in the recipe book); if not, the cook may give you a hint.
- The county fair: on the last day of each season (every 4th day without seasons), enter your best dish and biggest crop at the farmhouse. Win money, ribbons for the farmhouse, and rare biome seeds.
- A County fair alert reminds you on fair day.

**Limitations:** Food on belts, in carts, and inside machines doesn't spoil. Existing worlds keep freshness off.

versions.title: Biomes and fishing
versions.notes:
- Biomes: about 100 tiles out from the start the land turns to wetlands (more lakes, frogs), dry hills (more rocks), or cold pines (pine woods), each with its own soil and grass colours, on the map too.
- Six biome crops that grow wild only in their biome and at full speed only there: rice and cranberries, olives and grapes, mushrooms and blueberries. Greenhouses grow them anywhere.
- New dishes: Rice Bowls, Cranberry Sauce, Sushi, Olive Oil, Raisins, Focaccia, Mushroom Soup, Blueberry Muffins, and Mushroom Risotto (research Wetland, Hill, and Pine cooking). The Diner serves them.
- Fishing (research): Fish Traps on lake shores (fewer fish in smoggy water) and Fish Ponds that raise fish on grain. Grilled Fish and Fish Pie.
- Alt view now shows what coops, barns, hives, ponds, and traps have made.

**Limitations:** Land you've already explored keeps its old resources; biome crops and pines only appear in land explored from now on. The home valley stays meadow.

versions.title: The Great Seed Vault
versions.notes:
- The Great Seed Vault (research, $5,000): a 5×5 goal for long games. Fill it in three stages, by hand or with inserters: foundations, a seed bank, and provisions. When it's full it opens and a wave of green rolls 72 tiles out, clearing smog, rubble, ruins, and wrecks and turning blight nests into Bloom Nests.
- Copy and paste settings: Shift+right-click a building to copy its recipe, crop, filters, station mode, or chest limit, then Shift-click other buildings to paste.
- Alerts beside the minimap: no power, no fuel, no ingredients, output full, under attack, and orders due tomorrow. Click one to see it on the map. Turn them off in Settings.

**Limitations:** One vault per world. Alerts show the first building of each kind on the map.

versions.title: Smog wrecks
versions.notes:
- Smog wrecks: ruined factories and rusted cars dot the valley, trailing smoke. Their smog withers the grass and slows crops around them, so clearing them is part of bringing the valley into bloom.
- Nests don't smell wreck smog, so wrecks never bring attacks.
- Wrecks are too big to break up by hand. The Clearing Kit does it in one pull, for scrap and machine parts. Construction drones clear them too (deconstruction planner) once you have the Kit.
- A Smog wrecks slider under Landscape when making a new world. A new achievement: Scrap dealer (10 wrecks).

**Limitations:** Older worlds get wrecks only in land explored from now on.

versions.title: Farm carts and wildlife
versions.notes:
- Farm carts (research, $350): lay Cart Rails between Cart Stations, set one to Send and one to Receive, and put Farm Carts in the Send station. A cart carries up to 200 items to the nearest Receive station it can reach, unloads, and comes back. Inserters fill and empty stations like crates.
- Life returns to green land: butterflies flutter over it, rabbits hop about (and scatter when you come close), and fish jump in the lakes. They come out by day in fair weather.
- Grass sways in the wind.

**Limitations:** Carts follow the rails without crossings or signals. Each cart goes to the nearest Receive station.

versions.title: Bloom Nests and night raids
versions.notes:
- Bloom Nests: keep Blight Jelly in a tame nest's trough as well as crops, and after 2 minutes the nest blooms for good, covered in flowers. Its friendly bugs pollinate beds within 8 tiles and slowly green the land around it.
- Night raids: packs that set out after dark are half again as big.
- Lamps (1 power each, no research needed): they light the ground around them at night.
- A new tutorial, Defending the farm: turrets, walls, your gun, and taming a nest.
- Four new achievements: Pest control, Exterminator, Blight whisperer, and Flowers from blight.

versions.title: Orders and the Valley in Bloom
versions.notes:
- Villager orders: up to three on your farmhouse board ("30 bread by day 8"), shown top left. Click the house to deliver from your backpack, or run a belt and inserter into it.
- A filled order pays well over the market and earns reputation, and each point makes orders pay 5% more. Missing the day costs a point. New orders come each morning.
- Valley in Bloom: turn half the land of the valley you started in green to win. A summary screen shows your farm's story (days, food shipped, orders, smog made, nests tamed), then you keep playing.
- Two new achievements: Good neighbor (10 orders) and The valley restored.

versions.title: Animals, compost, greenhouses, and the diner
versions.notes:
- Chicken Coop ($150): hens eat wheat or corn and lay eggs. Dairy Barn ($250): cows eat wheat, corn, lettuce, or potatoes and give milk.
- New dishes: Omelette (2 eggs + a tomato, oven, $18), Cheese (2 milk, Prep Table, $14), and Cake (2 flour + 2 eggs + milk, oven, $45).
- Composter ($80): spare crops and seeds become Fertilizer. A fertilized bed grows at full speed for 3 harvests, however barren the soil.
- Greenhouse (research, powered, $500): grows a crop indoors at full speed, four beds' worth, whatever the soil, season, weather, or smog.
- Diner ($300): stock it with dishes. A customer buys one every 4 seconds, paying 15% more for each other dish on the menu, up to 75% more.

versions.title: Time-lapse
versions.notes:
- Each morning the game saves a map of your valley (on this computer, for each world).
- Time-lapse (pause menu): play the days back and watch the valley turn green, or scrub through them with the slider.
- Save GIF turns the whole time-lapse into an animated GIF to share. It downloads in the browser, or goes to your Downloads folder.

**Limitations:** Snapshots start from today, so older worlds' time-lapses begin now. Co-op friends each keep their own.

versions.title: Beehives and Air Scrubbers
versions.notes:
- Beehives (shop, $120): bees buzz around the planted beds and wild plants within 4 tiles. Beds they reach give a quarter more at harvest, and the hive fills with Honey, faster with more flowers. Bees rest in winter.
- Honey sells for $8, or makes Honey Bread ($22) and Honey Tarts ($40) at a Prep Table.
- Air Scrubbers (research, $400): a powered 2×2 machine that pulls smog out of the air within about 14 tiles, burning an Air Filter a minute. Filters come from charcoal and iron, or three from one Blight Jelly in combat worlds.

versions.title: Seasons and weather
versions.notes:
- Seasons (a New World setting, on by default; choose the season length and the season you start in). Each crop grows faster in its own seasons and slower out of them, and everything is slow in winter. Prices follow: crops out of season cost more, salads and tarts sell better in summer, and bread, pizza, and baked potatoes in winter.
- Weather (also a New World setting, on by default). Rain waters every bed (thirsty crops too) and washes smog away faster. Dry spells halve growth on beds without a sprinkler. Winter brings snow.
- A Forecast button (top left) shows the week ahead. Each morning's news says the weather and when a new season starts.
- The land shows the season: fresh in spring, warm in summer, golden in autumn, and patchy snow in winter. Rain darkens and shines the ground under grey skies.

**Limitations:** Older saves keep no seasons or weather. They're settings for new worlds.

versions.title: Blueprint library and planners
versions.notes:
- Blueprint library (L): save the blueprint in hand by name (kept across all your worlds) and take it back out any time. Copy any of them as a string to send a friend, or paste one in to import it.
- Deconstruction planner (K): drag over an area to mark buildings, rubble, rocks, trees, and ruins (a red X). Your construction drones take them away into your inventory, with what's inside. Planned ghosts there are dropped. Shift-drag unmarks.
- Upgrade planner (U): drag to mark belts, burner drills, stone furnaces, burner ovens, and assemblers (a green arrow). Drones swap each for its better version (fast belt, electric drill, electric furnace, electric oven, advanced assembler) when you have one, keeping its contents and settings. Shift-drag unmarks.

**Limitations:** The upgrade planner skips underground belts and electric drills (their better versions are a different shape).

versions.title: Production stats and map pins
versions.notes:
- Production window (P, or the new top button): every item made and used per minute over the last 5 minutes or hour, with net rates and a chart for each. Machines, drills, farms, crafting, gathering, burning fuel, and shipping all count. Esc or Tab opens the menu now (P used to).
- Map pins: right-click the map to pin a note there; right-click a pin to take it away. Pins show on the map, the minimap, and as flags in the world, and everyone in co-op sees them.
- Ping: Alt-click the world or the map to flash a ring there for everyone. Friends get told how far away it is and in which direction. Tapping Alt by itself still toggles Alt view.

versions.title: Equipment, taming, and water
versions.notes:
- Equipment bar (bottom left, like Factorio): three weapon slots and an armor slot. Guns you get fill empty slots. Click a slot to make it your active gun, or press X to switch. Hold a gun on the cursor and click a slot to equip it, or right-click to take one off. Click the armor slot to put on Modular Armor; right-click it to fit modules.
- The Pistol, Submachine Gun, and Shotgun have proper icons.
- Taming the blight: a Blight Trough (combat research) stocked with crops tames the nests within 8 tiles. Tame nests don't attack or spread, keep soaking up smog, and turn it into Blight Jelly. Sell it for $30, or make Jelly Toast (bread + jelly at a Prep Table) for $55. Each tame nest eats a crop every 15 s.
- Water has rolling waves that catch the sun, drifting light ripples, and lapping foam along the shore.

**Limitations:** Co-op farmers share the weapon slots (like the shared inventory), but each picks their own active gun.

versions.title: Landscape and clearing
versions.notes:
- New World has a Landscape section: sliders for how much Rubble, Rocks, Dead trees, and Ruins there are. The settings are in two columns now.
- Clearing Kit ($1000 in the shop, after Work Gloves): one pull on rubble, a rock, a tree, a ruin, or a wild plant takes the whole tile.
- Stone Furnaces hold 50 fuel. Stone and Electric Furnaces hold 50 ore (or stone) and 50 of what they make.
- The hover panel shows how much smog a building is making (or would make while working).
- Foresters replant where they cut a tree, and keep the ring right around them free for inserters.
- Trees you planted show deep green on the map, unlike wild plants and natural dead trees.
- Turning off Smog on the map turns it off on the minimap too.

versions.title: Smarter targets
versions.notes:
- Blight packs now go after what matters: buildings that make smog (the busiest first, idle ones too) and Gun Turrets. Lone poles, belts, pipes, crates and the like are no longer targets. They're only chewed when they're in the way.
- A nest with nothing worth attacking nearby doesn't send a pack.
- New world setting under Enemies: "Bugs attack every building", off by default, for the old behavior where anything can be a target.

versions.title: Walls and pathfinding
versions.notes:
- Blight bugs find their way: they walk around water and buildings, and when the only way in is long or there's none, they chew through the weakest spot.
- Stone Walls (combat research, 5 bricks each): 400 health and bugs can't walk through them. Drag to build a line. Bugs go around a short wall and chew through a wall that rings you in. They never attack walls for their own sake.
- A bug chasing you stops at a wall or building in its way and chews that instead.
- Attacks come from smog alone: nests soak up the smog that reaches them (taking it out of the air) and spend it on bugs, 4 smog for a bug and 20 for a brute. A nest the smog doesn't reach never attacks, however busy your base is. Nests can now be as close as 48 tiles to the start.

**Limitations:** Bugs follow the path they planned when they set out. A building put in their way later gets chewed rather than walked around.

versions.title: Combat mode
versions.notes:
- Combat mode: tick "Blight nests attack" when making a new world (it's off by default, and older saves stay peaceful). Blight nests grow out in the far valley.
- Nests smell the smog your buildings make and breathe in any that drifts over them. Enough of it and they send a pack of bugs at your smoggiest building. More smog means more and bigger attacks, and over time Blight Brutes join in. The first ten minutes are quiet.
- Bugs chew through buildings and go for farmers who come close. If they knock you out, you wake up at home. Damaged buildings mend slowly, and your house is safe.
- Gun Turrets (research) shoot bugs within 18 tiles. Load them with Magazines by hand or with an inserter.
- Guns: hold Space to shoot. You start a combat world with a Pistol and 10 Magazines. Craft Magazines (4 iron plates) and Pistols; research the Shotgun and Submachine Gun; or buy any of them in the shop's new Arms tab.
- Shoot a nest to destroy it for $50, but it sends bugs at you. Nests near your base slowly spread to new spots, away from other nests and from your buildings.
- New world sliders: Attack pressure and Nests. Smog from buildings now goes up to 5×.
- Nests show on the map, and pointing at one shows its health and how close it is to attacking. Help has a Combat page.

**Limitations:** Bugs walk straight at their target (over water and through buildings, which they chew on the way). There's no armor against bugs yet.

versions.title: Smoother co-op
versions.notes:
- Co-op is much smoother for whoever joins: their game now plays the world at a steady pace a moment behind the host, instead of jumping ahead in bursts whenever an update arrived. The host also sends far fewer messages.
- You can just squeeze between two buildings that touch.
- Belts carry you along when you stand on them.
- Limit how many slots a crate fills: click an empty slot to lock it and those after it (inserters and drones won't fill them); click a locked one to open them again.
- Belts stack 200 to a slot.
- Crafting tooltips list the raw materials a recipe comes to.
- Help lists every crop's growth time, harvest, price, water needs, and where it grows wild.
- Smog shows as a clear red wash on the map, and buildings are drawn grey so it stands out.

versions.title: Map and looks
versions.notes:
- The map has a Show row: tick each resource (iron, copper, stone, coal, oil, water, wild plants, ...) and buildings or green land on and off.
- Zoom far into the map to see a live view of that spot from above.
- Lake shores are rounded instead of square steps.
- Crop icons are drawn properly: wheat stalks, a tomato with its leaves, potato, lettuce, strawberry, and a corn cob.
- Pipes can carry steam: connect a boiler's steam outlet to engines farther away.

**Limitations:** The live map view only shows belt items and crops near where you are.

versions.title: Fixes
versions.notes:
- Co-op: the room box sits on the left now, out of the way of building windows, and folds away with [-].
- "Someone's standing there" checks the building's real shape, so long buildings like steam engines don't block a whole square.
- Tooltips stay up while a window refreshes under the mouse (they used to switch to whatever was in the world behind).
- Greenery: each tree greens the land around it by a share that falls off with distance (10% five tiles away), and shares from several trees add up.
- Placing a building shows yellow triangles on the exact tiles where things come out, and blue ones where pipes or steam go in.
- In a crate, hold right-click on a stack and drag to take just some; they go on your cursor.

versions.title: Play at bloomworks.onrender.com
versions.notes:
- Co-op uses the server at bloomworks.onrender.com from any https page, so a copy hosted elsewhere (like itch.io) can still host and join.
- Copy invite link always gives a link friends can click to join: from another site it points to bloomworks.onrender.com.

**Limitations:** The free server sleeps when idle, so the first visit can take up to a minute.

versions.title: TURN relay
versions.notes: - Co-op can relay through a TURN server when a direct connection is blocked (phone hotspots, strict NAT, some ISPs), so more friends can join.

versions.title: Roads under buildings
versions.notes:
- Stone Roads are now paving on the ground: you can build on top of them. Hold right-click on bare road to lift it. Roads in older saves are converted.
- In co-op, construction drones leave from the farmer nearest the ghost and fly back to that farmer.
- Crafting can still take you over the backpack limit, on purpose.

versions.title: Modular armor
versions.notes:
- Modular Armor (research): wear it from the inventory and fit up to 6 modules.
- Portable Solar Panels charge it in daylight; Armor Batteries hold more charge.
- Exoskeletons make you run 40% faster each (up to two) while the armor has charge; switch them off to save power.
- A Personal Roboport lets 10 more construction drones fly at once, half again as fast.

**Limitations:** In co-op the armor is shared, like the inventory.

versions.title: Logistic drones
versions.notes:
- Roboport (research): covers 12 tiles around it, and overlapping roboports form one network. It holds up to 20 Logistic Drones and needs power for them to fly.
- Supplier Chests offer their items; Requester Chests ask for up to 3 items with amounts you set. Drones carry up to 10 at a time from suppliers to requesters in the same network, then fly home.
- Logistic Drones are made from Construction Drones and plastic.

**Limitations:** Drones fly straight to the nearest supplier with the item; they don't balance between suppliers.

versions.title: Power switches and wires
versions.notes:
- Ctrl-click a pole, then another in reach, to cut the wire between them, or put a cut wire back.
- Power Switch (research): wires to poles within 7 tiles but only joins them while its rule holds: when the batteries around it are below (or above) a level you set, always, or never.
- Use it to bring in a backup burner grid when the batteries run low at night, or to cut off less important machines when power is short.

versions.title: Oil
versions.notes:
- Oil wells: dark pools out in the far valley (never near the start), shown on the map.
- Pumpjack (research): 3×3, placed centered on a well, pumps crude oil out of the pipe connection at its front. Wells empty slowly and pump slower as they run low.
- Refinery: 3×3, takes crude oil from pipes and makes Plastic or Fuel Oil. Fuel Oil is the strongest fuel (20 MJ).
- A pipe network carries one fluid: water or crude oil. Connect a pump and a pumpjack to the same pipes and nothing flows until you separate them.
- The Advanced Assembler now takes plastic, and its research needs the Pumpjack.

**Limitations:** Older worlds only get oil in land explored from now on.

versions.title: Pick an amount
versions.notes:
- Hold right-click on a stack in your inventory and drag left or right to choose how many to hold; let go to pick them up.
- Clicking a building then puts in just that many (across clicks if it can't take them all at once).

versions.title: Construction drones
versions.notes:
- Construction Drones (research, then craft them): carry them and they fly out to ghosts within 30 tiles of you, take the building from your inventory, build it with its blueprint settings, and fly back.
- Up to 10 fly at once. Ghosts you don't have the building for wait until you do.

**Limitations:** In co-op the drones fly from whichever farmer moved last.

versions.title: Blueprints
versions.notes:
- Blueprints: press C and drag over buildings to copy them, with their recipes, filters, crops, and splitter settings. V brings back your last blueprint.
- With a blueprint in hand, click to build what you have the parts for and plan the rest as ghosts, or Shift-click to plan it all. R rotates it.
- Ghosts are see-through plans: click one to build it from your inventory (it gets the copied settings), right-click to remove it. Drones to build them for you come later.
- Export a save from the load list to a file you can send to a friend, and Import a save from a file.
- Stone Roads (from bricks): you walk half again as fast on them.

**Limitations:** Buildings can't be placed on roads; roads are their own tiles.

versions.title: Power views
versions.notes:
- Power charts show battery charge over time and what the network could make if everything ran flat out, next to what's wanted and supplied.
- Point at a chart to read its values at that moment. Click a legend entry to hide or show that line (just wind, just renewables, ...).
- "Open the full power view" in a pole or generator's window shows the charts big, across the screen.
- The map has a Power checkbox: poles, their supply areas, and the wires between them.

versions.title: Steam like Factorio
versions.notes:
- Boilers are now 3×2: water goes in at either end, from a pipe or the boiler beside it, so you can line them up. Steam comes out the middle of the front.
- Steam Engines are now 3×6 and take steam at either short end, from a boiler's front or the engine before them, so they chain too.
- Turn them with R before placing; once placed they stay put.
- Boilers and Steam Engines from older saves go back in your inventory (with their fuel) to be placed again.

**Limitations:** Steam only passes boiler to engine and engine to engine, not through pipes.

versions.title: Drills, wind, and greening
versions.notes:
- The Electric Drill is cheaper but slower. The new Advanced Electric Drill (research) is 3×3, mines the 5×5 area under and around it, and is three times as fast.
- Place an upgrade right over the building it replaces: Stone Furnace to Electric Furnace, Burner Drill to Electric Drill, Electric Drill to Advanced, Burner Oven to Electric Oven, Assembler to Advanced. It keeps the contents, recipe, and direction; the old building comes back.
- Wind turbines close together share the wind (one neighbor within 6 tiles: 2/3 each). Holding or pointing at one shows the area.
- Trees and crops add up their greening, so trees don't need gaps between them to fully green the land.
- Grass killed by smog stays dead until a crop or tree grows right beside it.
- Help lists how much smog trees, beds, and green land soak up, and how many solar panels and batteries a steady load needs.
- Shadows fade out at night, so they no longer jump at midnight.

versions.title: World settings
versions.notes:
- New World has sliders: ore richness (how much each tile holds), vein size, vein frequency, smog from buildings, and how much trees and crops soak up.
- Settings are kept with the world.

**Limitations:** Settings can't be changed once a world has started. The starting ore patches always exist, whatever the frequency.

versions.title: Assemblers
versions.notes:
- Assembler (research): a 3×3 machine that makes anything you can craft by hand with up to 3 kinds of ingredient, at half your speed. Pick its recipe from a grid of icons.
- Advanced Assembler (research): up to 4 kinds of ingredient, at 75% of your speed.
- Burner Oven: bakes everything the Electric Oven does by burning fuel, at half speed. It comes first in the research tree; the Electric Oven now needs it and the Electric Furnace.
- Charcoal: pick the Charcoal recipe in a furnace to turn 2 wood into 1 charcoal, a long-burning (10 MJ), clean fuel. Furnaces never switch to it on their own, so wood fuel stays fuel.

versions.title: Underground and fast belts
versions.notes:
- Underground Belts (research): place an entrance, then an exit up to 4 tiles further on facing the same way; items pass under whatever is between.
- Fast Belts and Fast Underground Belts (research): twice as fast, with red stripes. Lay a Fast Belt over a belt to upgrade it in place; it keeps its items and gives the old belt back.
- Underground Pipes (with the Offshore Pump): a pair facing each other up to 10 tiles apart carries water underneath. Each connects to a pipe on its back.

**Limitations:** Underground belts can't be turned once placed; pick them up and place them again. Fast inserters aren't in yet.

versions.title: Readability
versions.notes:
- Save and load rows: the save's name on top, with smaller grey details (day, date, time played, version) under it.
- Hover ore on the map to outline its whole vein in white.
- Holding or pointing at a Forester shows the square it plants and cuts trees in, and how many free tiles it has.
- Research tree: links no longer run on top of each other, and hovering a card lights up its links in gold.
- Newly planted crops show up right away, so you can tell a bed is planted.

versions.title: Inventory and crates
versions.notes:
- The inventory shows each stack in its own slot (100 of an item, 50 of a building), with as many slots as your backpack has.
- Crates hold 10 stacks: up to 1,000 of one item, or 10 different things.
- In a crate, click a stack to take it and hold it on the cursor; Shift-click to just take it.
- The put-in grid in crate and burner windows is sorted into Fuel, Ores, Materials, Crops and seeds, Food, and Buildings.
- Inserter filters: click a slot to pick from a grid of every item, by category. Right-click a slot to clear it.

**Limitations:** Older crates holding more than 10 stacks keep their items but take nothing more until they're emptied below that.

versions.title: Quality of life 3
versions.notes:
- You can walk through trees and wild plants (rubble and rocks still block you).
- Ten hotbars: Shift + a number key switches between them.
- A list in the bottom-left shows what you just picked up, fading out after a few seconds.
- Smog: the Mill makes none; Burner Drills make a lot (10/s), Stone Furnaces 5/s, Electric Furnaces 2/s.
- The dock only chimes when you sell by hand, not for every item a belt delivers.
- Alt mode icons stay put while you move and no longer cover windows.
- Hover the dock's prices to see what each item is.

versions.title: Polish
versions.notes:
- Everything you can craft, directly or by crafting its parts, gets the green frame, with how many you could make in the bottom-left. Recipes you can't make are only slightly dimmed.
- Recipe ingredients are listed in the same order everywhere.
- Garden Bed and Farm Tower seed buttons are always in the same place; seeds you don't have are greyed out.
- Drill, Smelter, and Oven are now the Electric Drill, Electric Furnace, and Electric Oven. The Electric Oven costs more.
- Building windows no longer flicker while you craft.
- Closing the inventory (E) closes the building window next to it too.
- Crate windows: Shift-click an item to put it all in, right-click to put in 5.
- Sleeping passes the night faster. "Quit to Title" is now "Save and Quit".
- Greenery speeds things up 10× less per tile, with no cap.

versions.title: Quality of life 2
versions.notes:
- Long building windows scroll instead of running off the screen. The Biomass Burner's window has one grid of fuel to click instead of a button per item.
- A new Farm Tower to start with: it tends just the beds around it, one every 5 seconds, and needs no power. The old one is now the Advanced Farm Tower, in the research tree. Older saves that have it keep it.
- Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on a Mac) a crate or machine to take everything out.
- Alt mode: press Alt (or the Alt view button) to see what's in each crate and what each machine makes.
- Drag with a power pole to lay a line of poles as far apart as their wires reach; they step back around anything in the way.
- A Quicksave button in the pause menu.
- Gears look like gears and wood looks like logs.

versions.title: Main menu
versions.notes:
