- The title screen sits over a living farm and factory: wheat takes the long way to a Mill and a splitter, a belt loop carries a jumble of things in circles, drills feed smelters, turbines spin, and a sprinkler waters corn by a pond.
- The camera drifts slowly over it, and the game's buttons and bars stay hidden until you start playing.
- Leaving a game or a tutorial brings you back to it.

versions.title: Tutorials
versions.notes:
- Tutorials on the title screen: seven short lessons, each in its own practice world.
- By hand: gathering (scrap, wood, stone, ore), crafting, farming, building, and processing ore in a furnace.
- Automation: moving items with inserters and belts, and connecting a machine by copying a working example next to it.
- A panel on the left shows each step and moves on when you've done it. You can skip a step or quit, and go straight to the next lesson at the end.
- Practice worlds aren't saved and need no power.

versions.title: Water
versions.notes:
- Lakes in the valley, including a pond near the start of every world. Older worlds get lakes on empty land.
- Offshore Pumps go on the shore and push water into Pipes. Touching pipes join up.
- Sprinklers water the garden beds within 2 tiles.
- Potatoes, strawberries, and corn are thirsty: without water they take a whole day to grow. Wheat, lettuce, and tomatoes still grow fast.
- Boiler and Steam Engine: the boiler burns fuel to boil water into steam, and engines touching it make up to 300 kW each, twice as much power from fuel as a Biomass Burner.
- All of these are in the research tree, after the Smelter.
- Chimneys smoke again while their building works.

**Limitations:** Pipes only carry water (steam goes straight from a boiler to the engines touching it). Water can't be filled in.

versions.title: Research and backpacks
versions.notes:
- The shop's unlocks are now a research tree: each one needs the ones before it (Drill and Solar after the Smelter, Pylon after the Iron Pole and Battery, pizza after tomato sauce and the oven, and so on). Hover a card for details.
- Your backpack has 40 slots. Each slot holds 100 of an item, or 50 of a building. When it's full you can't gather, harvest, take things out, or pick up buildings.
- Three backpack upgrades in the research tree: +10, +10, and +20 slots.
- The inventory shows how many slots you're using.
- Picking up a splitter gives back the items inside it.

**Limitations:** Unlocks you already bought in older saves stay unlocked, even ones whose prerequisites you skipped. Crafting can still go over the limit.

versions.title: Splitters
versions.notes:
- Splitters (unlock in the shop, $120): two belts wide. One belt in becomes two belts out, split evenly, and two belts in can merge into one.
- Items keep their lane through a splitter.
- If one output backs up, everything goes to the other.
- Click a splitter to make it prefer the left or right input or output (it's even by default).
- R turns a splitter around in place. F picks up the items inside.

**Limitations:** Inserters can't take from or drop into splitters, and splitters don't filter items.

versions.title: Quality of life
versions.notes:
- A panel in the bottom-right shows what's under your cursor: contents, growth, progress, fuel, ore left, and the whole vein's total.
- The map tells you what's under the cursor too, including how much ore is in a vein.
- Inserters take up to 5 item filters, shown on a tag over them.
- Hold right-click like in Factorio: you keep working on what you started, even if the cursor moves off it.
- Right-click a recipe to craft 5. Recipes you can't make are greyed out; ones you can make have a green frame.
- Burner buildings show how much is left in the fire, and fuel items list their energy (also in Help).
- Burner drills hold 50 fuel.
- With an item on the cursor, Z drops one into the building, belt, or ground under it. F picks up items on the ground.
- Inserter arms swing and dip to grab again.
- Stone ore looks different from rocks and other ores.
- Buildings that keep their output for inserters no longer have an output chute.
- Settings have their own menu. The load list folds each world's saves away.

**Limitations:** Items on the ground aren't picked up by inserters.

versions.title: Endless world
versions.notes:
- The valley never ends: walk toward any edge and new land appears, with rubble, trees, rocks, ore patches, wild plants, and ruins with seed caches.
- New land comes from your world's seed, so the same seed always makes the same world, however you explore it.
- Older worlds keep everything and grow from their edges too.
- In co-op, whoever explores grows the world for everyone.
- The map shows everything you've explored.

**Limitations:** Rarer crops are still placed by distance from the start, so far-off land has every kind of wild plant.

versions.title: Map polish
versions.notes:
- The map (M) follows you as you walk with it open, and your dot moves live. Drag to look around; "Center on me" snaps back. It still zooms with the wheel.
- The map and minimap are sharp now: each tile is a crisp square instead of a blur.
- A Smog checkbox on the map shows or hides the smog haze.
- Crate windows: click an item to put 1 in, Shift-click for 10, right-click for all of it.
- Saves show the in-game day they were made on.

versions.title: Sound and music
versions.notes:
- Sound effects for building, taking apart, crafting, salvaging, mining, harvesting, selling, menu clicks, mistakes, and achievements.
- Birds sing now and then when you're on green land in daylight.
- A gentle music loop plays (it fades in a few seconds after the game loads).
- Pause menu: Music and Sounds volume sliders (remembered).

**Limitations:** All sounds are generated by the game itself, so they're simple for now.

versions.title: Help, commands, achievements
versions.notes:
- Help menu (H, or the Help button): basics and controls, building, farming, power and smog, money, co-op, commands, and a list of every item ID.
- Console (/ or T): /give ITEM_ID [X] gives you items (e.g. /give iron_plate 50); /help lists commands. Using a command marks the save as "commands used" for good, shown top left and on the load screen. Works in co-op.
- 16 achievements, from "First seed sown" to "Valley in bloom", each with the day and date you earned it. See them in Help, or Pause menu, then Achievements.

**Limitations:** Achievements count from this version on; earlier progress like crops planted isn't counted.

versions.title: Worlds and saves
versions.notes:
- New Game asks for a world name (a random one is suggested) and a seed: a number, any words, or blank for random. The same seed gives the same valley.
- The Load and Save screens group saves by world, showing each world's seed.
- Each world has three autosave slots that take turns, so an autosave never overwrites your most recent one. Quicksaves and exit saves are per world too.
- Pause menu: choose how often to autosave (off, 1, 2, 5, 10, or 15 minutes).

**Limitations:** Saves from before this version show under "Older saves".

versions.title: Foresters, chain crafting, fair sales
versions.notes:
- Forester (2×2): an automated tree farm. Give it saplings; it plants them on bare ground within 4 tiles, cuts grown trees for 4 wood each, and replants. Take the wood out with an inserter.
- Crafting fills in the gaps: click a recipe even if you only have the raw materials and it crafts the planks, gears, and so on it needs first. The tip says what else it'll make.
- Fixed: selling a stack at the dock by hand paid less than the price shown, because the price dropped with every item. Hand sales now pay the quoted price for the whole batch; the market price drops afterwards.
- The dock window sells 1, 10, 100, 1000, or all of an item, showing the payout before you click. Belts and inserters still sell each item at the market price as it arrives.

versions.title: Burner age
versions.notes:
- Coal: new ore patches (one near the start). Coal is the best fuel (8 MJ) but burns very dirty: 2.5× smog. Wood (0.6×) and crops (0.4×) burn clean but take farming.
- Stone Furnace (5 stone): smelts ore and stone with fuel, no power. It picks its recipe from the ore you give it (the Smelter does too now).
- Burner Inserter (1 gear + 1 plank): slower, runs on fuel, and grabs fuel for itself from what it handles when it runs low.
- Burner Drill: mines on fuel at half a Drill's speed.
- Burner buildings show their fuel and "No fuel" when empty; smog from them depends on what they burn.
- New games start with a Biomass Burner, a Stone Furnace, Burner Inserters, and more wood. Solar Panels are now a shop unlock ($150); the Biomass Burner is available from the start.

**Limitations:** Games that already have solar panels keep the solar unlock.

versions.title: Factorio rules for items
versions.notes:
- Farm Towers, Mills, Prep Tables, Ovens, and Smelters keep what they make until an inserter (or you) takes it out. They no longer push it out the front, so their facing doesn't matter. Drills still drop ore in front of them.
- Inserters drop onto belts like in Factorio: from the side onto the far lane; along the belt (with it or against it) onto the right lane.
- Fixed: an inserter without power used to grab an item and then freeze holding it. Now it waits, and shows "No power".
- Inserters dip down to grab and drop and lift as they swing.
- The Mill is a windmill: it runs on the wind with no power (faster when it's windy).
- You can't build something solid on top of yourself (or a co-op friend).

**Limitations:** Older factories that relied on machines pushing their output onto belts need inserters now.

versions.title: Trees and power charts
versions.notes:
- Fully grown trees look different: bigger, with a full dark canopy and blossoms. Young trees stay small and light green. Pointing at one says how grown it is.
- Taking apart a fully grown planted tree gives 4 wood (a young one gives the sapling back).
- Open a building, then open your inventory (E) next to it: Shift-click an item, or drag it onto the building's window, to put it in. The Farm Tower's seed buttons are gone in favor of this.
- Power windows (poles, generators, batteries) have line charts: demand vs. supply, satisfaction, and production by source (solar, wind, burners, batteries), over the last 5 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, or 60 min.

**Limitations:** Chart history starts when you load the game; it isn't saved.

versions.title: Clearer menus
versions.notes:
- Hover tips now always appear to the right of what you're pointing at (or to the left near the screen edge), and show more: what it is, what it does, and how to use it.
- The crafting menu is a grid of icons grouped into Materials, Logistics, Farming, Seeds, Processing, Electricity, and Home. Hover a recipe for its name, crafting time, and ingredients (with how many you have); faded icons are ones you can't afford yet.
- Fixed: scrolling past the end of the crafting list (or any menu) no longer zooms the camera.
- Fixed: machine recipes showed little boxes with numbers (an arrow the font couldn't draw). They now read "1 Dough from 2 Flour".
- Power poles no longer block walking.

versions.title: Building comfort
versions.notes:
- Hold right-click to take a building apart (a short moment, quicker for belts), so a stray click no longer removes things.
- Placing an inserter shows a big yellow arrow on the inserter's own tile, drawn over everything, so the building it feeds can't hide it.
- Your hotbar is yours: 10 slots (keys 1–0). Drag buildings or items onto it from the inventory, drag slots to swap them, right-click to empty one. Item slots put the item on your cursor. Newly unlocked buildings fill an empty slot. The layout is remembered.
- Crate windows have a "Put in from your inventory" grid (click: all of that item, Shift-click: 10), handy for loading crates for inserters.
- Farm Tower (and Drill) windows call their output "Products (ready to be grabbed)".

versions.title: Saves
versions.notes:
- F5 quicksaves into its own Quicksave slot; F9 loads it.
- Leaving a game saves it automatically into an "Exit save" slot: quitting to the title, starting a new game, closing the window, or closing or hiding the browser tab. Continue picks it up.
- Quicksaves, autosaves, and exit saves no longer rename your game.
- The Load list can be sorted newest first or by name.

versions.title: Map, minimap, and power info
versions.notes:
- The map (M) now scrolls (drag) and zooms (mouse wheel), and shows co-op farmers too.
- A minimap in the top-right corner shows the land around you. N hides or shows it.
- Click a power pole (or any generator or battery) to see its whole network: power supplied vs. wanted, how satisfied it is, what each kind of generator is making, battery charge, and how many machines are working.
- Holding a pole shows green wires to every pole it would link to, and says how many.

versions.title: Co-op
versions.notes:
- Play together in the browser: open the pause menu and choose Host Co-op, then share the room code or the invite link. Friends type the code on the title screen (or just open the link).
- Everything is shared: the farm, buildings, inventory, crafting queue, money, unlocks, and the explored map. Each player has their own farmer, shown with a name tag and a colored ring.
- Sleeping speeds up time once everyone is asleep.
- The game never pauses in co-op. Only the host autosaves; anyone can save a copy.

**Limitations:** Co-op needs the web version and the signaling server (see README). The host's browser tab must stay visible, and very strict networks may need a TURN server.

versions.title: Ready for multiplayer
versions.notes:
- Behind the scenes: everything you do (build, remove, craft, salvage, set recipes, buy) is now a command applied between game ticks. Two copies of the game given the same commands stay exactly in step, which is what co-op will use.
- The game can snapshot its exact state and check that two copies match.

**Limitations:** No visible changes yet; co-op comes next.

versions.title: Big factories
versions.notes:
- Large factories run much more smoothly. Belts, beds, poles, panels, and other simple buildings are drawn in batches (a 3,400-building test factory went from about 2,600 draw calls to 370).
- Items on belts and crops are only drawn near the camera.
- Belts that are backed up stop costing anything until they can move again.
- If the factory ever gets too big for your computer, the game slows down a little instead of freezing.

versions.title: Pollution
versions.notes:
- Working machines put out smog: Biomass Burners the most, then Smelters and Drills, Ovens, Mills, and a little from Prep Tables. Chimneys puff smoke while they work.
- Smog drifts to nearby land and slowly fades. Green tiles, planted beds, and trees soak it up.
- Thick smog turns the ground grey, withers grass (shrinking your greenery bonus), and slows crops.
- New: Tree Saplings (2 wood). They grow into trees in 90 s; trees green the land around them and soak up a lot of smog.
- The air where you stand is shown top left; machine windows say how much smog they make; the map shows smog as grey haze.

versions.title: Bloomworks and inserters
versions.notes:
- The game has a name: Bloomworks. Your saves carry over.
- Inserters: an arm that takes items from the tile behind it and swings them to the tile in front (the arrow). It works with belts, crates, machines, Farm Towers, burners, and docks, and only picks up what the target can use right now.
- Click an inserter to give it a filter (one item only). Long Inserters (shop, $80) reach two tiles each way.
- Inserters use a little power (8 kW, 12 for long ones) while they move. You start with 4.

versions.title: Exploration
versions.notes:
- New games have a much bigger valley (160×160), covered in fog until you walk near it. You can only build on land you've seen.
- Ruined farmsteads out in the valley: rich piles of salvage that sometimes turn up gears and plates, around an old seed cache with seeds and money inside.
- M (or the Map button) opens a map of what you've explored: green land, ore, caches, your buildings, and you.
- New Tools tab in the Shop: Work Gloves (salvage twice as fast), Pickaxe (mine ore three times as fast), Trail Boots (walk 40% faster), Lantern (see farther).
- Building icons are now little pictures of the buildings themselves.

**Limitations:** Older saves keep their smaller map, fully revealed.

versions.title: Sleep
versions.notes:
- You start with a Farmhouse just north of the clearing (more can be crafted).
- From evening on, press Z near your house (or click it) to sleep: time runs 12× faster while your farm keeps working, and you wake at sunrise. Any key wakes you early.

versions.title: Market supply and demand
versions.notes:
- Every item you ship lowers that item's price a little (down to a quarter); prices recover over a few minutes. Shipping a mix pays better than flooding one thing.
- Each morning brings market news: one item is wanted (its price climbs toward double) and one is in glut (it sinks toward 60%).
- The Shop's new Market tab shows every price, whether it's rising or falling, and a chart of the last few minutes.

versions.title: Shipping, money, and progression
versions.notes:
- Shipping Dock (2×2): belt crops and food into it to sell them. Cooked food is worth far more than raw crops (a pizza sells for $28, wheat for $1). You start with one and $30.
- The Shop (B, or the button at the top): buy seed packs, unlock recipes (sauce, salad, cornbread, tart, pizza, and more) and machinery (Smelter, Drill, Oven, Iron Pole, Wind Turbine, Biomass Burner, Battery, Pylon).
- Locked recipes show in machine windows as "locked (shop)"; locked buildings stay off the hotbar and out of crafting until you unlock them.
- Click the dock to see current prices and sell straight from your inventory.

**Limitations:** Saves from earlier versions have everything unlocked.

versions.title: Power
versions.notes:
- Day and night: a day lasts 8 minutes. Nights are darker but still easy to see.
- Farm Towers, Mills, Prep Tables, Ovens, Smelters, and Drills now need electricity. Without enough they slow down; with none they stop and show "No power".
- Generators: Solar Panels (60 kW in full sun), Wind Turbines (up to 40 kW, day and night), Biomass Burners (120 kW from wood, planks, crops, or seeds when the others fall short), and Batteries (store 6 MJ for the night).
- Poles: Wooden Poles (7-tile reach, power a 5×5 area), Iron Poles (10 tiles, 7×7), Pylons (28 tiles for long runs). Holding or pointing at a pole shows the area it powers; wires hang between linked poles.
- Click any powered building to see its network: power used, wanted, and battery charge.
- New games start with a Solar Panel, a Battery, and 4 Wooden Poles.

**Limitations:** Older saves keep working, but their machines need poles and power.

versions.title: Mining
versions.notes:
- Ore patches: iron, copper, and stone. There's one of each 13–18 tiles from the start, and bigger ones farther out.
- Hold right-click on bare ore to mine it by hand (1 s each).
- Drill (2×2): place it on a patch to mine the ore under it and send it out the front.
- Smelter (2×2): iron ore to iron plate, copper ore to copper plate, 2 stone to brick, 3 scrap to iron plate.
- Gears are made from iron plates (or from scrap, as before). Ovens now take bricks and iron plates.

**Limitations:** Copper plates are for power, coming next.

versions.title: Different plants
versions.notes:
- Five new crops: tomato, potato, lettuce, strawberry, and corn, each with its own look, grow time, and harvest.
- Wild plants grow out in the valley (rarer ones farther from the start). Hold right-click on one to gather its seeds. Any crop can also be crafted into 2 seeds.
- Farm Towers can be set to one crop or "any seeds".
- New recipes: cornmeal (Mill); tomato sauce, salad, raw pizza (Prep Table); baked potato, cornbread, pizza, strawberry tart (Oven).

versions.title: Named saves and loads
versions.notes:
- Save your game under any name from the pause menu, overwrite an old save, or load and delete saves (delete asks twice).
- F5 quick-saves under the current name. The game autosaves every 5 minutes.
- The title screen has Continue (your latest save) and Load Game.

versions.title: Processing machines
versions.notes:
- Mill (2×2): wheat into flour. Prep Table (1×1): flour into dough. Oven (2×2): dough into bread.
- Machines take ingredients from belts pointing into any side and push results out the front: onto a belt, into a crate, or straight into the next machine.
- Click a machine to pick its recipe, add ingredients from your inventory, watch progress, and take output.
- Machines run faster with the greenery bonus. The Mill's sails turn and the Oven glows while they work.

versions.title: Automated farming and greening
versions.notes:
- Garden Beds: plant seeds by hand (hold seeds and click), click a ripe bed to harvest. Each harvest gives crops and the seed back.
- Farm Tower (2×2): give it seeds and it plants every garden bed within 3 tiles, harvests when ripe, replants, and sends crops out the front onto a belt or into a crate.
- Plants bring the land back: tiles around planted beds turn green, and green spreads a fading halo to its neighbors. Dead trees on green ground come back to life.
- Greenery bonus: every green tile speeds up plants and machines, up to +100% at 1,500 tiles. It's shown top left.
- Wheat seeds can be crafted from wheat. You start with a Farm Tower, 12 beds, and 12 seeds.

**Limitations:** Wheat has no use yet besides more wheat.

versions.title: Conveyor belts
versions.notes:
- Belts carry items on two lanes, side by side. Items keep their lane from belt to belt and around curves.
- A belt pointing into the side of another puts its items on that belt's near lane.
- Belts feed whatever they point at: a crate fills up (400 items) and a full one backs the line up.
- Click an item in the inventory to hold it, then click a belt to drop one on the lane you clicked (Shift for more), or a crate to put it in.
- Click a crate to see inside and take things out. F picks up everything on the belt under the cursor.

**Limitations:** Nothing produces items onto belts yet except you.

versions.title: Inventory and hand crafting
versions.notes:
- Hold right-click on rubble, dead trees, and rocks within reach to salvage scrap, wood, and stone.
- E opens the inventory and crafting. Recipes take time; Shift-click crafts five.
- The craft queue runs down the left side of the screen. Click an entry to cancel it and get the ingredients back.
- Buildings now cost items: you start with 10 belts and 2 crates. Removing a building gives it back.

**Limitations:** Belts still don't carry anything.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- A dried-out valley full of rubble, dead trees, and rocks, with a clearing in the middle.
- Walk the farmer with WASD or the arrow keys; scroll to zoom.
- Pick a building from the bar (1-9), see a preview where it would go (green fits, red doesn't), press R to turn it, click to place. Drag to lay belts in a line.
- Right-click removes a building. Q empties your hand, or picks up the building under the cursor.

**Limitations:** Belts don't carry anything yet and buildings are free.

versions.title: TURN relay and joining spinner
versions.notes:
- Players on strict networks (phone data, some campus or work Wi-Fi) can now connect through a TURN relay when a direct link is blocked.
- A spinner shows while hosting or joining, with a Cancel button; Host and Join are disabled until it finishes.
- The connection timeout message now reminds you to keep the host's tab visible.

**Limitations:** TURN credentials are built into the game, so anyone can read them. Relayed connections add some latency.

versions.title: Names and custom room codes
versions.notes:
- Pick a name in the lobby; it shows above your player and in the HUD player list, and is remembered next time.
- The host can choose the room code (2-12 letters or numbers), or leave it blank for a random one.

**Limitations:** Custom room codes need the updated signaling server; an older server ignores the choice and hands out a random code.

versions.title: First release
versions.notes:
- Top-down co-op against waves of zombies for up to 8 players, in the browser.
- Host a room for a 4-letter code or an invite link; friends join over WebRTC (peer to peer).
- Signaling runs on Render (godotwebrtc.onrender.com) for https builds.
- Press I to toggle smoothing of other players and zombies.

**Limitations:** STUN only (no TURN), so strict NAT/CGNAT may not connect. The host's tab must stay visible. No rejoin after a refresh.

versions.title: Co-op rules
versions.notes:
- Double honk: when both geese honk within a second of each other, the second honk reaches twice as far and stuns half as long again.
- A bonked goose lies down for 30 seconds instead of going home; the other goose holds E next to it for 4 seconds to help it up with 30 health. Nobody comes: it is bonked for real.
- Each goose gets its own results. A host who gets out first waits (out of sight) until the friend is out or bonked; closing time catches whoever is still in.
- No dares in a raid together, and the lobby only starts normal raids (no Daily or Lost Gosling runs). The friend's stash is saved on their own computer from the host's word on what came home.

versions.title: Co-op: two geese
versions.notes:
- Co-op on the title screen: Host a raid for a room code and an invite link, or Join with a friend's code (or open their link). It uses the same signaling server as the other WebRTC games.
- The host's game runs the raid with a second goose, driven by the friend; the friend brings their own Nest loadout and sees the host's goose, the critters, dropped loot and opened containers. Critters go after whichever goose is nearer.
- The friend's E grabs loot or empties a container straight into its bag. Each goose gets out through any exit on its own; when the host gets out, a friend still in the raid comes home with them. The pause menu doesn't stop a raid together.
- First version: shots from the other goose and some events (gulls, carts, the cat) only show on the host's screen for now.

versions.title: Grid backpack
versions.notes:
- New setting, Backpack: Weight / Grid. On Grid, items take their own shape on the backpack grid (4x3, 5x4 or 6x4 by bag level): bats and baguettes 1x2, watermelons, gnomes, bowling balls and batteries 2x2. Weight still counts.
- The raid backpack and the Nest show the grid: drag an item to move it, R turns the picked one, click an empty cell to move the picked item there, and Auto-arrange (Arrange in the Nest) lays it all out biggest first.
- When nothing fits, pickups say No room on the grid; anything left without a place (after switching the setting on) waits under the grid and is never lost.

versions.title: Grid backpack: shapes
versions.notes:
- Groundwork for the optional grid backpack (the setting arrives next version): items have shapes. Bats, the Putter, the Rolled Newspaper, Baguettes and the Balloon Lobber take 1x2; the Watermelon, Garden Gnome, Bowling Ball and Car Battery take 2x2.
- The backpack grid is 4x3, 5x4 or 6x4 by bag level, with first-fit placing, turning and auto-arrange. Weight still counts.
- The packed loadout remembers where each item sits; old saves auto-arrange, and nothing that does not fit is ever lost (it stays in the bag, unplaced).

versions.title: Golden Goose
versions.notes:
- Retire your goose once it has brought home 50,000 crumbs' worth: the Hall of Geese on the Stats tab gets a plaque (name, crumbs, raids, heirloom), and a fresh goose starts out with one heirloom stack from the stash.
- Retiring resets crumbs, the stash and loadout, upgrades, perks, feathers, weapon mods, quests and trader levels, the Bread garden, the gosling and insurance. The Goosepedia, badges, stats, map unlocks, decor, name and scarf stay.
- Every retired goose adds 3% to sell prices for good (up to five geese, +15%).
- Retire asks twice before it happens.

**Limitations:** The Hall of Geese lives on the Stats tab (the Nest's tab row is full) and shows the last two plaques.

versions.title: Gosling sidekick
versions.notes:
- After 5 extractions Mom Goose sells a Gosling backpack (300 crumbs). From then on a small yellow gosling follows you on raids (a Bring/Leave button on her page switches it; it never comes on Lost Gosling runs or the Daily).
- It carries its own little bag, 4 slots and 2 kg, shown under the secure pouch in the backpack screen: To gosling / To backpack move things across. Its bag comes home with you when you get out.
- It peeps "!" when a critter comes within 12 m. It has 30 health: at 0 it puffs home (no loss) and its bag drops where it stood.
- The biggest backpack shows five slots across, so the backpack screen still fits with the gosling's row.

**Limitations:** Critters don't aim at the gosling, but their shots can hit it.

versions.title: Insurance
versions.notes:
- The Crow sells insurance: select a packed stack or weapon in the Nest and Insure it for 25% of its worth (at least 20 crumbs). One policy at a time, for the next raid.
- Get bonked with it and it comes back to your stash two raids later (the Crow's page on Home shows what's coming). It isn't offered at Lost Property, since it's coming back anyway. Getting out ends the policy.
- If a rival goose was within 20 m when you went down, the policy doesn't pay.

**Limitations:** Lost Gosling runs and the tour don't use or end a policy.

versions.title: Hot items and the Bread garden
versions.notes:
- Hot items: every day three junk or valuable items sell for double and one sells for half. The Crow's page lists today's prices, and item details say HOT or cold.
- Mom Goose plants a Bread garden: level 1 (250 crumbs) grows 2 Bread Crusts after every raid, level 2 (600) adds a Pretzel, level 3 (1200) a Half Sandwich. It grows whether you got out or got bonked, so you're never without a snack. The results screen says what it grew.

**Limitations:** Hot items follow your computer's date.

versions.title: Decoy goose
versions.notes:
- Make a Decoy Goose at the Workbench: 3 Bent Spoons, 2 Lost Socks, a Rubber Duck and 40 crumbs.
- In a raid, G sets it down 2 m ahead. Any critter that spots it walks over and stares at it, confused, for 5 s (each critter falls for it once, and doesn't look for you while it stares). It falls over after 3 critters or a minute.
- The Workbench lays weapons out in two columns so the whole list fits on screen (the Putter had pushed the Kazoo Cannon off the bottom).

**Limitations:** Possums don't care about decoys.

versions.title: Wanted: Big Tony
versions.notes:
- A Wanted board on the Nest's Quests tab. First up: Big Tony, a big raccoon in a gold chain (180 health) who turns up in about a third of raids once you've extracted 5 times, always with two raccoon bodyguards close by.
- The opening banner says which area his chain jingles in. Get within 20 m (or into a fight with him) and you've heard him: from then on he pings on the minimap every 20 s.
- Bonk him for a one-time 600-crumb bounty, his Gold Chain and two valuables. Once claimed, he doesn't come back.

**Limitations:** Big Tony is the only wanted critter so far.

versions.title: Golf carts and FORE!
versions.notes:
- Two golf carts loop the Golf Course's cart path at 5 m/s, honking 2 s before every corner and crossing. One that runs into you bumps you 3 m and hurts (8); critters get bumped too. They show as white dots on the minimap.
- Stray golf balls: every 20 to 35 seconds someone shouts FORE! and a shadow grows on the ground for 1.2 s before the ball comes down. Out in the open it lands near you; it hits for 15 within 1 m, then lies there as a Golf Ball you can pick up. Indoors you're safe. A tip the first time.
- The seagull tip is shorter, so it fits on the screen.

**Limitations:** The carts drive the loop only, not the spurs, and don't stop for anything.

versions.title: Golf Course
versions.notes:
- A fourth map, the Golf Course, unlocked after 3 extractions from the boardwalk: three wide-open fairways with hardly any cover, four sand traps that slow you to 60%, two ponds you can swim in, the clubhouse (lockers, a bar, and a Pro Shop behind a locked door; the Pro Shop Key turns up in golf course containers), the cart barn and a driving range. A cart path loops the course.
- Exits: Car Park (where you arrive), Cart Path Gate, Maintenance Shed, 18th Green and Groundskeeper's Truck.
- New things to find there: Trophies, Golf Gloves, Club Sandwiches, and the Putter, a melee weapon with a long reach.
- Fixed: the arcade's Prize Room on the boardwalk had no doorway, so even with the Prize Key you couldn't get in.

**Limitations:** No golf carts or stray balls yet (next).

versions.title: Seagulls and the tide
versions.notes:
- Seagulls on the boardwalk: with food in the backpack and no roof over you, one dives every 25 to 40 seconds. Its shadow grows on the ground and it screeches 2 s first; then it steals your cheapest food. Duck indoors (the arcade, fry stand or bait shop), roll at the last moment, or honk, which keeps them off for 20 s. A tip the first time they circle.
- The tide comes in at 5:00 on the clock: the Lifeguard Tower and Rock Pool exits say so in the exit list and on the map, a whistle and banner warn 20 s before, then the sea comes 6 m up the beach and those two exits close.

**Limitations:** The tide comes in once a raid and doesn't go back out.

versions.title: Seaside Boardwalk
versions.notes:
- A third map, the Seaside Boardwalk, unlocked after 3 extractions from the suburb: the arcade (with a Prize Room behind a locked door; the Prize Key turns up in boardwalk containers), the fry stand, the bait shop, the boardwalk itself, a pier out over the sea, and the beach, where sand slows you to 85%.
- The sea runs along the top of the map and you can swim in it (6 kg or less). The pier's railings are low enough to flap over.
- Exits: Beach Car Park (where you arrive), Pier End, Lifeguard Tower, Rock Pool and Under the Pier.
- New things to find there: Saltwater Taffy, Arcade Tickets, Shell Necklaces and Beach Balls.

**Limitations:** No seagulls or tide yet (next). Rival geese stay in the suburb.

versions.title: Cat on the fence
versions.notes:
- Suburb: a ginger cat sits on the garden fences. Once it has seen you it follows along the fence tops, hopping from fence to fence, and the second time it spots you it yowls: critters within 18 m come to where you are (and again every 15 s while it can see you).
- It can't be hurt: a shot just makes it hop along. A fully charged honk sends it off for 20 s.
- New item, the Tin of Tuna (in a couple of suburb bins, crates and coolers). Toss it near the cat (X tosses the tuna first when the cat is close) and it's your friend for the raid: no more yowling, and it purrs when a critter comes within 12 m. A tip on first sight.

**Limitations:** The cat only walks fences (not walls or roofs), and the tuna isn't in the regular loot tables yet, only placed at raid start.

versions.title: Possums
versions.notes:
- Possums: three per raid on either map, lying "bonked" on the paths with a tail that twitches now and then. Walk within 2 m and one gets up (after a moment) to chase and bite (12) for 6 s, then wanders off to play dead somewhere else.
- A honk, a shot or other noise within 8 m, or a hit, gets it up early. Bonked for real, it drops a little stash of found things.
- A tip the first time you get within 6 m of one.

**Limitations:** Possums don't use sight cones at all; hiding next to one doesn't wake it.

versions.title: Drag heavy loot
versions.notes:
- Drag heavy loot: when grabbing a heavy item (3 kg or more) would take the backpack over its weight limit, E drags it in your beak instead. It trails behind you all the way to an exit, and extracting with it adds it to the haul.
- Dragging is slow (2.5 m/s), with no sprinting, rolling, swimming or shooting, and the scrape is heard 10 m away. E lets go; a hit knocks it out of your beak.
- The backpack line on the HUD says what you're dragging. A tip the first time you're offered a drag.

**Limitations:** Only items lying on the ground can be dragged (drop one from a container first). One at a time.

versions.title: Hide
versions.notes:
- Hide: press E by a bush, one of the three big cardboard boxes on each map, or a searched, empty bin, and the goose crouches in with its tail poking out. Critters can't see a hidden goose from more than 1.5 m away, and an eye icon by the puff bar says you're hidden.
- Critters that were onto you when you went in come over to check the spot; one that pokes about up close for 2 s finds you ("Found you!").
- Moving, shooting or honking comes out where you went in. A tip the first time you're by a hiding spot.

**Limitations:** Curb bins only count once they're searched and empty (E on a full bin still searches it).

versions.title: Swim
versions.notes:
- Geese swim: with 6 kg or less in the backpack, waddle into the Duck Pond (or the paddling pool) and paddle at 3.2 m/s. No sprinting, rolling or shooting in the water, no footsteps to hear, and critters spot a swimming goose at 60% of their usual range.
- Critters won't follow you in (they can still shoot from the bank), so the pond is a real escape route.
- Over 6 kg the water stops you: "Too heavy to swim (6 kg)". A tip the first time you're near water.

**Limitations:** Ducks don't react to a swimming goose yet. Bonked in the water, the goose stays sunk.

versions.title: Gamepad
versions.notes:
- Gamepad support: left stick to waddle (click it to run), right stick to aim (up to 8 m out from the goose; it holds its aim when you let go), RT shoot, LT honk (hold to charge), A roll, B search/grab, X reload, Y snack, LB/RB weapons, the D-pad for emote, sneak, toss and throw, Start pause, Back map, R3 backpack.
- Once you use the pad, prompts and the controls hint name pad buttons; a key or click switches them back.

**Limitations:** Pad buttons are fixed (the Settings key grid is keyboard only). Menus are still best with the mouse.

versions.title: Text size and colour-blind setting
versions.notes:
- Settings: Text size Normal/Large. Large makes the raid HUD, prompts, the backpack and loot panels and the results a quarter bigger; the Nest gets slightly bigger text (its layout is full).
- Settings: Colour-blind On swaps the rarity colours for a set anyone can tell apart (Okabe-Ito), and outlines the hit arrows and the low-health pulse in white. The rarity shapes from v0.1.60 help too.

**Limitations:** Buttons keep their size; only labels grow.

versions.title: Rarity glints and shapes
versions.notes:
- Every rarity has a shape as well as a colour: circle (Common), triangle (Uncommon), diamond (Rare), star (Epic), crown (Legendary). It's on the top-left corner of every item slot and floats over loot on the ground.
- Uncommon-and-up loot on the ground glints in its rarity colour every 2-3 seconds, and so does an open container with a good find showing.

versions.title: Sleepy critters
versions.notes: - Critters far away (over 40 m) that you can't see now think a quarter as often, which saves time on busy maps. They keep walking in between, and a sound or a hit wakes them up at once.

versions.title: Performance pass and Low graphics
versions.notes:
- Faster maps: tree trunks and bushes are drawn in one batch each, and the map's shapes share their meshes (about 20% fewer things to draw and far fewer meshes in memory). Tree tops that fade when you walk behind them work as before.
- Hit puffs are capped at 60 at once, and dynamic lights (the ranger's flashlight, the garbage truck) at 4.
- Settings: Graphics High/Low. Low turns off shadows, the sunset tint and the rain (puddles still slow you).

versions.title: First-raid tutorial
versions.notes:
- How to Play on the title starts Mom Goose's tour: a guided Picnic Park raid with no clock, a picnic basket right by you, one gnome and only the Bus Stop open. Mom Goose's speech bubble walks you through waddling, searching, taking, honking, bonking and getting out.
- The first time a fresh save enters the Nest, Mom Goose offers the tour (Show me or Skip). It's nothing-to-lose like a Lost Gosling run; Esc then Give Up skips it. Finishing it the first time banks the haul plus 50 crumbs.

versions.title: Extraction moment and park ambience
versions.notes:
- Extracting now plays a short moment before the results: the goose hops in the Mail Truck, the Ice Cream Van or the bus and drives off, paddles away in the Duck Boat, climbs the Tree House Rope, or squeezes out through a gap. 2.5 seconds; click or press any key to skip. Your haul is already saved when it starts.
- Ambient sound under the raid music: birdsong around you in Picnic Park (quiet on Fireworks Night) and cars going by in the Suburb. It's off when the music is off.

versions.title: Garbage Day and the robot lawnmower
versions.notes:
- Garbage Day (Suburb only, +40 crumbs): six extra wheelie bins on the curb, each with a double roll of trash. The garbage truck drives up the road and round the turning circle twice; it beeps and sweeps its headlights for 5 seconds first, then shoves anything in its way 3 m for 10 damage (a roll dodges it).
- A modifier that can't happen on the picked map (Garbage Day in Picnic Park) makes that raid a normal day, and the Raid button doesn't show it.
- A robot lawnmower mows the Suburb's west Front Lawns in stripes at 1.6 m/s. Cut stripes go lighter and the next lane is marked; its whirr carries 15 m. Bump into it and it pushes you back 2 m and shreds one snack from your backpack. A tip the first time you see it.

**Limitations:** The truck and mower don't show on the minimap.

versions.title: Wasp nests and muddy footprints
versions.notes:
- Three trees in Picnic Park have a wasp nest that hums (you hear it from 10 m; a tip the first time). A shot or a honk lets the swarm out: it chases whatever's nearest, goose or critter, for 8 seconds, stinging for 3 a second. A roll may shake it off, and it gives up at the pond's edge.
- Rainy Day: walking through a puddle muddies your feet for 10 seconds, leaving footprints that fade over 20. An idle raccoon that finds the prints follows them to the newest one. "Muddy feet! Raccoons can follow your prints." the first time.

versions.title: Off-leash dog
versions.notes:
- The off-leash dog (some raids, once between 1:30 and 8:00): distant barking and a banner, and its route shows dotted on the minimap for 6 seconds. Then a golden retriever with a frisbee bounds across the map at 9 m/s.
- It bowls over anything within 1.2 m for a second (the goose too; no damage; a roll dodges it), and its barking brings critters within 12 m to look.

**Limitations:** The dog runs along open ground but doesn't stop for anything.

versions.title: Ice cream van and the raccoon party
versions.notes:
- The ice cream van (Picnic Park, most raids, once between 2:00 and 7:00): a jingle plays from the Parking Lot and for 30 seconds every raccoon that isn't already fighting you drops everything and queues at the van, not looking for geese. A banner says so and an ice cream cone with a countdown sits by the clock.
- Raccoon birthday parties (either map, some raids): bunting, balloons and three raccoons in party hats around a Birthday Cake, a container with a big roll. The opening banner names the area and party music plays within 20 m. Shoot a balloon to pop it and the party raccoons all look up for 2 seconds.

versions.title: Windy Day and Heatwave
versions.notes:
- Windy Day (+40 crumbs): leaves blow across the screen and mask your footsteps (critters hear them at 70% of the usual range), but foam darts and water balloons drift with the wind. A striped wind sock by the clock shows which way it blows.
- Heatwave (+50 crumbs): puff comes back half as fast in the sun and at full speed in the darker shade under trees; Ice Pops in the backpack melt 4 minutes in; water balloons hit 30% harder.
- The Daily Raid's opening banner is shorter, so it fits the screen.

versions.title: Kits
versions.notes:
- A Kits button in the Nest's Bringing column: save the current loadout (weapons, backpack, secure pouch, worn armor and dares) as one of three named kits, like "Cheap run" or "Ranger hunt".
- Loading a kit puts the current loadout back in the stash and packs the kit from what the stash has. Anything missing is listed, with a "Buy missing and pack" button showing the total.
- Fix: the Daily button no longer changes to "Daily done" (which pushed the Nest past the screen's right edge); it greys out and its tooltip says it's done for today.

**Limitations:** Kits remember armor by type, not its durability; items no trader sells at your level can't be bought in one click.

versions.title: Lost Property and scratch tickets
versions.notes:
- Lost Property: after a bonk, each stack you lost (backpack, weapons, worn armor, never the Golden Bread) has a 30% chance to turn up on the Crow's page for your next two Nest visits, to buy back at its worth. The Nest tells you what turned up.
- Scratch a Lottery Ticket in the stash instead of selling it: the numbers flicker and land on 0, 20, 80, 200 or 600 crumbs (about 83 on average, so a gamble, not a better deal).

**Limitations:** Lost Gosling and Daily runs don't fill Lost Property (their kit was free).

versions.title: Daily Raid and Snapshot
versions.notes:
- A Daily button in the Nest: once a day, Picnic Park from the date's seed (the same loot, exits and weather for everyone that day) with a fixed kit: a Foam Blaster, 48 darts, three Bread Crusts, a Half Sandwich and a Firecracker. Nothing from the Nest is at risk, perks stay home, and whatever you bring out is yours.
- The results show a shareable line, like "Honk Raid Daily 2026-11-06: OUT via Bus Stop, 412 crumbs, 3 bonks, 6:12", with a Copy button. The score counts what you found, not the kit.
- Your best daily is on the Daily button's tooltip and in the Stats tab.
- A Snapshot button on every results screen saves a 640x360 card with your goose's name, the exit, the crumbs and the best three items (a PNG download in the browser).

**Limitations:** The Daily Raid is always Picnic Park.

versions.title: Badges
versions.notes:
- 23 one-off badges with silly names: BONG! (bonk the Park Ranger with the Frying Pan), Heavy Lifter (extract with a Watermelon, a Bowling Ball and a Car Battery), Pacifist, Clean Getaway, Early Bird, Last Goose Out, Hoarder, Thief, Picklock, Daredevil and more.
- A badge won in the raid pops up in the feed with a chime; ones won by extracting are listed on the results screen.
- A Badges tab in the Nest shows every badge: gold once won, grey with its goal until then.

**Limitations:** Badges start counting from this version.

versions.title: Stats
versions.notes:
- The results screen adds the raid's bonks, shots and metres waddled, and if you got bonked, who did it, where and with what ("Bonked by a Raccoon in the Snack Shack with an Acorn Popper.").
- A Stats tab in the Nest: raids, extraction rate, crumbs' worth brought home, best haul, shots, distance, quests, extractions by map, critters bonked by kind, and the last three times you got bonked.

**Limitations:** Stats start counting from this version.

versions.title: Mail it home, Lost and Found
versions.notes:
- Three mailboxes on the suburb's front paths: with a Stamp, post your best stack weighing up to 1 kg home. It takes 3 seconds, the flag going up is heard 10 m away, and the item is in the stash whatever happens next. Each mailbox posts once a raid.
- Stamps are new junk: in the Big House's containers now and then, and lying by the Mail Truck.
- A Lost and Found box by the arrival exit on both maps wants one item each raid (it's on the box and in the exit list). Hand it in for three times its worth (at least 50 crumbs), banked and saved on the spot.

versions.title: Picking locks
versions.notes:
- No key? One Paperclip will do. Press E at a locked door to pick it: a marker sweeps a bar, and you press E (or click) while it's in the green, three times in a row.
- Miss and the paperclip snaps with a loud crack that critters 16 m away hear. Every click is heard 12 m away, and stepping away stops you.
- A successful pick keeps the paperclip.

versions.title: Quick hands, good timing
versions.notes:
- Hold Shift and click Take All to leave the junk behind.
- A Crumbs/kg box on the loot panel puts the most valuable-for-its-weight finds first. It remembers your choice.
- Quick Getaway: get out within the first 4 minutes for 15% of your haul's worth in crumbs.
- Last Goose Out: get out with under 30 seconds on the clock for 25%.

versions.title: Decorate the Nest
versions.notes:
- A Decorate tab: name your goose (up to 16 letters) and pick one of 8 scarf colours.
- A shelf across the top of the Nest for up to 6 pieces. Put up junk and valuables from the stash (they're used up, but come back if you take them down), or buy shelf-only pieces like the Lava Lamp and Framed Bread.
- Your goose's name shows when you arrive, on the results screen, and in the Nest; a Lost Gosling run is "Name Jr.".

versions.title: Quests
versions.notes:
- A Quests tab in the Nest: each trader has one job for you at a time. Bring them some things, bonk a few gnomes or raccoons (sometimes with a particular weapon), get out by a certain exit, or get out of a map with a big enough haul.
- Bonks and exits count in any raid; bring the items home and hand them in on the tab. Rewards are 80 to 400 crumbs and 150 XP with that trader, and one quest in six adds a rare item.
- Your quests show under the exits during a raid, with progress.
- The Nest's tab row is a bit more compact to make room.

versions.title: Traders
versions.notes:
- The Shop is now three traders. Mom Goose sells snacks and the bag, stash and pouch upgrades. Barry the Badger sells weapons, ammo, throwables and armor. The Crow buys junk and valuables for 25% more and sells keys.
- Every crumb you trade with someone is a point of their XP. Level 2 at 500 and level 3 at 1500: 5% better prices each level, and more stock (Mom's pretzels and pies, Barry's bigger ammo packs, the Crow's Lottery Tickets and the Ranger's Keyring).
- Selling goes to whoever wants it: the Crow takes shiny things and keys, Mom takes food, Barry the rest.

versions.title: The Workbench
versions.notes:
- A Workbench tab in the Nest: upgrade each kind of weapon for crumbs plus junk from the stash.
- Bigger Magazine (+50%, 120 crumbs and 3 Bent Spoons), Faster Reload (-30%, 150 and 5 Paperclips), Tighter Spread (-40%, 200 and 4 Bottle Caps). Melee weapons and the Kazoo Cannon get Heavier Hits (+15% damage) instead.
- Upgrades belong to the weapon kind, so they stay even if you lose the weapon, and cover any copy you find.

versions.title: Firecrackers and smoke bags
versions.notes:
- G throws the first throwable in your backpack toward the cursor, up to 12 m.
- Firecracker: goes BANG 1.5 seconds after you throw it, and every critter within 20 m comes to see. Great for pulling them away from a container.
- Smoke Bag: a cloud of flour 3.5 m wide for 6 seconds. Nothing sees through it, you included.
- Both stack to 5, turn up in bins and crates, and are in the shop. The Goosepedia has a Throwable shelf.

versions.title: Bubbles, squirts and kazoos
versions.notes:
- Bubble Wand (120 crumbs): slow, wobbly bubbles that halve a critter's speed for 2.5 seconds. Uses Bubble Mix.
- Squirt Gun (100 crumbs): a fast stream of tiny hits from a 40-squirt tank that refills itself in 6 seconds. No ammo needed.
- Kazoo Cannon (180 crumbs): a 4 m cone that hits for 10 and shoves everything back 4 m. No ammo, but everyone within 22 m hears it (and it breaks a Melee Only dare).
- All three, and Bubble Mix, are in the shop and in supply crates.

versions.title: Bread lures and pond ducks
versions.notes:
- X tosses your cheapest snack 4 m ahead (or pick one and press Toss in the backpack). Raccoons and rival geese within 12 m that can see it go and eat it for 4 seconds, too busy to look for geese.
- Four ducks paddle on the Duck Pond. Honk near them and they quack, and critters nearby come to look.
- Toss a bread crust to a duck and it follows you for a minute, quacking whenever a critter comes within 12 m and marking it on the minimap.
- Tips the first time a raccoon is close and the first time you're near the ducks.

versions.title: Charged honks and yoinking
versions.notes:
- Hold Q to charge a honk for up to a second: it reaches farther (8 m), wider, and stuns for 3 seconds. A full charge is heard across the whole map and takes twice as long to recharge. A tap is the usual honk.
- Every critter carries one thing you can see on its back. Sneak right up behind one that hasn't seen you and press E to yoink it. The critter turns round and comes for you (Hey!). Rival geese hand over something from their bag.
- Bonk a critter and what it carried drops too.
- Up close, critters notice a goose whichever way they face, unless it's sneaking.

versions.title: Wing flaps, emotes and idle geese
versions.notes:
- Roll into something low (a bush, a picnic table, a garden fence) and the goose flaps up and over it. The wings need 4 seconds to recover, and if there's nowhere to land it says Too high!
- T emotes: a happy wing-flap wiggle. A critter that sees it stops and stares for a second (once each per raid). The goose does it on its own as an extraction countdown ends.
- Stand still for 8 seconds and the goose preens, looks around, or pecks the ground, sometimes turning up a Bottle Cap or Paperclip. A critter that spots a preening goose says ? and takes a second longer to react.

versions.title: Sneak and the noise meter
versions.notes:
- Sneak: tap C to toggle it, or hold C. 60% speed, silent feet, and critters only spot you at half their usual distance (until they're already fighting you). Sprinting ends it.
- A Noise bar under the puff bar: sprinting fills it, shots and honks add to it, and it drains when you calm down. The noisier you are, the farther critters hear your footsteps.
- The goose crouches low while sneaking, and a tip explains sneaking the first time an unaware critter is close.

versions.title: Tips and a low health warning
versions.notes:
- Tips the first time something matters: too heavy, being spotted, an exit nearby (and a paid one), two minutes left, a locked door. Each shows once, and Settings can turn them off.
- The pigeon and sprinkler hints are tips now too (ones you've seen stay seen).
- Under 25 health: a heartbeat, red pulsing screen edges, and a line saying to eat (if you have a snack) or how far the nearest exit is.

versions.title: Settings
versions.notes:
- A Settings screen on the title and pause menus.
- Rebind any key except pause: two keys per action, and a key another action uses swaps over. Reset keys puts the defaults back. The controls line follows your keys.
- Camera lean slider (0 to 200%), Sound, Music, and Tips toggles.
- Switching tabs or windows mid-raid now pauses it, so tabbing away doesn't get you bonked. Turn it off in Settings if you'd rather not.

**Limitations:** There's no mouse sensitivity setting: you aim with the cursor itself.

versions.title: Armor and hats
versions.notes:
- Armor: a Bike Helmet, a Saucepan, and a Pool Noodle Vest. Each soaks a share of every hit until it's worn out.
- Wear one in the Nest's new Worn slot. Hats replace the goose's helmet, and the vest goes round its middle. A broken piece sits crooked.
- Repair worn armor in the Nest for a crumb a point. The HUD shows how much it has left.
- Sold in the shop and found in crates. Armor comes home when you extract, and stays in the park if you're bonked.
- Found armor can be put on mid-raid from the backpack if you're wearing nothing or yours is broken.

**Limitations:** One piece of armor at a time, so a hat and the vest can't be worn together.

versions.title: Dares
versions.notes:
- Dares: pick up to three in the Nest (the Dares button under the backpack) for a crumb bonus when you extract.
- Melee Only +30%, No Snacks +20%, Light Bag (half the weight limit) +25%, No Honk +15%. Each pays its share of the haul's worth.
- Fire a ranged weapon, eat, or honk and that dare is broken (the feed says so). The results list the dares you kept.
- The Raid button shows the bonus. Lost Gosling runs don't take dares.

versions.title: Goose perks
versions.notes:
- Feathers: every extraction earns one, and a haul worth 300+ crumbs earns a second.
- A Perks tab in the Nest: spend Feathers on six perks that last for good. Big Honk, Quick Beak, Nimble, Strong Back, Fast Eater, and Thick Feathers.
- Your Feathers show next to your crumbs in the Nest.

versions.title: The Goosepedia
versions.notes:
- The Nest has tabs now: Home (stash, bringing, shop) and the Goosepedia.
- The Goosepedia lists every item in the game by category. Ones you've never brought home are grey silhouettes until you extract with one.
- Complete a category for a one-off reward (up to 400 crumbs for every valuable) and a trophy.
- Saves from before this count whatever is already in your stash as found.

versions.title: Stash sorting and search
versions.notes:
- Sort the stash by Newest, Name, Value, Weight, Type, or Crumbs/kg. The Nest remembers your pick.
- Tick Sellable to see only junk and valuables, or type in Search to find an item by name.
- Every item's details now show its worth per kg, so it's easy to see what was worth carrying.

versions.title: Hit feedback
versions.notes:
- Critters flash white and shed bits when hit: ceramic chips from gnomes, fur from raccoons and the Ranger, feathers from rival geese.
- A bonked critter pops with a cartoon star burst and a puff.
- When the goose is hit, its helmet wobbles, and a red arc on the screen edge points toward where the hit came from for a second.

versions.title: Rival geese
versions.notes:
- Rival geese in the Suburb Cul-de-sac: about 5 minutes in, one or two Canada geese with backpacks waddle in far from you. A honk in the distance and a banner warn you.
- They raid containers (emptying them), then head for the nearest exit and leave with their haul. With a minute left, they leave anyway.
- They shoot back ("Mine!"), but bonk one and its whole bag spills out.

**Limitations:** Rival geese don't fight the gnomes or raccoons, and they don't pay for exits.

versions.title: The Park Ranger
versions.notes:
- The Park Ranger: a big bear in a ranger hat who patrols one Picnic Park raid in four. A whistle and a banner warn you when he's on duty.
- He sees far, but only along his flashlight beam, which shows on the grass even when he's out of sight. Honks only dizzy him half as long.
- His Net Launcher tangles the goose for 2 seconds: no waddling, no rolling. Roll before it lands and it misses.
- Bonk him for the Ranger's Keyring (opens both locked rooms, and isn't used up) and a pocketful of good loot.

versions.title: Critter barks
versions.notes:
- Critters speak their minds: "Huh?" when a noise or a hit makes them suspicious, "Goose!" when they spot you, and "Where'd it go?" when they lose you.
- Barks float over critters you can see, so you can tell at a glance who's hunting you. Hidden critters keep quiet.

versions.title: Pigeons
versions.notes:
- Pigeons! Flocks peck along the paths. Walk past and they ignore you, but sprint, roll, shoot, or honk nearby and they burst into the air, and every critter within 20 m comes to see why.
- The first flock you get near comes with a hint: walk past them.

versions.title: Sprinklers
versions.notes:
- Sprinklers in the Picnic Meadow and on the suburb's lawns: about every two minutes they tick and hiss for 3 seconds, then spray for 12.
- Get caught in the spray and you're soaked for a few seconds: slower, and your footsteps squelch loud enough for nearby critters to hear. Critters in the spray slow down too.
- The first time one is near, the HUD explains them.

versions.title: Locked rooms
versions.notes:
- Locked rooms: the Snack Shack's Back Room and the Restrooms' Staff Closet. Find the Shack Key or the Closet Key (in bins, on the ground, on gnomes and raccoons) and press E at the door to unlock it.
- Inside each is a Supply Crate with a better roll. Keys are used up, and the doors lock again every raid.
- The Restrooms' partition now leaves a gap, so the west side (and its bin) can be reached.
- Rolled Newspapers turn up in trash bins now, as promised.

versions.title: Raid modifiers
versions.notes:
- Raid modifiers: half the time the next raid rolls a condition, shown on the Raid button before you go. Extract for a crumb bonus.
- Rainy Day (+40): rain and puddles that slow everyone, and footsteps that squelch loud enough for nearby critters to hear.
- Fireworks Night (+60): it's dark, but every firework lights up the critters around you for a moment, even behind walls.
- Big Sale (+30): more loot in containers and on the ground, and more raccoons after it.

versions.title: Paid exits
versions.notes:
- Paid exits: some raids, an exit wants something to let you through. The Ice Cream Van wants 150 crumbs' worth of loot, the Duck Boat a Car Battery, and in the suburb the Storm Drain wants 100 crumbs' worth and the Back Alley Gate some Car Keys.
- The price is on the exit's sign, in the exit list, on the map, and in the opening banner. Payment comes out of your backpack as you leave, cheapest loot first.

versions.title: The Golden Picnic
versions.notes:
- The Golden Picnic: with 3 minutes left, a golden box parachutes into the map (banner, and a gold square on the minimap and map). It's packed with 5 to 7 rare things.
- Only the few critters close to where it lands (the 3 nearest within 30 m) come to look, so the rest of the map isn't left empty.

versions.title: Music
versions.notes:
- Music! All of it made in code like the sounds: a cosy plucky loop on the title and in the Nest, a calm park tune in raids, and a tense beat with drums whenever a critter is fighting you.
- Music: On/Off on the title screen and in the pause menu, separate from Sound, and remembered.

versions.title: Import and export saves
versions.notes:
- Save Data on the title screen: copy your save as a text code (or download it as a file in the browser) to back it up or move it to another computer.
- Paste a code (or load a file) to bring a save back. It shows what you'd be replacing and asks before it does.

versions.title: Melee weapons
versions.notes:
- Melee weapons that need no ammo: the Rolled Newspaper (quick swats), the Baguette Bat (long reach), and the Frying Pan (slow, huge BONG that dizzies what it hits).
- A swing hits every critter in an arc in front of the goose, and it's quiet: only critters close by hear it.
- Find them in crates (and newspapers in bins), or buy them in the Nest. They swish and bong.
- Fixed: weapons you found and carried out in your backpack now go in the stash (they used to vanish).

versions.title: View cone
versions.notes:
- A view cone: everything outside a 110-degree cone toward the cursor (and beyond how far you can see) is darkened, with a small bright circle around the goose.
- Critters outside your cone are hidden, just like ones behind walls. Turn to look! They can still hear you.

versions.title: Bigger stash
versions.notes:
- The stash has a size now: 40 slots to start, one per stack (125 Foam Darts take 3). The Stash column shows how full it is, and each item says how many slots it takes.
- Bigger stashes in the Nest's shop: 60 slots for 500 crumbs, 90 for 1500, and 130 for 4000.
- Extracting always banks everything, even past the limit, but an overflowing stash has to be sold down (or upgraded) before the next raid.

versions.title: Sharper maps
versions.notes:
- Sharper maps: the map screen (M) and the minimap are drawn at 4 and 3 pixels per meter instead of 1, so they're no longer stretched and blurry.
- Walls, hedges, cars, and the pond get a dark outline on the map, so shapes read at a glance.
- Area names on the map step aside for nearby exit labels instead of overlapping them.

versions.title: The Suburb Cul-de-sac
versions.notes:
- A second map, the Suburb Cul-de-sac: a turning circle, The Big House you can walk into, a garage, a paddling pool behind a fence, a veggie patch, a playhouse garden, front lawns, a back alley, and a tree house.
- Its own exits: the Mail Truck where you arrive, plus two of the Storm Drain, the Back Alley Gate, the Cat Flap, and the Tree House Rope.
- A map picker in the Nest. The suburb unlocks after 3 extractions from Picnic Park (old saves count the extractions they already have).
- The Nest's Bringing column is more compact (weapons and the secure pouch side by side), and Repack moved up next to the Lost Gosling button.

versions.title: Lost Gosling runs
versions.notes:
- Lost Gosling runs: a free raid from the Nest with a random cheap kit (a Foam Blaster or Pea Shooter, some ammo, a snack or two). Nothing from the Nest comes along, so nothing is at risk.
- Extract and the haul (and the kit's weapon) goes in the stash. Get bonked and you lose only the free kit.
- One every 20 minutes; the button counts down, and the wait is remembered.

versions.title: Secure pouch
versions.notes:
- A secure pouch: two small slots (1 kg) that always come home, even if you're bonked, locked in, or give up.
- Pack it in the Nest with To pouch, or move things in and out of it from the backpack screen (Tab) during a raid.
- Bigger pouches in the Nest's shop: 3 slots and 2 kg for 400 crumbs, then 4 slots and 3 kg for 1000.
- The results screen shows what the pouch saved.

versions.title: Polish
versions.notes:
- Sound! All of it made from scratch in code: honks, squawks when you're hit, foam dart pffs, pea pops, balloon splashes, slingshot thwips, a cartoon boing when a critter goes down, rummaging, loot bloops, reloads, munching, footsteps, a happy chime when you extract, and a sad wah-wah when you don't.
- Sound On/Off on the title screen and in the pause menu (remembered).
- A minimap in the top right, turned like the camera, with the open exits (far ones pinned to the edge pointing the way).
- You can only see critters that are in your line of sight: walls, hedges, cars, and bushes hide them (and you). Hide in a bush!
- The camera shakes when you get hit or honk, and the Nest jingles when you buy and sell.

versions.title: The Nest
versions.notes:
- Enter the Nest from the title screen: your stash on the left, what you're bringing in the middle, the shop on the right. Click anything to see it and what you can do with it.
- Sell loot for breadcrumbs (or sell all junk and valuables at once). Buy weapons, ammo packs, and snacks; buying costs twice what selling pays.
- Pack your raid: two weapon slots (slot 1 starts in hand) and the backpack. Weapons start the raid loaded from the ammo you pack.
- Bigger backpacks: 16 slots and 25 kg for 300 crumbs, then 20 slots and 30 kg for 800.
- Whatever you bring is at risk. Extract and it all comes home (weapons straight back to their slots); get bonked, locked in, or give up and it stays in the park. Repack copies last raid's backpack from the stash.
- A new save starts with 100 crumbs and a Foam Blaster kit. Broke with no weapon? Mom Goose slips you a spare.
- The pause menu's Quit is now Give Up, which costs your backpack.

versions.title: Combat
versions.notes:
- The park fights back. Garden Gnomes guard spots with slingshots; Raccoons roam the park with acorn poppers, strafe, and more of them wander in as the day goes on.
- They notice you when you're in front of them and in sight (walls and hedges hide you), hear your shots, and come looking where they last saw you.
- You start each raid with a Foam Blaster and 36 darts. Click to shoot (hold for the blaster), R to reload, 1/2 or the mouse wheel to switch.
- Find the Pea Shooter (six peas per shot) and the Balloon Lobber (arcs over cover and splashes) in crates and on raccoons, plus ammo all over. Equip them from the backpack.
- Space dodge rolls through shots (costs puff). Q honks: stuns everything in front of you, alerts everything nearby, then needs to recharge.
- 100 health. H eats the snack that best fits how hurt you are (or use Eat in the backpack); food now heals.
- Bonked critters fall over and drop loot. Get bonked yourself and you lose your backpack and weapons.

**Limitations:** Every raid starts with the same free kit until the Nest arrives.

versions.title: Getting out
versions.notes:
- The park closes in 10 minutes. The clock is in the top right, and the sun sets as closing time nears.
- Ways out: the Bus Stop where you came in is always open, plus two of the Duck Boat, the Ice Cream Van, the Drain Pipe, and the Hole in the Fence, different each raid.
- Open exits glow green with a light column and a sign. Stand in one for 5 seconds to extract; stepping out cancels. The HUD lists each open exit and how far it is.
- M opens a map of the park, turned to match your view, showing the areas, the open exits, and where you are.
- Extract and everything in your backpack goes to your stash, saved between visits. Still in the park when it closes? The ranger confiscates your backpack.
- A results screen shows what you brought out (or lost) and your stash; the title screen shows the stash too.

**Limitations:** The stash can't be opened or spent yet: that's the Nest, coming later.

versions.title: Grabbing loot
versions.notes:
- Loose loot lies all over the park: walk up to anything bobbing on the grass and press E to grab it. Uncommon and better items glow with a beam in their rarity color.
- Tab opens your backpack: click an item to read about it, then Drop it (or Drop One from a stack) at your feet. Dropped things stay on the ground to grab again.
- Heavy new finds: Lawn Flamingo, Bowling Ball, Watermelon, Garden Gnome, and the very valuable, very heavy Car Battery.
- The backpack has a 20 kg limit. Go over it and you waddle slower (down to 60% at 30 kg, a crawl beyond) and can't sprint. The HUD warns you when you're too heavy.
- If your backpack is full, you only pick up what fits.

**Limitations:** Loot still doesn't leave the park: extraction is next.

versions.title: Looting chests
versions.notes:
- Picnic baskets, coolers, trash bins, and supply crates all over the park, each with its own kind of loot. Every raid rolls fresh contents.
- Walk up to one (it gets a glowing ring) and press E to search. Items turn up one at a time; rare things take longer to find, so keep the panel open.
- Click an item to move it into your backpack, or Take All. Click a backpack item to put it back.
- 26 items to find, from Bottle Caps and Soggy Fries to Gold Rings and the legendary Golden Bread. Hover for a description, weight, and worth in breadcrumbs.
- The backpack holds 12 slots; stackable things stack. The HUD shows what you're carrying and a feed of what you just grabbed.

**Limitations:** Loot doesn't leave the park yet: extraction comes in a later release.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- You are a goose in a tiny tactical helmet. Press Raid on the title screen to waddle into Picnic Park from the bus stop.
- WASD waddles (up is up on the screen), the goose faces your cursor, and Shift sprints until you run out of puff.
- Picnic Park: a duck pond, the Snack Shack, restrooms, a parking lot, a playground, a picnic meadow, and a fountain plaza, all hemmed in by hedges.
- The camera follows from an isometric angle and leans toward the cursor. Walls, trees, and cars in front of the goose turn see-through.
- The HUD shows which part of the park you're in.

**Limitations:** Nothing to loot or shoot yet: this release is the park and the goose.

versions.title: Gamepad menus
versions.notes:
- Every menu works with the pad: press any pad button and the first button on the screen lights up. The D-pad or left stick moves between buttons, A presses, B backs out (Settings, hangar, campaign map, briefing, replays, leaderboard, pilot, version log, and the pause menu, where B resumes).
- The mutator pick between endless waves takes the focus too, so you can choose with the pad mid-run.
- Settings: B (or Menu) cancels waiting for a key, and a pad group button that already has a job says so (Group 3 on Y also pings).
- The mouse and keyboard keep working everywhere.

**Limitations:** Text boxes (room code, pilot name) still need the keyboard. Not tested with a real pad yet.

versions.title: Gamepad play
versions.notes:
- Play with a gamepad: the left stick walks, the right stick aims (a light push aims close, a full push far, and the aim stays put when you let go).
- Triggers and bumpers fire the weapon groups: RT group 1, LT group 2, RB group 3, LB group 4. A dashes, B vents, X reloads, Y pings, L3 is overdrive, R3 siege mode, the D-pad zooms (up/down), orders the wingman (left) and holds the heat link (right). View opens the hangar, Menu pauses.
- Settings: a pad button beside each weapon group. Click it, then press a pad button or trigger.
- The controls line, the weapon rows, the training steps and tips switch to pad names when you last used the pad, and back to keys when you use the keyboard or mouse.

**Limitations:** Menus still need the mouse (next update). Skipping the training course has no pad button. Not tested with a real pad yet.

versions.title: Damage numbers and pilot radio
versions.notes:
- Damage numbers are colored by weapon type (kinetic cream, energy cyan, plasma violet, fire orange, blasts amber). Resisted hits look greyer, weak spots brighter; hits on you stay red.
- Fast weapons like the machine gun add up their hits on one target into a single number every quarter second instead of a cloud of 9s.
- Pilot radio: short lines at the bottom of the screen from your pilot, mission control or your wingman (heat climbing, armor critical, a boss inbound, the uplink half done, the dropship down, overdrive charged, wave clear, wingman down). Each line waits a while before it can repeat.
- Settings: Damage numbers and Pilot radio can each be turned off.

versions.title: Heat link and team stats
versions.notes:
- Co-op heat link: hold L within 4 m of a friend to shed heat into them over a glowing cable (30 a second). They take it only up to 85, so it never locks their weapons. A tip explains it the first time a friend links to you. Not in versus.
- Team stat line in the co-op lobby and the between-wave hangar: the team's damage per second, its lowest armor, which ranges its weapons reach (short up to 25 m, mid to 40 m, long past that), and the first gap (no long range, nothing close, or no energy or plasma weapon).

**Limitations:** Only the two linked players see the cable.

versions.title: Wingman orders and revive
versions.notes:
- T orders your wingman: Hold (it stays where it stands and shoots what comes) or Follow (back on you).
- Ping a robot (G) and your wingman goes after that one until it's dead, then goes back to its last order.
- A line under your bars shows the wingman's order and armor. When it goes down, stand beside it for 3 seconds to bring it back at a quarter armor (a ring shows the progress).

**Limitations:** The wingman never revives you.

versions.title: AI wingman
versions.notes:
- Solo campaign missions: pick a wingman on the briefing from your four loadout presets (or fly alone). It's remembered for the next mission.
- The wingman is an AI mech on your side, in olive with a green trim: it follows you, turns on the nearest robot within 30 m, and robots shoot back at it. Its kills count toward your stats. A name tag shows its armor, and it's a green dot on the minimap.
- Anything in that preset you haven't unlocked falls back to what you have. It hits a bit softer than you do.

**Limitations:** No orders yet, and a downed wingman stays down (both next version). Not in co-op: hosting mid-mission sends it home.

versions.title: Endless mutators
versions.notes:
- Deploy: after waves 5, 10, 15... pick one of three mutators. The break waits until you pick, and they stack for the rest of the run.
- Swarm (robots 30% faster, 30% less armor), Scrap rush (double salvage, no repair kits), Drone storm (twice the drones), Armor column (tanks only; bosses still come), Cold guns (40% less heat, 20% less damage), Powder keg (many more barrels, restocked every wave), Blackout (no minimap, kills score 50% more).
- The top bar tags the mutators in play; the end screen and leaderboard entries list them. In co-op the host picks and friends get the same.

versions.title: Campaign upgrades
versions.notes:
- The first time you clear a campaign sector, pick one of three upgrades: Armor plating (+15% armor), Tuned actuators (legs 8% faster), Heat sinks (cool 15% faster), Autoloaders (kinetic reloads 25% faster), Capacitors (energy weapons 20% less heat), Jump jets (dashes recharge 35% faster), Scrap magnet (+25% salvage) or Field medic (kits heal 50% more).
- Upgrades stay with you for every mission until you press Start over on the campaign map (press it twice; it also clears your sectors). They don't apply in Deploy, training or versus.
- The campaign map lists your upgrades, and an offer you left on the win screen waits there. In co-op the host picks and only the host's mech gets them.

**Limitations:** Retrying a sector you've cleared doesn't offer another upgrade.

versions.title: Collapsing bridges
versions.notes:
- Foundry: a steel bridge crosses the middle of every lava channel. Walk over it between its girders; robots use it too.
- Bridges take about 400 damage (blasts and plasma best, fire does nothing). At half they sag and groan with a 'Bridge failing' warning, then they drop into the lava and the strip burns again.
- A tip explains bridges the first time you step on one. The minimap and replays show them. In co-op the host owns bridge health, like cover.
- Long tips (an arena's warning plus the weather) now wrap instead of running off the sides of a small window.

**Limitations:** Robots don't aim at bridges, but their stray shots and shells still wear them down.

versions.title: Sandstorm and weather picker
versions.notes:
- Sandstorm: tan fog and blowing dust. Aiming lasers and hitscan, beam, rail and tesla weapons reach only 60% as far, and robots see and fire only 60% as far too. Signal Spire is now in a sandstorm.
- A weather picker beside the theme picker on the title (Random, Clear, Rain, Night, Sandstorm), saved with your settings. It sets Deploy's weather; missions keep their own. Random can now roll a sandstorm.

**Limitations:** Bullets, shells and missiles keep their full range in a sandstorm.

versions.title: Weather: rain and night
versions.notes:
- Weather: rain (falling rain, a greyer light, heat cools 25% faster) and night (dim blue moonlight; robots' eyes, lasers and lava glow brighter). It stays the same for the whole run.
- Campaign sectors have fixed weather, shown on the briefing: Supply Run and Downtown in the rain, Relay Station, Cold Road and The Core at night. Endless runs are clear 60% of the time, otherwise rain or night. Versus stays clear.
- A tip explains each weather the first time. Co-op friends get the host's weather with the arena.

versions.title: Eject
versions.notes:
- Solo campaign missions, once per mission: when your mech is destroyed the pilot ejects and runs on foot (60 armor, no weapons). Robots go after the pilot.
- Reach the amber drop beacon 18-25 m away (a tall beam, and on the minimap) and stand in it for 3 s: a fresh mech drops in there at full armor, overdrive meter kept.
- Shot down on foot, the mission fails. A tip explains it the first time; the goal line counts the hold.
