- By day you see well, but 10% more infected are about and all of them awake. A tip explains night on your first one.

versions.title: Locked rooms
versions.notes:
- Zones of danger 1 and up have a locked strongroom with a well-stocked crate inside. Once you've seen its door, a padlock marks it on the minimap.
- Its key is in the container farthest from the door. Or make a crowbar at the workbench (3 scrap, 1 parts) and force the door: 3 seconds standing still, loud every second, and a hit stops you.

versions.title: Set pieces
versions.notes:
- Every zone now has a landmark that stays put from run to run, named in its zone text on the world map.
- A crashed supply truck, with a cargo crate full of loot beside it. A barricaded house with one door, clean ground inside and a survivor holding out. A collapsed overpass: a long wall of rubble across the zone that you have to go round.

**Limitations:** Zones' layouts change a little where the landmark now stands.

versions.title: Docile kinds play differently
versions.notes:
- A sedated infected keeps its kind, and once trained it fights like one. The camp list names the kind and says what it does.
- Runners scout a few metres ahead of where you aim and mark the infected near them, so you see those through walls for a moment. Spitters stay back and spit at infected from range.
- Brutes have 200 health and their blows shove infected back and stun them. Shamblers and the rest follow and claw as before.

**Limitations:** Docile infected from older saves count as shamblers.

versions.title: Migrating herds
versions.notes:
- From your third run a herd of infected wanders the world map (HERD on its zone), moving to a neighbouring open zone or staying put after each run.
- The herd's zone has twice the shamblers, and they all move as one group. A noise any of them hears draws the whole herd, so a rock or noise arrow thrown far away can lure it off your path.
- A tip explains the herd when you arrive; the zone text and the deploy screen warn you before you go.

versions.title: Corpse sprouting
versions.notes:
- In zones of danger 1 and up, the infected you kill leave their bodies behind. After a minute a body sprouts into a new mushroom clump and the ground around it turns purple.
- For the last 15 seconds the body swells, twitches and glows. Slash it with the machete or burn it to stop it. A tip explains this with your first kill there, and the field guide keeps it.

**Limitations:** Bloated infected burst as before and leave no body.

versions.title: Trader caravan
versions.notes:
- Every 4 runs, if you have a safe zone, a trader caravan stops at one of them for 2 runs (TRADER on the world map).
- At camp the Trader section lists 4 swaps at the trader's own rates (scrap for parts, food for medicine, sticks for arrows...) and one rare item such as a pistol, a cure, a vaccine or a respirator. Each swap can be made once, paid from the stash.

versions.title: Settlers and defences
versions.notes:
- Settle a ready survivor in a safe zone (world map, zone selected): they live there and rest, the zone makes 1 more of its goods a run, and it holds one more run without supply. Recall them from their card.
- Defences for safe zones, up to 3 of each: barricades (3 scrap, 1 parts) hold one more run without supply; lantern posts (scrap, parts, fuel) light the zone and push the infection in the zones beside it back 25% faster.
- On later visits you see the extra fences, the lantern posts and your settlers. A zone that falls loses its defences and sends its settlers home.

**Limitations:** Someone always stays ready at camp: you can't settle your last ready survivor.

versions.title: Zone roles
versions.notes:
- Safe zones get a role: pick it on the world map with the zone selected (the first pick is free; changing it later costs 3 scrap).
- Farm: food each run. Workshop: scrap and parts by turns. Clinic: medicine, and every supplied clinic makes quarantine 3% a run faster. Watch post: no goods, but shows what waits in the zones beside it, like the watchtower.
- Until you pick, a zone makes what it always made. The map shows each safe zone's role, or pick a role.

versions.title: Post-game strongholds
versions.notes:
- Once the source burns, the three hardest zones become strongholds (STRONGHOLD on the world map): danger 3 higher, even if you had made them safe.
- Each stronghold is held by a named warden, a giant infected that is very tough and hits hard. A tip names it when you arrive; the deepest containers hold extra loot.
- Put the warden down (kill or subdue) and extract to take its relic home and break the stronghold. Each relic lifts camp morale by 5.

**Limitations:** Saves where the source already burned get their strongholds when they load.

versions.title: Camp morale
versions.notes:
- Camp has a morale meter (0-100) in the side panel, with what is raising or lowering it: food in the stash, safe zones, survivors lost lately and requests you filled lately.
- After each run morale moves part of the way towards where those point. At 70 or more quarantine works 25% faster and research costs a spore sample less.
- Below 30 an extra request comes in. Below 20 camp warns you; if it is still that low after the next run, someone who isn't on the run leaves for good (never your last survivor).

**Limitations:** Morale starts at 60 in older saves; losses and requests count from this version.

versions.title: The tide
versions.notes:
- Open zones you leave alone get worse: every 4 runs (6 if a safe zone is next to it) a zone's danger goes up by 1, up to 3 above where it started. More and tougher infected come with it; its spore hearts stay the same.
- The world map shows worse in N runs on zones about to tip, and a purple border on zones that have already worsened. The zone text gives the details.
- The first time a zone worsens, camp explains the tide.

**Limitations:** The count starts with this version: zones in older saves begin their first 4 runs now.

versions.title: Regions
versions.notes:
- The world map is split into three regions, one per row: the City, the Outskirts and the Farmland, each with a heading on the map.
- Safe zones open the zones beside and above them, but the next region only opens once you clear its region heart zone (Water Works for the City, Mill District for the Outskirts; RH on the map). Its spore hearts are bigger and tougher.
- Clearing a region heart zone opens the region below every safe zone in that row. Camp: building and research buttons are shorter, with their description underneath, so the side panel no longer runs off the screen.

**Limitations:** Saves where a lower row was already open keep it open.

versions.title: Experimental cures
versions.notes:
- New research: Experimental cure (3 spore samples). Then brew cheap cures at the workbench: 1 spore sample and 1 medicine.
- Using one clears infection like a cure, cleanly 70% of the time. Otherwise the survivor is cured but has a side effect for 3 runs: slow stamina, or a cough that won't stop (it coughs even when Clean). The odds and effects show next to the button.
- The survivor's line at camp shows the side effect and how many runs it has left.

versions.title: Decon shower and field injector
versions.notes:
- Field injector: craft one at the workbench (medicine, chemicals, a spore sample); a run takes up to 2. Press J on a run and stand still for 4 seconds: infection drops by 15%. Getting hit stops it (you keep the injector).
- Decon shower: a new camp building (5 scrap, 3 parts). When you extract, it spends 1 chemicals to wash off 30% of the infection you gained on the run; the summary shows how much.
- J can be rebound in Settings > Controls like the other keys.

versions.title: Strains
versions.notes:
- Each zone's infection is one of three strains. Creeping: blooms come every 75 s and spread twice as far. Airborne: spore clouds from bursts and puffballs spread 40% wider. Rooting: infection caught there comes out at half speed in quarantine for 2 runs.
- Bring home a spore sample from a zone to learn its strain: the world map shows it and a tip explains it when you go back.
- Once a strain is known, research a targeted cure for it: curing someone that strain infected gives back a spore sample and leaves them resistant 2 runs longer.

versions.title: Death recap
versions.notes:
- The run summary now says what hurt you: damage and infection by source (each kind of infected's claws, spitter globs, bloated bursts, puffballs, fire, infected ground, searching bodies), worst first.
- On a lost run it's shown larger, so you can see what did it.

versions.title: Practice zone
versions.notes:
- A Practice zone you can play any time from the title screen or from camp: a strip of stations, each with a prompt, for crouching past a cone, throwing a rock, sealing a find in the pouch, puffballs, a lurker clump, a spitter, a shrieker, burning a patch with the torch and calling a flare.
- You get a free loadout (arrows, fuel, medicine, a respirator) and nothing is saved. Each station moves on when you do it, or when you walk past it.
- The guided first run for new players is unchanged.

versions.title: Field guide
versions.notes:
- A Field guide at camp: every kind of infected you've met, with a line on how it behaves, how many you've put down, what it drops and its tip. Kinds you haven't met show as ???.
- Hazards and tips: every hazard tip you've seen (blooms, coughing, phantoms, puffballs, fire, light, weather, radio posts) can be read again there.

**Limitations:** Kill counts start with this version; kinds you met before it show up again once you see them.

versions.title: Deploy screen
versions.notes:
- Deploy now opens a deploy screen first: who's going (and who comes along), what they'll carry, the zone (biome, danger, weather, contract, distress call, radio), its threats if you have a watchtower, and how fast infection will build for this survivor.
- The infection line counts their Resist skill, cures, vaccines, specialisation and a partner, and says how long on purple ground until Critical; a respirator is mentioned when you'll carry one.
- Go starts the run; Back to camp lets you change your mind.

versions.title: Conditions
versions.notes:
- Zones now have weather for the next run, rolled after every run (half the time there's none): rain, fog or a blackout. The world map shows it on the zone and says what it does.
- Rain: your footsteps make half the noise, but blooms spread the infected ground twice as far. Fog: you and the infected both see less far. Blackout: darker, you see less, and containers hold batteries.
- Every condition puts extra loot in three containers. A tip explains each the first time, and the HUD names the condition.

versions.title: Shriekers
versions.notes:
- New infected from the second ring of zones: the shrieker, tall, pale and frail. When it spots you it glows and rears back for a moment, then screams, and every infected within 18 m comes for you.
- Hit it while it rears (an arrow, a rock, a shove) to cut the scream off. It can scream again after 12 seconds.
- A tip explains it the first time one rears, and that first one takes twice as long to scream.

versions.title: New player model
versions.notes:
- Survivors are now proper figures instead of capsules: a head, a torso in their colour, legs that swing as they walk, arms (one holds the bow or pistol) and a backpack.
- Crouching leans the body forward; a respirator shows as a mask.
- Survivors you rescue, partners and settlers in safe zones use the same figure.
- Low graphics keeps the figures but skips the walk swing.

versions.title: Survivor roster
versions.notes:
- The camp's survivor list is now one short line each (colour, name, status, infection bar, level) in a column that only scrolls up and down.
- Click a line to see that survivor in full below the list, with all their actions (quarantine, treat, cure, bring along, skill points, specialising).
- Choose on a line (or Choose for this run in the details) picks who deploys; the line says Going.

versions.title: Save export and import
versions.notes:
- Export a save as text: Save slots > Export / import on the title screen, or Save: export / import at camp. It's copied to the clipboard too, so you can keep it safe or move it to another browser.
- Import pastes a save back into any slot. Replacing a slot that has a save asks you to press Import again first.
- Text that isn't a save (a run log, a cut-off paste) is refused with the reason; saves from older versions import and get the newer fields filled in.

**Limitations:** Export and import go through a text box and the clipboard; there's no file download yet.

versions.title: Save slots
versions.notes:
- Three save slots. The title screen has Save slots: each shows its runs, survivors, safe zones and when it was last saved, with Continue, New game and Delete (both ask first if they'd lose a save).
- New game starts in the first empty slot; Continue loads the slot you played last.
- Your existing save moves into slot 1 automatically, untouched.
- A small "Saved (slot N)" note shows at camp and on the run summary each time the game saves, so you know progress is kept in the browser.

versions.title: Run log
versions.notes:
- Run log at camp: every run you finish is kept (the last 30) with its route and what happened on it. Pick one to replay its route on the map.
- Delete runs you don't want, Export the log as text (also copied to the clipboard) and Import a log someone pasted, without doubling runs you already have.

versions.title: Route replay
versions.notes:
- The map on the run summary now replays your route: the line draws itself over a few seconds, and each moment (searched, kill, subdued, sedated, recruited, heart) pops up with its letter as the line reaches it.
- Click the map to skip to the end, or Replay route to watch it again.

versions.title: Web performance
versions.notes:
- Faster busy fights, especially in the browser: infected vision cones are worked out again only when an infected moves or turns (about 9 times less work a frame with a crowd).
- Infected ground, the fog of war and mushroom clumps redraw only what changed, and arrows and spit reuse their meshes instead of making new ones.

versions.title: Graphics setting
versions.notes:
- Settings has a Graphics option: Low (faster) turns off shadows, spore particles and the vision cones of infected more than 8 m away, for slower machines and browsers.
- An optional FPS counter (Settings) shows frames a second in the top right.

versions.title: Camp walkthrough
versions.notes: - The first time you come back to camp, a short walkthrough frames quarantine, the cure, the workbench and the world map one at a time, with a line on each. Next moves on; Skip ends it.

versions.title: Guided first run
versions.notes:
- A guided first run: a small training ground that walks you through moving, shooting the bow, searching a crate, crossing infected ground and extracting, one prompt at a time.
- New players get it from the title screen (Play) or can skip it; it's always there as Guided first run. Nothing from it goes into your save.
- The pause menu's list of controls sits on its own panel, and the controls line at the bottom of a run fits the screen.

versions.title: Key rebinding
versions.notes:
- Rebind every key in Settings > Controls: click an action, then press its new key (Esc cancels). Taking a key another action uses swaps the two; Reset to defaults puts them back.
- The pause menu lists your controls, and the hint line at the bottom of a run follows your bindings.

**Limitations:** Tips still name the default keys.

versions.title: Minimap
versions.notes:
- A minimap in the bottom right shows the part of the zone you've explored, turned to match the camera, with infected ground in purple.
- It marks the exit (green), containers you've seen (yellow, grey once searched), spore hearts you've seen (red), and you with the way you're aiming.

versions.title: The outbreak's story
versions.notes:
- Every zone hides one note in a container. Get it home and it goes in the journal at camp (Journal button), telling where the mushroom came from.
- With 6 notes the journal points to the source of the outbreak, deep in the hardest open zone (SOURCE on the world map): a giant red spore heart.
- Arrows and blades can't hurt the source; only fire on the ground at its roots (a torch or fire arrows) burns it out. A tip explains it when you get there.

versions.title: Distress calls
versions.notes:
- Distress calls: after a run, a survivor may call for help from one of the open zones. The world map marks it with ! and the runs left.
- Go there within 2 runs: the caller is always somewhere in the zone, and the HUD reminds you to find them. Bring them home and they join the camp with 2 medicine.
- Leave it too long and the call goes silent.

versions.title: Camp requests
versions.notes:
- Survivors at camp ask for things: 5 food, 3 medicine, a pistol, 15 arrows, 4 parts, 3 spore samples, or a rescue. Two requests are open at a time, in a new Requests section at camp.
- Give what they ask from the stash for a reward: XP or a skill point for the one who asked, or rare gear (broadhead arrows, a vaccine, filters or batteries).
- A rescue request is filled when a run brings a survivor home. A new request comes in after each run.

versions.title: Specialisations
versions.notes:
- At level 5 a survivor specialises: pick one of two upgrades to their perk on their card at camp.
- Scout: Ghost (sprinting is as quiet as walking) or Keen eyes (see 3 m farther). Brute: Bulwark (+25 health) or Thick skin (hits infect 30% less).
- Medic: Field medic (also heals recruits and party members near you) or Quick heal (heals sooner and twice as fast). Botanist: Spore ward (infected ground infects 25% slower) or Collector (three times the spore samples).
- Marksman: Deadeye (focused hits +100%) or Quickdraw (draws the bow 30% faster). Forager: Scavenger (searches 30% faster) or Packer (three times the sticks and food).

versions.title: Trust
versions.notes:
- Survivors build trust with each other: every run two of them finish together (leader and party member) adds one, and a survivor you rescue starts out trusting whoever brought them home.
- At 3 trust a party member is trusted: they move faster when you give orders, hand you 3 arrows when you run dry, and add only half the usual infection liability. A tip explains it the first time.
- Survivor cards at camp list who they trust.

versions.title: Party of two
versions.notes:
- Bring along a second ready survivor from camp (Bring along on their card): they come on the run as a party member who follows your orders and shoots with up to 10 arrows from the stash.
- They bring their skills: Health gives them more health, Aim makes their arrows hit harder, Resist slows their infection. Like any recruit, they make infection build faster for the party.
- Party members earn XP (half the run's), keep the infection they picked up, and bring their pack home if they're with you at the exit. If they fall they come home wounded; if they turn, they're gone.
- Survivors you rescue now earn XP on the run they join, so recruits level up like everyone else.

versions.title: Conveyor belts
versions.notes:
- Join two neighbouring safe zones with a conveyor belt (2 parts, 3 scrap), from the selected zone's supplies at camp.
- Every run a belt moves up to 2 supply from the better-stocked end to the other, and carries the far zone's goods to the zone nearer camp. Chain belts and a single supply line to a near zone keeps far zones stocked.
- Zones on a belt show = on the world map. A belt stops if either end falls.

versions.title: Reclaim moment
versions.notes: - When a run makes a zone safe, the camp's world map celebrates it: the zone's purple shrinks away and it glows green, with a rising sting.

versions.title: Reclaimed zones look reclaimed
versions.notes: - Going back into a safe zone now shows the progress: the ground has grown back green, fences stand round the start and the extraction, lamps light the way, and a few settlers stroll about.

versions.title: Camp buildings
versions.notes:
- Build up the camp with scavenged materials. Each building is bought once.
- Greenhouse (4 scrap, 2 parts, 2 food): grows 1 food every run.
- Lab (4 scrap, 2 parts, 3 chemicals): cures and research cost 1 spore sample less.
- Watchtower (6 scrap, 2 parts): the world map tells you which infected and hazards wait in a zone (and who turned there) before you deploy.
- Storeroom (5 scrap, 3 cloth): runs take half as much gear again: 30 arrows, 36 rounds, more filters, batteries, lanterns and special arrows.

versions.title: Quarantine ward
versions.notes:
- The quarantine ward has beds now: 2 to start with, so you can't quarantine everyone at once. Add more at camp (3 scrap, 1 part each, up to 6).
- Treatment: switch it on for a quarantined survivor and they recover twice as fast (24% a run instead of 12%), for 1 medicine a run while you have some.
- The camp shows how many beds are in use; survivor cards show who's being treated.

versions.title: Cure research
versions.notes:
- Research at camp, paid in spore samples, unlocks things for good.
- Refined cure (4 spore samples): cures cost 2 spore samples and 1 medicine instead of 3 and 2.
- Suppressant (3 spore samples): make suppressants (1 spore sample, 1 chemicals). Give one to a survivor at camp and their infection can't grow at all on their next run.
- Vaccine (6 spore samples, 1 medicine): make vaccines (2 spore samples, 1 medicine). A vaccinated survivor takes 40% less infection for 3 runs.
- Survivor cards show who's suppressed or vaccinated.

versions.title: The lost return
versions.notes:
- A survivor overrun by the infection now comes back in the zone where they turned: a named, tougher infected (150 health, harder claws) still carrying everything they had on them.
- The world map shows who turned in each zone, and the zone note lists what they carry, before you go back in. The first time you see one, a tip names them.
- Put them down (kill or subdue) and their gear drops where they fall. Extract afterwards and they're laid to rest; fail the run and they'll be back.

versions.title: Radio posts
versions.notes:
- Some zones have a radio post (R on the world map: Rail Yard, Orchard, Stadium, Greenhouses, The Bloom). It's a crate with a tall mast and a blinking red lamp, and a tip points it out early in the run.
- Press E at the radio to call in another ready survivor. Whoever is out there goes home with everything they carry and the sealed pouch (plus a little XP), keeping their infection; the new survivor takes over at the radio with their own loadout.
- One call a run. Use it to rotate out a survivor whose infection is climbing without losing the run.

versions.title: Puffball mines
versions.notes:
- Puffballs grow on infected ground in the harder zones (from Rail Yard on): fat pale caps that pulse and glow once you're within 4 m.
- Step on one (or right next to it) and it bursts into a spore cloud: a big jump in infection and freshly infected ground round it.
- Shoot one from a distance, or burn it, to clear it safely.
- The first zone you find them in shows a tip as soon as one glows, and keeps them out in the open, away from the mushroom clumps.

versions.title: Lurkers
versions.notes:
- A new infected: lurkers hide inside mushroom clumps in the harder zones (one or more a run from Rail Yard on).
- They give themselves away: within 5 m their clump twitches and puffs spores, and the first time you see one a tip explains it.
- Get within 2 m after the twitching starts and the lurker lunges at you. Shooting the clump flushes it out first; noises don't move it.

versions.title: Light and the infected
versions.notes:
- Light now changes how some infected behave, and you find out by trying it (a tip explains each one the first time you see it happen).
- Runners can't stand the flashlight: one caught in the beam is blinded for 2 s and staggers on the spot (the same runner can't be dazzled again for a few seconds).
- Spitters are drawn to light: they drift toward lanterns, and toward you while your flashlight is on.
- Shamblers standing in lantern light calm down: they get suspicious much more slowly.

versions.title: Lanterns
versions.notes:
- Make lanterns at the workbench (2 scrap, 1 fuel). A run takes up to 3.
- B sets one down where you stand. It lights 5 m round it, and the zone keeps it for every later run (up to 8 a zone), even if this run goes wrong. Dark places get safer the more you light them.
- In the dark, lantern-lit ground shows from up to 13 m away, so you can see what's waiting in the light.
- The camp's world map counts the lanterns lit in each zone. The flashlight beam is brighter.

versions.title: Flashlight
versions.notes:
- Make a flashlight (2 parts, 1 scrap) and batteries (1 part makes 2) at the workbench. A run takes the flashlight and up to 3 batteries.
- L switches it on: a 70 degree cone of light where you aim lets you see out to 13 m, even in the dark subways where you'd otherwise see 7 m.
- The catch: infected see the beam. Any infected it shines on notices you whichever way it faces, and the rest spot you from half again as far while it's on.
- A battery lasts 90 s switched on; a spare is fitted when one runs flat, and the light goes out when they're all spent. The HUD shows what's left.

versions.title: Biomes
versions.notes:
- Every zone now has a biome with its own ground, walls, light and loot: ruins (as before), fungal forest (dense mushroom clumps, more sticks and food), flooded subway (dark: you only see 7 m; chemicals and parts), hospital (tight rooms; medicine and cloth) and greenhouse farm (food and spore samples).
- The camp's world map tells you a zone's biome before you deploy, and warns when you'll see less there. The dark subways are only in the harder zones (Water Works, Mill District).
- The HUD shows the biome next to the zone name.

versions.title: Machete
versions.notes:
- Make a machete at the workbench (3 scrap, 2 parts). A run takes it along.
- With the machete out, F is a quiet slash: infected that haven't noticed you die on the spot, aware ones take a 30 damage cut (brutes only ever take the cut).
- Slashing cuts down the mushroom clumps in front of you, clearing their spores, and sometimes gathers a spore sample.
- M puts the machete away so F shoves again (for subduing instead of killing).

versions.title: Burn it back
versions.notes:
- Fire: fire arrows and the new torch (T, 1 fuel: sets the ground 2.6 m in front of you alight) burn infected ground clean for the rest of the run, leaving it scorched.
- Fire is loud and creeps into neighbouring mushroom ground. Small yellow flames show where it will catch 1.5 s before it does; clean ground doesn't burn.
- Standing in fire hurts you, your recruits and infected alike. A tip explains fire the first time you start one.
- The tip line moved right so it no longer covers the health bars.

versions.title: Arrow types
versions.notes:
- Three new arrows from the workbench: broadheads (2 scrap, 1 stick for 3) hit 60% harder but always break; noise arrows (1 parts, 1 stick for 3) do no damage and make a racket where they land, pulling infected away from you; fire arrows (1 cloth, 1 fuel, 1 stick for 3) burn the infected ground clean where they land.
- R now cycles sharp, blunt and any special arrows you carry. When the last special arrow is gone, the bow goes back to sharp.
- A run takes up to 6 of each special arrow. Special arrows can't be picked up again.

versions.title: Flare extraction
versions.notes:
- A second way out: with fuel in your pack, press X to fire a flare right where you stand (1 fuel, once a run).
- The flare is loud: every 4 s it calls every infected within 20 m. Hold inside its red ring for 20 s in all (time outside doesn't count) and you're picked up there.
- Recruits near the flare come home with you. The first time you carry fuel, a tip explains the flare.

versions.title: Spore bloom
versions.notes:
- Runs now have a clock: 3 minutes in, the zone blooms, and again every 90 s after. Each bloom spreads infected ground outward and wakes more infected near the spore hearts, out of your sight.
- The HUD counts down to the next bloom, and the screen warns you 30 s before each one (the first time with a tip).
- The three containers farthest from the extraction are deep: they hold more loot. Staying for them is the gamble.
- Safe zones don't bloom.

versions.title: Respirators and filters
versions.notes:
- Craft a respirator (2 cloth, 2 parts) and filters (1 cloth, 1 chemicals) at the workbench.
- A run takes your respirator and up to 3 filters. While a filter lasts (60 s of breathing on infected ground each), infection from the ground is halved; a spare is fitted when one runs out.
- The HUD shows how much filter is left. Like other gear, the respirator is lost if the run is (seal it in the pouch to be safe).

versions.title: Symptoms
versions.notes:
- From Exposed on, survivors cough now and then (more often as the infection grows). A cough is a noise enemies hear from 6 m.
- The screen warns you a second before each cough: crouch (C) to cover your mouth and muffle it to 2 m. Muffled, not silent, so Exposed survivors still carry a risk.
- Critical survivors see phantom shamblers at the edge of their sight: faint, flickering, harmless, and they fade if you look straight at them.
- New one-time tips at the top of the screen explain each symptom before it matters (the first cough comes 8 s after its tip). Tips show once per save.

versions.title: Infection on screen
versions.notes:
- A purple vignette closes in from the screen edges as your infection grows, and spores drift across the screen from Exposed on.
- At Critical you hear your heartbeat and the vignette throbs with it.
- Infected pop in a puff of spores when they die (a smaller puff when subdued).

versions.title: Sounds
versions.notes:
- New sounds for recruiting and healing survivors, searching (a rustle while you search, a clunk when it opens), spitters spitting and their globs splatting, bloated bursting, sealing the pouch, and meeting a contract.
- Sounds far from you are quieter, and ones more than 28 m away aren't heard at all.

versions.title: Zone contracts
versions.notes:
- Open zones offer a contract for their next run ($ on the world map): bring back 3 spore samples, search 5 containers, bring a survivor home, destroy a spore heart, or extract without killing anyone.
- Meet it and extract to get paid: materials and XP. A new contract appears there afterwards.
- The HUD shows the contract's progress on the run, and the run summary says whether it paid out. Sealed spore samples count.
- A rescue contract always has someone to rescue.

versions.title: Run summary
versions.notes:
- After every run a summary screen before camp: how it ended, what you brought home (items new to the stash marked NEW), infection gained, XP and any level up, kills, subdues, containers searched and spore hearts destroyed.
- A map of the zone shows the route you took, with where you searched, killed, subdued, recruited, lost a survivor or destroyed a heart.

versions.title: Sealed pouch
versions.notes:
- A sealed pouch with 2 slots: press P on a run to seal the item you found last (up to 5 of one item a slot). What's sealed comes home even if you die, are overrun or pull out.
- Sealed items can't be used on the run (seal arrows and you can't shoot them).
- Upgrade the pouch at the workbench to 3 and then 4 slots (3 cloth, 2 parts each).

versions.title: Hit feedback
versions.notes:
- Arrows and bullets knock enemies back a little (brutes barely budge), and every hit flashes white.
- You flash when hurt, the screen edges flash red, and claws, pistol shots, bursts and dying hearts shake the camera.
- Spore hearts flash when hit.

versions.title: Noise meter
versions.notes:
- A ring on the ground around you shows how far your last noise carried: any enemy inside it comes to look. It turns from white to red as you get louder and fades when you're quiet.
- A Noise bar under Infection shows the same in metres (silent, walking 3 m, sprinting 7 m, a pistol shot 16 m).

versions.title: Logistics lines
versions.notes:
- Safe zones now need supplies to stay safe: each uses 1 a run (it starts with 6, up to 10). The world map shows every safe zone's supply.
- Out of supply, a zone stops pushing the infection back, and after 3 unsupplied runs it falls: one spore heart regrows. The camp warns you each run before that happens.
- Supply a zone by hand from camp (1 fuel and 1 food for +3), or put a survivor on a supply line: each run they bring the zone's goods home and carry +1 supply in, or +3 if there's fuel for the truck. Runners can't deploy; Recall brings them back.
- Every supplied safe zone makes something each run (food, parts, scrap, fuel, medicine...), waiting there until a supply line collects it.

**Limitations:** Supply lines run between camp and one safe zone; there are no conveyor belts or zone-to-zone lines yet.

versions.title: More enemy types
versions.notes:
- Runners (orange caps): fragile but faster than you walk.
- Bloated (swollen, yellow): slow, and they burst into a spore cloud when they die or reach you, soaking the ground and anyone close in infection. Shoot them from a distance.
- Spitters (green, from the second ring of zones): keep their distance, back off if you close in, and spit spores from up to 7.5 m.
- Mycelium brutes (big and dark, from harder zones): 220 health, hit hard, and can't be shoved or taken down.
- Harder zones mix in more kinds; the Outskirts only has shamblers, runners and bloated.

versions.title: Scavenging
versions.notes:
- Zones hold crates, cabinets, wrecked cars and bodies to search. Press E to start searching; stay close and don't get hurt until it's done.
- Each kind has its own loot: cabinets hold medicine, cloth and chemicals; cars hold parts, fuel and scrap; bodies hold food, cloth, ammo and spores.
- Searching takes time: 1 s for a crate up to 3 s for a car. Cars are noisy to search, and bodies breathe spores at you.
- The camp workbench makes medicine (cloth, chemicals), pistol ammo (parts, chemicals) and a pistol (parts, scrap), as well as arrows.

versions.title: Rescue survivors
versions.notes:
- Most runs in an unsafe zone have a survivor waiting somewhere for help. Press E by them to recruit them.
- Recruits follow you; G tells them all to hold where they stand or follow again.
- By a recruit: E takes what they carry like a chest, V gives them 5 arrows (they shoot infected within 8 m), H heals them with 1 medicine.
- The catch: every recruit makes infection build 25% faster for the whole party. Recruits pick up infection too; at 100% they turn into one of the infected.
- Extract with recruits close by and they join the camp with their own perk; anyone left far from the extraction stays behind.
- E, V, H and G now act once per key press.

versions.title: Limited vision
versions.notes:
- Your own vision needs line of sight: you see 13 m all round, but not through walls.
- What you cannot see is dark; ground you have seen this run stays dimly lit. Infected, their vision cones and dropped items only show while you can see them.
- You can only focus (cursor bonus) on infected you can see.

versions.title: Docile infected
versions.notes:
- Stand by a subdued infected and press E to sedate it (1 medicine). It turns docile and follows you.
- Extract with it and it joins the camp. Docile infected train for 3 runs (1 food each a run).
- Trained ones can come on your next run as a companion (choose on the camp screen): it follows you and claws infected within 5 m. Infected fight back; a companion that falls is gone.
- Subdued and dazed infected no longer show vision cones.

versions.title: Lethal and non-lethal
versions.notes:
- F shoves: an enemy that has not spotted you is knocked out on the spot (a takedown); one that is chasing you is knocked back and dazed. Costs stamina.
- R swaps the bow between sharp and blunt arrows. Blunt arrows subdue instead of killing, and never break.
- Subdued infected lie on the ground, harmless, for 30 seconds before they get up. You can still kill them.
- Camp counts infected killed and subdued; subdues earn the same XP as kills.

**Limitations:** Subdued infected only get back up for now; sedating and training them comes next.

versions.title: Perks
versions.notes:
- Every survivor has a perk that changes how they play, shown on their camp card.
- Mara, Scout: walks silently and crouches faster. Okafor, Brute: +30 health, 40% less claw damage. Lin, Medic: heals after 4 seconds unhurt. Dace, Botanist: double spore samples.
- Newcomers can also be a Marksman (+50% focused damage) or Forager (double sticks and food).
- Pushed-back zones now lose infection more evenly.

versions.title: Safe zones expand
versions.notes:
- Safe zones push the infection back: every run, each open zone next to a safe zone loses 6% of its infection (shown as -% on the world map), up to 70%. Pushed-back zones also have fewer infected.
- Build an outpost in a safe zone (6 scrap, 2 food) to double its push.
- The camp shows how much of the world is reclaimed.

versions.title: Safe zones and the world map
versions.notes:
- A world map of 12 zones at camp. Pick where the next run goes; each zone keeps its layout between runs.
- Spore hearts: pulsing growths at the heart of each zone infection. Shoot one to destroy it and the ground around it is cleansed (it also wakes nearby enemies).
- Destroy every heart in a zone and extract: it becomes a permanent safe zone, with clean ground and no infected, and the zones next to it open.
- Hearts destroyed on a run you extract from stay destroyed; die and they grow back. Further zones have more hearts and more enemies.

versions.title: Skills and levels
versions.notes:
- Survivors earn XP on runs: 10 per kill, 5 per crate, 25 for extracting (failed runs give half).
- Each level gives a skill point to spend at camp on the survivor card: Health (+15 max health), Resist (12% slower infection) or Aim (steadier aim, +15% focus damage). Up to 5 in each.
- Camp cards show level, XP and skills.

versions.title: Stealth
versions.notes:
- Enemies see in a cone (drawn on the ground) that walls block. The cone turns from yellow to red as they notice you; they only attack once it fills.
- Anything within 1.5 m is noticed whatever way they face.
- C toggles crouch: half speed, silent, and enemies see you from only 60% as far. Sprinting stands you up.
- Noise draws enemies to look: walking (2.5 m), sprinting (7 m), the pistol (16 m), the bow (2.5 m), arrows hitting walls.
- Q throws a rock at the cursor (up to 10 m). Enemies near where it lands go to look.

versions.title: Bow and arrows
versions.notes:
- The starter weapon is a bow: hold left click to draw, release to shoot. A full draw hits about three times harder and flies faster.
- Arrows land where they stop and can be picked up again (some break in bodies).
- Sticks lie around every zone, every run. At camp, craft 4 arrows from 2 sticks and 1 scrap. Deploying with no arrows gives you 5 makeshift ones.
- Pistols are rare crate finds: 2 to switch to it, 1 back to the bow. It fires while held and needs ammo.
- Each run takes up to 20 arrows, and the pistol with up to 24 rounds. Gear is lost if the run is.

versions.title: Cursor focus damage
versions.notes:
- Put the cursor right on an enemy to focus it: a red ring marks it, and shots fired while focused deal 75% more damage when they hit it (like Escape from Duckov).
- Damage numbers float up from hits; focused hits show in gold.

versions.title: Mushroom infected enemies
versions.notes:
- Shamblers: people overgrown by the mushroom infection. They wander infected ground, chase you when they see you, and route around walls.
- Their claws hurt and add infection. Health at zero means you are killed and the loot is lost.
- Shots kill them (3 hits). Some drop spore samples; walk over drops to pick them up.
- Shot enemies come looking for you; enemies that lose sight keep tracking you for a few seconds.

**Limitations:** One enemy type so far. They see all around them; vision cones and stealth come later.

versions.title: Quarantine and the cure
versions.notes:
- Quarantine a survivor at camp: they cannot deploy, eat 1 food a run and lose 12% infection a run (only 5% if there is no food).
- Critical survivors (75%+) left outside quarantine get worse every run and turn at 100%.
- Brew a cure from 3 spore samples and 2 medicine. Only a cure clears infection for good, and the survivor gains infection at half rate for their next 3 runs.

**Limitations:** Still no enemies; they arrive next.

versions.title: Extraction and the camp
versions.notes:
- A camp between runs: four survivors, each with their own infection. Choose who deploys.
- Crates in the zone (E to open). Crates on infected ground hold more, including spore samples.
- Stand in the green extraction ring for 3 seconds to extract and keep your loot. Dying or being overrun loses it.
- Survivors who sit out a run recover 5% infection, so rotate them. Killed survivors are wounded for two runs; overrun survivors turn and are gone.
- The camp is saved. Title screen: Continue or New game. Pause menu: Abandon run.
- Walls are lower so they no longer hide you.

**Limitations:** No enemies yet. Infection only comes down slowly by resting; quarantine and the cure are next.

versions.title: Infection on the body
versions.notes:
- Walking on infected ground builds infection on your character (0-100%), faster on worse ground. It does not go down in the field.
- Stages: Clean, Exposed, Infected, Critical. From Infected your aim wobbles; infection also slows stamina regen. The screen tints as it grows.
- At 100% the character is overrun and the run ends.
- Shift to sprint (uses stamina). Health, stamina and infection bars.

**Limitations:** Nothing heals infection yet; quarantine and the cure come in later versions.

versions.title: Isometric core
versions.notes:
- An isometric camera follows you through a generated zone of ruins, rubble and infected ground.
- WASD moves relative to the screen, the mouse aims, left click shoots. Shots stop at walls.
- Mushroom clumps grow on badly infected ground; the ground turns purple where the infection is.

**Limitations:** No enemies or goals yet: this is the movement and shooting core.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: Named save slots with pictures
versions.notes:
- Save slots have names: a new game is named after the first of your squad, and Rename in the slot list changes it (Enter to keep it).
- Each save carries a small picture of the game (taken when you pause or autosave, about 5 KB), shown in the slot list. Saves from older versions show none until they're saved again.
- Exported save files carry the name and picture with them.

**Limitations:** The picture includes the HUD as it was on screen.

versions.title: Gear on the portraits, and a paper doll
versions.notes:
- Each squad card shows a small figure of that person in the colours of their hat, jacket or shirt, trousers and weapon, with lost limbs missing. It greys out when they're down.
- The character panel has a paper doll with what's in each slot beside it. Hover a slot for what it is; click a worn one (or Off) to put it in the pack. The weapon can be put away too.

**Limitations:** Cards in a very big squad are too narrow for the figure.

versions.title: Speech: talk or bribe your way past the Holy Patrol
versions.notes:
- New stat: Speech. Older saves start everyone at 1; new characters and drifters roll it like the rest.
- When the Holy Patrol stops someone for a tithe you can also talk them down (the odds show on the button: Speech and your standing with the faith help; fail and the tithe goes up by half, Holy -3) or bribe a paladin with half the tithe (better odds; fail and they're insulted, Holy -10, nothing paid). One try of each per stop.
- Both train Speech, and so do bribes at the bar, which a smooth talker gets cheaper (1% off per point of Speech, up to half).

**Limitations:** Speech only matters with the patrol and the barkeep so far.

versions.title: Formations and follow
versions.notes:
- Formations for group moves: Loose (everyone at their own pace, as before), Line, Column and Wedge. Pick one on the row over the squad cards (shown with two or more selected), or press V to step through them. They face the way they walk.
- Line, Column and Wedge keep pace with the slowest of the group, so a limping or overloaded carrier isn't left behind.
- Follow: Shift+right-click a squadmate (or Follow... in the panel) and the selected people fall in behind them. Stop following in the panel ends it.
- A big squad gets narrower cards in two rows, and the log moves up out of their way.

**Limitations:** A formation is kept on arrival, not while walking round obstacles.

versions.title: Guard posts and hired guards
versions.notes:
- Guard this spot (G, or the button in the character panel): they hold where they stand, fight any bandit or beast that comes within 15 m, and walk back after. Stop guarding ends it.
- The bar has guards for hire: 150 cats, then 25 cats each midnight. Fair fighters with a blade and a hat, no food needed. They walk to the middle of your base and guard it (outside the bar if you have no base yet); you can order them around like anyone else.
- Miss a night's wage and you're warned; miss two in a row and they quit. Dismiss them from their panel. Up to four at a time; they don't keep the game going if your squad is gone.

**Limitations:** Guards stand where they're posted; they don't patrol or man the walls.

versions.title: Walls that matter, and gates
versions.notes:
- New building: the Gate (3 ore, 40 cats). Your people, the Hub's and the Holy Patrol walk through it; bandits and beasts can't.
- Raiders, and bandits or beasts chasing someone, break through your walls and gates when going round is much further, and take a gap when there is one. Walls take 400 damage, gates 600; a broken one is gone.
- You're told first: a tip with your first wall or gate, the raid warning says when they'll have to break in, and a red line when they start hacking.
- Right-click a damaged wall or gate with someone to repair it (Labour makes it faster). Its label shows how damaged it is.

**Limitations:** Only walls and gates can be broken; other buildings just block the way.

versions.title: Raids
versions.notes:
- Bandits raid your base. Once a Storage Box has something in it, the first raid comes a day later, then one every one and a half to three days. Three raiders at first, up to five as the days go on.
- You get warned: a red log line says where they're gathering, and the minimap marks the spot with a red X and rings the box they're after. They wait about 40 minutes, then walk in.
- Raiders fight anyone in the way, take half of every stack in the boxes near the one they reach, and walk off the map with it. Down them before they leave and the loot is on their bodies.

**Limitations:** Raiders go for storage only; they don't break walls or other buildings.

versions.title: The Holy Patrol's tithe
versions.notes:
- Now and then (at most twice a day, never in your first 12 hours) the Holy Patrol stops one of your people on the road and demands a tithe: 10% of your cats, 20 at least and 300 at most. The game waits for your answer.
- Pay it (Holy +4), refuse it (Holy -25), or run: get clear of the paladins, or into the Hub, and they give up (Holy -5); get caught and they take twice the tithe (Holy -20).
- Leave them waiting for half an hour and they take it as a refusal.

**Limitations:** Only the person they stopped is chased; the rest of the squad can walk on.

versions.title: Grudges fade, bribes help
versions.notes:
- Reputation drifts back toward neutral: bad standing recovers a point every 72 minutes (from hostile to neutral in about two and a half days), good standing fades half as fast.
- The bar shows your standing with the Hub and the Holy Patrol. When they hold something against you, bribe the barkeep: up to 20 points at 8 cats a point, never past neutral.

**Limitations:** The barkeep won't serve enemies of the Hub, so a hostile Hub has to wait out the drift.

versions.title: Limbs and armour on the figures
versions.notes:
- Characters have arms and legs now. A lost arm or leg is gone from the figure too; a prosthetic shows in iron, or bone white for Skeleton limbs.
- Worn armour shows: a hat, a jacket or shirt over the body, trousers on the legs. Weapons show in the hand.
- Loot a body and its armour comes off the figure.

versions.title: Save slots, export and import
versions.notes:
- Three save slots. Your old save is in slot 1. Each game remembers its slot, and autosave and Save game write there.
- Title screen: Continue loads the newest save; Load game lists the slots; New game asks which slot to use once you have a save.
- Pause menu: Save or load a slot, to save into another slot or load one.
- Export a slot as a .kenshi file (a download in the browser) and Import one into any slot. A file that isn't a good save is refused and the slot keeps what it had.

versions.title: Turn items in the pack
versions.notes:
- Pick an item in the pack grid and press R (or the Turn button) to turn it sideways. It turns in place if there's room, otherwise it moves to the first spot where it fits turned.
- New items go in sideways when they only fit that way, so a full pack holds a little more ore.
- Turned items stay turned in saves.

versions.title: Grid inventory
versions.notes:
- Packs are a 6 by 5 grid, like Kenshi's. Items take up space: ore is 1x2, weapons 1x3, jackets and trousers 2x2; food stacks ten to a cell.
- A pack can be full before it's too heavy, and the weight limit from Strength still applies.
- Click an item in the grid to use, wear, wield, fit or give it; click an empty cell to move it there.
- Older saves have their packs laid out in the grid when loaded.

**Limitations:** Items can't be turned sideways (added in 0.1.15).

versions.title: Research
versions.notes:
- A Research Bench to build (5 ore, 200 cats). Right-click it to see the tech tree; starting a tech costs cats, and someone has to work at the bench to finish it.
- A new stat, Science, trained by researching and crafting.
- Techs: Drill Upgrade (drills dig twice as fast), Better Beds (heal 6 times faster), Armour Crafting (make a Leather Jacket from 2 animal hides at the bench), and Skeleton Limbs (after Armour Crafting: the store sells full-strength Skeleton Arms and Legs).

versions.title: Base building
versions.notes:
- Build button in the top bar: lay out Walls, Beds, Storage Boxes and an Ore Drill out in the desert (not in the Hub). Left-click to place, R to turn, Shift-click to place several, right-click to cancel.
- Buildings cost iron ore (taken from packs and storage boxes) and some cost cats. Right-click a site with your people to build it; building trains Labour.
- Finished walls, boxes and drills block the way, and people walk around them. Walls can meet at corners.
- Storage Box: right-click it to put things in or take them out.
- Ore Drill: right-click it to run it. It digs ore into a storage box close by.
- Beds you build are free to sleep in.

**Limitations:** Nobody raids your base yet. Buildings can't be torn down.

versions.title: Factions
versions.notes:
- The Holy Patrol: three well-armed paladins who walk a loop from the Hub's south gate past the eastern ore fields, hunting bandits and beasts. They leave you alone unless you attack them.
- Reputation with the Hub and the Holy Patrol, shown in the top bar. Downing bandits and beasts near the Hub raises it with both; attacking their people drops it hard.
- At hostile reputation the guards attack you, and the store and bar won't deal with you.
- Ctrl+right-click attacks anyone, townsfolk and paladins included. Their side comes to help.

**Limitations:** Reputation doesn't recover on its own yet.

versions.title: Minimap, day and night
versions.notes:
- A minimap in the top-left corner: the Hub, the bandit camp, the bonedog den, ore (dull when mined out), mesas, your squad, and any threats close to your people. Click or drag on it to look there.
- Day and night: dusk from 18:00, dark from 20:00 to 05:00, dawn until 07:00. The light dims and turns blue.
- At night, bandits and beasts spot you from about half as far.

versions.title: Mining job
versions.notes:
- Keep mining: while someone is mining, a button in the character panel turns it into a job. They mine until their pack is full, haul the ore to the General Store, sell it, walk back and carry on, moving to the next node when one runs dry.
- The store has a button to sell the iron ore of everyone standing at the counter.

versions.title: Carrying bodies
versions.notes:
- Right-click a downed squadmate who isn't bleeding (or a dead one) to pick them up. Still bleeding? Right-click patches them up first.
- The carrier walks slower and drops the body to fight back if attacked.
- Right-click a bed while carrying to lay them in it; they heal there and keep resting once they wake.
- Pick up and Put down buttons in the character panel.

**Limitations:** Only squadmates can be carried.

versions.title: Lost limbs
versions.notes:
- An arm or leg hacked far below zero is lost for good: a lost arm weakens your swings, a lost leg leaves you crawling. It bleeds hard when it happens.
- A warning in the log when a limb is badly hacked up, before it goes.
- The General Store sells an Iron Arm and an Iron Leg (600 cats). Fit one from the pack: it works again, with less health than the real thing, and never comes off.
- Body parts in the character panel turn yellow when badly hurt, red below zero, and say LOST when gone.

**Limitations:** The figures don't show missing limbs yet.

versions.title: Armour
versions.notes:
- Armour slots for head, body and legs. Armour cuts the damage to the parts it covers (a jacket covers torso and arms).
- The General Store sells a Leather Hat, Leather Jacket and Leather Trousers. Bandits wear ragged shirts (and some wear hats); guards wear full leathers.
- Wear and Take off in the character panel; looting a body takes its armour too.
- The character panel is more compact, and one Give button lists your squadmates.

versions.title: The bar
versions.notes:
- A bar in the Hub, east of the gate. Right-click it or the barkeep to go in.
- Hire drifters looking for work, for about 200 to 350 cats each; a new one turns up most days. Your squad can grow past three.
- Rent a bed out back for 60 cats: a character in bed heals four times faster and stops bleeding sooner, and gets up once healed.
- Right-click a bed to lie in it. Squad cards make room for a bigger squad.

versions.title: Easier to read
versions.notes:
- Smaller names, and a health bar over each character (orange while bleeding). Downed characters only show their name when selected, so a pile of bodies stays readable.
- The event log shows the time of each line, and danger (down, robbed, died, starving) in red.
- A hint by the cursor says what a right-click will do: mine, attack, loot, trade or patch up.
- Squadmates within 12 m who are idle or mining join the fight when one of them is attacked. Ones you've told to walk keep walking.
- H hides the controls text.

versions.title: Walking around things
versions.notes:
- Characters walk around the town walls, buildings, mesas, rocks, tents and ore rocks instead of through them, and leave town by the gates.
- Nobody gets pushed into a wall when a crowd bunches up.

versions.title: Save and load
versions.notes:
- The game autosaves every two hours on the clock and when you quit to the title.
- Continue on the title screen picks up where you left off; New game starts over.
- Save game in the pause menu (Esc) saves right away.
- If your whole squad dies, you can load the last save.

**Limitations:** One save slot. Characters still walk through buildings and rocks.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes:
- A bleak desert map with the Hub (walled town, General Store, guards), a bandit camp, a bonedog den and eight iron ore nodes.
- Free camera: WASD, arrows or the screen edge to pan, wheel to zoom, Q and E or middle-drag to turn, F to find your squad.
- Three squad members controlled RTS-style: click or drag to select, right-click to move, attack, mine, trade, loot or patch up.
- Stats that grow with use: Strength, Toughness, Melee Attack, Melee Defence, Athletics, Labour and First Aid. Fighting someone better teaches more.
- Health per body part (head, torso, arms, legs) and blood. At 0 head or torso a character goes down, can bleed out, and gets back up if the bleeding stops.
- Ruined legs slow you to a crawl, ruined arms weaken your swings.
- Hunger: characters eat from their pack, or a squadmate's, and starving hurts.
- Dust Bandits and Bonedogs roam the wastes, knock you out, rob you and move on; wiped-out groups come back later.
- Mine iron ore and sell it at the General Store for cats; buy food and better weapons. Loot downed enemies.
- Pause with Space; 1x, 2x and 3x speed with 1, 2, 3 or the buttons.
- Placeholder sound effects.

**Limitations:** No saving yet. Characters walk through buildings and rocks. One shop, one town, no recruiting or base building.

versions.title: Scaffold
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: One more job
versions.notes: - New level 23: Spare key.

versions.title: Monster fixes
versions.notes:
- The level list scrolls by dragging on a phone, and tapping a level there works.
- Monsters no longer growl as a level starts; they react the moment you pull a pin.

versions.title: Monster levels
versions.notes:
- Five more levels (18-22): monsters with water, padlocks and double pockets.
- Fixed: rings of neighbouring pins no longer overlap on Night watch.

versions.title: Monsters
versions.notes:
- Monsters! Open a way to the thief and one will come running, and it's a KO.
- Lava kills a monster. Water and gold don't slow it down; stone and walls do.
- Five new levels (13-17).

versions.title: No more hints
versions.notes:
- Level subtitles are gone: work each puzzle out for yourself.
- Levels whose names gave the trick away have new names.
- Pins wiggle if you leave them alone for a few seconds.
- The level list scrolls.

versions.title: Thuds and splashes
versions.notes:
- A heavy load hitting the floor thuds and shakes the screen.
- Water splashes droplets where it lands; stone crumbles with a gritty pop.
- Sparkles twinkle around the thief when the heist works.

versions.title: Juicy screens
versions.notes:
- Buttons squash when pressed; menus fade and pop in; level cards bounce in.
- Winning: stars pop in one by one with rising chimes, and confetti falls.
- Coins rain behind the title; levels fade in, so a retry is quick and smooth.
- The gold counter punches up as coins land.

versions.title: Juicy board
versions.notes:
- Pins strain and wiggle before they slide, with a metal glint and a small screen kick.
- Lava glows and bubbles, gold sparkles, stone crumbs pop where water meets lava.
- The thief blinks, trembles when lava gets close, and keels over when busted.
- Phones buzz on a pin pull and at the end of a level (where the browser allows it).

**Limitations:** No buzz on iPhone (Safari has no vibration).

versions.title: Locked pins
versions.notes:
- Padlocked pins: a red padlock won't budge (it rattles) until the pin it waits for is pulled.
- Level 11, Padlock, and level 12, Hot key: the gold is locked behind the lava pin.

**Limitations:** Padlocks don't show which pin holds their key.

versions.title: Clinks, sizzles and stars
versions.notes:
- Sounds: pin clink, sizzle when water meets lava, coins landing, win and lose jingles (made in code).
- Steam puffs rise where water cools lava.
- 1 to 3 stars per level by how much of the gold reaches the thief; best stars show in the level select.
- The win panel waits until the gold has finished landing.

**Limitations:** No locked pins yet.

versions.title: Two fires and the grand heist
versions.notes:
- Level 9, Two fires: drain one lava pool and cool the other.
- Level 10, Grand heist: cool a wide lava floor, then empty both gold pockets.
- Upright pins no longer put their ring on top of another pin's ring; levels pick which side each ring sits on.

**Limitations:** No sound yet. No locked pins.

versions.title: Two more heists
versions.notes:
- Level 7, Two pockets: drain the lava into a pit and collect gold from both sides.
- Level 8, Upside down: lava falling onto water hardens into stone too.

**Limitations:** No sound yet. 8 levels; no locked pins.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes:
- Pull-the-pin puzzles: tap or click a pin to slide it out and let gold, water and lava fall.
- Falling-grain sim: water cools lava into stone, lava melts gold and burns the thief.
- 6 levels that teach one idea each, a level select that saves cleared levels, and Restart always on screen.
- Portrait layout for phones that also fits a desktop browser; touch and mouse only.
- Title screen, pause menu (Menu button, Esc or Tab), volume setting, and this version log.

**Limitations:** No sound yet. Only 6 levels; no locked pins.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes:
- Tap a monster with a number less than or equal to yours to chomp it and grow by its number.
- Tap one bigger than you and you get bonked; eat the boss at the top to win.
- Gold stars multiply you (x2, later x3), bombs shrink you. Order matters!
- Endless levels that grow taller and wider; every level is checked to be winnable.
- Level select, saved progress, retry, pause, volume, silly sounds and confetti.
- Portrait and touch-first: built for phones.

**Limitations:** Sounds and art are made in code. No stars rating or par yet.

versions.title: Shorter save codes
versions.notes:
- Save codes are about a quarter shorter (PD2): one byte per move and the seed stored as a number. Every move is still in the code.
- Older PD1 codes still import.

**Limitations:** Codes still keep every move, so they grow with your records.

versions.title: Themes
versions.notes:
- Unlock new looks as you beat levels: Liquid (10 levels, with a wobbling surface and bubbles), Candy (25, glossy stripes) and Gems (50, cut facets).
- Dark background unlocks after 5 levels.
- Pick them in Settings; the win screen tells you when something new unlocks.

versions.title: Hints
versions.notes:
- New Hint button (3 per level): a pointing hand shows a move on a shortest way to win from where you are.
- The search runs a little each frame, so the game never freezes while it thinks. Restarting doesn't refill hints.

**Limitations:** On hidden-layer levels the hint can see under the ? layers.

versions.title: Fast pours
versions.notes:
- Settings, Fast pours: pours animate in about half the time.
- Tap your next move while a pour is still running: up to two taps wait and play as soon as it lands.

versions.title: Tutorial
versions.notes:
- First time on level 1, a pointing hand shows which tube to tap, then where to pour it.
- The first time a pour is turned down, a one-line tip explains the rule. Both show once.

versions.title: Stars and the level map
versions.notes:
- Earn up to 3 stars per level: 3 at or under par, 2 within a quarter over par, 1 for any win. The win screen says how many moves the next star needs.
- The level map shows each level's stars and your total, and opens scrolled to your current level.
- Next unbeaten on the level map jumps to the lowest level you haven't beaten yet.
- The top bar shows the level's par next to your moves.

versions.title: Harder puzzles
versions.notes:
- Every level up to 200 is now the hardest of several candidate puzzles (the one needing the most pours), so later levels make you think. Levels 1-3 stay gentle.
- Par is worked out ahead of time for levels 1-200, so it shows right away, hidden and locked levels included.

**Limitations:** Levels changed, so earlier bests on changed levels show as New puzzle; those levels stay beaten.

versions.title: Locked tubes
versions.notes:
- From level 72, every third level has a locked tube: a padlock in one color. Nothing pours in or out until you finish a tube of that color.
- Tapping a locked tube shakes it and says which color opens it; it pops open with a glow when you finish that color.
- Old records stay safe: levels that changed keep their check but show New puzzle, and your next win sets a fresh best.

versions.title: Sound pass
versions.notes:
- A sandy pour hiss that lasts as long as the pour and rises in pitch as the tube fills.
- Glassy clinks when you lift and set down a tube, a chord on each finished tube (each color has its own), and a fanfare on a win.
- A soft music loop, made in code like every other sound.
- Settings: separate Volume, Effects and Music sliders, and a Vibration toggle.
- Phones buzz briefly on a pour, a finished tube and a win.

**Limitations:** iPhones don't vibrate from a web page (Safari has no vibration API); Android phones do.

versions.title: Save codes
versions.notes:
- Settings, Export save: your progress, records and settings as one code, copied to the clipboard and shown so you can select it.
- Settings, Import save: paste a code (Paste button or Ctrl+V), check what it holds, then confirm to replace your save.
- Codes are versioned and checksummed: a damaged or cut-off code gets a clear message and never touches your save.

**Limitations:** Codes grow with your records, since they keep every move: about 1,600 characters after 30 levels.

versions.title: Level select
versions.notes:
- Levels screen from the title and pause menus: a scrolling grid of every level up to your furthest, plus the next few locked ones.
- Beaten levels show a check and your fewest moves; the level you're on is outlined.
- Replay any unlocked level to beat your record.

versions.title: Move records
versions.notes:
- Each beaten level keeps your fewest moves. The win screen and the top bar show it.
- Par: the fewest possible pours, worked out in the background, shown on the win screen when it's found in time (not on hidden-layer levels).
- Undone pours don't count toward your moves; the + Tube booster doesn't count as a move.
- Records keep the level's seed and your whole move list, ready for a leaderboard that can check them later.

**Limitations:** Par isn't shown on big levels where the search runs out of room, or on levels with hidden layers.

versions.title: Pour, sort, win
versions.notes:
- Tap a tube to lift it, tap another to pour. Pours go onto an empty tube or the same top color, and move the whole top run that fits.
- Pour animation: the tube flies over, tilts, and a stream of sand fills the target. Finished tubes get a cork, a pop and confetti.
- Endless levels that get harder: more colors, one-spare-tube levels, deeper tubes from level 18, hidden ? layers from level 36.
- Every level is checked by a solver before you see it.
- Undo (5 per level), Restart, and a + Tube booster (1 per level). Your level and best level are saved.
- Tells you when there are no moves left and offers undo, an extra tube or a restart.
- Each color has its own shape for colorblind players (Settings, Color shapes).

**Limitations:** Placeholder sounds. Hidden layers only reveal one at a time.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: Pick a level
versions.notes:
- Levels screen (from the title or the pause menu): every unlocked level with its stars, to replay for a better score. Locked levels are greyed out.
- The title shows your stars and how many levels you've cleared.
- Orange cars are a deeper orange, easier to tell from the yellow ones.
- Testing: add ?level=N to the web address to jump to a level. It's only saved once you clear it.

versions.title: Three hearts
versions.notes:
- Three hearts per level: every bump costs one, and a third bump fails the level (Try again).
- A move counter against the best possible (one tap per car) and 1 to 3 stars per level: 3 with no bumps, one fewer per bump. Stars are saved.
- Restart button to start the level over (there is no undo).
- Hint button: a car that can leave right now bobs up, preferring one that is in other cars' way.

**Limitations:** No level select yet.

versions.title: Vroom
versions.notes:
- Sound: a tap click, an engine rev as cars pull away, a knock and a honk on a bump, and a fanfare when the lot is clear. All made in code.
- Cars squash when tapped, lean back as they pull away, kick up tyre smoke and roll their wheels.
- Bumps jolt the camera and puff smoke where the cars meet; the car that was hit wobbles.
- New levels drop their cars in one by one, a clear lot bursts into confetti, and menus pop in.

**Limitations:** No stars, hearts, hint button or level select yet.

versions.title: Clear the lot
versions.notes:
- Tap or click a car to drive it forward. With a clear road it drives out; with a car in the way it bumps and rolls back.
- Clear every car to finish the level. Levels are generated from the level number, always solvable, and grow from a small lot to a packed 8 by 10.
- Tilted 3D lot that fits the screen in portrait and landscape, bright cars with windscreens, headlights and a roof arrow.
- Pause button for phones, a hint line on the first levels, and your progress is saved: Play continues where you left off.

**Limitations:** No sound or particles yet; no stars, hearts, hint button or level select yet.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: Restock: buildings that pack up
versions.notes:
- The Konbini Syndicate's gimmick. Select a Microwave Bank, Loading Dock, Break Room, Parking Lot, Security Monitors, First Aid Aisle or Lottery Counter and press U (or Pack up): it folds into a Restock Cart at once, keeping its share of health; anything waiting in its queue is refunded. Drive the cart anywhere and press U to unfold it on a clear footprint (green when it fits). Turrets, the Neon Sign, walls, the Drone Roof and the Sale Billboard stay put.
- The Delivery Drone lifts a cart too: a cart takes three of its six seats. Right-click the drone with the cart selected, fly it, U to set it down.
- Harvesters find a moved Loading Dock on their own. While you still have a cart rolling you are not beaten. A tip explains packing the first time you select a building that packs.
- AI against AI: unchanged (the rival does not pack up); every row of the balance table is the same as v0.1.52.

**Limitations:** The rival never packs or airlifts its buildings. A packed building's rally flag is forgotten.

versions.title: Konbini Syndicate
versions.notes:
- A fourth faction: the Konbini Syndicate, late-shift convenience-store workers who took over the supply chain. Mint and orange, permanently tired, always polite. Their resource is Loyalty Points, harvested from Stamp Cards by Delivery Scooters (smaller loads, quicker trips).
- Everything is a little cheaper and quicker to build than the other factions (about 10%), and a lot flimsier (about 28% less health, 15% less damage). Buildings: Flagship Store, Microwave Bank, Loading Dock, Break Room, Parking Lot, Drone Roof, Price Gun Kiosk, Neon Sign (anti-air), First Aid Aisle (repair bay), Security Monitors (radar), Lottery Counter (income), Sale Billboard, Cart Corral walls and an Automatic Door.
- Units: Clerk (barcode rifle), Shift Manager (price gun: anti-vehicle and anti-air), Night Shift (a very fast raider with a tape gun, after the Parking Lot), Forklift (tank), Shelf Launcher (artillery), Bottle Rocket Van (anti-air), Bike Courier (scout), Franchise Truck (mobile yard), Delivery Drone (carries six infantry) and the Hot Food Bomber. No fighter: anti-air is the van, the Manager and the Neon Sign.
- Superweapon: the Midnight Sale. Charges in three and a half minutes; your units in a wide ring heal half their health and fire 60% faster for 14 seconds.
- AI against AI, the balance table for the new pairings (both seatings, four maps, 420 s): the Konbini Syndicate beats the Council on every map (291 to 398 s), loses to Sparkle on Rocky Spine (262 to 280 s) and Twin Isles (182 s), and draws the Covenant and Sparkle on the long maps; the Konbini mirror is even. The first try (everything 25% cheaper and faster) won 46 of 48 games by about 200 s, so the prices went up. The old pairings' rows are unchanged.

**Limitations:** The Restock gimmick (packing buildings up and moving them, and the Drone carrying them) comes next. Night Shift has no stealth yet.

versions.title: Pick your seat, and a Controls page
versions.notes:
- The title screen has a Start pick: Random, or any start of the map by where it is (bottom left, top right, left, ...). Your first rival takes the start farthest from yours, any others the remaining starts. The map screen's preview marks your start in pink (all plain for Random). The pick is saved.
- A Controls page on the title screen lists every control, grouped (Mouse, Orders, Camera, Groups, Sidebar, Base, Game). The pause menu shows the same list, and the hotkey strip at the bottom is made from the same table the keys are read from, so none of them can fall behind a new key.

**Limitations:** A random start is rolled for each new game, so two games in a row may land on the same one.

versions.title: Sidebar tabs that page
versions.notes:
- A sidebar tab with more than eight entries now shows seven a page and a More button in the eighth cell ("More 1 / 2"). The More button, key 8 after the tab key, the tab's key pressed again, or the mouse wheel over the build buttons turn the page; changing tab starts on page one. More shows a star while something on the other page is building, queued or ready.
- No tab needs it yet (the fullest have eight); it is ready for the fourth faction.

versions.title: The rival pays its snipers and answers a siege
versions.notes:
- A rival whose units pay for every shot (the Council's Treasurers) only buys another one when it also has eight shots' worth of money in the bank for it and the ones it already has, so its snipers fire in the fights instead of clicking empty.
- Siege answer (Normal and Hard): when one of the rival's buildings is shelled by something standing outside the reach of all its defences (Bass Droppers, Projector Cannons, any artillery), its idle army near home attack-moves at the shooter. Units already in a fight are never pulled. If it owns nothing that reaches as far, the next unit it buys is its own longest-range ground unit.
- AI against AI, the balance table (every pairing, both seatings, four maps, 420 s), before and after: Council games lost 19 before, 15 after, none won either way. Twin Isles Council against Sparkle: two Sparkle wins (363 and 411 s) become draws. River Crossing Council against the Covenant: the Covenant won all four (305 to 361 s); now three draws and one win at 398 s. Four Corners Council against Sparkle from one seating: a draw becomes a Sparkle win at 399 s. Rocky Spine is unchanged for the Council (Sparkle still wins there at 313 to 351 s). Overall results: 40 draws, 20 Sparkle and 12 Covenant wins before; 45, 18 and 9 after. Unpaid shots in Council games: 124 before, 68 after. Sieges answered: 161 across the 72 games.
- The balance table can be narrowed and run under fog or on another level (tests/balance.gd -- skirmish_1 council fog hard) and now prints unpaid shots and sallies.

**Limitations:** A sally goes to where the shooter stood when it fired; artillery that moves away after firing leaves the sally walking to an empty spot.

versions.title: A tune that swells, and a ceremony
versions.notes:
- Music: an original chiptune idol tune, written for the game and synthesized in code (no recordings). It starts on the title screen. In a game a second layer of drums, a busier bass and the tune an octave up swells in over a couple of seconds when enemy units close on your base (eight or more makes it full), and fades again once they are gone; a rival superweapon about to fire raises it a little.
- Settings has a Music slider, under the main Volume.
- A rank-up ceremony: when one of your units earns its third star where you can see it, the camera holds on it for a moment, stars burst around it, a fanfare plays and its legend line appears in a big bubble. At most one ceremony every ten seconds.

**Limitations:** One tune, about fifteen seconds long, on a loop. The music takes a second or two to be made when the page first loads, so the title starts quiet.

versions.title: Four Corners
versions.notes:
- A fourth map, Four Corners: 80 x 60 tiles with a base in each corner. Every corner is the same ground, flipped: a field by the base, a field on each edge shared with a neighbour, and a rich field near the middle behind a broken rock ridge.
- On Four Corners the title screen has a Rivals pick: 1 rival (across the map), or 2 or 3 for a free-for-all. The first rival plays the faction you picked for it, the others the next factions in turn. When a rival is knocked out a banner says so; if you are knocked out the game ends there, and the result screen counts the rivals that fell.
- The rival superweapon line on the sidebar shows the soonest one and how many more there are.
- AI against AI, four-way free-for-alls to 900 s: Sparkle / Council / Covenant / Sparkle: Sparkle wins at 633 s (the Council falls first, at 499 s); Council / Covenant / Sparkle / Council: Sparkle wins at 495 s; Covenant / Sparkle / Council / Covenant: a Covenant wins at 668 s; three-way Sparkle / Council / Covenant: Sparkle at 600 s. One on one across the map (both seatings, 420 s): mirror matches and Sparkle against the Council draw; Sparkle beats the Covenant (338 to 365 s) and the Covenant beats the Council (373 to 399 s), whichever corner they start in.
- A four-player game costs about 0.8 ms a step headless (two players: about 0.3 ms).

**Limitations:** No teams yet: it is every base for itself. The AIs attack whoever is nearest. Saves from v0.1.46 are not offered.

versions.title: Twin Isles
versions.notes:
- A third map, Twin Isles: open water, a home island on each side and a rich island in the middle whose four fields hold more than the ones at home. Two causeways lead from each home island to the middle one, so every field can be reached on foot; there is no straight way across.
- Twin Isles is a mirror image left to right rather than a half turn, so both bases have the same top and bottom. The rules that keep the two seats equal (which ore tile a harvester picks, where units leave a building, how the rival lays out its base, how paths break ties) now flip as well as turn, and both seats still deposit exactly the same until the armies meet.
- AI against AI on Twin Isles (both seatings, 420 s): every mirror match is a draw; Sparkle beats the Council from one seating (363 s) and draws from the other, and beats the Covenant from either (224 to 238 s); the Council and the Covenant draw. On Rocky Spine and River Crossing every game plays out exactly as before.

**Limitations:** The Covenant has a hard time against Sparkle on Twin Isles. Saves from v0.1.45 are not offered (the seat rules changed).

versions.title: Save and load
versions.notes:
