versions.title: Ropes and snips
versions.notes:
- Our own rope physics: a ball of yarn hangs from ropes pinned to sewing buttons.
- Drag the mouse or swipe a finger across a rope to snip it; the yarn swings and falls.
- Play opens a test level with two ropes.

**Limitations:** No kitten or goal yet: the yarn just falls off the bottom.

versions.title: Scaffold
versions.notes:
- Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.
- A blank 2D stage: the rope puzzles arrive in the next releases.

versions.title: Reconnect window
versions.notes:
- Online: when a player drops, the match pauses and their seat waits 45 seconds for them, with a countdown for everyone. The host can choose "Continue without them"; after the wait an AI takes the seat.
- A player who lost the host tries to get back in by themselves ("Reconnecting... 45 s"), or can play on offline.
- Reloaded the tab? The Online screen offers "Rejoin your match" for a few minutes.
- A rejoining player is brought up to date from the host's copy of the match.

**Limitations:** If the host drops, the match can't wait for them: everyone else plays on offline.

versions.title: Resync
versions.notes:
- Online: when a player's game drifts out of sync, the host sends its copy of the match and everyone carries on from it, with a short "resynced" banner, instead of playing on in two different matches.
- The sync check looks at more (reload timers, slows, transports, wrecks and shots in flight), so drift is caught where it starts.
- If a match goes out of sync three times in two minutes, you can play on offline against AIs or leave.
- Each machine writes what it had to a desync file, to compare when something goes wrong.
- Big online messages are compressed and sent in pieces.

**Limitations:** After a resync the match's replay starts from the resync. Not yet tried between two real browsers with a forced desync.

versions.title: Playtest pass 3
versions.notes:
- Fixed a crash in Beige Alert: Lilith answering a ping made some units look for lines they don't have.
- Heart to Heart: Lilith's silo now fires on a timetable with a warning 30 s before each bomb, instead of stockpiling from the first second (which starved her and made the mission easy). She's a Normal AI now, and you start with a Plushie Lab and three Guard Kitties.
- Candy Crush Hour: the four waves are a little smaller and further apart, and you start with five Guard Kitties.
- Beige Alert: Lilith is a Hard ally and one Bureau Commander is Normal; the finale was out of reach for most players.
- Bomb Shelter: Lilith has a real base now (pumps, panels, a lab, more turrets), so rushing her Commander isn't a five-minute three-star win.
- Locked buttons (Story missions, outfits) have dark, readable text.

**Limitations:** Air Show, Fleet Week, Stork Raid and Lagoon Day were checked in the web build only briefly; the headless autoplayer can't play them.

versions.title: Map editor
versions.notes:
- Map editor on the title screen: paint hills, water, Sparkle Wells and start spots on a top-down map, with Erase and three brush and map sizes.
- Save checks the map first and says what's wrong (a start in the water, hills too close together, too many starts...).
- Play starts a free-for-all on it with an AI on every other start; saved maps also show up on the New Game screen.
- Saves and replays of a custom map keep the map inside them, so they still work if you delete the map.

**Limitations:** Custom maps can't be played online yet. Hills are flat mounds (no height).

versions.title: Sundae Circle
versions.notes:
- A fifth map, Sundae Circle: 240 m across, six starts on a ring, wells for every base, a well between each pair of neighbours and a contested centre behind a ring of rocks.
- Free-for-all now takes up to five AI opponents: six Commanders at once.
- Two more team colours: Team Peach and Team Soda.
- Picking more opponents than a map has starts moves a free-for-all to Sundae Circle.

versions.title: Spectate
versions.notes:
- Spectate on the New Game screen: watch the match you set up with AIs in every seat, fog off.
- A speed slider from 0.5x to 8x, Pause, View (any team's eyes, or everything) and Exit.
- Live graphs of Sparkle income and army value, with the big moments marked; Graphs hides them.
- The end screen names the winner, and Rematch spectates again.

**Limitations:** The resource bars at the top show the first team's economy.

versions.title: Commander outfits
versions.notes:
- Clear a challenge or a story mission with 3 stars to unlock a named outfit for your Commander: twelve in all, from Pyjama Lilac to Sunset Orange.
- Pick it in the new Outfit row on the New Game screen, or in an online room (everyone sees each other's). Locked outfits say which challenge or mission unlocks them.
- Your outfit comes along into challenges and story missions, and into saves and replays. Her ribbon keeps your team colour.

versions.title: Story, part 2: the twist
versions.notes:
- Mission 4, Meanwhile, in the Gloom: play as Lilith and hold her manor for 6 minutes against six Kawaii waves.
- Mission 5, Heart to Heart: a Hard Lilith has a Love Bomb silo. Build Cuddle Catchers, then push in and pop her.
- Mission 6, Beige Alert: the Boring Bureau wants everything beige. Team up with Lilith (an AI ally) against two Hard Bureau Commanders.
- Finish mission 6 for the ending. The Story list can play it again afterwards.

versions.title: Story, part 1
versions.notes:
- Story on the title screen: Hoshiko against Lilith, with chibi dialogue before and after each mission. Tap or Space for the next line, Skip to jump ahead.
- Mission 1, First Sparkle: build your first base on Marshmallow Meadow (Tier 1 only) and pop an Easy Lilith.
- Mission 2, Candy Crush Hour: hold your Candy Canyon outpost through four waves, then counter-attack.
- Mission 3, Lagoon Day: sink Lilith's Pier and her submarines on Lollipop Lagoon.
- Missions open in order and keep your best stars. Hoshiko and Lilith chat during missions too.

**Limitations:** Missions 4 to 6 and the ending come next.

versions.title: More challenges
versions.notes:
- Fleet Week: on Lollipop Lagoon with land and air factories banned, sink the enemy's Dockyard and every boat. You start with a Dockyard of your own. More stars for winning fast.
- Bomb Shelter: Lilith's silo fires Love Bombs at your base at 4, 7 and 10 minutes, with a warning 30 s before each. Survive all three; more stars for each one your Cuddle Catchers stop.
- Stork Raid: one Stork Carrier, eight Kitty Racers, no factories. Pop five enemy Sparkle Pumps inside 8 minutes; more stars for bringing the Stork home and for being quick.
- Challenges can now be lost on time, and start with buildings and units on either side.

versions.title: Online play
versions.notes:
- Online on the title screen: host a room and send friends the code or the invite link, or join theirs. 1v1 or 2v2, in the browser, no install.
- In the room each player picks a side and a faction; the host picks the mode, the map and how good the AIs are. Empty seats get AIs, so two friends can team up against two AIs.
- Everyone must run the same version; the room says so if not.
- In a match the menu doesn't pause anything, saving is off, and Leave match goes back to the title. If someone drops out an AI takes over their team; if the host leaves, the others play on against AIs.
- Watch replay works for online matches too.

**Limitations:** The host's tab must stay visible: a hidden tab freezes the match for everyone. Built-in maps only.

versions.title: Lockstep for online play
versions.notes:
- Under the hood: the engine for online matches. Every player runs the same battle; only orders travel, gathered by the host into short turns (a tenth of a second) and run at the same moment everywhere.
- Players check every few seconds that their battles still match, and a red banner says so if they don't.
- If a player drops out, an AI takes over their team at the same moment for everyone; if the host drops out, the others play on against AIs.
- Online matches can be watched as replays too.
- The lobby to actually start one comes in the next version.

versions.title: Match replays
versions.notes:
- Watch replay on the end screen (skirmishes, challenges and loaded games): the whole match plays again from the start, exactly as it happened.
- The replay bar at the top has Pause, 1x, 2x and 4x, the time, View (you, each other team, or everything with no fog) and Exit. If your computer can't keep up with 4x it shows the speed it really reaches.
- While watching you can select units to see their cards and move the camera freely, but not give orders.
- Replays are kept until you leave the end screen, and only play in the version that recorded them.
- Dev key F7 pops every enemy Commander (to test end screens quickly).

**Limitations:** Not for the guided first match. Replays aren't saved to disk yet.

versions.title: Commands and a deterministic match
versions.notes:
- Under the hood: every order you give (moves, builds, factory queues, toggles, pings, specials, even the dev keys) is now a recorded command. A match fed the same commands plays out exactly the same, which is what replays and online play need.
- Fog of war now works per side inside the battle itself, so what your units can shoot no longer depends on whose screen it is.
- Nothing should look or play differently.

versions.title: The AI reaches the late game
versions.notes:
- Hard AI: while its first Tier 2 lab is going up, its constructors help build it and the Commander waits to level up, so Tier 2 arrives minutes sooner.
- Hard AI: when it's short of money with a decent army at home, its Tier 1 factories rest so the money goes to Tier 2, the Gigantic Gate and the Love Bomb silo.
- Hard AI builds a Hug Shield over home on its own, a Gate a bit sooner, and doesn't wait for a full store before starting its silo.
- All AIs stop building Sunshine Panels when Sparkle is the real shortage (they used to sink Sparkle into panels while stalled).
- When anyone starts a Love Bomb silo, the nearest Normal or Hard AI constructor drops what it's doing to build a Cuddle Catcher. Hard adds a second over its forward factory and rebuilds lost ones.
- An AI's first boat is a quick Rubber Duck scout.

**Limitations:** AI-vs-AI matches still usually end before 20 minutes, so the late tech shows most in long or defensive games.

versions.title: Phone polish
versions.notes:
- Menus scroll when they don't fit, and on screens with options (New Game, the end screen) the buttons stay pinned at the bottom. Titles are smaller on phones.
- Hold a finger on a unit or a build button for half a second to see its info card. Lifting the finger after that does nothing else; the next touch closes the card.
- On touch, build buttons act when the finger lifts (so a long-press can show the card instead).
- Pinch with two fingers on the minimap to make it bigger (up to 2x, or 60% of the screen height), kept for the session.
- The info card wraps long lines instead of running off the right edge.

**Limitations:** Checked with synthesized touches and desktop renders at 844x390; a real phone check is still Josh's.

versions.title: Depth charges and the Sonar Buoy
versions.notes:
- Swan Cruisers drop depth charges on enemy subs their sonar has found within 12 m (240 damage every 3 s). One Swan narrowly beats one sub; subs still sink Whale-ships.
- New Sonar Buoy (Defence tab, any constructor): sits in the sea by the shore, finds subs within 22 m and lobs depth charges at found ones within 16 m. Now a player without a Dockyard can answer subs.
- Torpedoes can hit buildings in the sea (Dockyards and Sonar Buoys).
- A sonar ring shows around a selected Sonar Buoy and while placing one.
- Normal and Hard AIs build Sonar Buoys by their shore after a torpedo hit, and build more Swans when they know of subs.
- New warning the first time your sub is depth-charged; the torpedo warning now says Swans and Sonar Buoys are the answer.

versions.title: Round 4's rough edges
versions.notes:
- The Commander's Upgrade button now shows the next level as soon as she levels up, without reselecting her.
- The battle music finishes getting ready in smaller slices while a match is running, so a match started right after the page loads no longer stutters for the first seconds.
- Checked in the browser: save a match, reload the page, and load it again.

versions.title: Touch and small screens
versions.notes:
- Play on a phone or tablet: the first touch turns touch controls on. Tap to select (double-tap: everything of that type on screen), drag a box, tap the ground or an enemy to give orders. Two fingers pan and pinch to zoom.
- A touch command bar (top right) has Attack, Patrol, Reclaim, Stop, Stance, Special, Upgrade, Load and Unload, Launch, Ping, a Queue toggle, Deselect and Pause, showing only what fits the selection.
- Building by touch: pick a building, then drag the ghost where you want it and lift your finger; Cancel is on the bar.
- Small screens (a phone on its side) draw everything 1.5x bigger with one scrolling row of big build buttons. Held upright, the game asks you to turn the phone sideways.
- On phones the browser build turns anti-aliasing off and uses half the confetti, to keep it smooth.

**Limitations:** Tested with synthesized touches and a desktop render at 844x390; a real phone check is still to do.

versions.title: Team pings and end-screen markers
versions.notes:
- Alt+click the ground or the minimap to drop a heart ping for your team (once every 5 seconds). It pulses on the ground and blinks on the minimap.
- AI allies answer: if your side can see an enemy near the ping, their idle army attacks there; if not, half of it comes to guard the spot for 45 seconds. Their Commander says so in a speech bubble.
- AI allies ping where their own attack waves are heading, so you can see the plan.
- The end-screen graphs mark the match's key moments: each side's first Tier 2 unit and first giant, Love Bomb launches, Commanders popping, and the biggest fight (the ten seconds with the most damage). Up to eight markers.

versions.title: Battle music that follows the fight
versions.notes:
- The battle music now has three moods of the same song: a calm build-up (pads and arps), the fight (the full idol-pop loop) and danger (driving drums, an alarm bell, a lower lead).
- It picks the mood once a second: danger while your Commander is low or under fire, fight when your side has dealt or taken 400+ damage in the last 8 seconds, otherwise calm. Each mood is held at least 8 seconds.
- The three play in step and crossfade over 2 seconds, so the beat never jumps. A match opens calm.

versions.title: Skirmish challenges
versions.notes:
- Challenges on the title screen: short scenarios with a briefing, a goal panel during the match, and a rating of 1 to 3 stars. Your best rating is kept.
- Sleepover Siege: your base is already built; hold out for 5 minutes against six scripted waves. More stars for losing fewer buildings.
- Air Show: win on Candy Canyon with flyers only (bot, vehicle and boat factories and the Gigantic Gate are banned). More stars for winning fast.
- Gloom Queen: beat a Hard Kawaii AI as Lilith. More stars for winning fast.
- The end screen of a challenge shows your rating and offers Retry. Challenges can't be saved.

**Limitations:** Three challenges for now.

versions.title: Commander upgrades
versions.notes:
- Your Commander can level up to Level 4: the Upgrade button on her panel, or G. It's paid through the economy like a build: Level 2 600 Sparkle and 8000 Moe (40 s), Level 3 1200 / 16000 (60 s), Level 4 2400 / 30000 (90 s).
- She stands still while she upgrades; any other order pauses it and keeps the progress. Her card shows the level, the next cost and a progress bar.
- Each level: +100 build power, +600 health, +15% damage, a 3 m longer Love Beam (1 m wider Hug of Doom for Lilith), and a new outfit: a tiara, then a cape, then wings of light, with a burst of hearts.
- A warning when an enemy Commander levels up in sight. AI: Normal and Hard level their Commander when they're rich and she's safe.

**Limitations:** The panel's Upgrade button shows the old level until you reselect her.

versions.title: Stork Carrier
versions.notes:
- The Idol Sky Studio builds the Stork Carrier (Goths: Vulture Hearse), an unarmed air transport with 4 seats. Big or Tier 2 units take two. It can't carry Commanders, giants, boats, flyers or buildings.
- Select Storks and press L, then click one of your ground units (or just right-click it) to pick it up; Shift queues more. U, then a click, drops everyone there. Walkers dropped over water land on the shore.
- Passengers stay selected while they ride. If the Stork is shot down they fall out at half health; walkers that fall into the sea pop, amphibious ones swim.
- A warning the first time you see an enemy Stork. AI: Hard builds one and flies four raiders over your defences to drop them near a far pump.

**Limitations:** Passengers can't be given orders while they ride; anything you order them is dropped when they get out.

versions.title: Mega Love Bomb and the Cuddle Catcher
versions.notes:
- Tier 2 constructors can build the Mega Love Bomb Silo (Advanced tab; Goths: Doom Kiss Silo). It stockpiles bombs through the economy, about two minutes each (900 Sparkle and 12000 Moe), two at most.
- K (or the button on its panel), then click anywhere: the bomb flies for 25 seconds and lands with a 20 m blast, 5000 damage in the middle down to 1500 at the edge. It hurts everyone, your own units, flyers and subs too, and goes straight through Hug Shields.
- Where it will land shows as a pink ring with a countdown, on the ground and blinking on the minimap. Everyone is warned when a silo is started and when a bomb is launched at them.
- The Cuddle Catcher (Defence tab, no Tier 2 needed; Goths: Raven Catcher) shoots down enemy bombs aimed within 45 m. It starts with one interceptor and makes another every minute, two at most.
- AI: Hard builds a silo 8 minutes after it techs up, Normal 12; it bombs the biggest cluster of your buildings it knows, avoiding your Catchers until it has two. Any AI builds a Catcher when an enemy silo appears and walks its units out of a ring no Catcher covers.
- Long warnings now shrink to fit the screen. Timed specials (Crypts, shields, Catchers) ran about 6% slow; fixed.

**Limitations:** AI-vs-AI matches usually end before the silo comes online, so its bombing is tested in the smoke test more than in real matches.

versions.title: Hug Shield
versions.notes:
- Tier 2 constructors can build the Hug Shield (Advanced tab; Goths call it the Gloom Veil). Its bubble, 11 m across, soaks enemy bullets, shells and bombs that come in from outside, from a 2500 charge.
- Beams, stomps, Commander specials and shots fired from inside the bubble pass straight through, and so do your allies' shots. Empty, the shield drops for 15 seconds, then refills at 50 a second for 40 Moe a second.
- The bubble shows over the building and flashes when it soaks a hit; its info card has a charge bar.
- A warning the first time you see an enemy Hug Shield. AI: builds one (two at most) when its base is being shelled or bombed, and makes less artillery and fewer bombers once it knows you have one.

**Limitations:** Shields stack: two overlapping bubbles both soak, whichever is checked first.

versions.title: Whale-ship, subs, Otter Tank and an AI navy
versions.notes:
- The Dockyard now also builds the Narwhal Sub and the Whale-ship. The Whale-ship is a slow battleship that shells ground, boats and the shore from 34 m.
- The Narwhal Sub is unseen unless an enemy Rubber Duck (18 m) or Swan Cruiser (14 m) is close with its sonar, or it just fired. Only torpedoes hit it, and its torpedoes hit boats and subs only.
- The Otter Tank (Neko Motor Works) is amphibious: it drives straight across water at 60% speed. Goths get the Abyss Eel, Leviathan Coffin and Bog Gator.
- Warnings the first time you see an enemy Whale-ship and the first time a torpedo comes your way, each saying what beats it.
- AI: on water maps, Normal and Hard AIs build a Dockyard on the shore nearest home, keep their navy under a quarter of their army, group three boats and hunt enemy boats, or sail over and shell the enemy shore.

**Limitations:** Subs are hit only by other subs until the Love Bomb arrives. Boats leave no wreck.

versions.title: Water, Lollipop Lagoon and the Dockyard
versions.notes:
- A new map, Lollipop Lagoon: a round sea in the middle that every base can reach, two little lakes, four starts (free-for-all or 2v2).
- Walkers and vehicles go round water (and rocks) instead of bumping along them; send them into the sea and they stop at the shore. You can't build on water.
- The Bubble Bath Dockyard (Factories tab) sits in the sea by the shore and launches the Rubber Duck (fast scout with great eyesight) and the Swan Cruiser (guns that hit ground, boats and flyers). Boats stay in the water and bob. Goths get the Sunken Pier, Drowned Duck and Black Swan.

**Limitations:** The AI doesn't build boats yet (next version). Boats leave no wreck.

versions.title: Kawaii's own: Cheer Idol and Pep Drummer
versions.notes:
- Kawaii gets support units the Goths don't have. The Cheer Idol (Plushie Bot Lab) heals friendly units within 8 m by 12 health a second.
- The Pep Drummer (Neko Motor Works) makes friendly units within 8 m move 25% faster. Two of the same don't stack; a drummer's haste and a Banshee's slow multiply.
- So the factions now play differently: Goths slow you down and raise the dead, Kawaii heals and hurries. The AI brings support units along with its waves.

**Limitations:** Balance from 12 Normal AI-vs-AI matches: Kawaii 4, Goths 5, 3 long games still going at 25 minutes.

versions.title: Goth-only twists: Banshee and Crypt
versions.notes:
- The Gloom Goths get units Kawaii doesn't have. The Banshee (Belfry Roost) is a frail flyer whose wail slows ground units to 60% for 3 seconds.
- The Crypt (Goth Defence tab) raises the nearest wreck within 14 m as a Ghoul every 4 seconds, for 150 Moe, up to six at a time. The wreck is used up, so reclaim fields near it first. T switches it on and off.
- Warnings the first time a Banshee slows you and the first time you see an enemy Crypt, each saying what beats it.
- The Goth howitzer is now the Dirge Howitzer.
- AI: Goths build Banshees and a Crypt (two on Hard). While an AI's first Tier 2 constructor is being built on a short budget, its Tier 1 factories wait, so long matches reach Tier 2.

**Limitations:** Kawaii's own extras come in the next version.

versions.title: Veterans
versions.notes:
- Units earn xp for kills, by value: popping something pricier than you counts for more. Ranks 1, 2 and 3 each give +15% health and 10% faster reloads. Turrets and Commanders rank up too.
- Ranked units wear little gold stars over their heads, their info card says "Rank 2, 7 kills", and they cheer (with a jingle) when they rank up.
- The AI pulls ranked veterans home for repairs sooner (at half health).

**Limitations:** No xp for popping friends, unfinished buildings, or for a shell that lands after its shooter popped.

versions.title: Save and load
versions.notes:
- Save game and Load game in the pause menu, Load game on the title screen: three slots plus an autosave.
- The autosave is written every time you open the pause menu, so a long match is never more than one Esc away from safe.
- Slots show the map, the mode, the match clock and when they were saved. Everything comes back: units mid-build, orders, wrecks, shells in the air, fog you've explored, your control groups, the camera and what the AIs were planning.

**Limitations:** No saving in the guided match, the title demo or after the game is over. Saves from a later change to the save format will say they can't load.

versions.title: Playtest pass 2
versions.notes:
- Moe Converters keep at most 1500 Moe back instead of 60% of storage, so building a Moe Battery no longer switches them off (AIs were sitting on 11,000 useless Moe).
- The AI now techs up a few minutes after its tech time even on a thin Sparkle income, so long matches get Tier 2 constructors and Advanced Pumps instead of grinding to a stalemate.
- Fixed: the first click on a freshly loaded page did nothing when the page got focus with that click (no mouse movement reached the game first). Such a click is now replayed after a mouse move to the same spot.

**Limitations:** Long 3v3 games still often finish before anyone reaches Tier 2.

versions.title: Graphs, rematch, voices and KAWAII ANNIHILATION!
versions.notes:
- The end screen now draws two graphs over the whole match: Sparkle income and army value, one line per team in its colour (yours thickest).
- Rematch (new seed) replays the same settings on a fresh random game.
- Speech bubbles babble: little procedural voice blips, squeaky for Commanders and small units, low rumbles for the big ones.
- Whenever any Commander pops, a giant wobbling KAWAII ANNIHILATION! banner says whose it was.

**Limitations:** Only one unit babbles at a time, so busy fights stay listenable.

versions.title: How to play
versions.notes:
- A guided first match: six short goals (select your Commander, build a pump, make Moe, build a factory, make four fighters, attack) shown in a panel that ticks along as you do them. The Easy AI waits politely until you're done. Skip any time.
- The first time you press Play, the game offers the guided match. You can always find it again under How to play on the title screen.
- A Controls page in the title and pause menus with every key and mouse action.

**Limitations:** The guide only covers the basics; Tier 2, specials and team games are up to you.

versions.title: Twin Ribbon Rows and 3v3
versions.notes:
- A third map built for team games: Twin Ribbon Rows, six bases in two rows facing each other across a river of rocks with three crossings.
- New Game Mode 3v3: you and two AI allies against three AIs on Twin Ribbon Rows (picking 3v3 on another map switches to it). 2v2 and free-for-all work there too.
- AI armies are capped per team (120 in a duel, 60 in 2v2, 40 in 3v3) so big team games stay smooth.
- The AIs' scouting memory is now worked out once per side and shared, about 17 times cheaper in a six-AI game.

**Limitations:** Six teams share the wells, so everyone's economy is tighter and 3v3 games run long (15-25 minutes between AIs).

versions.title: Team games: 2v2
versions.notes:
- New Game has a Mode: Free-for-all or 2v2, you and an AI ally against two AIs, on either map.
- Allies share vision, never shoot each other, take only a quarter of each other's splash, and wear shades of the same colour (your ally is a lighter version of you).
- Your side wins together: if your Commander pops while your ally's still stands, you keep playing with what's left. Lose both and your whole side pops.
- AI allies defend each other's bases, share what they've scouted, and never aim waves at a friend.
- In team games your ally picks your faction; the enemy faction setting is for the other side.

**Limitations:** The end-screen stats compare you with the whole enemy side. 3v3 and a map built for teams come next.

versions.title: Music
versions.notes:
- Music! A bouncy idol-pop battle loop (drums, bass, sparkly arps and a lead tune that climbs an octave near the end) and a calmer title tune with soft pads and bells.
- Both are made by the game itself, a few milliseconds per frame while you're on the title screen, so the page doesn't freeze while loading. The title tune starts a few seconds after the page opens.
- A Music slider in Settings, separate from the sound effects volume.

**Limitations:** The battle loop is about 27 seconds long, so it repeats often in a long match.

versions.title: Smarter AI
versions.notes:
- The AI now plans with what its units have actually seen: waves head for buildings it has found (or your start, which everyone knows), not for things hidden in the fog.
- Normal and Hard counter your army: more fighters and anti-air when they've seen flyers, more artillery against turrets, more assault units against raiders, heavies against big assault armies.
- Normal and Hard pull badly hurt units home, and constructors repair them before they rejoin the army.
- Hard sends a fast scout past your base and the far wells now and then, and sends small raids at lone Sparkle Pumps it knows about.
- New alert: "A Sparkle Pump is under attack!" (or a Sparkle Siphon, for Goths).

**Limitations:** Easy plays as before. Matches against Normal and Hard run a little longer now that hurt units go home.

versions.title: Gloom Goths get their own look
versions.notes:
- Lilith has her own model: black lolita dress with a frilly hem, long black hair, a red bow, little bat wings and a parasol.
- The Bat Drone is a real bat with scalloped wings, and the Coffin Tank is a coffin on wheels with a sleepy vampire peeking out. Every other Goth unit wears bat wings on its head, and Goth buildings are dusk-coloured with a bat spire.
- Stat tilts: Goth ground fighters have 15% more health but are 8% slower and cost 10% more; Goth flyers cost 15% less and have 15% less health. Commanders, constructors and buildings match the Kawaii ones.
- Goth units have their own catchphrases (and the vampire bats really want your fuel).
- The battle behind the title screen is now Kawaii vs Goth.

**Limitations:** In 8 AI-vs-AI test matches the Goths won 5; close to even, but watch it.

versions.title: Gloom Goths
versions.notes:
- A second faction: the Gloom Goths. Every Kawaii unit and building has a spooky-cute Goth twin with its own name and joke: Skitter Spiders, Coffin Tanks, Bat Drones, the Crypt of Dolls, the Gate of Gloom and its Giga Mecha-Bat.
- The Goth Commander is Gloom Commander Lilith. Her special is the Hug of Doom (D, 500 Moe): it pops every enemy within 6 m right away and heals her for each one. Enemy Commanders and experimentals take 1500 instead.
- The New Game screen has Your faction and Enemy faction (Random, Kawaii Kingdom, Gloom Goths). The AI plays either side.

**Limitations:** For now the Goths share the Kawaii models and stats (Lilith gets a dark dress); their own looks, stat tilts and lines come next.

versions.title: Giga Mecha-Bunny
versions.notes:
- Tier 2 constructors can build the Gigantic Gate (Advanced tab), which slowly builds one Giga Mecha-Bunny: about 6 minutes on its own, faster with constructors helping.
- The bunny has 40,000 health, an eye-laser, and a stomp that hurts every enemy around its feet. It can't hit flyers, so bring anti-air friends... or enemies will.
- Everyone gets a banner when a bunny starts building and when it wakes up, even through the fog.
- It walks right over small units, takes 1500 from a Love Beam like a Commander does, and goes out in a big blast that leaves a very rich wreck.
- The Normal and Hard AI build one in long games.

**Limitations:** AI-vs-AI games usually end before the AI gets to its Gate.

versions.title: Tier 2 fighters
versions.notes:
- Advanced Plushie Lab: Teddy Titan (heavy mech with a splashy cannon) and Ninja Plush (stealthy raider).
- Advanced Motor Works: Maine Coon Tank (the toughest thing on treads) and Purr Howitzer (artillery with 60 m range, useless up close).
- Stealth: a Ninja Plush shows no radar blip and can't be seen or shot unless an enemy is within 9 m or it fired in the last 2 seconds.
- Banners the first time you see enemy Tier 2 units and a revealed Ninja Plush.
- The AI builds Tier 2 fighters once it has its Tier 2 constructors.

**Limitations:** Stealth is all-or-nothing for every team at once (any enemy close by reveals it to everyone).

versions.title: Tier 2 labs
versions.notes:
- T1 constructors can build the Advanced Plushie Lab and the Advanced Motor Works (new Advanced tab).
- They make Tier 2 constructors, the Grand Puff and the Grand Neko, with golden crowns and lots of build power.
- Tier 2 constructors build the Advanced Sparkle Pump: 6 Sparkle/s, placed on top of your own Sparkle Pump, which it replaces.
- The Normal and Hard AI tech up mid-game and upgrade the pumps nearest home first.
- AI constructors that help a factory now come back for new jobs after a while, so the AI keeps expanding (it used to stop).
- Dev key F8 spawns one of every unit and building, to look at the models.

**Limitations:** The advanced labs only make constructors so far; Tier 2 fighters come next.

versions.title: Moe Converter
versions.notes:
- New building in the Economy tab: the Moe Converter turns 60 Moe/s into 1 Sparkle/s, so a big Moe economy can pay for Sparkle-hungry armies.
- Converters only eat Moe while your storage is over 60% full, so they never slow your building down. T (or the Converting switch) turns the selected converters on and off.
- The Sparkle bar shows how much is being converted; the converter's whisk spins while it works.
- The AI builds converters when its Moe piles up.

versions.title: Area commands
versions.notes:
- Right-drag: your selection lines up along the line you drew (a short line makes extra rows). Right-click orders now happen when you let go of the button.
- P then click: patrol back and forth, fighting anything on the way; Shift+click adds more stops. Builders on patrol eat wrecks they pass.
- A then drag a circle: attack every enemy inside it, nearest first.
- R then drag a circle (builders): reclaim every wreck inside it. R then click a wreck reclaims just that one.
- Patrol loops and area circles show with the order lines.

**Limitations:** Line formation always walks; there's no attack-move version yet.

versions.title: Info cards and build tabs
versions.notes:
- Hover a build button or any unit to see its card: cost, build time with your selection, health, damage per second, range, speed and a silly line about it.
- With one unit selected, its card stays up with live health.
- Builders' menus are split into Economy, Factories and Defence tabs; Q (Shift+Q back) or a click switches, and Z X C V B N M , . are the buttons of the open tab, so every building has a hotkey.

**Limitations:** Factory menus are still one flat list.

versions.title: Playtest fixes
versions.notes:
- Every match plays out differently now (the battle used the same dice every time).
- When a Commander falls in a free-for-all, her whole army and base pop in a chain of confetti instead of standing around forever.
- The AI balances its economy better: it builds Moe when it runs dry and stops piling up orders while stalled, so it builds 60-80% faster on average.
- Kitty Racers hit a little softer and Meowtars reach a little less far: vehicle openers were winning 4 of 5 AI matches.
- Damage stats count real damage, not the overkill from Love Beams and heart blasts.
- The Love Beam tip says it pops your own units too.
- A limiter keeps the sound from crackling in big fights.
- The match starts with the camera a little further out, so you can see around your Commander.

**Limitations:** Sound was checked by numbers, not by ear.

versions.title: Performance and Candy Canyon
versions.notes:
- Big battles run much faster: each unit's model is merged into a couple of meshes (draw calls at 220 units: 3568 down to about 1000).
- Unit pushing rewritten (4x faster) and the battle simulation runs 30 times a second with smooth in-between drawing.
- Measured on desktop: 220 units fighting hold about 119 fps (low 110, was 41); 400 units about 80 fps (low 61, was 6).
- New map: Candy Canyon, a peach crater with a ring of rocks, four bases and a rich middle.
- F10 shows an FPS and draw-call overlay; add ?bench=220 to the page address for a benchmark fight.

**Limitations:** Web speed depends on the browser; the overlay shows what you get.

versions.title: Air
versions.notes:
- Idol Sky Studio: a stage that builds flyers.
- Idol Glider (fast scout with long sight), Starlet Jet (fighter, flyers only), Heartbreaker Bomber (heart bombs on ground targets), Wing Constructor (flying builder).
- Flyers hover above the battlefield with a shadow, go straight over rocks, and can only be hit by anti-air: Bubble Towers and Starlet Jets.
- The AI builds a Sky Studio later in the game and Bubble Towers when it sees your flyers.

**Limitations:** Flyers hover rather than circle; bombers stop over their target.

versions.title: Fog of war, radar, minimap, defences
versions.notes:
- Fog of war: you only see what your units see; explored ground stays lighter, enemy buildings stay on the map once seen.
- Radar Bunny: hears enemies far away and shows them as red blips. Units can shoot radar contacts but not unseen enemies.
- Minimap (bottom right): left-click or drag to move the camera, right-click to send the selection.
- Defences: Guard Kitty turret, Bubble Tower anti-air, Big Kawaii Cannon (48 m artillery). Turret heads turn to aim.
- The AI builds a radar and a few Guard Kitties.

**Limitations:** No flyers yet, so the Bubble Tower has nothing to pop.

versions.title: Anime silliness pass
versions.notes:
- Chibi models get ink outlines, blushing cheeks, tiny smiles and a ribbon for Hoshiko.
- Speech bubbles with catchphrases when you select or order units, and on kills and deaths (rate-limited).
- Bullets and stars leave sparkly trails.
- Announcer banners: First blood, Commander under attack, enemy wave incoming, factory ready, enemy Commander defeated.
- Cute procedural sounds: chirps, boops, pews, pops, a big heart boom, victory and defeat jingles.
- Title screen: pastel candy buttons over a live AI-vs-AI battle.

**Limitations:** Sounds are synthesized placeholders; no music yet.

versions.title: Skirmish AI
versions.notes:
- New Game screen: map, 1-3 AI opponents (free-for-all), Easy / Normal / Hard, and your team colour.
- The AI expands to Sparkle Wells, balances Sparkle and Moe, builds factories and constructors, reclaims wrecks.
- It gathers an army and sends growing attack waves, pulls back to defend its base, and its Commander uses the Love Beam (Normal and Hard).
- Hard AI gets a 25% income bonus. Four start spots on Marshmallow Meadow; Team Matcha and Team Lemon join the colours.

**Limitations:** One map. The AI doesn't scout or adapt its unit mix to yours yet.

versions.title: Combat and winning
versions.notes:
- Weapons with real travel: bullets, beams and arcing artillery shells with splash.
- Units shoot enemies in range on their own. Right-click an enemy to attack; A then click for attack or attack-move.
- Fire stances on F: fire at will, return fire, hold fire. Right-click a friendly unit to guard it.
- Units pop into confetti and hearts and leave plushie wrecks; right-click a wreck with a builder to reclaim its Sparkle.
- Hoshiko's Love Beam (D or the button, 500 Moe) pops everything in a line.
- Losing your Commander loses the game: she goes out in a giant heart explosion. Win/lose screen with stats.

**Limitations:** No AI opponent yet: the enemy Commander just stands there.

versions.title: Factories and units
versions.notes:
- Plushie Bot Lab (walkers) and Neko Motor Works (cat vehicles), built by the Commander or constructors.
- Factory queue: click (Shift: x5) to add, right-click to remove, Repeat toggle, right-click the map to set a rally point.
- Puff and Neko Constructors build and help; right-click a factory with a builder to guard it and speed it up.
- Starter roster per factory: raider, assault and artillery (Pom-Pom Scout, Mochi Guard, Star Lobber, Kitty Racer, Tabby Tank, Meowtar).
- Health and build-progress bars over damaged, unfinished or selected units.
- Matches now start with just your Commander, like a real RTS.

**Limitations:** Units don't shoot yet (next update).

versions.title: Economy and building
versions.notes:
- Sparkle and Moe flow economy: income and spending per second, storage caps, a resource bar on top.
- Commander build menu (Z X C V B or buttons): Sparkle Pump, Sunshine Panel, Wind Chime, Candy Jar, Moe Battery.
- Placement ghost turns green or red; pumps snap to Sparkle Wells. Shift+click queues several builds.
- Construction runs on build power with a sparkly beam; when you're short everything slows evenly.
- Right-click an unfinished building with a builder selected to help build it.

**Limitations:** No factories or combat yet.

versions.title: Battlefield, camera and orders
versions.notes:
- Marshmallow Meadow: a pastel map with rocks and Sparkle Wells.
- Each team starts with Magical Commander Hoshiko and six Pom-Pom Scouts.
- RTS camera: arrow keys or screen edges pan, wheel zooms toward the cursor, middle-drag rotates.
- Click or drag a box to select; Shift adds; double-click selects every unit of that type on screen.
- Ctrl+1-9 sets a control group, 1-9 recalls it (twice quickly centres the camera).
- Right-click moves the group in formation; Shift+right-click queues waypoints (shown as lines); S stops.

**Limitations:** Nothing to build or fight yet.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: Save code
versions.notes: - Settings > Save code: copy your whole save as a text code, and load one pasted from another device, to move between your phone and your computer.

versions.title: Lane patterns on the HUD
versions.notes: - With Lane patterns on, the HUD shows them too: a chip per lane under Nightmares incoming with how many nightmares are in it, the hover square outlined in the lane's colour, and the picked card shows which lane you're pointing at.

versions.title: Paper Airplane squadrons
versions.notes: - On Wide Awake, nights 30 and 31 send a Paper Airplane squadron: a dozen planes in three Vs across every lane. Nets and Zappers at the ready!

versions.title: Nightmare costumes
versions.notes:
- On some nights the nightmares dress up: pirate socks (night 3), dust bunnies in tiny tuxedos (night 4), wizard Roombas (night 6), bats in vampire capes (night 27).
- Purely silly. The Toy Box shows the last costume you met.

versions.title: Tooth Fairy Shop, round two
versions.notes:
- Three new treats: a Pre-Puffed Cushion (an armed Whoopee Cushion waiting in the middle lane), Dress-Up Night (a toy wears a skin you don't own yet) and an Extra Card Slot (bring 7 toys).
- Bedtime stats show how many Tooth Fairy teeth you've earned.

versions.title: Pillowcase Catch
versions.notes:
- After a boss win, a Bonus round! button: catch falling Couch Coins in a pillowcase for 15 seconds.
- Every 6 coins caught becomes a Tooth Fairy tooth; gold coins count triple.

versions.title: Rubber Chicken and Plush Octopus
versions.notes:
- New toy: the Rubber Chicken (unlocked by night 27). BWAAAK! Nightmares in the next 3 cushions run backwards in a panic.
- New toy: the Plush Octopus (unlocked by night 28) hugs up to three nightmares in its lane and the lanes next to it, and holds them for a moment.
- The Pick your toys screen fits all 16 toys.

versions.title: Sleepy toys and juice boxes
versions.notes:
- Toys that fight all night slowly get drowsy (Zs, droopy eyes) and attack a little slower: at most 5% on Sleepy, 10% on Normal, 35% on Wide Awake.
- Tap a drowsy toy for a juice box (25 coins): wide awake again and no drowsiness for 40 seconds.
- The Haunted Rocking Horse is a little softer (400 health) and night 32's last wave a little smaller.

versions.title: The Morning After
versions.notes: - The bedtime diary has a sixth page, The Morning After: the kid slept until lunch, with a doodle of every toy asleep. It's written once the last night is beaten.

versions.title: Accessibility
versions.notes:
- Settings > Lane patterns gives each lane its own colour and shape, so lanes read without colour.
- Settings > Storm flashes: Calm swaps the lightning's white flash for a faint glow.
- Settings > Place toys: Hold means holding on a cushion for a moment to place a toy, so stray taps don't.

versions.title: Pillow Fight extras
versions.notes:
- Pillow Fight: Send x5 sends five waves one behind another.
- Save mix remembers the nightmares you picked; My mix picks them again.
- The Speed button has a Slow-mo step in Pillow Fight.

versions.title: Wide Awake Insomnia and Boss Rush
versions.notes:
- With Wide Awake picked, Insomnia and the Boss Rush now play Wide Awake too, with their own best wave and best time.
- The map shows both bests and puts the wide-open-eye badge on them once you have one. Sleepy still plays them on Normal; the Daily stays Normal for everyone.

versions.title: Bedtime stats
versions.notes:
- A Bedtime stats page (Achievements, then Bedtime stats): nightmares poofed, Couch Coins collected, toys put away, your favourite toy, the longest night and nights played.
- Counting starts now; older nights weren't recorded.

versions.title: The Tooth Fairy Shop
versions.notes:
- Every story win now drops a Tooth Fairy tooth per star.
- The Tooth Fairy Shop (on the house map and the result screen) sells one-night treats for teeth: Pocket Money (100 extra coins), Mom on Speed Dial (a second Call Mom), and a Ready-Made Wall (a Blanket Wall already up).
- Treats are used on your next story night. The shopkeeper has a lisp.

versions.title: Rule-breakers
versions.notes:
- New nightmare: the Sleepwalker, arms out and eyes shut, wanders into the next lane every couple of cushions (nights 24, 26, 30, 31).
- New nightmare: the Paper Airplane glides over walls and toys, so nothing can block it; shoot it down (nights 28, 30, 31, 32).
- New toy: the Butterfly Net (75 coins, unlocked by night 26) scoops up the first flyer or sleepwalker that reaches it, then needs 6 seconds.
- Bosses fit their Toy Box picture.

versions.title: Tonight's nightmares
versions.notes:
- The loadout screen shows a "Tonight:" row of the nightmares coming, with "new!" on any you haven't beaten a night with yet, so you can pick toys to match.
- Hurt nightmares already show a small health bar (bosses have the big one).

versions.title: Turn round!
versions.notes:
- A nightmare chewing a toy turns round to bite a toy dropped in the cell right behind it (the one its back still pokes into), with a little "huh?". Drop a Blanket Wall there to rescue the toy in front.
- Works for every nightmare that bites, bosses included (big ones reach further back).
- The Blanket Wall's Toy Box card, tooltip and unlock message explain the trick.

versions.title: The bedtime diary
versions.notes:
- The kid keeps a diary now: a page per world, written once you beat its boss, with a crayon doodle of what happened.
- Open it from Diary on the house map; it says (new!) when there's a page you haven't read.

versions.title: Pillow Fight
versions.notes:
- A new sandbox on the bunk bed in the Sleepover, open once the Duvet Dragon is beaten: pick any toys, coins never run out, and nothing can lose the fort.
- Pick nightmares along the bottom and press Send wave! to send them in, or Clear to poof them all. Just for fun: no stars or achievements.

versions.title: Combo hints
versions.notes: - Pick a toy card and the cushions where it would make a combo glow pink, with a little twinkling star.

versions.title: Keyboard shortcuts
versions.notes:
- Space pauses (as do Esc and Tab), F switches to 2x speed.
- Pause, Speed, Call Mom and Pillow show their key in the corner. 1-6 pick cards, Q puts away, P picks the pillow, M calls Mom.
- A Keyboard keys page in the pause menu and in Settings.

versions.title: World 5: The Attic
versions.notes:
- Six new nights up in the attic (27-32), across the top of the house map.
- New nightmares: Attic Bats swoop between lanes, Dusty Boxes break open into moths, and Cobweb Spiders drop from the rafters and web up your toys.
- Boss: the Haunted Rocking Horse. It rocks forward, rocks back, kicks boxes off the rafters and neighs out bats. Beat it for the ending.
- The Boss Rush now has all five bosses.

versions.title: Sleepy, Normal or Wide Awake
versions.notes:
- Pick a difficulty at the bottom left of the house map. Sleepy gives more coins and slower nightmares; Wide Awake makes them tougher, faster and sooner.
- Stars count on any difficulty. Win a night on Wide Awake to put a little wide-open-eye badge on it.
- New achievement: Too Wired to Sleep (beat a boss on Wide Awake).

versions.title: Tidier insides
versions.notes: - Under the hood: the battle, the board, the art and the menus are each split into smaller files. Nothing should look or play any differently.

versions.title: Daily streak
versions.notes:
- Daily Insomnia has a calendar: a tick for every day you play, a star sticker whenever you beat your best daily wave ever, and your streak.
- The calendar on the house map opens it; Play today's night from there.

versions.title: World intro comics
versions.notes:
- Each world now opens with a little three-panel comic: the kid hears a noise, peeks out, and GASPS.
- Shown once per world, and you can skip it.

versions.title: Thunderstorm nights
versions.notes:
- A thunderstorm night in every world (nights 7, 10, 17 and 24).
- Lightning scares every nightmare back a tile, but the thunder makes your toys hide for a second.

versions.title: Boss Rush
versions.notes:
- Boss Rush: beat every boss and a trophy appears in the bathroom. All four bosses, one after another, in one night.
- Your fastest Boss Rush is saved, and beating it earns a new achievement.

versions.title: Toy combos
versions.notes:
- Toy combos: some toys get a bonus side by side. Squeaky Duck + Lava Lamp makes a Disco Duck that squeaks in a ring!
- Two Piggy Banks gossip (more coins), Teddy + Twin Teddy is a Bear Hug, Bubble Wand + Squirt Gun is a Bubble Bath.
- A sparkle when a combo forms, and the Toy Box lists every combo.

versions.title: Settings polish
versions.notes:
- Screen shake is now Big, Small or Off.
- Big text option for menus, the night's labels and the silly words.
- Reset progress (Settings, from the title): the kid asks twice, in a very silly voice, before forgetting everything.

versions.title: World 4: The Bathroom
versions.notes:
- World 4, the bathroom: nights 21 to 26, with the rubber-duck armada, Captain Quack and Slippery Soap.
- Wet floors: nightmares slide across puddles and soap suds, and toys won't stand in them. Night 23 is soaking.
- The Plughole (night 26) slurps your toys down the drain. Beat it to see the ending.
- New toy: the Squirt Gun soaks everything in its row. The house map has four rooms now.

versions.title: Bigger buttons for phones
versions.notes:
- Tested by touch at phone size: every button is now big enough for a thumb (menus, the night's buttons, Back and Skip, the Toy Box and the settings sliders).
- The loadout screen shows every toy on one screen.
- Coins can be scooped by dragging a finger across them (they always could; now the README says so).

versions.title: Toy skins
versions.notes:
- Toy skins: once every upgrade is owned, spend stars on Pirate Teddy, Disco Duck, Royal Piggy, Wizard Lamp and Cool Blanket.
- Wear them or take them off in the Toy Box. They're just for looks.

versions.title: The Ending
versions.notes:
- Beat the Toaster of Doom and the sun comes up: the kid falls asleep, the toys tuck them in, and the credits roll over the snoring.
- Watch it again from the title screen once you've earned it.

versions.title: Daily Insomnia
versions.notes:
- Daily Insomnia: a calendar on the living-room wall. Everyone gets the same waves and the same six toys each day.
- Today's best wave is saved and shown on the calendar.
- New achievement for playing a Daily Insomnia.

**Limitations:** The daily date comes from your device's clock, so the day changes at your local midnight.

versions.title: Achievements
versions.notes:
- 13 achievements with medals drawn in code, like Slept Through It (win without picking up a coin) and Mom's Favourite (a whole world without calling Mom).
- A pop-up slides in when you earn one; see them all from the title screen or the house map.

versions.title: The Brave Kid
versions.notes:
- The Brave Kid joins the fight: once a wave, press Pillow! (or P) and tap a lane, or tap the fort, to throw a pillow down it.
- The pillow bonks and knocks back everything in the lane, hits bosses extra hard, and offends cats into leaving.

versions.title: The house map
versions.notes:
- The level select is now a map of the house: the living room, the bedroom and the kitchen, with a path through every night.
- The kid shuffles along the path in bunny slippers to the next night to play.
- Boss nights have a red ring, twist nights a ! badge, and Insomnia is the moon in the bedroom window.

versions.title: Silly nightmares
versions.notes:
- Sock Puppet: holds up a stolen sock that soaks up rubber bands until it gives up.
- Roomba Riders: break the Roomba and three tiny dust bunnies hop off.
- Grumpy Cat: sits in a lane, blocks your shots and can't be hurt. Put any toy next to it to pet it away.
- They show up in the later sleepover nights, the kitchen and Insomnia.

**Limitations:** Nobody has played these yet; balance comes from the autoplayer.

versions.title: World 3: The Kitchen
versions.notes:
- World 3, The Kitchen: nights 15-20 on a tiled kitchen floor, with the fridge light on.
- New nightmare: the Midnight Snack Goblin pinches coins off the floor (or out of your pocket). Pop it to get them back.
- New boss: the Toaster of Doom pops burnt toast onto your toys from across the kitchen.
- New toys: Wind-Up Chattering Teeth (CHOMP, then chew) and the Bubble Wand (floats nightmares backwards).
- The autoplayer now brings 6 toys like you do, and a few nights got easier to match.

**Limitations:** Nobody has played World 3 yet; balance comes from the autoplayer.

versions.title: Balance and boss feel
versions.notes:
- Nights 1-3 get going sooner and are shorter, so the first nightmare shows up within 12-20 seconds.
- Night 8's last wave is bigger, so the Vroominator night feels like the end of the living room.
- Bosses are announced before they walk in, show a big health bar, and go down in slow motion.

**Limitations:** A balance pass from the autoplayer and numbers, not from people playing.

versions.title: More silliness
versions.notes:
- Stunned nightmares wear pink sleep masks.
- Toys wave hello when you place them.
- Win a night and your toys throw a pyjama party: dancing, party hats and confetti.
- Fix: the Whoopee Cushion's puff-up picture follows Quick Puff.

versions.title: Lullaby
versions.notes:
- A sleepy music-box lullaby, made in code, that speeds up during big waves and boss fights.
- A Music slider in Settings (all the way down mutes it).

versions.title: Star upgrades
versions.notes: - Spend your stars in the Toy Box: one upgrade per toy, like Bouncy Bands (a Teddy's band hits a second nightmare), Lava Lamp XL and Triplets.

versions.title: Call Mom!
versions.notes: - Call Mom! (button or M), once per night: Mom yells from the hallway and every nightmare freezes in fright for 4 seconds (bosses 2).

versions.title: Night twists
versions.notes:
- Lights-flicker nights: the far columns go dark and nightmares show only as glowing eyes, except in the lane with a night-light.
- Coin-drought nights: the couch drops far fewer coins.
- The night's intro tells you about its twist.

versions.title: World 2: The Sleepover
versions.notes:
- World 2, The Sleepover: nights 9-14 in a bedroom with a bunk bed, a nightlight and glow-in-the-dark stars.
- New nightmares: Monster Under the Bed (pops up mid-lane), Moths (fly over toys, love anything glowing), Alarm Clock (makes everything sprint), and the Duvet Dragon boss.
- New toys: Jack-in-the-Box (bonks what's close in front) and Bug Zapper Nightlight (zaps nearby nightmares, double vs flyers).
- The level select shows both worlds; Insomnia gets the new nightmares too.

**Limitations:** Balance is checked by an autoplayer; World 2 may be hard for people.

versions.title: Pick your toys
versions.notes:
- Bring up to 6 toy cards into a night. Once you own more toys than that, a Pick your toys screen comes first and remembers your last pick.
- Retry and Restart night keep the same cards.

versions.title: Insomnia
versions.notes:
- Insomnia: an endless mode, unlocked by winning night 8. Waves keep coming, bigger and tougher, with the Vroominator every 5th wave.
- Your best wave is saved and shown on the Insomnia tile.

versions.title: Phone friendly
versions.notes:
- Hover over a coin to collect it; a tap scoops up every coin within about a cell.
- Drag a card onto a cushion to place it (tapping the card then the cushion still works); bigger cards.
- In portrait the game asks you to turn your phone sideways.

versions.title: The Toy Box
versions.notes:
- The Toy Box (from the title and the level select): every toy and nightmare you've met, with its joke and numbers.
- Night 1 walks you through it: a bouncing pointer shows the Teddy card, a cushion, and the falling coins.
- The title screen has a parade of toys and nightmares bobbing around the fort.
- The wave bar no longer pokes out past its end before the first nightmare.

**Limitations:** Balance is checked by an autoplayer, not yet by people; nights 7 and 8 may be hard.

versions.title: Hold the fort: core loop, level select and 8 nights
versions.notes:
- A 5-lane cushion grid in front of the pillow fort; nightmares march in from the right and you lose if one gets into the fort.
- Couch Coins fall from the couch and pop out of piggy banks: click them to collect, spend them on toys.
- Toy cards with costs and recharge times (keys 1-7), Put Away (Q), pause and 2x speed buttons, and a wave bar with big-wave flags.
- 7 toys: Rubber-Band Teddy, Piggy Bank, Blanket Wall, Squeaky Duck, Lava Lamp, Whoopee Cushion and Twin Teddy.
- 6 nightmares: Dust Bunny, Lost Sock, Party Hat Bunny, Bedtime (yawns toys to sleep), Roomba, and the Vroominator boss.
- Level select with 8 nights, each unlocked by winning the one before; best stars saved. Win/lose screen with Next, Retry and Level select.
- Silly juice: squash and stretch, poofs with goofy words, screen shake, and synth sounds made in code.

**Limitations:** Balance is checked by an autoplayer, not yet by people; nights 7 and 8 may be hard.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: Replay your win
versions.notes:
- After a three-star win, Watch replay plays your own digs and valve taps back at triple speed, with a ghost brush showing your strokes and the gravy flowing exactly as it did.
- Works on main levels, the daily plate and Kitchen plates.

**Limitations:** Only your latest three-star win is kept, and only until you close the game.

versions.title: Star rewards
versions.notes:
- Courses now open with stars instead of finishing every level: Dessert table at 20, Leftovers at 40, Hot Kitchen at 55, Breakfast at 65.
- Earning the stars that open a course shows a New course unlocked banner on the result card, with a cheer.
- Locked course tabs say how many stars they need. Inside a course, levels still open one after another.

**Limitations:** Courses you've already played a level in stay open even if you have fewer stars.

versions.title: Breakfast
versions.notes:
- A fifth course, Breakfast, dug through a stack of pancakes: five new levels (Short Stack, Sticky Situation, Butter Pecan, Two Pancakes, Full Breakfast).
- A new liquid, maple syrup: slow, sticky (it stops where it touches anything) and it never boils. Syrup sitting on a crouton glues it, so gravy can't grab it until a fast stream of gravy washes the syrup off.
- Syrup is amber with glossy streaks; a glued crouton gets an amber glaze and drips.
- Kitchen: a Syrup tool. Share code: on the web, Show as text opens the code in a box you can copy anywhere (browsers often block the Copy button), and Paste asks for a code the same way.

**Limitations:** Syrup only appears in the breakfast levels and Kitchen plates.

versions.title: The Kitchen
versions.notes:
- The Kitchen (from the title screen): paint your own plate with mash, china, butter, air, gravy, hot sauce, hot plates, valves, up to three croutons and the boat.
- Test it straight away, save up to 12 plates on this device, and share one as a code a friend can load in their Kitchen.

**Limitations:** Bells, gates, lids, caramel and the special courses' rules aren't Kitchen tools yet. Saved plates live in this browser only.

versions.title: Daily plate upgrades
versions.notes:
- Daily plates get harder through the week: Tuesday a plate shard blocks the short way down, Wednesday a butter seal, Thursday a valve, and the weekend mixes them, with hot sauce on Sundays.
- A daily streak: days in a row you've won the daily plate, shown on the level select and the result card.
- Each day's plate has its own gravy train medal.

**Limitations:** Monday's plate is still the easy one. Every plate is still proven winnable before it's offered.

versions.title: Hot Kitchen
versions.notes:
- A fourth course, the Hot Kitchen: here hot sauce that's flowing eats through mashed potato (never china), so its channel gets deeper as it runs.
- Sauce left alone never moves, so a pool can't eat its own plug; and each drop can only eat a little before it's spent.
- Three new levels: Hot Potato, Scorched Earth and Ghost Pepper. Spicy mash has chili flecks and scorched edges.

**Limitations:** Only the Hot Kitchen levels are spicy; hot sauce everywhere else still just burns gravy.

versions.title: Daily plate
versions.notes:
- A new level every day: the Daily plate button on the level select builds today's plate from the date, the same for everyone.
- Before it's offered, the game plays the plate's own solution in the background to prove it can be won with all three stars.
- Your best stars for each day's plate are saved.

**Limitations:** Daily plates are simple: one cup, slabs off the path, sometimes a pot of hot sauce. They're checked on your device, so the button takes a few seconds to appear.

versions.title: Leftovers
versions.notes:
- A third course, Leftovers: gravy that sits still for about five seconds goes cold and sets solid where it is.
- Set gravy shows as grey-brown lumps with a pale skin; a hot plate's warmth (up to 7 blocks above it) keeps gravy runny, and steam warms set gravy back up.
- Five new levels: Cold Shoulder, Hold the Gravy, Butter Me Up, Two Pools One Pot and Steamed Leftovers.
- Leave gravy waiting too long and the level is lost: The gravy went cold and set.

**Limitations:** Only the five Leftovers levels use cooling; the main course and desserts are unchanged.

versions.title: Color-safe liquids
versions.notes:
- Hot sauce has dark pepper flecks and a dark outline, so it stands out from gravy without relying on red.
- Custard has a creamy ripple, and caramel blocks have diagonal stripes.
- Settings has a Liquid patterns toggle (on by default) for anyone who finds them busy.

**Limitations:** Gravy and steam keep their look; only hot sauce, custard and caramel got patterns.

versions.title: Pea hats
versions.notes:
- A Wardrobe on the title screen: six hats for the pea crew, from the pirate tricorn to a crown.
- Hats unlock as your star total grows (6, 15, 30, 45 and 65 stars).
- The crew wears the picked hat in every level, and it's saved.

**Limitations:** Hats are cosmetic only.

versions.title: Gravy train
versions.notes:
- A fourth medal per level: fill the boat under the par time to earn the gravy train.
- The top bar shows your time and the level's par; the result card says how you did.
- The level select shows each level's medal, and counts them under the stars.
- Wins with Show me still count for stars, not for the medal.

**Limitations:** Par times come from each level's scripted solution (1.5 times its time plus 5 s), not from human play.

versions.title: Phone play
versions.notes:
- Bigger buttons and text everywhere, so the top bar, menus, hint cards and level select are easy to tap on a phone.
- A drag that starts on the top bar no longer digs.
- Holding a phone upright shows a Turn your phone sideways card and pauses the level.

**Limitations:** Portrait isn't supported: the table is wide, so the game asks you to turn the phone.

versions.title: Show me
versions.notes:
- Stuck? After two failed tries on a level, a Show me button appears (on the loss card and the top bar).
- Show me restarts the level and a see-through ghost spoon digs the solution for you, turning valves on the way.
- Press anywhere on the field to take over from the ghost at any time.

**Limitations:** The ghost only knows each level's one scripted solution.

versions.title: Dessert table
versions.notes:
- A second course: five dessert levels dug through sponge cake, with thick, slow custard instead of gravy.
- Caramel: it can't be dug and custard won't melt it, but steam softens it away.
- The level select has Main course and Dessert table tabs.

**Limitations:** Dessert levels reuse the main course's bells, valves and hot sauce; no new dessert-only hazards beyond caramel.

versions.title: Mixed grill
versions.notes:
- Five new levels that mix everything: Butter Ring Twice, Let Off Steam, Spice and Service, Two Taps No Waiting and Chef's Special.

**Limitations:** No dessert course yet.

versions.title: Sea shanty
versions.notes:
- A short sea shanty loop plays, with its own Music slider in Settings.
- Gloopier glugs that climb in pitch as the boat fills, a crunchier crouton and a soft pour while gravy flows.
- The peas cheer when a crouton pops and squeak in panic when hot sauce gets close.

**Limitations:** The shanty is one 10-second loop.

versions.title: Splish splash
versions.notes:
- Gravy splashes where it lands, and potato crumbs fly as you dig.
- Win a level and the boat floats up, unfurls its sail and sails away.
- The pea crew cheers when gravy or croutons arrive, and panics when hot sauce gets close.

**Limitations:** Sounds are still simple placeholders; no music yet.

versions.title: Bells and valves
versions.notes:
- Service bells: gravy that touches one rings it, opening the breadstick gates (and shutting the dashed ones).
- Valves you tap to open or shut, so gravy can wait while you dig.
- Three new levels: Ding Dong Dinner, Last Orders and Turn the Tap.

**Limitations:** Sounds are still simple placeholders; no music yet.

versions.title: Full steam
versions.notes:
- Hot plates: gravy that touches one boils into steam that rises and spreads under ceilings.
- Frosty lids turn steam back into gravy at once; steam left too long cools back into gravy on its own.
- Hot sauce boils away for good on a hot plate.
- Two new levels: Full Steam Ahead and Pressure Cooker.

**Limitations:** No switches or valves yet.

versions.title: Dig and flow
versions.notes:
- Mashed potato you dig by dragging (mouse or touch), china plate shards you can't.
- Gravy is a particle liquid: it pours, pools in dips and spills over edges.
- Fill the peas' gravy boat to win; croutons the gravy touches are stars.
- Cold butter that warm gravy melts, and hot sauce that burns up gravy.
- 10 levels, a level select with best stars saved, hint cards before new hazards.

**Limitations:** No steam, switches or valves yet. Sounds are simple placeholders.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.

versions.title: Compare with a friend
versions.notes:
- The Epilogue page shows your choices as a short code, like FM-DRTXRRF-K, with a Copy code button. The code is in the copied and saved text too.
- Paste a friend's code into the field under it (Ctrl+V or the Paste button) and press Compare: both epilogues side by side, mission by mission, marked where you chose alike and where one story ended sooner. Only mine goes back.
- A code with a typo says so instead of showing the wrong story. Pasting a friend's whole saved epilogue works too.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Union leaflets on Kell Hill
versions.notes:
- A new paper on both Kell Hill desks: a Union Brigade leaflet, dropped by air over the Canton lines, telling the side you left's version of what you did. Old Margaret: the crossing at the ford. Battery M: Old Margaret.
- Read it next to the Canton bulletin: the two sides do not tell the same story, and neither may be the one you remember.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: An epilogue you can keep
versions.notes:
- The Epilogue page has two buttons: Copy as text puts the whole page on the clipboard, and Save as file downloads it as fire-mission-epilogue.txt (on desktop it goes in the game's user folder, and the page says where).
- The text ends with a one-line list of your choices, mission by mission, so two playthroughs can be compared at a glance.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Canton radio intercepts
versions.notes:
- A new paper under the map on four Union desks: our signals section's log of Canton army radio, reporting an earlier mission the way the Cantons tell it to each other. Counter-battery: the ridge radar. The Tannery: The Works. The Mill: The Tannery. Across the River: The Works and The Mill.
- Read it next to the Courier: what they print and what they say on the radio are not always the same thing.
- The papers under the map fit six now, so the tabs are a little narrower on busy desks. Town plan tabs read Plan: Vessen and so on; the met tab after a wind shift reads Met: NEW.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: The epilogue
versions.notes:
- When the story ends, wherever your choices end it, the mission file gets an Epilogue page after the last mission, and the last debrief has an Epilogue button.
- It lists each choice you made and what came of it, in the debrief's plain voice: the ridge radar, The Works, The Tannery, The Mill, and the river and Kell Hill if you got that far. Plus the rounds you fired in all.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Papers that change
versions.notes:
- Later editions: the papers under the map now report what you did on an earlier mission, or what the other side says you did. A new Harl Courier on the Counter-battery, Mill and Across the River desks, and a Canton HQ bulletin on both Kell Hill desks.
- What they print depends on how that mission went: the ridge radar, The Works, The Tannery (whichever building you hit), The Mill, the crossing and Old Margaret.
- The debrief now remembers which targets each mission hit. Saves from before this version read The Tannery as nothing hit.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: The Canton desk
versions.notes:
- The second act has its own desk: a colder Canton command post, orders on a grey Canton message form, a field telephone instead of the radio, Canton papers with a red rule.
- Canton firing tables give elevation in mils (6400 to the circle), and the Kell gun's elevation counter reads mils too. Range is still metres and the protractor still degrees.
- Canton recon: both act missions can send Canton photo flights, but your old Union radar on the hill at Tamm (426 721) shoots them down while it turns. One round on it opens the sky. Your old papers know where it is.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: The other bank
versions.notes:
- If you cross the river at the end of Across the River, the story goes on: two secret missions on the Canton gun on Kell Hill, aimed back at your old side.
- 11, Old Margaret: Canton HQ wants Battery K's command post hit tonight. Your old standing orders are still in your pocket. 12, Battery M: the Union guns walk their salvos onto Kell Hill; a fire plan you never handed in knows where they are. Each ends on your choice.
- The map table, protractor and radio now follow whichever gun you're on. The protractor goes all the way round.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Town plans that disagree
versions.notes:
- Town plans of Osk and Harlby join the Vessen one. The Works now has the Osk plan on the desk.
- New mission 8, The Tannery (Harlby), before The Mill: Brigade wants a Canton depot in the old tannery. An old town plan, a Canton notice and the Harl Courier don't agree about what is in the building. Recon prints can settle it, if Air can fly. The debrief says what was really there.
- The Mill and Across the River are now missions 9 and 10.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Wind that shifts
versions.notes:
- On The Works, The Mill and Across the River the wind changes partway through: a while after your first round, a new met message comes off the teletype and the solution that was hitting starts to drift.
- The radio only says a message has come in. The tab under the map reads Met station: NEW; open it and the wind vane swings round, with the new strip under the morning's (struck through).

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Across the river
versions.notes:
- A secret mission 9, Across the River, comes after The Mill, but only if you fired on neither the school nor the works. It isn't listed in the mission file until then.
- Brigade orders a column on the north bridge shelled. A note from across the river says what the column is and offers a way over. You can fire as ordered, hold fire, or put your rounds somewhere that makes sure nobody fires at all, and cross.

**Limitations:** Charges (more than one muzzle speed per shell) are planned for later.

versions.title: Weather on the desk
versions.notes:
- From mission 4 on, the weather moves the shells: wind drifts them downwind, warm air carries them further, high pressure and rain bring them short.
- A met station under the map table: wind vane, anemometer, thermometer, barometer, rain gauge and the morning's met message.
- The range book has a MET page with the corrections and how far the wind drifts each shell. Or just correct from the spotter, as before.
- Smoke on the map now drifts with the wind.

**Limitations:** Switching sides and charges are planned for later rounds.

versions.title: Recon flights
versions.notes:
- A recon request form sits under the map table: put the pin on a square, send the form, and a plane flies out over it. The prints come back pinned to the map.
- While the Canton radar on the ridge is working, recon planes are shot down and bring nothing back. Knock it out in Radar Before the Raid and the sky opens for later missions.
- The Works and The Mill no longer come with photos on the table: ask Air for them, if you can. Counter-Battery gets one flight too.

**Limitations:** Weather and switching sides are planned next.

versions.title: Find it yourself
versions.notes:
- Nobody tells you what a target really is any more: no note to check the photos, no spotter's gasp. What you hit is told plainly in the debrief, after the fact.
- Papers tucked under the map table: click an edge to pull one out. A town plan of Vessen with every 100 m square numbered, a Canton notice, the Harl Courier, a letter off a prisoner.
- New mission 7, The Works: the Osk shell works, a real target. The Mill is now mission 8.

**Limitations:** Recon flights, weather and switching sides are planned next.

versions.title: Against the clock
versions.notes:
- Timed missions: a stopwatch clipped to the orders runs while you work.
- New mission 5, Radar Before the Raid: three minutes to knock out the radar before the bombers cross.
- New mission 6, Counter-Battery: no grid, just a flash bearing and a rough range. Enemy salvos land closer every 40 seconds; the fourth hits the gun.
- The Mill is now mission 7, still the last.

**Limitations:** Switching sides, wind and charges are planned for later rounds.

versions.title: Sound and feel
versions.notes:
- Sounds, all made in code: the gun's boom, the breech clank, a shell sliding home, wheel ratchets, the far-off crump, radio static, paper.
- The desk shakes when the gun fires; impacts flash on the map, and smoke rounds leave a cloud that drifts east and thins out.
- On the first two missions the loader gives a hint for the next step if you've been still a while.

**Limitations:** Timed missions, counter-battery fire and switching sides are planned for later rounds.

versions.title: Recon photos and the mill
versions.notes:
- Recon photos pinned to the map: click one to see what's really in that square.
- Mission 5, The Mill: the orders' grid and the photos don't agree. Fire as ordered, fire on what the photos show, or question the order on the radio and hold fire.
- Each choice has its own ending in the debrief, and the choice is remembered.
- A QUERY switch on the radio when an order can be questioned.

**Limitations:** No sound yet. Timed missions and switching sides are planned.

versions.title: Campaign: four missions and a choice
versions.notes:
- A mission file to pick missions from, with briefings; each mission unlocks the next. Progress is saved.
- Debrief after each mission: what your shells did (or didn't) change.
- Smoke and armour piercing shells, each with its own range table page. HE can't hurt a bunker; smoke only blinds.
- Missions 2 to 4: Supply Road, Two Bridges (six rounds, three targets: choose), Smoke for the Crossing.
- CEASE FIRE switch on the radio ends a mission where it stands.

**Limitations:** No sound yet. Recon photos and the harder choices come next.

versions.title: Gun, breech and the fire loop
versions.notes:
- Lay the gun: traverse and elevation each have a big wheel (drag it round, or scroll for 1°) and a fine knob (0.1° a notch), with mechanical counters.
- Lift a shell from the rack, load it into the open breech, close the breech with the lever and pull the lanyard.
- The shell flies across the map; the spotter radios where it landed and the correction. Hit the water tower to finish the mission.
- Right-click puts a carried shell back in the rack.

**Limitations:** One mission so far. No sound yet.

versions.title: Map table and range table
versions.notes:
- The command post desk: the Harl valley map sheet on the map table, orders on a clipboard, the spotter's radio log.
- Click a 100 m square on the map to drop a pin; the plotting arm and protractor show its range and bearing as tick marks to read.
- A range table booklet for HE: find the elevation for your range (turn pages with the corners or the mouse wheel).

**Limitations:** The gun can't be laid or fired yet; that's next.

versions.title: First playable
versions.notes: - Title screen, pause menu (Esc or Tab), settings, and this version log.
